headline: ExxonMobil signals $4.5 billion refining earnings boost as margins soar By Reuters
summary_text: Oct 16 (Reuters) - ExxonMobil signaled on Friday that higher refining margins during the third quarter could boost its downstream profit by $4.5 billion compared with the previous three months. Refining margins have soared due to the ongoing Iran war, which has restricted energy exports through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries. The resulting higher fuel prices have created political risks for the administration of US President Donald Trump ahead of the midterm elections in November. The top US oil producer’s expected refining boom could further draw the ire of the president, who complained in August that Exxon and Chevron were making "too much money". Exxon’s regulatory filing indicates that adjusted net income for the refining business could jump to $8.5 billion, wrote BMO Capital Markets analyst Phillip Jungwirth in a research note. That would be more than double last quarter’s profit level. Here are more details from Exxon’s earnings preview: • Upstream earnings could take a $1.3 billion hit compared with the second quarter. The average closing Brent benchmark price declined about 5.6% during the third quarter compared with the previous three months, according to LSEG data. • Exxon indicated that there were no volume-related disruptions during the quarter stemming from the Iran war. • The company’s move to divest some upstream assets will boost earnings by $700 million. • Exxon will release full third-quarter results on October 30. • Exxon shares were up less than 1% in pre-market trading.

headline: ExxonMobil at Barclays energy-power conference: growth through disruption By Investing.com
summary_text: Wednesday, 09 September 2026 — ExxonMobil (XOM) used the Barclays 40th Annual Energy-Power Conference to argue that its scale, technology and project discipline are helping it navigate a volatile energy market. Chief Financial Officer Neil Hansen said the company is benefiting from supply disruptions and higher refining pressure even as it faces a modest drop in Guyana volumes and a broader market still shaped by geopolitical risk. Hansen presented a largely upbeat case for ExxonMobil’s strategy, while acknowledging that the current energy system is under strain. He said the company is leaning on its integrated model, strong balance sheet and long-term investment approach to create value across commodity cycles. ... ## Key takeaways - ExxonMobil said its core strengths are technology, project execution and operations, which it believes help it outperform rivals in volatile markets. - The company said its Pioneer acquisition is producing about $4 billion in annual synergies, double the original target. - Guyana cost recovery reached $55 billion about two years ahead of schedule, setting up a lower volume profile but stronger free cash flow. - Management said the company remains highly selective on acquisitions and wants deals where its capabilities can create more value than the current owner. - ExxonMobil highlighted new growth areas in LNG, Proxxima advanced resins and graphite battery materials, along with continued frontier exploration. ... ## Financial results and capital discipline Hansen pointed to ExxonMobil’s balance sheet and shareholder returns as evidence of financial strength. - Net debt to capital stood at 11%, after a $7 billion reduction in the most recent quarter. - The company holds an AA- credit rating. - ExxonMobil has raised its dividend for 43 consecutive years. - Management said that record represents performance that is 95% better than most S&P 500 companies. - The 2030 plan still calls for $25 billion in earnings growth and $35 billion in cash flow growth, though Hansen said the cash flow figure is now trending closer to $30 billion. Hansen said ExxonMobil’s capital allocation remains disciplined and focused on projects that can generate returns through the cycle. He said the company does not chase volume for its own sake and prefers opportunities where its capabilities can unlock more value. ... . - In the Permian Basin, the company said it is developing 40 complementary and stackable technologies aimed at improving primary and secondary recovery. - The stated goal is to double recovery rates in the Permian. - ExxonMobil said it is improving capital efficiency, lifting volume recovery and reducing the number of wells needed for similar production. - The Pioneer acquisition has been integrated successfully, combining ExxonMobil’s scale with Pioneer’s operating methods. - Hansen said the deal has gone better than expected, with synergies rising from an initial $2 billion annual estimate to about $4 billion. He also said ExxonMobil is executing major projects at a pace and cost advantage over peers. - The company said it is executing double the number of major projects relative to competitors. - Those projects are being delivered at 20% lower cost and 20% faster than peers. - Turnaround costs are about 30% lower than in the previous cycle. - Turnaround duration is about 50% shorter than in the previous cycle. ... On Guyana, Hansen said ExxonMobil reached a major milestone by recovering its $55 billion cost bank about two years ahead of schedule. He said the fifth floating production, storage and offloading vessel, or FPSO, is now operating in Guyanese waters, and a ninth FPSO is under evaluation. - The cost bank desaturation happened in the third quarter. - Entitled volumes are expected to fall by about 100,000 barrels a day starting in the third quarter. - Even with that reduction, ExxonMobil expects Guyana free cash flow to roughly double between 2025 and 2030. - Hansen said the faster recovery shows the value of ExxonMobil’s execution and its role as a preferred partner for resource owners. ... ## Supply disruption and market response Hansen discussed the impact of Middle East tensions and the Strait of Hormuz on global energy flows. He said the market has been able to function through inventory releases and demand destruction, but refining has become the main pressure point. - He said the biggest pinch point in the system is now refining capacity. - ExxonMobil has qualified alternative crude sources for Asian refining operations. - The company used its trading and supply chain network to redirect products to the highest-value outlets. - Hansen said the company’s technology and operations teams can respond quickly when supply routes are disrupted. He said the scale of available inventory releases, including strategic and commercial stocks in the U.S. and Brazil, was larger than many expected. Still, he noted that the market remains exposed to geopolitical shocks, and the current tension in the Strait of Hormuz may be viewed by some as a new normal. ... ## Future outlook ExxonMobil said its growth plan through 2030 remains intact, with several major drivers already in motion. Supporting this outlook, InvestingPro data shows that 6 analysts have revised their earnings upwards for the upcoming period, signaling growing confidence in the company’s trajectory. For investors seeking deeper insights, InvestingPro offers access to over 10 additional exclusive tips for XOM, along with comprehensive financial health scores and Fair Value analysis. - Permian Basin growth is expected to come from technology-led recovery gains. - Guyana remains a major source of earnings and cash flow growth, with more FPSOs possible over time. - LNG projects are advancing in Papua New Guinea, Mozambique and Golden Pass on the U.S. Gulf Coast. - Management said confidence in the 2030 plan is rising as execution continues. Looking beyond 2030, Hansen said ExxonMobil is preparing for a broader set of opportunities. - The company plans to keep investing $1 billion a year in frontier exploration. - It will continue pursuing discovered but undeveloped resources with strategic partners. - Future structural savings are expected to come more from organizational redesign and enterprise-wide systems than from asset sales. - Hansen said the company is increasingly defined by its capabilities rather than by a single product line. ... ## New businesses: Proxxima and graphite Hansen highlighted two newer businesses as examples of how ExxonMobil is trying to extend its chemistry and materials expertise into new markets. - Proxxima, the company’s advanced resins business, has completed final investment decision on a blend plant with 120,000 KTA of capacity. - He said the technology is proving out, with uses that include lighter and stronger rebar and single-coat applications instead of three coats. - In graphite, ExxonMobil is working with original equipment makers to show benefits such as faster charging, more capacity and longer battery life. - Both businesses are still in the market development and customer adoption phase. ... During questions, Hansen returned several times to the theme of value creation across the full energy chain. - He said ExxonMobil’s integrated model gives it visibility across the value chain and helps it see where value is moving. - He noted that value can shift over time, citing the pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine war as examples of how different parts of the chain can become more profitable. - He said the company’s central capabilities in technology, project execution, operations, supply chain and trading help it respond to those shifts. - On M&A, he said ExxonMobil wants to be a “very picky acquirer” and only pursue deals where it can add capabilities and create more value than the current owner. - He described the Pioneer deal as a template for future acquisitions, though he said geography is not the main driver; low-cost, advantaged and high-return assets are. ... It’s doing that in a way where we can leverage our capabilities, and again, hopefully the capabilities of the other company to create more value for our shareholders and their shareholders. headline: NNPCL, Shell, ExxonMobil, Eni Advance $21bn Bonga Southwest Project Towards FID - businessstandardsng.com
summary_text: Nigeria’s deepwater oil industry has moved a major step closer to a new investment cycle, with the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and its partners advancing the Bonga Southwest/Aparo (BSWAp) project towards Final Investment Decision (FID). NNPCL, Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production Company Limited (SNEPCo), Esso Exploration and Production Nigeria (Deepwater) Limited and Nigerian Agip Exploration Limited (NAE) have executed addenda to the Oil Mining Lease (OML) 118 Production Sharing Contract (PSC) and the related Dispute Settlement Agreement (DSA). The agreements give effect to fiscal and commercial terms approved by the Federal Government for the development of the BSWAp project, potentially unlocking between $15 billion and $21 billion in investment over the life of the project. NNPCL announced the development in a statement signed by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odey. The milestone comes as Nigeria seeks to attract fresh capital into its oil and gas sector after years of declining upstream investment and production challenges. The BSWAp development is therefore significant not only for the participating companies but also for the country’s efforts to expand crude output, strengthen foreign-exchange earnings and restore investor confidence in deepwater projects. ... ##### Bonga Southwest project targets 175,000 barrels per day The BSWAp project is projected to reach peak production of approximately 175,000 barrels of oil per day, alongside about 140 million standard cubic feet of gas per day, according to NNPCL. At that production level, the project could become one of Nigeria’s most important new deepwater developments and provide a significant addition to national crude oil output. The project is also expected to generate substantial economic activity through spending on engineering, fabrication, offshore construction, marine logistics, operations and other services. For Nigeria, the investment could translate into higher government revenues and foreign-exchange inflows, while creating opportunities for indigenous companies across the oilfield services value chain. ... The latest agreements follow President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s approval of the Deep Offshore Oil and Gas Projects Incentives (Tax Remission) Order, 2026, which forms part of the government’s broader efforts to improve the competitiveness of Nigeria’s deepwater petroleum industry. The policy measures are aimed at making large-scale offshore projects more commercially attractive at a time when international oil companies are increasingly demanding competitive fiscal terms before committing billions of dollars to complex developments. ... phase The OML 118 contractor parties have also completed the project’s Pre-Front End Engineering Design (Pre-FEED) phase. The partners said the work had helped mature the technical and commercial scope of the development and positioned the project to proceed to the Front End Engineering Design (FEED) stage. However, the transition remains subject to the required partner, assurance and governance approvals. The partners have also selected a preferred Floating Production Storage and Offloading (FPSO) contractor following a competitive process. The selection is still subject to applicable partner, regulatory, assurance and governance requirements. Once approved, the preferred contractor will provide a basis for advancing the FPSO concept into FEED and completing the engineering and commercial work needed to move the project towards FID. Any eventual award of the FPSO Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Installation (EPCI) contract will similarly remain subject to the necessary approvals. ... The movement of BSWAp towards FID will also be closely watched by investors as a test of whether Nigeria’s recent petroleum-sector reforms can convert policy changes into large-scale capital commitments. Deepwater projects typically require substantial upfront investment, long development timelines and sophisticated offshore infrastructure. Consequently, fiscal stability, regulatory certainty and timely project approvals are critical to securing investment. The BSWAp agreements therefore represent more than a contractual milestone. They signal an attempt by Nigeria to rebuild confidence among international oil companies and accelerate the development of large offshore resources.

The overall headwinds affecting its chemicals business have weighed on Shell's earnings in recent years, though improved chemicals margins in the second quarter of this year helped boost earnings. ... ## What a winning bid would mean for ExxonMobil If Exxon wins the bidding for Shell's U.S. chemicals assets, it would significantly expand the U.S. energy giant's domestic petrochemical footprint. That would enhance its scale advantages, enabling it to leverage its greater scale to get more out of these assets. A core aspect of Exxon's long-term strategy is delivering structural cost savings, which it could enhance by acquiring assets that would increase its scale and enable operational synergies. Further, it would do so at a significant discount to replacement cost. It would be buying assets near the cycle's low point, which is ideal timing because it would enable the company to capitalize on the next cyclical recovery and expansion. ... A deal for Shell's U.S. chemicals assets would also enable ExxonMobil to continue to diversify beyond oil and gas. Exxon already has a meaningful product solutions portfolio (energy, chemical, and specialty products) that it's investing heavily to expand, including new products like Proxxima. Exxon currently aims to deliver $9 billion in earnings growth from its product solutions businesses by 2030, at constant margins relative to 2024, driven by investments to expand its high-margin products and achieve structural cost savings.

headline: ExxonMobil Pushes Ahead With $20bn Mozambique LNG Project
summary_text: ## KEY POINTS - ExxonMobil has awarded new engineering contracts for the Rovuma LNG project in Mozambique as it moves towards a 2026 final investment decision. - The $20 billion project is designed to produce 18.6 million tonnes of LNG annually from 12 modular trains, with start-up targeted for 2031. - Rovuma LNG could strengthen Mozambique’s position as a major global LNG exporter and boost foreign investment, government revenue and industrial development. ExxonMobil is advancing preparations for the $20 billion Rovuma LNG project in Mozambique, awarding new engineering contracts as the massive gas development moves closer to a final investment decision (FID) expected in 2026. The development represents a significant step for Mozambique’s ambition to turn its large offshore gas reserves into a major source of export revenue, industrial growth and energy investment. ExxonMobil has awarded engineering contracts for the first phase of Rovuma LNG, allowing detailed project planning to move forward ahead of the expected 2026 FID. McDermott has received a letter of intent from ExxonMobil, acting on behalf of the Area 4 partners, for limited engineering and procurement services. McDermott will work alongside the SMDC joint venture, made up of Italy’s Saipem, South Korea’s Daewoo Engineering and Construction and China Petroleum Engineering and Construction Corporation. The companies will work on advancing the project’s engineering definition and planning for the midstream development. McDermott previously carried out front-end engineering design work for Rovuma LNG. Its latest involvement will allow engineering activities for the liquefaction facilities to progress as ExxonMobil and its partners prepare for a potential final investment decision. ... Rovuma LNG is planned as a major onshore liquefaction project with an annual production capacity of 18.6 million tonnes of liquefied natural gas. The facility will comprise 12 modular LNG trains supplied with natural gas from Mozambique’s offshore Area 4 reserves. If approved and developed as planned, the project is expected to begin production in 2031. However, construction and the start-up schedule remain dependent on ExxonMobil and its partners reaching the expected FID in 2026. The scale of the project makes it one of Mozambique’s most significant planned energy developments and a major potential contributor to the country’s future LNG exports. ... Despite the progress on Rovuma LNG, Mozambique’s LNG industry continues to operate against the backdrop of security challenges, particularly in Cabo Delgado. The security situation previously disrupted TotalEnergies’ major LNG project and has remained an important consideration for companies and investors evaluating Mozambique’s energy sector. ... The movement into further engineering work is an indication that preparations are continuing ahead of the crucial FID. If Rovuma LNG receives final approval and reaches production, it could significantly strengthen Mozambique’s position in the global LNG market. An annual output of 18.6 million tonnes would place the project among the major LNG developments globally and could substantially increase Mozambique’s export capacity. The project could also generate demand for construction, engineering, logistics, marine services and other supporting industries. For Mozambique, increased LNG exports could provide foreign exchange earnings and government revenue while attracting additional international investment into the country’s energy infrastructure. The development of Rovuma LNG also has wider implications for Africa’s energy sector.

headline: ExxonMobil Proposes $80 Billion Kashagan West Venture Wit...
summary_text: ExxonMobil proposed an $80 billion Kashagan West venture with KazMunayGas targeting 600,000 bpd, pending resolution of Kazakhstan's $150 billion arbitration. ExxonMobil has formally proposed an $80 billion joint venture with KazMunayGas to develop the untapped western portion of Kazakhstan's Kashagan oil field in the Caspian Sea. The venture targets production of 600,000 barrels per day from reserves ExxonMobil estimates at roughly 10 billion barrels. One condition controls the entire deal: Kazakhstan must first resolve a $150 billion international arbitration claim and a separate $5 billion environmental fine against current Kashagan operators. ExxonMobil holds a 16.81% stake in the existing Kashagan eastern section, which currently produces approximately 450,000 barrels per day, according to World Oil. The western section remains entirely undeveloped. ExxonMobil has proposed offering minority stakes to existing Kashagan consortium partners as part of the new venture structure. ... Kazakhstan's government claims roughly $150 billion in revenue lost to development delays at Kashagan over two decades. That claim is in international arbitration. A separate $5 billion environmental fine has been levied against the consortium, of which ExxonMobil, Eni, Shell, TotalEnergies, and CNPC are all members. The government has made clear that new investment approvals depend on resolving both matters. The scale of the dispute dwarfs the proposed investment. ExxonMobil's $80 billion offer equals roughly 53 cents for every dollar Kazakhstan claims it is owed. Whether Astana treats this venture as compensation or as consideration separate from the arbitration will likely determine whether a final investment decision is reachable by 2030. ... Kazakhstan already carries significant overproduction pressure within the OPEC+ framework. Compensatory cut obligations ran from 503,000 barrels per day in January 2026 to 669,000 barrels per day in June, as Oil Authority reported in its OPEC+ compliance analysis. Much of Kazakhstan's production reduction reflected infrastructure disruptions rather than voluntary restraint, per that reporting. Adding 600,000 new barrels per day at peak Kashagan West output would deepen the country's OPEC+ compliance burden when the project eventually comes online. ... ExxonMobil reported $14.7 billion in adjusted Q2 2026 earnings, with the Pioneer Natural Resources integration driving free cash flow to $17.2 billion for the quarter, as Oil Authority covered in its Q2 earnings analysis. That cash generation gives the company leverage to fund the $250 million concept study and an estimated $2 billion in front-end engineering design work scheduled to begin in 2028. A final investment decision is targeted for 2030 at the earliest.

headline: ExxonMobil Offers $80 Billion Kashagan Expansion if Disputes Are Settled
summary_text: ExxonMobil is prepared to develop the western section of Kashagan with KazMunayGas and invest around $80 billion in the project. The proposal, however, is conditional on Kazakhstan settling its long-running disputes with the field’s foreign shareholders, Orda.kz reports, citing Bloomberg. The plan calls for a joint venture owned equally by ExxonMobil and KazMunayGas. If implemented, the western section of Kashagan could produce an additional 600,000 barrels of oil per day. The field’s eastern section currently produces around 450,000 barrels per day. According to Bloomberg’s sources, KazMunayGas has backed the proposal. The main obstacle is Kazakhstan’s unresolved claims against the foreign members of the North Caspian consortium. Kazakhstan is seeking around $150 billion in compensation for revenue it says was lost because of years of delays in developing Kashagan. A separate dispute concerns an environmental fine of approximately $5 billion over sulfur storage. Orda.kz previously explained how Kazakhstan seized NCOC property and vehicles during the sulfur dispute and warned the company’s managing director that he could face criminal liability. ExxonMobil’s proposal would tie the settlement of these cases to the launch of the new project. Existing consortium members could be offered minority stakes in the joint venture. Companies that join would be released from the environmental claims once the venture is established. The remaining claims would be dropped after a final investment decision is made. Consortium members that decline to participate could also have the claims against them withdrawn if they agree not to challenge the new venture’s right to develop western Kashagan. However, once the current license expires in 2041, they would not be able to extend their participation in the eastern section of the field.

headline: Guyana LNG Export Capacity Cut: Exxon’s Gas Needs Reshape the Project
summary_text: Energies Media reports that Guyana is considering reducing planned LNG export capacity or using more gas domestically, following ExxonMobil’s estimate that roughly 2 billion cubic feet per day could be needed for reinjection to support oil production. The article says a proposed facility originally planned for 6 million tonnes per year might instead start at up to 3 million tonnes, though no government decision had been made. The issue highlights a trade-off between oil production, LNG exports and domestic industrial and power needs.

headline: ExxonMobil signals $4.5 billion refining earnings boost as margins soar
summary_text: ExxonMobil indicated that stronger refining margins could lift third-quarter downstream earnings by about $4.5 billion compared with the second quarter. Reuters linked the margin surge to disruptions to energy exports through the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on Russian refineries. The company also signaled a possible $1.3 billion upstream earnings decline quarter over quarter as average Brent prices fell, while asset divestitures were expected to add about $700 million.

headline: Exxon raises 2050 global emissions forecast, sees slower coal decline
summary_text: ExxonMobil’s annual energy outlook raised its estimate for annual global energy-related carbon emissions in 2050 to 30 billion metric tons, from 27 billion in the prior outlook. The company cited a slower projected decline in coal use and lowered its estimate for carbon capture and storage by 2050. Reuters also reported that Exxon expects oil demand to reach about 105 million barrels per day in 2050, unchanged from its previous projection.

headline: Floodwater overwhelmed pump at Exxon Mobil's Joliet, Illinois refinery; facility remains offline following outage
summary_text: ExxonMobil said floodwater overwhelmed a pump at its Joliet refinery, which remained offline after a power outage triggered a shutdown. The outage was traced to ComEd power lines feeding the facility, and the company said power had been restored. The disruption affected a key fuel supplier to the U.S. Midwest during a period of pressure on global fuel supplies.

headline: Exxon advances talks to return to Venezuela's Orinoco Belt, sources say
summary_text: ExxonMobil was negotiating a possible return to Venezuela and had expressed interest in the Petromonagas heavy-oil project and areas of the neighboring Carabobo block, according to sources cited by Reuters. The company had sent a technical team to assess deposits. Reuters noted that Petromonagas has an operating upgrader but may require substantial maintenance and repairs after years of underinvestment.

headline: Exxon Mobil shuts down Joliet refinery after power outage
summary_text: ExxonMobil shut its Joliet, Illinois, refinery after a power outage triggered the facility’s safety flare and a plant-wide shutdown. The company said it was assessing the refinery’s status and investigating the cause. The refinery supplies key fuels to consumers in the U.S. Midwest.

headline: Angola's ANPG, ExxonMobil and Block 15 partners announce new offshore discovery
summary_text: ExxonMobil and its partners announced a discovery at the Vicango Este-01 exploration well in Angola’s offshore Block 15. The well encountered about 25 metres of high-quality hydrocarbon-bearing sandstone. It was the block’s 20th discovery; Block 15 has produced more than 2.7 billion barrels over three decades.

headline: TotalEnergies to lower stake in Papua LNG, hand operatorship to Exxon
summary_text: TotalEnergies agreed to sell a 9.1% interest in Papua LNG to its partners and transfer operatorship to ExxonMobil, which would raise Exxon’s stake to 34.1%. The partners were working toward a final investment decision expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. Reuters reported that project capital costs had been reduced to about $14 billion and that the planned facility would produce 5.6 million tonnes of LNG annually.

headline: ExxonMobil awards $1.1 billion in contracts for Mozambique's Rovuma LNG project
summary_text: ExxonMobil awarded about $1.1 billion in pre-investment contracts for upstream equipment for Phase 1 of the Rovuma LNG project in Mozambique. OneSubsea received the largest award, covering subsea production systems, controls and umbilicals; other named suppliers included Aker Solutions Mozambique, Advanced Technology Valve, Corinth Pipeworks, Sumitomo Corporation of America and Zhejiang Jiuli Hi-Tech Metals. The contracts advance the project while establishing a broad supplier base.

headline: ExxonMobil advances Rovuma LNG with McDermott engineering award
summary_text: ExxonMobil awarded McDermott a letter of intent for limited engineering and procurement services for Phase 1 of the Rovuma LNG project in Mozambique. The work represents a step toward a final investment decision expected later in 2026, advancing ExxonMobil’s regional LNG development plans.

headline: ExxonMobil Picks Sercel's Marlin for Guyana Offshore Operations
summary_text: ExxonMobil Global Projects selected Sercel’s Marlin solution to help manage simultaneous offshore operations on the Whiptail development in Guyana’s Stabroek Block. Under a one-year contract, the system will support pipelay and mooring installation campaigns, representing a specialist supplier award for the offshore project.

headline: Shafaq News..Iraq signs seawater project deal with ExxonMobil
summary_text: [ExxonMobil: partnership] Iraq's Basra Oil Company signed a memorandum of understanding with US energy giant ExxonMobil on Wednesday for the second phase of a seawater supply project designed to support oil production, with a planned capacity of 2.5 million barrels of water per day, the Oil Ministry announced. Oil Minister Bassem Al-Abadi said the project would help maintain reservoir pressure at oilfields by supplying water for injection, supporting sustained production and future output increases. According to a ministry statement, the project will complement a separate seawater development project being implemented by France's TotalEnergies, with a capacity of 5 million barrels per day. Al-Abadi said the agreement was part of the government's strategy to attract international energy companies, introduce advanced technologies and develop Iraq's oil industry. He added that the ministry had signed memoranda of understanding with several US companies, including Chevron and ExxonMobil, to support oilfield development and technology transfer.

headline: Exxon AI Guyana oil analysis cut to days
summary_text: [ExxonMobil: organization] ExxonMobil is deploying artificial intelligence to transform how it reads seismic data offshore Guyana. His core claim: interpretation that once took several months now completes in a few days. The system applies deep learning and classification methods, alongside reinforcement-learning techniques. It scans subsurface and seismic information, then produces a ranked list of geological anomalies.

This capability is particularly important for operations in the European northern region, where uninterrupted deliveries are critical to maintaining production reliability. In addition to increasing supply security, the vessel supports Borouge International's focus on operational efficiency. Equipped with an LPG dual-fuel engine and energy-saving technologies, the ship is designed to reduce fuel consumption and lower emissions compared with conventional vessels. ... The addition of Lumi Aurora builds on Borouge International's long-standing collaboration with shipping partner IINO Lines. It also reflects the company's continued efforts to strengthen its global logistics network and ensure reliable access to feedstock from international markets. ... ##### About the vessel - World's first VLGC with Ice Class IB certification - Approximately 93,000 m³ cargo capacity - Designed for year-round service in Baltic Sea conditions - Powered by a LPG dual-fuel engine with energy-efficiency technologies - Will transport LPG from North America to Borouge International's Porvoo site

headline: Borouge International expands European recycling capacity to strengthen circular materials supply | Borouge International
summary_text: # Borouge International expands European recycling capacity to strengthen circular materials supply Vienna, Austria; October 7, 2026 – Borouge International today announced investments to expand its European mechanical recycling capacity at its sites in Niedergebra, Germany, and Wildon, Austria.The expansion strengthens Borouge International’s ability to meet growing customer demand for mechanically recycled polyolefins produced in Europe. It also supports customers in securing more reliable access to circular materials driven by brand preference, evolving regulatory requirements such as the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR), and supply resilience needs. At Borouge International Niedergebra, formerly mtm plastics, annual output of recycled mixed polyolefin (rPO) materials will increase by close to 9 kilotonnes.The facility transforms post-consumer mixed polyolefin waste into valuable recycled materials for a broad range of rigid applications. The additional capacity is expected to become operational in the first quarter of 2027. At Borouge International Wildon, formerly Ecoplast, annual recycled polyethylene (rPE) output will increase by up to 5 kilotonnes. The additional capacity is expected to come on stream in the fourth quarter of 2027 and will support growing demand for recycled materials, particularly for flexible packaging applications. Borouge International Elin Pelin in Bulgaria, a facility which produces more than 20 kilotonnes of premium-quality grades of post-consumer recycled polypropylene (rPP) annually, completes Borouge International’s European mechanical recycling portfolio and complements capabilities across flexible PE, rigid PP and mixed polyolefin streams. ... Borouge International serves its customers with circular solutions in Europe and beyond. In North America, top quality PE film grades are supplied from the Syndigo™ plant in Indiana, US and in Asia, Borouge International collaborates with a wide portfolio of suppliers for recycled material. ... “Circular materials are a strategic resource for Europe and around the world, not only to meet sustainability and regulatory requirements, but also to strengthen industrial competitiveness, brand differentiation and supply resilience,” said Dirk Langhammer, Senior Vice President Circular Solutions, Borouge International. “The investments in our European recycling platform give an even larger range of customers more reliable access to circular polyolefin solutions, from premium Borcycle™grades to fit-for-purpose Recleo™ materials tailored to diverse applications.”

headline: Investments to boost Borouge’s mechanical recycling capacity for plastics
summary_text: Borouge International has invested in mechanical recycling capacity at multiple plastic recycling facilities, aiming to boost its annual output by 14 kilotonnes and help customers meet recycled content requirements. At its facility in Niedergebra, Germany (formerly mtm plastics GmbH), Borouge International converts post-consumer mixed polyolefin waste into recyclate materials for various rigid plastic applications. The latest investment is set to boost its annual recyclate output by almost 9 kilotonnes once the additional capacity becomes operational in Q1 2027. Meanwhile, its facility in Wildon, Austria (formerly Ecoplast) is expected to increase its annual recycled polyethylene output by up to 5 kilotonnes in Q4 2027. This is anticipated to support growing demand for recycled materials, especially in flexible packaging applications. The investments are anticipated to help Borouge International offer customers more reliable access to mechanically recycled polyolefins produced in Europe. In turn, it hopes to help brands meet incoming legal requirements, including those set out in the EU’s Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation. The increased outputs are also thought to contribute to a more competitive and resilient materials value chain and help scale circular solutions around the world. ... Borouge International’s European mechanical recycling portfolio is completed by its facility in Elin Pelin, Bulgaria. Said to produce over 20 kilotonnes of ‘premium-quality’ post-consumer recycled polypropylene every year, this location is intended to complement capabilities across flexible polyethylene, rigid polypropylene, and mixed polyolefin streams. In North America, it supplies polyethylene film grades from its Syndigo plant, located in Indiana, USA. Borouge International also collaborates with various suppliers for recycled material across Asia. Earlier this year, Borouge and Borealis teamed up with Catalytic Finance Foundation, Pelita Mekar Semesta and Reciki Solusi Indonesia to establish Indonesia’s ‘first’ fully integrated circular waste management ecosystem. The initiative set its sights on transforming plastic waste into a valuable feedstock for recycling.

summary_text: # Investering van ruim 1 miljard in Antwerpse haven: Borouge International, het vroegere Borealis, opent eind dit jaar nieuwe fabriek Terwijl de Europese chemiesector kraakt onder de hoge energieprijzen, opent Borouge International, het vroegere Borealis, eind dit jaar toch een nieuwe fabriek in de Antwerpse haven om propaan om te zetten in propyleen. Het gaat om een investering van meer dan 1 miljard euro, die in Kallo honderd extra jobs heeft opgeleverd. Christof Willocx Antwerpen 05 oktober, 2026 Dat de fabriek weldra opengaat, is opvallend nieuws. Momenteel worden er immers volop jobs afgebouwd in de Europese chemiesector, door de hoge gasprijzen die de productiekosten doen oplopen. Borouge International heeft op de site in Beringen in Limburg enkele weken geleden nog aangekondigd dat daar tegen 2029 dertien jobs zullen verdwijnen door de hoge productiekosten, weliswaar zonder naakte ontslagen. Maar in december opent Borouge International dus toch een gloednieuwe fabriek in de Antwerpse haven. Waarom doet het bedrijf dat, terwijl de Europese chemie in een crisis verkeert? Het gaat hier officieel om een propaandehydrogeneringsfabriek – dertig letters die bij het woordspel Scrabble 58 punten zouden opleveren. Het bedrijf spreekt dan ook liever van een PDH2-installatie: de ‘2’ omdat er in Kallo al een soortgelijke installatie staat, die PDH1 heet. ... “We zijn al in 2019 met de bouw van de fabriek in Kallo begonnen, dus lang voor de huidige problemen in de Europese chemie”, zegt Wim De Smet, sitemanager van Borouge International in Kallo. “Maar we hebben zeker geen spijt van onze investering, omdat we onze productie in het huidige geopolitieke klimaat over de hele wereld willen spreiden, zodat we beter bestand zijn tegen conflicten (zoals bijvoorbeeld de sluiting van de Straat van Hormuz in het Midden-Oosten, red.).” “We zijn lang voor de problemen in de chemie met de bouw van deze fabriek begonnen. Maar we hebben zeker geen spijt, omdat we onze productie over de hele wereld willen spreiden, zodat we beter bestand zijn tegen conflicten” ... “Bovendien is deze nieuwe PDH2-fabriek veel milieuvriendelijker dan onze andere installaties. We hebben minder energie nodig om onze productieprocessen te laten draaien, en worden in die zin dus iets minder hard getroffen door de hoge energieprijzen.” ... “Tot slot komt er tijdens het productieproces van de fabriek ook waterstof vrij”, zegt Wim De Smet. “Door het sterke netwerk van chemiebedrijven in de Antwerpse haven kunnen we die waterstof via pijpleidingen makkelijk tot bij klanten brengen. Het propyleen dat we met de fabriek produceren, kunnen we overigens ook in andere Europese fabrieken van Borouge International gebruiken, waardoor we minder afhankelijk worden van schommelende marktprijzen voor propyleen.” ... De nieuwe PDH2-fabriek levert ongeveer honderd extra jobs op. “Die mensen zijn in de voorbije maanden en jaren al aangeworven, omdat we ze een lange opleiding hebben gegeven om met de nieuwe installaties te kunnen omgaan”, zegt De Smet. “In totaal stellen we op onze site in Kallo nu 330 mensen te werk. Dat is dus met de PDH1-fabriek en onze polypropyleenfabriek inbegrepen. Het zijn niet alleen medewerkers die rechtstreeks in de productie werken, maar ook mensen die ondersteunende functies uitoefenen, bijvoorbeeld in het laboratorium, of in de onderhouds- en veiligheidsdiensten.” ... Borouge International vertrekt voor zijn PDH2-fabriek van propaan. Dat is een bijproduct van aardgas. Voordat aardgas kan worden gebruikt, worden gassen zoals propaan eruit gehaald, vloeibaar gemaakt en opgevangen. “Wij kopen ons propaan voor de site in Kallo aan in de Verenigde Staten en ook in Europa”, zegt Wim De Smet. “Met onze PDH-installaties maken we daar propyleen van, de grondstof van onze polypropyleenfabriek. Dat product verkopen we aan bedrijven in Noord- en West-Europa die het gebruiken in voedselverpakkingen, maar ook in auto-onderdelen of voor medisch materiaal zoals infuuszakken in ziekenhuizen.” ... De investering van Borouge International is de derde investering van meer dan 1 miljard euro die momenteel in de Antwerpse haven wordt uitgevoerd, naast de renovatie van de Europaterminal en de bouw van de ethaankraker van Ineos Project One.

summary_text: # Borouge International Inaugurates Specialty Compound Plant in Austria and Strengthens European Supply of Advanced and Circular Polypropylene Vienna, Austria; September 28, 2026 – Borouge International today announced that it has started commercial operation of its specialty polypropylene compounding facility in Schwechat, Austria. The start-up follows an investment of more than €100 million to expand and upgrade the site. The new facility further strengthens Borouge International’s manufacturing footprint in Europe, helping ensure a reliable supply of advanced compounds for customers across the region. The investment supports regional economic growth and reinforces Austria's position as a strategic location for advanced industrial production, while enhancing Schwechat's role as a key hub for innovation, manufacturing excellence and customer collaboration. ... At the new facility, polypropylene resins are compounded with recycled polypropylene and performance-enhancing additives to create tailored material solutions that combine lightweight design, optimized performance and increased circularity. The expansion increases the availability of specialty compounds for key growth sectors, including: - Appliances, Structured Products and household applications, where high-performance materials with recycled content help manufacturers respond to growing market demand. - Mobility, where more circular materials help car manufacturers meet the requirements of the European End-of-Life Vehicles (ELV) regulation. Lightweight polypropylene compounds also help reduce the overall weight of battery electric vehicles and contribute to a lower environmental impact. - Infrastructure, where specialty compounds are used in protective coating solutions for steel pipes transporting oil and gas at high temperatures. These materials help provide corrosion resistance and long-term performance in demanding operating environments.

headline: OMV-Tochter: Stolperstart für Österreichs Milliarden-Start-Up Borouge International – DiePresse.com
summary_text: Ende August war die Hektik groß in der Wiener Trabrennstraße. Die OMV-Tochter Borouge International (BI) musste ihren geplanten Milliarden-Börsengang für heuer absagen. Zudem verabschiedete sich Vertriebschef Stefan Doboczky völlig überraschend aus der Führungsriege des neu geformten Petrochemiegiganten. Sein Wechsel an die Spitze der Schweizer Hovione Holding habe durchaus irritiert, erzählen Involvierte. Mit Roland Janssen fand sich zwar rasch guter Ersatz. Die Staatsholding Öbag aber verlor ihren letzten Österreicher im Vorstand von BI. Was ist los bei Österreichs größtem Konzern? ... Einer, der es wissen muss, ist der Roger Kearns. Der Amerikaner ist seit Anfang des Sommers in Wien, von wo aus er die Geschicke des Kunststoffkonzerns Borouge International lenkt. Aus dem Zusammenschluss der OMV-Tochter Borealis, Borouge aus Abu Dhabi und der kanadischen Nova Chemicals soll bekanntlich der viertgrößte Polyolefin-Hersteller der Welt werden. 10.000 global Beschäftigte soll der Industrieveteran Kearns dafür zusammenführen. „Unser Ziel ist es, ein Unternehmen mit einer gemeinsamen Kultur zu sein“, sagt der BI-Chef zur „Presse“. ... Neben einer gemeinsamen Kultur stehen natürlich auch noch 500 Millionen Dollar an Kosteneinsparungen (Synergien) auf seiner To-do-Liste. Was ihm bei seiner Arbeit am „60-Milliarden-Dollar-Start-Up“ in die Karten spielt, ist die starke Technologie aus Europa, die günstige Produktion im Nahen Osten und der gute Zugang zu allen großen Weltmärkten. ... ## Warum musste Borouge International den Börsegang verschieben? Das Problem: Borouge International braucht Geld, da es eine kostspielige Expansion hinter sich hat. Der Börsegang, mit dem auch eine Kapitalerhöhung geplant ist, sollte 3,5 bis vier Milliarden US-Dollar in die Kassen spülen. Derzeit winken die involvierten Investmentbanken aber ab. Das Marktumfeld für Petrochemieunternehmen sei einfach zu schlecht, heißt es. Auch auf die Verschuldung müsse das Unternehmen aufpassen. Statt an die Börse zu gehen, halbierte Borouge International daher die geplante Dividende. Der Hälfteeigentümer OMV erhält für 2026 damit nur noch 250 statt 500 Millionen US-Dollar. Der Börsegang soll nun 2027 erfolgen – vorausgesetzt das Umfeld bessert sich. ... Dem erhofft reibungslosen Start von Borouge International kam vor allem die Geopolitik in die Quere. Der Krieg im Nahen Osten hat zwar Preise für Kunststoff in Europa und den USA nach oben getrieben, aber auch die wichtigste Produktionsbasis des Unternehmens stark beschädigt. Im Frühling wurden die Borouge-Anlagen in der Industriestadt AL Ruwais getroffen, zwei Cracker standen in Flammen, die Produktionskapazität im zweiten Quartal sank auf 60 Prozent. Dazu wurde der Export der Ware über die Straße von Hormuz schlagartig beendet. Plötzlich waren Erfolgsmeldungen aus den Vereinigten Arabischen Emiraten Mangelware. ... Zumindest manche Probleme sind heute aber gelöst. „Die Reparaturarbeiten wurden erfolgreich vorangetrieben, und die volle Verfügbarkeit der Anlagen war bis Ende Juni wiederhergestellt“, heißt es vom Unternehmen. Im September eröffnete BI das lange erwartete neue Werk für Spezialkunststoffe in Al Ruwais. Projekt „Borouge 4“ soll über drei Jahre einen kumulierten Nettogewinn von bis zu 400 Millionen Dollar bringen. Mitarbeiter von Borouge im Kontrollraum des Industriekomplexes Ruwais. Reuters/Christopher Pike Auch der Transport aus der Region ist inzwischen kein Problem mehr. Täglich sind tausend LKW von den Produktionsanlagen zum Hafen in Fujairah am Golf von Oman unterwegs. Von dort werden die Waren in alle Welt verschifft. „Wir haben unsere Lieferkette und unsere Versandrouten so widerstandsfähig wie möglich gestaltet“, meint Kearns dazu. „Unser Ziel ist es, sicherzustellen, dass sich unsere Aktivitäten in allen drei Weltregionen gegenseitig unterstützen und wir unseren Kunden zusichern können, dass wir weiterhin liefern“. ... Mittelfristig wird es für die Standorte in Europa aber nicht reichen, den Ersatzmann für die Golfregion zu spielen. Dafür ist die Produktion hierzulande schlichtweg zu teuer. Damit Werke wie die Raffinerie in Schwechat langfristig im Konzern mitspielen können, müssen sie mehr liefern als nur kleine Plastikkügelchen aus Öl und Gas. Die Borealis-Anlagen in der OMV Raffinerie Wien Schwechat sollen Kunststoff-Spezialitäten liefern. Imago / Imago Möglich wird das durch eine sogenannte Compounding-Anlage, wie sie am kommenden Montag in Schwechat im Rahmen eines Besuchs von Wirtschaftsminister Wolfgang Hattmannsdorfer eröffnet wird. Hier werden die Basis-Kunststoffe mit weiteren Materialien und Rezyklaten zu maßgeschneiderten Werkstoffen veredelt. „Bei Hochleistungs-Seekabeln beispielsweise sind die Reinheitsanforderungen an das Polyethylen außerordentlich hoch, um elektrische Entladungen durch das Kabel zu verhindern“, gibt Roger Kearns ein Beispiel. Für diese Spezialitäten kämen „Technologien und Produktionsanlagen zum Einsatz, über die wir in Europa verfügen.“

headline: Borouge International Showcases Advanced Polyolefin Cable Solutions at Wire China 2026 | Borouge International
summary_text: # Borouge International Showcases Advanced Polyolefin Cable Solutions at Wire China 2026 - Strengthening customer access to a broader global platform with localized support and reliable supply across Asia’s energy infrastructure needs - Showcasing advanced cable material solutions for critical power transmission, renewable energy and optical fiber applications - Advancing capacity investments through Borouge 4’s new XLPE plant in the UAE and semiconductive material production in Cheonan, South Korea to support electrification, renewable energy growth and long-term customer value Borouge International is presenting its strengthened global platform and full portfolio of advanced energy polyolefin solutions at wire China 2026 under the theme of “Bringing Energy All Around, Together.” At the exhibition, Borouge International is highlighting a broad portfolio of advanced material solutions for submarine, land-based, high-voltage direct current (HVDC), extra-high-voltage (EHV) and optical fiber cable applications. headline: Borouge International commercializes XLPE products from new Borouge 4 UAE plant | Borouge International
summary_text: press-release Thursday, September 10, 2026 # Borouge International commercializes XLPE products from new Borouge 4 UAE plant - Following successful testing of materials with industry partner Ducab, Borouge International’s new Cross-Linked Polyethylene (XLPE) plant reaches commercialization - XLPE plant, part of Borouge 4 project in the UAE adds 100,000 tonnes of annual capacity, doubling Borouge International’s XLPE output in the Middle East & Asia regions - New plant strengthens company’s ability to deliver premium polyolefin solutions, driving value for shareholders ABU DHABI, UAE – VIENNA, Austria, September 10, 2026 – Borouge Group International AG (“Borouge International”) today announced that, following the successful completion of performance testing, it has delivered the first batch of materials from its new Cross-Linked Polyethylene (XLPE) plant in the UAE to customers in the region. The new XLPE plant adds 100,000 tonnes of annual capacity, doubling Borouge International’s current XLPE output in the Middle East and Asia region per year. XLPE is used in high-voltage underground and underwater power cables that support grid expansion, electrification, and the transformation of energy systems. Borouge Plc, part of Borouge International, operates the region’s only XLPE plant of its kind, strengthening its ability to meet rising demand from fast-growing economies and data centers across Asia and the Middle East. Borouge International collaborated with Ducab, a leading UAE-based end-to-end energy solutions provider and manufacturer of high-quality cables and wires, to successfully test the performance of the initial batch of materials produced at the new XLPE plant. Following the successful completion of testing, Borouge International is ramping up production at the new plant to deliver material for medium and high voltage applications that will support the global energy transformation and decarbonization initiatives. ... As part of the required approval process for any materials produced at the new XLPE facility, Borouge International completed extensive benchmark testing against approved materials from its existing assets. Building on the ongoing collaboration between Borouge International and Ducab, medium and high voltage cables will be manufactured at Ducab’s cable plant where they have been subjected to a rigorous testing program in accordance with international standards. ... Borouge International and Ducab’s collaboration has supported landmark UAE developments including Saadiyat Cultural District, Zayed National Museum, Ducab Headquarters, and the Borouge 4 expansion, with future demand expected from major projects such as Palm Jebel Ali. Borouge 4 will be operated by Borouge Plc on behalf of the project’s owners ADNOC and OMV and will boost the company’s production capacity by 1.4 million tonnes to make Ruwais the world’s largest single-site polyolefin complex. Borouge 4 is expected to generate a cumulative net profit of up to $400 million over three years, representing approximately 10% annual accretion to Borouge Plc earnings post-ramp-up. Borouge Plc has been granted operational control and marketing rights for Borouge 4 by the project owners via a usage agreement. This framework gives Borouge Plc greater flexibility in managing the asset and in capturing value over time, without requiring upfront capital investment from Borouge Plc.

ABU DHABI, UAE – 31 July 2026: Borouge Plc (ADX symbol: BOROUGE / ISIN AEE01072B225) (“the Company”) delivered a resilient second quarter performance in 2026, demonstrating the strength of its operations, supply chain agility and financial discipline despite adverse regional developments. Following the incident on 5 April at its Ruwais complex, the Company restored full asset availability ahead of schedule with the successful repair of affected assets completed by the end of June. The Company successfully shipped all volumes produced during the quarter as well as additional volumes from inventory. As a result of the Company’s operational and commercial resilience, Borouge Plc, reported in Q2 2026 an increased revenue of $1.4 billion (Q1 2026: $1.2 billion), adjusted EBITDA of $401 million (Q1 2026: $343 million), and net profit of $191 million (Q1 2026: $156 million), supported by sales volumes of 0.9 million tonnes. The Company benefitted from a 53% increase in average realised prices quarter-on-quarter (QoQ), supported by stronger global polyolefin pricing and record premia for Borouge’s differentiated products. ... Repair work commenced following a period of assessment and was expedited throughout the second quarter. Asset availability at the site was fully restored by the end of June, although production has since been constrained by feedstock availability. The cost of repair is expected to result in only a limited increase in maintenance capex for 2026. ... In the second quarter, Borouge Plc recorded production volumes of 0.7 million tonnes and sales volumes of 0.9 million tonnes. The Company successfully developed alternative logistics routes via road, rail and sea which enabled it to ship beyond volumes produced during the quarter, supporting continued customer supply despite regional disruption. Borouge’s utilisation rates in the quarter averaged at 60%. With asset availability now fully restored, Borouge is well positioned to return to high utilisation rates during the second half of 2026 depending on logistics and feedstock availability. ... Borouge Plc delivered increased revenues of $1.4 billion in Q2 2026, 20% higher QoQ. The Company maintained customer supply across its core markets, with sales volumes of 0.9 million tonnes during the quarter. Delivering growth – Borouge 4 Borouge Plc continues to make positive progress on the Borouge 4 expansion project, set to boost the Company’s production capacity by 1.4 million tonnes, with the new Cross-Linked Polyethylene (XLPE) plant reaching commercialisation. Following successful performance testing, the Company delivered the first batch of materials to customers with the new plant set to add 100,000 tonnes of annual capacity, doubling Borouge Plc’s XLPE output, and strengthening its ability to deliver premium polyolefin solutions. As the world's fourth-largest polyolefins producer with 13.6 million tonnes of annual production capacity across 30 global manufacturing sites, Borouge International is well positioned to deliver long term growth and value. Borouge International delivered a strong adjusted EBITDA of $1.8 billion in Q2, demonstrating the resilience of its business model and the immediate benefits of its diversified global footprint, premium product portfolio, and disciplined operational execution. As part of Borouge International, Borouge Plc’s annual dividend intention of 16.2 fils per share remains in place. The timing of the proposed tender offer, which will convert Borouge Plc shares to Borouge Group International AG shares, will align with the new company’s future equity raise, to maximise value for all shareholders. The tender offer is expected to take place in 2027, subject to market conditions and approval by the UAE Capital Market Authority. ... Outlook In the second half of 2026, a recovery in utilisation rates will be dependent on the level of free movement of maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, with Borouge production facilities fully positioned for a fast recovery in production and sales volumes, subject to feedstock availability. Average realised pricing is expected to remain elevated in the short term, while logistics costs are expected to remain high. Further guidance will be given as appropriate and as the regional situation develops. Borouge retains significant financial resilience to navigate short term operational disruption.

headline: Sigma Healthcare posts 21% EBIT growth in first full merger year, flags double-d
summary_text: Sigma Healthcare posts 21% EBIT growth in first full merger year, flags double-d # Sigma Healthcare posts 21% EBIT growth in first full merger year, flags double-digit sales momentum Sigma Healthcare (ASX: SIG) has delivered its first full-year results as a merged entity with Chemist Warehouse Group, reporting normalised EBIT of $1.09 billion for FY26, a 20.6% increase that… FC Fiona Calder Health & Biotech · 21 Oct 2026 · 4 min read Sigma Healthcare (ASX: SIG) has delivered its first full-year results as a merged entity with Chemist Warehouse Group, reporting normalised EBIT of $1.09 billion for FY26, a 20.6% increase that validates the strategic logic of the February 2025 combination. Chairman Michael Sammells and Managing Director Vikesh Ramsunder addressed shareholders at the company’s annual general meeting on Wednesday, outlining a year of integration progress and sustained retail momentum that has carried into FY27. ## The numbers Group revenue rose 15.5% to $10.8 billion for the year ended 30 June 2026. The normalised EBIT figure of $1.09 billion compares to pro forma EBIT of $605 million disclosed in the merger prospectus for FY24, a near-doubling of earnings power across the combined platform. The balance sheet remains conservatively positioned. Net debt of $663 million at year-end represented 0.57 times normalised EBITDA, providing headroom for growth investment. Sigma paid fully franked dividends totalling 4 cents per share for the year. ## Integration and synergies The company achieved $32 million in annualised synergy benefits during FY26, at a one-off cost of $26 million. The work included consolidating support centres in Preston, closing a standalone e-commerce distribution centre, and rationalising Western Australian distribution with volume absorbed into the Canning Vale facility. Since year-end, South Australian volumes have also transferred into Sigma’s Pooraka distribution centre. The company is now mapping change management requirements for an integrated technology solution built on Sigma’s established SAP platform. “While some financial benefits have already been realised, we expect further benefits to flow through on an annualised basis,” Ramsunder said. ## Network expansion The global pharmacy network now exceeds 950 stores. In Australia, Chemist Warehouse operated 561 stores at 30 June, adding 24 new locations and refurbishing 18 during the year. The domestic network still represents less than 10% of Australia’s more than 5,900 community pharmacy licences. Internationally, the company added 20 stores with New Zealand leading growth. Ireland is now profitable after intensified efforts during the year. In May, Sigma announced a joint venture with Greenlight Pharmacy to enter the United Kingdom. The company expects to open two stores in London before Christmas, with a further three planned for 2027. The physical presence in China is being progressively closed. ## Boots decision Sammells addressed the company’s participation in due diligence for the potential acquisition of Boots UK, the largest pharmacy group in the United Kingdom. Following a disciplined assessment, Sigma made a commercially driven decision not to proceed. “A business like Boots rarely comes to market so we felt obliged to have a look at it and regardless of where that may have taken us, it also provided an interesting insight into the UK market,” Sammells said. The withdrawal, announced in June, followed preliminary discussions confirmed earlier that month. ## Trading update Ramsunder provided a trading update showing continued momentum in the current financial year. Australian Chemist Warehouse stores recorded sales growth of 12.1% to 16 October, above the 10-year compound annual growth rate of 11.3%. Like-for-like sales for the same period rose almost 10.0%. Some discretionary categories including ladies fragrances, vitamins and supplements are experiencing softness as consumers adjust buying behaviour amid cost-of-living pressures. Less discretionary categories such as beauty, healthcare and GLP-1 supporting products delivered strong performance. The company noted it has now cycled the initial structural uplift from GLP-1 sales introduction. Oral GLP-1 formulations are anticipated to enter the market in the second half of FY27, expected to enhance accessibility for patients and sales growth for the network. International sales for the three months to 30 September rose 30.2%, with like-for-like sales up 15.8%. For the first half, Sigma remains on track to onboard 14 Chemist Warehouse stores and 42 Amcal and Discount Drug Stores in Australia, together with 19 stores internationally. “For the balance of the first half, we expect Chemist Warehouse branded store sales to deliver double digit sales growth consistent with this trading update,” Ramsunder said. ## Governance Sammells addressed questions about board composition, acknowledging that a majority of directors are not currently independent and the board does not yet meet gender diversity expectations of some shareholders. The current board composition resulted from a shareholder vote at the February 2025 extraordinary general meeting. “I remain confident that the current Board brings the skills, expertise, experience and knowledge required at this stage of our journey. As the business evolves, there will be appropriate opportunities to consider changes to the Board’s balance and composition,” Sammells said. Related-party transactions remain a significant feature of the business. Sammells noted that achieving the stated goal of 900 Chemist Warehouse stores across Australia will require an increase in non-related-party franchisees, and the proportion of related-party transactions is expected to decline over time as the network grows. ## What’s next Sigma enters FY27 focused on capturing remaining integration benefits, sustaining domestic momentum and measured international expansion. The UK joint venture with Greenlight Pharmacy provides the first test of the company’s ability to export its retail model beyond Australasia, with the initial London stores due before year-end. The Christmas trading period will provide the next read on whether the double-digit sales momentum can extend through the first half. ## Key questions What was Sigma's EBIT growth in FY26? Normalised EBIT rose 20.6% to $1.09 billion for the year ended 30 June 2026, the first full 12-month period operating as a merged group with Chemist Warehouse. How is the Australian Chemist Warehouse network performing in FY27? Sales grew 12.1% to 16 October, above the 10-year compound annual growth rate of 11.3%. Like-for-like sales for the same period rose almost 10.0%. What is the status of the UK expansion? Sigma expects to open two stores in London before Christmas through a joint venture with Greenlight Pharmacy, with a further three planned for 2027. Why did Sigma withdraw from the Boots acquisition process? Following a disciplined assessment during due diligence, Sigma made a commercially driven decision not to proceed with the potential acquisition of the UK pharmacy chain.

headline: Chemtrade Logistics Income Fund Announces Plans for Conversion to a Simplified New Corporate Structure to Support Long Term Growth - Chemtrade Logistics Inc.
summary_text: ### Chemtrade Logistics Income Fund Announces Plans for Conversion to a Simplified New Corporate Structure to Support Long Term Growth - Simplifies Chemtrade’s structure and enhances comparability with publicly traded peers - Broadens access to global investors by removing the non-resident ownership restrictions - Provides greater financial flexibility to execute Chemtrade’s Vision 2030 growth strategy - Expected to maintain the current annualized distribution level through a quarterly dividend TORONTO, Ontario, October 9, 2026 – Chemtrade Logistics Income Fund (TSX: CHE.UN; OTCQX®: CGIFF) (“ Chemtrade” or the “ Fund”) announced today a proposed conversion of the Fund from an income trust to a corporate structure pursuant to a court-approved statutory plan of arrangement (the “ Plan”), and subject to the terms and conditions set forth in an arrangement agreement entered into between the Fund and Chemtrade Inc. (“ PubCo”) dated October 9, 2026 (the “ Arrangement Agreement”). Subject to the receipt of certain approvals, unitholders of the Fund (“ Unitholders”) will receive one common share of PubCo (each, a “ PubCo Common Share”), a new public corporation formed under the Business Corporations Act (Ontario) (the “ OBCA”), for each unit of the Fund (each, a “ Unit”) held by such Unitholder. The transactions under the Plan are expected to be completed on or about December 18, 2026, subject to obtaining Unitholder, stock exchange and court approvals and the satisfaction of all other customary conditions. ... “By focusing on operational excellence, disciplined commercial execution, and balance sheet optimization, Chemtrade today is a different company than it was several years ago. Rohit Bhardwaj, Chemtrade’s Chief Financial Officer, added, “Over the past several years, we have focused on strengthening our balance sheet, optimizing our capital structure, and lowering our cost of capital. Converting to a corporate structure is an important next step in that progression and we expect that it will broaden our investor base over time. The Fund is a publicly traded open-ended trust established under the laws of the Province of Ontario. The principal considerations in favour of converting the Fund to a corporation are to expand Chemtrade’s investor base, simplify the capital structure to one that is more generally accepted and understood by the capital markets and global investors, permit more streamlined comparison of financial and operational performance to Chemtrade’s corporate peers, and remove the inherent restriction on non-resident ownership (under the Fund’s existing Declaration of Trust, ownership of Units by non-residents of Canada cannot exceed 49%). ... Sigma today announced a 20.6 per cent lift in normalised EBIT to $1.09 billion, with the group’s international segment the standout after delivering EBIT growth of 91.3 per cent to $55.8 million. This was generated from $1.6 billion in sales from a 98-store offshore network including Chemist Warehouse stores across New Zealand, Ireland and China. The UK market entry will be pursued through a joint venture with Greenlight Healthcare, with two stores expected to open by the end of calendar year 2026. Notably, Sigma separately withdrew from the sale process for UK pharmacy chain Boots in June this year, concluding the acquisition would not meet its strategic and capital objectives. The company appears to have opted for a ground-up market entry rather than a large-scale acquisition. ... The group launched more than 470 new own and exclusive label products during the year, with sales approaching $1 billion, or almost 10 per cent of Chemist Warehouse network sales. “Our Wagner Pharmaceuticals generics business grew over 30 per cent as it achieved 88 per cent customer adoption across the Chemist Warehouse network, and our INC. sports nutrition protein brand is the number two selling protein brand across our Australian pharmacy channel,” says Ramsunder. Ireland became profitable for the first time during the year, with sales growth of 45 per cent, while New Zealand delivered more than 20 per cent sales growth from its network of 75 stores. ... Across the domestic business, Sigma operates 561 Chemist Warehouse-branded stores in Australia as part of a broader franchise network that also includes the Amcal and Discount Drug Stores banners. The group reported normalised EBIT of $1.03 billion from its Australian retail pharmacy segment, up 17.8 per cent. The company declared a final dividend of 4c per share, fully franked, bringing total FY26 dividends to 7.5c per share. Sigma's results mark the first full financial year since the Chemist Warehouse merger was completed, a deal that transformed the former pharmaceutical wholesaler into one of Australia's largest listed retail groups. The merger received ACCC approval after the competition regulator concluded it was unlikely to substantially lessen competition in the retail pharmacy or wholesale pharmaceutical markets. In the first half of FY27, Chemist Warehouse plans to open 13 stores across Australia, at a similar pace to prior years, along with the planned 19 Chemist Warehouse stores internationally, including its entry into the UK market. The Amcal and Discount Drug Stores networks will also return to growth, with a combined 42 stores to open across Australia in the first half.

That’s an additional 35 million units for the year. This is where the benefits of scale, automation, and our fixed and variable cost structure make a difference to the bottom line. It is important to note, this is not an SAP implementation. It is an SAP upgrade and integration of the Chemist Warehouse Group onto existing IT architecture.

Based on current guidance assumptions, including the anticipated spending on Growth capital expenditures and changes in capital allocation, Chemtrade expects to end 2026 with a Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio of close to 2.5x and an implied Payout ratio of approximately 40%. ... In May 2025, Chemtrade shared Chemtrade Vision 2030 where one of the key aspects is to grow mid-cycle annual Adjusted EBITDA to between $550.0 million and $600.0 million by 2030. Chemtrade expects to achieve this target by continuing to focus on operational and commercial excellence while pursuing both organic and external growth opportunities such as the acquisitions of Polytec and the assets of Thatcher Group in 2025. This improvement in Adjusted EBITDA, alongside Chemtrade’s commitment to returning capital to unitholders while maintaining a prudent balance sheet, is expected to deliver compelling value on a per unit basis. Chemtrade remains focused on its long-term objective of delivering sustained earnings growth and generating value for investors. To accomplish this, Chemtrade has identified various organic growth initiatives. In 2026, Chemtrade plans to invest between $40.0 million and $60.0 million in growth capital expenditures with a focus on water treatment chemicals projects. In Ultrapure Acid, following quality improvement upgrades and plant start-ups at the Cairo, Ohio and Tulsa, Oklahoma facilities, Chemtrade is actively progressing through certification and commercialization with several customers and remains well-on track to achieve targets throughout 2026. ... Rezoning Application Related to the North Vancouver Chlor-Alkali Facility On July 20, 2026, the District of North Vancouver (“District”) adopted Chemtrade’s proposed by-law amendment completing the rezoning application process and allowing Chemtrade to continue production of liquid chlorine at its North Vancouver Facility (the “Facility”) until the earlier of the expiry of Chemtrade’s prospective lease with the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority (the “Port”) or 2046, subject to the terms outlined in a covenant entered into between Chemtrade and the District. Chemtrade continues to engage with the Port to finalize its land lease for a portion of the Facility situated on Port lands. In 2025, Chemtrade and the Port entered into a non-binding letter of intent (the “LOI”) outlining terms of a new 20-year agreement. On July 29, 2026, a petition for judicial review was filed in the Supreme Court of British Columbia seeking to set aside the District’s July 20, 2026 decision to adopt the bylaw amendment. Chemtrade disputes the legal and factual basis of the petition, denies the allegations made, intends to be added as a respondent and a party to the proceeding, and will vigorously oppose the relief sought. In order to comply with the LOI and the covenants agreed with the District, multi-year capital investments are required, including new chlorine liquification facilities on the portion of land owned by Chemtrade and improvements designed to further enhance the strong safety infrastructure of the Facility. headline: Why Sigma's Chemist Warehouse and Greenlight deal matters for the UK
summary_text: Australia’s drugstore wholesaler, Sigma Healthcare, has announced it will expand into the UK, with the acquisition of a 75% stake in a number of stores from Greenlight Healthcare Limited. Sigma Healthcare will license the Chemist Warehouse brand and lead the customer-facing retail model, including assortment strategy, store execution, inventory flow and marketing. In parallel, Greenlight will underpin the operating model, managing dispensary services and core back-end infrastructure. Chemist Warehouse’s entry into new markets has historically been accompanied by significant price disruption. Its operating model of high-volume purchasing, lean store formats, and strong supplier negotiations has allowed it to undercut competitors. ... ## Growth drivers and expansion In its latest half-yearly results (H1 2026), Chemist Warehouse’s Australia-based sales were up 17.2%, with like-for-like sales up 15%. Growth also accelerated in its international markets, where network sales rose by 24.5%. The retailer also revealed that demand for blockbuster weight-loss drugs is driving double-digit sales growth at its pharmacies. With cheaper pill versions of the weekly injection expected in the Australian market in 2026, growth is expected to accelerate. Sigma Healthcare is driving growth through four pillars: maintaining leadership in its domestic market, driving profitable growth internationally, product differentiation through owned and exclusive products and delivering efficiencies and synergy programmes. ... ## What’s next? The partnership will initially focus on identifying suitable existing Greenlight pharmacy locations and, where viable, converting or relocating these into Chemist Warehouse formats. Phase one will centre on the rebranding and development of up to five pilot stores, providing a test-and-learn platform ahead of a potential broader rollout in phase two, subject to performance. The first site is set to launch on Hoxton Street in northeast London, marking the initial step in establishing a physical presence in the market. ... For established players such as Boots, Superdrug, Savers and the grocers, Chemist Warehouse adds a competitor willing to run on lower margins to win scale. Its simple, functional store format is built for volume rather than experience. This is likely to increase pressure in categories where profits are already tight, especially OTC, vitamins, fragrance and everyday personal care. The model also brings new expectations for suppliers. Chemist Warehouse typically seeks exclusive packs, sharper net pricing and fast‑moving promotional mechanics, creating both opportunities for volume growth and challenges around margin. Its partnership with Greenlight further signals the potential for hybrid pharmacy‑retail formats to gain traction, reshaping competitive dynamics across community pharmacy and mass health & beauty.
