headline: Cartonnage de Vaucanson ajoute les cartes à son jeu - Les Echos
summary_text: Le fabricant d'emballages haut de gamme se lance dans la fabrication de cartes à jouer. Une diversification opérée en partenariat avec l'éditeur de jeux Sentosphère, pour qui il produit déjà des puzzles. Cartonnage de Vaucanson vise une production annuelle de 2 millions de cartes, avec une première année à 120.000 unités. (Photo Vaucanson) Par Françoise Sigot Publié le 5 oct. 2026 à 09:20 Mis à jour le 5 oct. 2026 à 15:59 Racheté il y a dix ans à la barre du tribunal de commerce par Véronique Debroise, présidente de l'éditeur de jeux Sentosphère, Cartonnage de Vaucanson poursuit sa diversification. Le fabricant d'emballages et de jeux installé à Romans-sur-Isère, dans la Drôme, se lance dans la production de cartes à jouer. La société a investi 400.000 euros dans une machine consacrée à ces produits lui permettant de viser le haut de gamme. « Nous disposons d'une capacité de production d'environ 2 millions de cartes par an », indique la dirigeante. Cette année, Cartonnage de Vaucanson pense en produire environ 120.000 avant de passer la vitesse supérieure l'an prochain. Sentosphère sera aux manettes de la commercialisation de ces nouveaux produits. Comme pour l'ensemble des jeux qu'elle édite, la société vise les boutiques et, dans un second temps, les musées, les sites historiques et les chaînes spécialisées.

headline: Les Rencontres du cartonnage entre incertitudes et nouveaux débouchés
summary_text: ## Entre évolution des habitudes de consommation, nouvelles propriétés du carton et contraintes réglementaires, les Rencontres du Cartonnage ont exploré plusieurs transformations susceptibles de modifier les marchés de la filière. Faustine Loison Publié le 29-09-2026 Comment continuer à avancer, investir et innover dans un environnement économique, géopolitique et réglementaire incertain ? La Fédération française du cartonnage et des articles de papeterie (Cap) a placé cette question au centre de ses 12e Rencontres du cartonnage, organisées le 23 septembre 2026, à Paris, devant une centaine de professionnels de la filière. Emily Mayer, directrice des études chez Circana société américaine d'études de marché et de technologies, a détaillé plusieurs changements de consommation susceptibles de créer de nouveaux besoins en emballages carton. La progression de la livraison et du snacking, la digitalisation des achats ainsi que les évolutions liées au vieillissement de la population et à la taille des ménages figurent parmi les tendances présentées. ... Philippe Martinez, directeur de la division Produits fonctionnels du Centre Technique du Papier, a présenté le potentiel de la chromatogénie. Cette technologie modifie le comportement de surface du carton face à l'eau sans plastification ni ajout de couches supplémentaires. Elle peut notamment être testée pour les emballages dont les propriétés se dégradent au contact de l'eau. Les exigences réglementaires françaises et européennes ont également occupé les échanges. Kareen Desbouïs, déléguée générale Carton Ondule de France du Comité français de l' emballage papier carton (Cofepac), s'est penchée sur la mise en conformité avec le règlement européen sur les emballages et déchets d'emballages, le PPWR. Bruno Garnier, président de l'agence française de conseil en stratégie RSE et en transition environnementale Moultipass Agency, a abordé les évolutions géopolitiques et réglementaires ainsi que les enjeux liés au réemploi et leurs conséquences pour le cartonnage. "Dans un environnement qui évolue rapidement, nous avons besoin de prendre du recul, de croiser les regards et de partager les réalités de nos entreprises", a déclaré Jean-Marc Lebhar, président de Cap. Les Rencontres ont ainsi confronté les inquiétudes économiques exprimées par la profession aux évolutions de la consommation, aux possibilités techniques et aux nouvelles contraintes réglementaires.

headline: Alma Pack Le Carton Deal: Morocco Packaging Consolidation Deepens | MMO
summary_text: The proposed acquisition would bring flexible films, cardboard packaging, plastic labels and aluminium tubes within a broader private-capital-backed manufacturing platform—if it secures regulatory approval and converts greater scale into industrial capability. ... A proposed acquisition involving two established Moroccan packaging companies points to a larger industrial shift: the consolidation of specialised manufacturers into platforms capable of investing more, producing across several formats and serving increasingly demanding customers. ... On 17 September 2026, Morocco’s Competition Council published notification of a proposed transaction under which Société Marocaine des Manufactures de Mohammedia SA would acquire exclusive control of Alma Pack SA and Le Carton SA. According to the non-confidential summary supplied by the notifying parties, Société Marocaine des Manufactures de Mohammedia is a Moroccan company controlled by private-equity group Mediterrania Capital Partners. It operates in Morocco through Advanced Flexible Materials, a producer of flexible packaging and, to a lesser extent, aluminium tubes. Alma Pack manufactures flexible packaging from plastic films and has what the notification describes as a very limited plastic-label activity. Le Carton specialises in rigid cardboard packaging. If approved and successfully integrated, the transaction would place flexible films, cardboard, plastic labels and aluminium tubes within a broader industrial platform. Its significance lies not only in adding two companies to an existing business, but in the possibility of building a supplier with greater product breadth, investment capacity and relevance across several Moroccan value chains. The transaction has neither been approved nor completed. The Competition Council states that publication of the notice does not establish that the regulatory file is complete and does not prejudge its eventual decision. Interested third parties have until 28 September 2026 to submit observations. No transaction value, seller, financing structure, ownership percentages, completion timetable or market-share figures were disclosed. (Morocco’s Competition Council) ... The Competition Council identifies four affected markets: flexible packaging, rigid packaging, plastic labels and aluminium tubes. Advanced Flexible Materials and Alma Pack both operate in flexible packaging. Le Carton would add rigid cardboard products, while the label and aluminium-tube activities would extend the platform into adjacent formats used by consumer and industrial manufacturers. Large customers frequently require more than one type of packaging. A food producer may need printed film, seals or labels and cardboard for secondary packaging and transport. Pharmaceutical, cosmetics and household-products manufacturers may require tubes or flexible materials alongside cartons carrying branding, instructions and regulatory information. A supplier operating across these categories could deepen customer relationships, coordinate packaging development and offer a broader commercial proposition. Greater volume could also strengthen raw-material procurement, spread technical and administrative costs across a larger base and support investment in printing, converting, quality control and product development. ... The first test is regulatory. The Competition Council must assess the transaction and its implications for the four markets identified in the filing. Until that process has been completed and authorisation obtained, this remains a proposed acquisition rather than a completed combination. If approval is granted, integration becomes the central industrial task. Flexible films, cardboard and aluminium products rely on different machinery, materials and technical disciplines. Procurement, sales, investment and governance can be coordinated, but each operation must continue to meet the standards expected by its customers. Customer retention will be essential. Manufacturers depend on packaging suppliers for continuity, exact specifications and predictable delivery. Integration must therefore improve the organisation without interrupting production or weakening established commercial relationships. Raw-material exposure will also remain significant. Plastic films, aluminium, paper and cardboard are affected by commodity prices, energy costs, exchange rates and freight conditions. A larger purchasing base can improve planning and negotiating power, but it cannot remove external volatility. Environmental performance will require sustained investment. Customers and regulators increasingly expect packaging producers to reduce material use, improve recyclability and document environmental characteristics. Meeting those expectations demands expertise in materials, design and manufacturing—not simply corporate scale. Quality and certification will be equally important, particularly when serving food, pharmaceutical, cosmetics and export customers. The platform’s credibility will depend on maintaining consistent standards across every format and production line.

headline: Applebee’s® and IHOP® Continue Nationwide Growth With New Dual-Branded Restaurant in San Antonio, TX | Dine Brands
summary_text: Applebee’s® and IHOP® Continue Nationwide Growth With New Dual-Branded Restaurant in San Antonio, TX September 15, 2026 New location marks a milestone for Dine Brands as the company approaches 50 dual-branded restaurants nationwide, offering guests variety, convenience, and value under one roof. PASADENA, Calif. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sep. 15, 2026-- Dine Brands Global, Inc. (NYSE: DIN), the parent company of Applebee's Neighborhood Grill + Bar ® and IHOP ®, today celebrates the rapid expansion of its dual-branded restaurant concept with the opening of a new location in San Antonio, TX. Less than two years after launching the first standalone U.S . dual-branded restaurant in nearby Seguin, Texas , the two iconic brands are approaching 50 dual-branded locations nationwide, reflecting growing guest demand for greater variety, convenience, and value under one roof. ... The dual-branded restaurant offers guests the best of both brands under one roof, allowing them to mix and match signature Applebee's and IHOP items from a single menu any time of day, from morning to late night. Within the space, guests enjoy the unique identity and atmosphere of both brands, connected by shared spaces that create a seamless experience and complemented by specialty cocktails* and exclusive menu innovations available only at dual-branded locations, including the Loaded Buffalo Chicken Omelette and Ultimate Breakfast Burger. ... “What began as a bold idea has evolved into a meaningful complement to our development and growth strategies,” said John Peyton , CEO of Dine Brands Global . “In under two years, we’ve gone from one dual-branded U.S . location to nearly 50 nationwide, and the momentum continues. By bringing Applebee’s and IHOP together under one roof, we’re creating a more flexible operating model, giving guests more reasons to visit, and offering franchisees an additional pathway to strengthen their businesses over time.” ... As Dine Brands advances its development and growth strategies, the dual-branded model is emerging as a valuable addition to its portfolio. The company remains on track to open approximately 80 domestic dual-branded restaurants by the end of 2026. ... The new Applebee’s | IHOP restaurant – located at 2607 W. Loop 1604 S. San Antonio, TX , 78245 – is now open daily from 6 a.m. to 1 a.m.

headline: Inés Rosales renueva los formatos de la Torta de Aceite orientados a tiendas de especialidad y canal Horeca - AION SUR
summary_text: Inés Rosales continúa desarrollando su propuesta de producto con el lanzamiento de nuevos diseños para su gama de estuches de cartón, un formato ya presente en el mercado que la compañía actualiza ahora con una renovada propuesta visual y la incorporación de nuevas variedades. La actualización responde a una estrategia de innovación orientada a adaptarse a un consumidor cada vez más complejo y exigente, con hábitos cambiantes tanto en sus formas y momentos de consumo como en sus decisiones de compra. En este contexto, Inés Rosales mantiene una actividad continua de desarrollo de formatos y variedades, adaptando su propuesta a las particularidades y oportunidades de cada mercado. Entre las novedades destaca la incorporación de la Torta de Aceite con Romero y Tomillo a este formato, ampliando una gama que permite acercar diferentes variedades de la marca a nuevas ocasiones de consumo y a espacios donde la presentación del producto adquiere especial relevancia. Los nuevos diseños mantienen la esencia de un formato concebido para presentar las Tortas de Aceite en un contexto más vinculado al regalo, los espacios gourmet y la experiencia de producto, al tiempo que buscan reforzar la identidad de la marca y su conexión con el origen andaluz. El estuche de cartón incorpora, además, cartón 100 % reciclado, en línea con la evolución de los materiales y formatos que la compañía utiliza. ... El desarrollo de formatos y variedades forma parte de una estrategia más amplia de crecimiento de Inés Rosales, basada en aprovechar los atributos universales de sus productos para ampliar su presencia en nuevos mercados y canales. El Aceite de Oliva Virgen Extra como ingrediente principal, el uso de ingredientes naturales de primera calidad, la versatilidad del producto y la tradición asociada a su presentación y forma de consumo constituyen algunos de los principales valores sobre los que la compañía continúa construyendo su propuesta. Estos atributos permiten a Inés Rosales identificar oportunidades más allá de sus mercados tradicionales y adaptar su oferta a diferentes perfiles de consumidor y ocasiones de consumo. Dentro de esta estrategia, la compañía trabaja en extender su presencia en Europa y Estados Unidos, ampliar su gama de productos en Estados Unidos y desarrollar nuevos canales, con especial atención a ámbitos como HORECA, tiendas de especialidad y Travel Retail.

headline: Jean-René Cazeneuve salue l’investissement industriel des Cartonnages d’Auch – La Gazette Gersoise
summary_text: # Jean-René Cazeneuve salue l’investissement industriel des Cartonnages d’Auch Par Le correspondant 14 septembre 2026 14 septembre 2026 À l’occasion de la livraison d’une nouvelle presse offset 7 couleurs, Jean-René Cazeneuve a visité les Cartonnages d’Auch, mettant en lumière le dynamisme et le savoir-faire industriel de cette entreprise familiale emblématique du Gers. Jean-René Cazeneuve s’est rendu aux Cartonnages d’Auch à l’occasion de la livraison d’une nouvelle presse offset 7 couleurs, signée Koenig & Bauer. Cet investissement industriel vient renforcer les capacités de production de l’entreprise et illustre, selon le député, le dynamisme du tissu économique gersois. Fondés en 1955, les Cartonnages d’Auch constituent aujourd’hui un acteur majeur de l’industrie locale. Cette entreprise familiale affiche un chiffre d’affaires de 10 millions d’euros, produit chaque année près de 110 millions de boîtes et emploie 80 salariés. Pour Jean-René Cazeneuve, les Cartonnages d’Auch représentent « un modèle de réussite économique et d’esprit d’entreprendre », particulièrement précieux pour le territoire. L’entreprise incarne également pleinement le savoir-faire industriel et le Made in Gers. La livraison de cette nouvelle presse offset témoigne de la volonté des dirigeants de poursuivre leur développement et d’investir dans leur outil de production. Un choix stratégique qui intervient toutefois dans un contexte économique marqué par les crises successives et une certaine incertitude pour les entreprises. Au cours de sa visite, Jean-René Cazeneuve a ainsi insisté sur l’importance de donner aux entrepreneurs « visibilité et stabilité » afin de leur permettre de poursuivre leurs investissements, de se développer et de créer de l’emploi sur les territoires. ... Avec ce nouvel investissement, les Cartonnages d’Auch confirment leur ancrage industriel dans le Gers et leur ambition de continuer à écrire leur histoire, près de 70 ans après leur création.

headline: Guerre commerciale | Le cartonnier RYAM reporte l’arrêt de son usine de Témiscaming
summary_text: L’entreprise américaine Rayonier Advanced Materials (RYAM) reporte de trois semaines l’arrêt temporaire de son usine située à Témiscaming, en Abitibi-Témiscamingue. Publié à 12 h 03 Martin Vallières La Presse Cette usine de produits de carton, qui implique 400 travailleurs dans la région, devait interrompre sa production à compter de mardi prochain 15 septembre. Selon la direction de RYAM, cet arrêt de production pour une durée indéterminée « découle directement des [droits de douane] imposés depuis le 22 août (par l’administration Trump aux États-Unis) qui compromettent la viabilité des activités de l’usine. ». Mais vendredi matin, à quelques jours de l’arrêt prévu, et après quelques reportages d’actualité économique et électorale à ce sujet, la direction de RYAM a annoncé que « grâce à de nouvelles commandes de carton provenant de clients canadiens, nous sommes en mesure de maintenir la production et de reporter au trois octobre l’arrêt initialement prévu le 15 septembre. » Toutefois, même si elle « remercie la communauté pour le soutien manifesté depuis l’annonce de l’arrêt économique temporaire de son usine de Témiscaming », la direction de RYAM avertit que ce report de trois semaines « ne constitue qu’un répit temporaire, et l’incertitude demeurera tant qu’une solution durable n’aura pas été trouvée. » Et pour parvenir à cette « solution durable », sans en préciser la teneur, la direction de l’entreprise américaine indique qu’elle « compte sur le soutien des gouvernements du Québec et du Canada pour mettre en place des solutions durables permettant de rétablir les conditions nécessaires à la viabilité économique du site. »

headline: Mayr-Melnhof expands packaging production in Romania - packaging journal
summary_text: Mayr-Melnhof (MM) is advancing the expansion of its packaging production in Romania. According to the company, the investment in the local plant is proceeding on schedule. Commercial production is set to start in October 2026. The project is part of MM's growth investments and belongs to the Food & Premium Packaging division. Looking ahead to the second half of the year, the Group confirms that the expansion investments in Romania and the USA are proceeding according to plan. They are scheduled to contribute to the Group's earnings from 2027 onwards. MM does not provide any further details regarding the investment volume or the additional production capacities in Romania in the half-yearly figures not. ... ## Weak demand for folding cartons The expansion is taking place in a still difficult market environment. MM describes demand for folding cartons in the first half of 2026 as sluggish. At the same time, the intensity of competition in most end markets remained unchanged and high. Towards the end of the second quarter, the order situation improved slightly in selected markets. In the Food & Premium Packaging division, revenue fell on a comparable basis, excluding the divested Tann group, by 5.6 percent to 684 million euros. The volume produced decreased by 7.1 percent to 1.019 billion square metres. By contrast, adjusted EBITDA rose slightly by 0.9 percent to 97.9 million euros. The corresponding margin increased from 13.4 to 14.3 percent. MM attributes this development, amongst other things, to process improvements, fixed cost reductions and lower cartonboard costs.

headline: RDM sells cartonboard business in Arnsberg to MM Board & Paper - packaging journal
summary_text: RDM Group is selling its business in Arnsberg, North Rhine-Westphalia, to MM Board & Paper. The two companies have signed a corresponding agreement regarding an asset transaction. The Arnsberg plant is a long-standing production site for recycled cartonboard and supplies customers throughout Europe. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. With the sale, the Italian cartonboard manufacturer Reno De Medici (RDM) is continuing its strategic realignment. According to the company, the transaction is intended to help optimise the group's business plan and focus its activities more strongly on product categories and markets that, from RDM's perspective, offer good prospects for sustainable growth, innovation and value creation. RDM has not disclosed the financial terms of the agreement. According to the company, the conditions and expected impact of the transaction, including on the group's liquidity and business performance, have already been factored into the business plan forecasts. They also align with the assumptions published by RDM on 15 July 2026. ... In MM Board & Paper, RDM sees an industrial owner for the further development of the site. „We are convinced that MM Board & Paper is the right industrial player to support the future development of the Arnsberg business and its employees,“ said Bianchi. Completion of the transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions, including the necessary regulatory approvals. According to current planning, closing is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.

headline: EQS-News: Mayr-Melnhof Karton AG: MM Board & Paper signs agreement to acquire the operations of R.D.M. Arnsberg | 17.08.26 | finanzen.at
summary_text: MM Board & Paper has signed an agreement with the R.D.M. Group to acquire the operating business of the R.D.M. Arnsberg recycled fibre-based cartonboard mill in Germany through an asset deal. The Arnsberg mill has an annual production capacity of about 230,000 tonnes of recycled fibre-based cartonboard and is particularly specialised in the production of liner products. The transaction represents an investment in MM's core business and complements its existing production network. By integrating the Arnsberg mill into its established industrial platform in Germany, comprising several cartonboard mills and packaging plants, MM expects to realise significant synergies that should facilitate the turnaround of the mill. In addition, the acquisition is expected to increase production flexibility, improve security of supply, and further broaden the product and service offering for customers. All employees at the Arnsberg mill will be transferred to MM. The purchase price has not been disclosed. The acquisition remains subject to the receipt of the required antitrust approvals. From today's perspective, closing of the transaction is expected in the 4 th quarter of 2026.

headline: MM signe une entente pour acquérir R.D.M. Arnsberg - Le Maître Papetier
summary_text: MM a signé une entente en vue d’acquérir les activités de l’usine R.D.M. Arnsberg, en Allemagne. ## MM Board & Paper a signé une entente avec R.D.M. Group en vue d’acquérir, dans le cadre d’une transaction d’actifs, les activités de l’usine de carton à base de fibres recyclées de R.D.M. Arnsberg, en Allemagne. L’usine possède une capacité de production annuelle d’environ 230 000 tonnes de carton à base de fibres recyclées et se spécialise notamment dans la fabrication de liners. Le projet d’acquisition devrait renforcer les activités principales de MM dans le secteur du carton et compléter son réseau de production existant. MM prévoit intégrer l’usine d’Arnsberg à sa plateforme industrielle allemande, qui comprend plusieurs usines de carton et sites d’emballage. L’entreprise s’attend à ce que cette intégration génère d’importantes synergies opérationnelles et contribue au redressement de l’usine. Selon MM, l’opération devrait également accroître la flexibilité de la production, renforcer la sécurité d’approvisionnement et élargir son offre de produits et de services. Tous les employés de l’usine d’Arnsberg seraient transférés à MM dans le cadre de la transaction. Le prix d’achat n’a pas été divulgué. Le projet d’acquisition demeure soumis aux autorisations requises des autorités de la concurrence. Selon l’échéancier actuel, MM prévoit conclure la transaction au quatrième trimestre de 2026.

headline: How Dine’s dual-brands can stave off closures | Restaurant Dive
summary_text: Dine Brands has a novel way to keep struggling restaurants open: add another concept to a single-branded restaurant. The chain has been deploying dual-branded Applebee’s and IHOP restaurants since last year, and has now reached 45 units in the U.S., including seven company-owned locations, with 12 more under construction. Some restaurants close because they don’t generate enough revenue, but adding another brand can make it a more viable location, CEO John Peyton said. During the second quarter, Applebee’s and IHOP had 13 new restaurant openings and 30 restaurant closures. This activity also included nine net dual-brand openings, according to an earnings release. Peyton said closures aren’t related to industrywide trends. “We've got restaurants that are 20, 30, even 40 years old. Landlords change, markets change, leases change, and so it's all part of the normal course of business,” Peyton said. “For a system our size, one can expect up to 2% a year of restaurant closures, and that's where we are and where we've been.” ... Dine Brands reported mixed sales performance during the second quarter, with Applebee’s year-over-year comparable sales down by 1.8% while IHOP’s U.S. same-store sales increased 1.5%, according to an earnings release. ... ### Dual brands boost sales, revenue Dine Brands plans to have 80 co-branded IHOP/Applebee’s by the end of this year and is already seeing a significant sales uptick from the conversions. “We’re very pleased that this 2x revenue is settling in and repeatable now that we’ve got 45 restaurants,” Peyton said. The cost to convert a single restaurant into a dual-branded unit is about $1 million, and guest feedback has been positive, he added. About two out of three guests order from both elements of the menu. In the morning, there might be omelets and ribs at the table, while in the evening there could be skillets and pancakes, Peyton said. “Our focus going forward is now fine-tuning the operational model, looking at making the kitchen more efficient, making the labor more efficient and doing the next generation of the menu,” Peyton said. ... Another way Dine Brands is boosting sales and revenue is through single-brand remodels. It is currently in the midst of remodeling Applebee’s restaurants through its Lookin’ Good program. The program refreshes various exterior elements, including the tower, the lighting, iconography and landscaping, Peyton said. Internally, restaurants get new wall coverings, art and lights, as well as new chairs, tables, upholstery and a new floor and a refreshed bar. “The guests love it,” Peyton said. “We’re getting great feedback from guests and we’re seeing an increase on average of about 5% in sales after a restaurant renovates. We’re also seeing a great response from team members who work in the restaurants who feel great about working in a new, fresh environment that’s been invested [in] and nurtured.”

headline: Dine Brands (DIN) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript | The Motley Fool
summary_text: ## TAKEAWAYS - Total Revenue -- $240.9 million, representing a 4.4% increase year over year driven primarily by the acquisition of restaurants from franchisees. - Adjusted EBITDA -- $54.2 million, a decrease from $56.2 million in the prior year period. - Dual-Brand Revenue -- 2.0 times the sales levels of single-branded units on average, with conversion costs stabilizing around $1 million. - Applebee's Remodels -- 66 completed year-to-date under the Lookin' Good program, delivering an average mid-single-digit sales lift. - Company-Owned Portfolio -- 136 restaurants owned at quarter-end, representing approximately 4% of the total system. - Applebee's Commodity Costs -- 8.2% increase year over year, primarily driven by higher beef prices and the expiration of favorable contracts. - headline: Consiliul Concurenţei supune dezbaterii angajamentele propuse de Hartmann pentru a putea prelua Dentas România - 05.08.2026 | BURSA.RO
summary_text: Consiliul Concurenţei supune dezbaterii publice angajamentele propuse de Hartmann Packaging A/S pentru a înlătura îngrijorările concurenţiale identificate în contextul preluării Dentas Romania SRL, potrivit unui comunicat de presă remis redacţiei. În urma analizei, autoritatea de concurenţă a constatat că tranzacţia poate conduce la consolidarea poziţiei Dentas Romania pe piaţa suporturilor alveolare din fibră turnată pentru ouă din România. Pentru a înlătura aceste îngrijorări, Hartmann se angajează: 1. să convertească două linii de producţie, deţinute anterior de Dentas Romania, astfel încât acestea să nu mai fabrice cofraje standard pentru ouă, ci caserole cu capac, şi să modernizeze alte două linii de producţie pentru caserole cu capac, deţinute anterior de Dentas Romania. Ulterior, întreaga producţie rezultată din cele patru linii ar urma să deservească exclusiv pieţele de export, pentru o perioadă de doi ani; 2. să menţină, timp de doi ani, preţurile medii ponderate anuale la nivelul preţurilor medii ponderate de referinţă aplicate în anul 2025, actualizate cel mult cu variaţia cumulată a Indicelui Preţurilor de Consum (IPC). În acest fel, Hartmann urmăreşte să răspundă îngrijorării concurenţiale referitoare la posibila creştere a preţurilor pentru suporturile alveolare din fibră turnată pentru ouă, după autorizare tranzacţiei; 3. să nu impună clienţilor contracte cu o durată mai mare de 12 luni, restricţii privind cantităţile sau penalităţi şi să faciliteze accesul concurenţilor pe piaţă prin transmiterea unor notificări adresate clienţilor, în care să îi informeze că au libertatea de a contacta, de a negocia şi de a colabora cu orice furnizor de pe piaţa românească a ambalajelor din fibră turnată pentru ouă; 4. să înceteze importurile de la Dentas Kagit Sanayi A.S. din Turcia prin intermediul Dentas Romania şi să nu mai utilizeze mărcile Dentas.

headline: L’UE autorise l’acquisition de Thimm par Saica - Le Maître Papetier
summary_text: ## La Commission européenne a autorisé l’acquisition par le groupe Saica des activités de Thimm en Allemagne, en Pologne, en République tchèque et en Roumanie, permettant au fabricant espagnol d’emballages d’amorcer l’intégration des installations acquises. Approuvée le 24 juillet, la transaction comprend neuf usines de fabrication d’emballages en carton ondulé ainsi qu’une installation de préimpression, renforçant considérablement la présence industrielle de Saica en Europe centrale et orientale. ... ### L’acquisition accroît les capacités de production Cette acquisition ajoute environ 1,2 milliard de mètres carrés de capacité annuelle de production de carton ondulé et près de 2 500 employés aux activités du groupe Saica. Les actifs acquis comprennent des usines situées à Alzey, Wolnzach, Eberswalde, Castrop-Rauxel et Northeim en Allemagne, à Tychy et Skarbimierz en Pologne, à Všetaty en République tchèque et à Sibiu en Roumanie, ainsi qu’un site de préimpression à Ilsenburg, en Allemagne. À la suite du feu vert des autorités européennes de la concurrence, Saica a indiqué avoir lancé le processus d’intégration des nouvelles installations. ... ### Une implantation renforcée en Europe Selon l’entreprise, cette acquisition constitue une étape importante de sa stratégie de croissance à long terme. Elle permettra à Saica de se rapprocher de ses clients en Europe centrale et orientale tout en renforçant ses capacités locales de production et d’approvisionnement. La présidente et chef de la direction, Susana Alejandro, a indiqué que l’intégration des équipes de Thimm viendra enrichir l’expertise du groupe et soutenir son développement dans la région. Cette acquisition permettra à Saica de renforcer sa présence sur les marchés locaux, de se rapprocher de ses clients et d’élargir son offre de solutions d’emballage.

summary_text: ### ‘Made in Europe’: Sovereignty for the home network of today and tomorrow – for all connections FRITZ! will be showcasing high-end solutions for fibre-optic, cable and 5G networks at Network X in Vienna from 13 to 15 October. At the FRITZ! Stand (Hall B, stand J4) trade visitors can discover a wide spectrum of new products such as the FRITZ!Box DSL/Fiber 7-90, the FRITZ!Box 5630 XGS, the FRITZ!Box 6835 5G and the FRITZ!Repeater 6700 Pro, which are ready today for the home network of tomorrow. headline: Foss & Company closes US$58 million tax equity deal - Energy-Storage.News
summary_text: # Foss & Company closes US$58 million tax equity deal for GridStor’s Texas BESS project By April Bonner October 13, 2026 The transaction for the utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS), which generates Section 48 Investment Tax Credits (ITCs), marks the second deal between Foss & Company and US-based developer-operator GridStor. Image: GridStor US tax equity syndicator Foss & Company has closed a US$58 million partnership flip transaction to finance an energy storage project in Hidalgo County, Texas, developed by GridStor. The transaction for the utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS), which generates Section 48 Investment Tax Credits (ITCs), marks the second deal between Foss & Company and US-based developer-operator GridStor. The BESS project remains on schedule to be placed in service this month (October).The deal adds another utility-scale BESS to Foss & Company’s growing renewable energy tax equity portfolio. The Hidalgo County transaction comes amid accelerating activity for both Foss & Company and GridStor across the US. For Foss & Company, the deal reinforces its continued conviction in utility-scale BESS, a sector the firm moved into quickly following the passage of the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). Speaking to Energy-Storage.news Premium in July, Bryen Alperin, managing director, and Sophie Brkovic, vice president of energy & infrastructure project finance at Foss & Company, explained that the firm has historically entered emerging technologies as they mature, with standalone BESS marking one of its earliest post-IRA moves. That same month, Foss & Company closed its first microgrid transaction—a US$30 million Section 48 tax equity investment in a solar-plus-storage microgrid developed by energy-as-a-service provider AlphaStruxure in Montgomery County, Maryland. Alperin noted at the time that the firm typically transacts in the US$20 million-and-above tax credit range, with BESS offering portfolio diversification benefits alongside solar, given its relative resilience to weather-related risks such as hail and windstorms. “We’re looking now at expanding that beyond what was primarily solar into other technologies,” Alperin said. “Obviously, there’s a lot of energy storage that’s going to get built in this country.” ... For GridStor, the Hidalgo County financing follows a separate, larger deal in Arizona. On 21 September, the company closed a US$220 million tax equity bridge, construction, and term debt financing agreement to complete its 100MW/400MWh White Tank BESS project. GridStor acquired White Tank from Strata Clean Energy in September 2025, with the project originally awarded through Arizona Public Service’s (APS) 2023 all-source request for proposals. White Tank will operate under a 20-year tolling agreement with APS and is expected to enter service in the first half of 2027. The White Tank deal also followed GridStor’s acquisition of the 199MW/796MWh Birdseye BESS project in Adams County, Colorado, from developer Accelergen in May—the company’s fifth acquisition in 18 months.

headline: Foss & Company Closes $58 Million Tax Equity Investment in Utility-Scale Battery Storage Project with GridStor

headline: Foss Group of Companies Launches, Uniting Businesses Built Over Six Decades
summary_text: Foss Group of Companies Launches, Uniting Businesses Built Over Six Decades Oct 06, 2026, 07:11 ET Third-generation Canadian family business honours its legacy while building a platform for what's next in mobility TORONTO, Oct. 6, 2026 /CNW/ -- After more than six decades of growing alongside Canada's automotive industry, a leading name announced today the launch of Foss Group of Companies, bringing its expanding portfolio of automotive retail, fleet management, mobility, and real estate businesses together under one organization. Founded in 1962 as a single-point General Motors dealership in North Toronto, the family-owned company now operates three dealerships in the Greater Toronto Area, manages 50,000 vehicles nationally, and holds a growing portfolio of investments in mobility, technology, and real estate. Foss Group of Companies comprises four divisions: - Roy Foss -- three GTA dealerships, with a multi-year run as Canada's #1 volume Cadillac store. Three-time Automotive News Best Dealership to Work For. - Foss National Leasing -- Canada's largest independently owned fleet management company. With offices in Toronto, Laval, Calgary, and Vancouver, Foss National Leasing manages over 50,000 vehicles nationwide through leasing, fleet services, mobility solutions, technology and data. - Foss Ventures -- investing at the frontier of automotive, fleet and mobility technology. - Foss Real Estate -- strategic real estate holdings, property management and development. Each division stands on its own, but together they cover every stage of the vehicle lifecycle --access, funding, ownership, and resale. Foss National Leasing brings national scale with a large fleet portfolio, leading technology and solutions for Canadian companies and a Canada-wide partner network. Roy Foss brings more than six decades of automotive retail experience and longstanding automaker relationships in Ontario. Foss Ventures extends that expertise into emerging mobility and technology, while Foss Real Estate supports the physical footprint behind the businesses. Together, they give Foss a platform to identify, invest in and build opportunities across the changing mobility landscape. ... The launch comes at a pivotal time for Canada's automotive sector. Tariffs and trade uncertainty, shifting global supply chains, the transition to electric vehicles, and emerging mobility models are reshaping how Canadians buy, use, and manage vehicles. "We didn't arrive here overnight, and we're not finished," Ricci said. "Foss Group of Companies names what we've built and the platform for what comes next -- more rooftops, a larger national fleet, and investment in emerging businesses and technology that moves people and goods." ... In 2027, the company will celebrate 65 years in business.

headline: Smarter, faster, more secure: FRITZ! releases major update to FRITZ!OS 8.50 | FRITZ! Company
summary_text: # Smarter, faster, more secure: FRITZ! releases major update to FRITZ!OS 8.50 ## Pressrelease 29/09/2026 ### Smarter, faster, more secure: FRITZ! releases major update to FRITZ!OS 8.50 FRITZ!OS 8.50 makes the home network even more robust: new features such as DNS filter mechanism, intelligent prioritization for data streams, and enhanced smart home options ensure maximum security and stability. > Press photo FRITZ!OS 8.50 is here! The rollout starts with the FRITZ!Box 7690 and will follow for all current FRITZ!Box and FRITZ!Repeater models in the coming weeks. This major update offers a wide range of expanded features ranging from improved diagnostic tools to additional smart home automations. A key focus is on improving the stability and security of the home network. The new DNS filter mechanisms, optimized failover protection options and intelligent prioritization of data streams make the FRITZ!Box 7690 even more robust and secure across all applications – including working from home, gaming, and the smart home. Users will have the update to FRITZ!OS 8.50 installed automatically if the Automatic Update feature is activated, or can request it directly by clicking on 'Start Update' in the 'fritz.box' user interface. Find out more about all the new features and improvements at fritz.com/fritzos. ... With FRITZ!OS 8.50, the FRITZ!Box 7690 can block access from home network devices like smartphones or computers to certain internet addresses (known as ‘domains’). The FRITZ!Box supports common standards to read in and process lists of undesirable domain names. Users can also resort to publicly available DNS filter lists to filter out advertising, trackers, and malware – and also phishing pages, botnets, or other unwanted content. This function will gradually be made available to additional select models as part of the rollout. When a device in the home network calls up a blocked address, the FRITZ!Box blocks the query automatically. ... No more delays during important video conferences while working from home or during gaming sessions: In addition to the existing device prioritization, FRITZ!OS 8.50 can now also automatically prioritize applications that need to run in real time. The FRITZ!Box automatically detects applications such as gaming or video conferencing and prioritizes them within the home network completely automatically so that the connection remains stable. If such a connection is currently in progress, the active prioritization is displayed directly in the user interface for the respective network device and can be retraced up to 24 hours later. Automatic prioritization will be introduced for select models in the next weeks. ... With FRITZ! Failsafe – the FRITZ!Box's failover protection – FRITZ! users already stay online at all times. Starting with FRITZ!OS 8.50, it is now possible to use FRITZ! Failsafe directly on the FRITZ!Box models for 4G and 5G. For the first time, these mobile broadband devices can also connect to the internet over a LAN port, for instance, via an upstream ONT on a fiber optic connection. FRITZ! Failsafe then ensures that the mobile broadband connection temporarily takes over internet provision in the home network should a landline connection fail. ... Starting with FRITZ!OS 8.50, the FRITZ!Smart Energy 200, 210 smart plugs, as well as the upcoming new indoor model FRITZ!Smart Energy 201, can be automatically turned off for safety purposes if a specified current limit is exceeded for a defined amount of time. Preconfigured automations such as ‘Leaving the House’, ‘Coming Home’ or ‘Holidays’ can be created with just a few clicks and triggered with zones (geofences) that were previously configured in the FRITZ!App Smart Home. With the next update, routines can combine multiple triggers, including zones (geofences) defined on the smartphone. This way you can configure, for instance, that a routine only becomes active when all residents have left the house. What's more, the FRITZ!Box 5690 Pro can now be used as a Matter bridge. As a consequence, all FRITZ! Smart Home devices and compatible smart home devices from other manufacturers that are registered with the FRITZ!Box 5690 Pro can be integrated into an existing matter network from Apple Home, Google Home or Amazon Alexa. Users can even benefit from voice controls.

headline: FOSS Group Launches New-Generation Aerogel-Based Fire Suppression Technology to Address Battery and Industrial Fires - Prime News Post
summary_text: The INDONESIAN, (JAKARTA)— FOSS Group, through its subsidiary PT Genetic FOSS Indonesia Teknologi, has officially introduced FOSS Aerogel Fire Protection, a line of fire suppression technology built on aerogel materials, designed to meet evolving fire safety and protection needs across Indonesia. The technology is engineered to support effective fire suppression, block heat transfer, reduce oxygen exposure, and significantly lower the risk of re-ignition. ... FOSS Aerogel Fire Protection has been developed as a comprehensive solution family spanning multiple device formats: a compact 500 ml extinguisher, a throw-type extinguisher bottle of approximately 600 ml, portable units of 2–9 litres, wall-mounted 4–8 litre models, a 15‑litre backpack extinguisher, automatic suppression systems, mini fire trucks, and fire motorcycles — enabling effective response across a wide range of field conditions and operational requirements. Its application spans critical sectors: lithium batteries and electric vehicles, energy storage facilities, industry and manufacturing, mining and energy, petrochemicals, transportation, public infrastructure, and solutions for forest fire suppression operations. ... Concurrent with the launch, FOSS Group through PT Genetic FOSS Indonesia Teknologi is also opening collaboration opportunities with the Central and Regional Governments, relevant ministries and disaster management agencies — including BNPB and BPBD — fire services, state‑owned enterprises, industrial parks, energy and mining companies, the transport, automotive and electric vehicle sectors, as well as distributors and technology partners nationwide. Areas of collaboration may include product demonstrations, technical testing and verification, pilot projects, application development tailored to field requirements, safety system integration, and the expansion of marketing and distribution networks. The company’s development roadmap explicitly covers demonstration, testing, pilot initiatives, and partnership expansion. In the long term, FOSS Group also intends to explore assembly, refilling, technology transfer, and eventual local production within Indonesia — should conditions prove feasible. The goal is for this technology to move beyond product distribution and become an integral part of the nation’s domestic safety technology capacity.

headline: Smart Home at IFA: Matter cameras, AI guardians, and nimble door locks | heise online
summary_text: Just in time for the approaching autumn, following Tado and Philips Hue, other manufacturers presented new technology for the connected home at IFA 2026. In addition to more affordable heating hardware, Matter security cameras are in the starting blocks, AI tricks are intended to improve video surveillance, and additional talents of smart locks are to make unlocking the door more convenient. ... ### Fritz heats more affordably With the Fritz!Smart Thermo 303 manufacturer Fritz, formerly AVM, is adding a cheaper, stripped-down model to its thermostat selection. For 59 euros, available from the end of October or the beginning of November, there will be neither a locking ring nor buttons to change the temperature precisely. Instead, a multifunction button is used to cycle through five temperature values by pressing it repeatedly. Fritz presets them ex-factory, but they can be changed via app. A screen is also missing. The thermostat is therefore primarily suitable for radiators that are not normally controlled directly at the valve but via app or time schedule. ## FritzSmart Thermo 303 auf der IFA (3 Bilder) Der FritzSmart Thermo 303 wird der preisgünstigste Heizkörperregler des Herstellers (59 Euro). (Bild: Berti Kolbow-Lehradt In terms of software, the Thermo 303 essentially offers what the more expensive models 302 and 301 can do. It communicates with the Fritzbox via Digital Enhanced Cordless Telecommunications Ultra Low Energy (DECT-ULE). Time schedules, open window detection with and without a contact sensor, boost function, and interaction with the external temperature sensor FritzSmart Control 440 are retained. Three batteries power the device. Fritz does not specify the runtime. For 49 euros, the smart DECT plug-in adapter FritzSmart Energy 201 will be available in stores in October. Compared to its 200 predecessor, it has shrunk significantly and now corresponds more to the size of current smart plug-in adapters. The new arrival inherits the essential software features: it switches on according to a schedule and measures the energy consumption of connected devices up to a load of 3680 watts. Via the Matter standard, both devices officially connect to the major smart home platforms. The Fritzbox 5690 Pro has recently become another possible intermediary in the Fritz cosmos. It functions as the manufacturer’s first Wi-Fi router as a Matter bridge – albeit only with beta firmware so far. However, the manufacturer assured at the IFA stand to heise online that it is well advanced and practically final and therefore could well be used in everyday life.

headline: Von Anker bis Fritz: Die Smart-Home-Highlights der IFA 2026 | heise online
summary_text: Pünktlich zum nahenden Herbst zeigten nach Tado und Philips Hue weitere Hersteller im Zuge der IFA 2026 neue Technik fürs vernetzte Zuhause. Zum Preis von 59 Euro gibt es ab Ende Oktober oder Anfang November weder Stellring noch Tasten, um die Temperatur gradgenau zu ändern. Stattdessen wählt man mit einer Multifunktionstaste durch wiederholtes Drücken einen von fünf Temperaturwerten. Fritz gibt sie ab Werk vor, ändern lassen sie sich per App. Auch ein Bildschirm fehlt. Der Thermostat eignet sich somit vor allem für Heizkörper, die man gewöhnlich nicht direkt am Ventil temperiert, sondern per App oder Zeitplan steuert. ## FritzSmart Thermo 303 auf der IFA (3 Bilder) Der FritzSmart Thermo 303 wird der preisgünstigste Heizkörperregler des Herstellers (59 Euro). (Bild: Berti Kolbow-Lehradt ) Softwareseitig beherrscht der Thermo 303 im Wesentlichen, was auch die teureren Modelle 302 und 301 können. Per Digital Enhanced Cordless Telecommunications Ultra Low Energy (DECT-ULE) kommuniziert es mit der Fritzbox. Zeitpläne, Fenster-auf-Erkennung mit und ohne Kontaktsensor, Boost-Funktion und das Zusammenspiel mit dem externen Temperatursensor FritzSmart Control 440 bleiben erhalten. Drei Batterien versorgen das Gerät mit Energie. Die Laufzeit nennt Fritz nicht. Für 49 Euro startet der smarte DECT-Zwischenstecker FritzSmart Energy 201 im Oktober in den Handel. Er ist gegenüber dem 200er-Vorgänger deutlich geschrumpft und entspricht nun eher der Kragenweite aktueller smarter Zwischenstecker. Die wesentlichen Softwaretalente übernimmt der Neuzugang: Er schaltet etwa nach Zeitplan und misst den Energieverbrauch angeschlossener Geräte bis zu einer Last von 3680 Watt. Über den Matter-Standard finden beide Geräte offiziell Anschluss an die großen Smart-Home-Plattformen. Als weitere mögliche Vermittlungsstelle im Fritz-Kosmos eignet sich seit Kurzem die Fritzbox 5690 Pro. Sie fungiert als erster WLAN-Router des Herstellers als Matter-Bridge – bisher allerdings nur mit einer Beta-Firmware. Die sei aber weit gediehen und faktisch final, könne also durchaus schon im Alltag eingesetzt werden, beteuerte der Hersteller am IFA-Stand gegenüber heise online.

headline: FRITZ! Unveils New Wi-Fi 7 Routers Alongside Matter Bridge Support
summary_text: FRITZ! unveiled its latest generation of FRITZ!Box routers at IFA 2026, alongside an upcoming software update that should be of particular interest to Apple Home users. FRITZ!OS 8.50 introduces Matter Bridge functionality, allowing compatible smart home devices connected to a FRITZ!Box to be exposed to Apple Home and other Matter ecosystems. The company is also introducing several new Wi-Fi 7 routers, including the FRITZ!Box DSL/Fiber 7-90 and FRITZ!Box 6690 Pro, with the latter offering integrated Zigbee and DECT ULE support. ... For Apple Home users, the most significant announcement is the Matter Bridge functionality coming as part of FRITZ!OS 8.50. FRITZ! says the feature will allow its own smart home products, along with compatible third-party devices registered with the FRITZ!Box 5690 Pro, to be integrated into existing Matter ecosystems, including Apple Home, Google Home, and Amazon Alexa. ... Also announced at IFA is the market launch of the FRITZ!Box 6690 Pro, which the company describes as the first cable router to offer tri-band Wi-Fi 7. The router combines a DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem with Wi-Fi 7 across the 2.4GHz, 5GHz, and 6GHz bands, with a combined theoretical wireless throughput of up to 12.2Gbps. Of more relevance to smart home users is its integrated support for Zigbee and DECT ULE. This allows compatible smart plugs, sensors, lights, and other devices to connect directly to the router without requiring their own Zigbee bridge. Interestingly, FRITZ!’s announcement describes the 6690 Pro as offering “Zigbee/Matter and DECT ULE support”, although its more detailed specifications currently list smart home support via DECT ULE and Zigbee. FRITZ! has not explicitly stated that the 6690 Pro will offer the same Matter Bridge functionality announced for the 5690 Pro. The FRITZ!Box 6690 Pro is available now, priced at €429. ... Making its world premiere at IFA is the FRITZ!Box DSL/Fiber 7-90, which also introduces a completely redesigned appearance for the FRITZ!Box range. As its name suggests, the router is designed to work with both DSL and fibre connections, including GPON and AON fibre networks. It offers tri-band Wi-Fi 7 with theoretical speeds of up to 12.2Gbps, along with multi-gigabit WAN and LAN connectivity. headline: The 24-hour CRA deadline is changing software supply chain visibility
summary_text: #### TL;DR Starting September 11, the EU Cyber Resilience Act will require manufacturers to notify regulators within 24 hours of learning a vulnerability in their product is being actively exploited. For companies whose products contain software from multiple suppliers, the bottleneck is not having an SBOM but knowing whether it accurately reflects the underlying code. FossID’s Aaron Branson argues source-code analysis provides the verification layer that turns SBOM documents into reliable supply-chain intelligence. ... According to an analysis published by The Hacker News, manufacturers of products with digital elements sold in the European Union will face a September 11 deadline under the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) to notify regulators within 24 hours after learning that a vulnerability is being actively exploited, with a fuller report due within 72 hours. For manufacturing executives, the 24-hour window may bring greater attention to software supply-chain visibility. Complex products can contain proprietary software, supplier-developed applications, commercial packages, microcontroller software, and open-source libraries, with dependencies extending across several tiers. A manufacturer may maintain numerous supplier relationships while having limited insight into the software embedded within individual components. ... Under the CRA, the relevant product can encompass the complete finished product, creating a need to connect information from numerous suppliers into a coherent software inventory. Automotive, medical-device, aerospace, and consumer-electronics manufacturers may face particularly intricate versions of this challenge. ... This is the environment in which FossID, a software composition analysis company focused on source-code intelligence and software supply-chain transparency, has developed its role. Chief Growth Officer Aaron Branson views the underlying issue through the reliability of the information reaching manufacturers. “ An SBOM is only as useful as the confidence an organization can place in the information inside it,” he states. “ For companies receiving software from numerous suppliers, that confidence requires an additional layer of examination at the point where supplier information enters the enterprise.” ... Source-code analysis aims to provide that layer by examining the software itself to identify components, dependencies, licenses, and vulnerabilities. FossID’s technology can scan code and identify open-source and third-party components, including smaller code fragments and dependencies that may be difficult to establish from declared package information alone. According to Branson, this creates an important distinction between receiving an SBOM and examining whether the SBOM corresponds with the underlying software. ... The supplier relationship may add another layer to the visibility challenge. For large manufacturers, the usefulness of an SBOM may depend partly on whether information from different suppliers can be evaluated consistently and brought into a common record. This is an area where software composition analysis can play a broader role. Supplier-provided information can be examined against the software itself, helping distinguish a document that has been submitted from information that has been sufficiently validated. ... Ultimately, the September 11 requirement may represent an early milestone in a broader evolution of software governance. The Hacker News notes that the CRA’s reporting obligations arrive before the regulation’s wider engineering requirements, which are scheduled to apply in December 2027. This sequence may give manufacturers an opportunity to examine the systems supporting vulnerability identification, supplier information, and product-level software visibility.

headline: Oldefar startede familieimperiet, og arvinger får overskud på over en halv milliard | Økonomisk Ugebrev
summary_text: Den nordsjællandske familie, der ejer den gamle familievirksomhed Foss, kan juble hele vejen til banken. Foss har netop fremlagt et rekordregnskab, der viser, at millionerne bogstavelig talt fosser ind hos Foss. Det er ikke altid det går lige godt, når virksomheder går i arv til 3., 4. og 5. generation. Splid, ballade og salg har flere gange været resultatet. Men hos den gamle familievirksomhed Foss, hvis ejerfamilie er blandt Danmarks rigeste, ser det ud til at gå fantastisk. Den Hillerød-baserede virksomhed, som laver analyseinstrumenter til landbrugs- og fødevareindustrien, har netop offentliggjort regnskab for 2025 – og det viser flere rekorder. Omsætningen lød på 2,73 milliarder kroner, hvilket var en stigning på 142 millioner kroner i forhold til året før. Årets resultat efter skat lød på 504 millioner kroner, hvilket er 30 millioner kroner mere end året før. Det skriver virksomheden Udskiftning på toppen Det gode resultat kommer i et år, hvor Foss også lavede en udskiftning på topposten. Kim Vejlby Hansen trådte tilbage som CEO for Foss og blev i stedet administrerende direktør for holdingselskabet N. Foss & Co. Dermed overtog Christian Rosenkrantz de Lasson posten som CEO i selve ​​Foss. Familien Foss’ overhoved, Peter Foss, som er 4. generation i dynastiet, og som også er bestyrelsesformand, roser begge topchefer: ... Familien er i dag Danmarks 15. rigeste med en formue vurderet til 14,1 milliarder kroner. I dag er også 5. generation af familien blevet medejere af virksomheden. ... Årets overordnede resultat var usædvanligt: De 100 rigeste familiers samlede formue faldt fra 1.240 mia. kr. til 1.225 mia. kr. – et fald på 15 mia. kr. Det er kun anden gang på femten år, at gruppen samlet set er blevet “fattigere”. Mest markant var udviklingen i toppen: De ti rigeste familier tabte samlet omkring 45 mia. kr., især trukket ned af fald hos Louis-Hansen-familien bag Coloplast, LEGO-familien Kirk Kristiansen og Danfoss-familien Clausen. Omvendt gik Bestseller-familien Holch Povlsen frem med 27 mia. kr., mens familien efter Lars Larsen øgede formuen med 13 mia. kr. LEGO-familien er dog fortsat klart Danmarks rigeste med over 350 mia. kr.

headline: Deadline Alert: GPGI, Inc. (GPGI) Shareholders Who Lost
summary_text: What Happened? On August 7, 2024, GPGI, then known as CompoSecure, announced that investment firm Resolute Holdings ("Resolute"), intended to acquire a majority interest in the Company. That transaction was completed on September 17, 2024. On January 12, 2026, CompoSecure, Inc. announced the completion of its acquisition of Husky Technologies Limited ("Husky"), and rebranded itself as GPGI. On February 26, 2026, Jehosaphat Research published a report alleging, among other things, that GPGI had overstated the value of Husky in order to gain shareholder approval for the acquisition, stating that " [all] major aspects of the financials appear to be affected" including that free cash flow was overstated by 90%. Then, on March 12, 2026, GPGI released fourth quarter and fiscal year 2025 financial results, disclosing that Husky saw its EBITDA decline 5.4% year-over-year in the quarter and 3% year-over-year for the full year. headline: Husky faces weaker injection moulding demand
summary_text: # Husky sales fall 9 per cent as cost controls take effect August 11, 2026 Husky Technologies was acquired in January 2026 Husky Technologies has reported a 9 per cent decline in sales for the second quarter of 2026, as economic uncertainty and other market pressures led customers to defer some capital investment projects. Husky, headquartered in Ontario, Canada, reported sales of $339.6 million in the second quarter of 2026, down 9 per cent from the same period a year earlier. Husky president and chief executive Robert Domodossola said the results reflected a demand environment affected by macroeconomic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, elevated oil and resin prices, and changing tariff policies. “These factors resulted in deferral of certain capital investment projects,” Domodossola said during a quarterly conference call. ... Husky manufactures injection moulding machines, moulds, hot runners, controllers and auxiliary equipment for applications including beverage and food containers, medical devices and consumer electronics. The company has installed about 13,500 systems worldwide for the production of beverage preforms and packaging. New systems account for 30 to 35 per cent of Husky’s sales, while aftermarket tooling, including moulds, hot runners and controllers, contributes about 40 per cent. Services, parts and remote monitoring account for the remaining 20 to 25 per cent. The company is implementing an operational improvement programme called the Resolute Operating System, which is intended to standardise processes, control costs, improve cash flow and expand profit margins. At Husky, the programme has introduced daily cross-functional meetings focused on factory loading, while the company has also reduced lead times and increased production output. The company has also been working to expand its aftermarket business and reduce indirect spending through procurement measures. “At the same time, we continue to make investments in innovation and product development,” Domodossola said. Sales expectations For the remainder of 2026, Husky expects sales to be flat to slightly higher than in the second half of 2025. Husky operates as a subsidiary of Great Positions in Good Industries (GPGI), alongside metal payment card manufacturer CompoSecure. GPGI was formed earlier this year after CompoSecure acquired Husky for about $5 billion. Husky was previously owned by private equity firm Platinum Equity, which acquired the company from Berkshire Partners and Omers Private Equity for about $4bn in 2018. Husky and CompoSecure have retained their existing trade names and operate as separate GPGI reporting segments. In July, a shareholder filed a federal securities class action lawsuit against GPGI, alleging that the company and its senior executives misled investors about Husky’s financial outlook and the value of the acquisition before it was completed. The lawsuit follows a February report by Jehosaphat Research that questioned Husky’s valuation and financial performance.

Pour nous, malheureusement, ce n'est qu'un début." ## Pas d'investissement L'inquiétude est vive, dans les rangs du personnel et des syndicats. " Les informations que l'on vient d'avoir sont assez faibles, analyse Christelle Palermo, permanente centrale générale Namur-Luxembourg à la FGTB. On rencontre les mêmes problèmes dans toute l'industrie, à savoir la mise en concurrence des prix. On nous parle des coûts salariaux sans considérer la production des travailleurs." Et Michel Duby, permanent CNE Namur-Luxembourg d'enchérir : " On ne sait pas qui ça concerne. Et on n'a aucune garantie en termes d'investissements. Ils voudraient que la machine tourne plus longtemps, mais on a du matériel qui est vieillissant sur le site. Sans investissement, ça ne fonctionnera pas." Un manque d'investissement pointé par le personnel : " Il va être compliqué d'être rentable et compétitif vu le peu d'investissements réalisés sur le site", explique un ouvrier. " Ils nous disent qu'ils veulent bien investir si c'est pertinent, dénonce un autre. Quand on leur demande ce qu'ils considèrent être pertinents, ils répondent que ça doit être rentabilisé en deux ans. Ça n'existe pas dans l'industrie ! Ils laissent mourir l'outil, ils pressent le citron." L'entreprise est actuellement en bénéfices de 7 à 8 %. Or, le groupe exige une rentabilité de 10 à 15 % : " C'est en dehors de toute considération logique du marché", estime Michel Duby. ... ## Éviter une procédure Renault ? La crainte est que les effectifs continuent de se réduire au fil des ans. " Pour être clair, ce qu'on pense, c'est qu'ils essaient d'être en dessous des 10 % de licenciements qui les mettraient sous le coup de la loi Renault, estime un travailleur. On a peur que ça aille comme ça au fur et à mesure des mois." Un comble pour les syndicats, c'est la concurrence instaurée au sein même du groupe. "On nous parle beaucoup de Brindisi (une implantation italienne de Jindal Films, NdlR), qui reçoit davantage de subsides. Cette mise en concurrence crée un déséquilibre que les travailleurs paient.", précise Christelle Palermo. " Alors qu'ici, ils reçoivent déjà 1 million de subsides de la part de l'État, ajoute Michel Duby. Depuis qu'ils sont arrivés ici, Jindal n'a rien investi et a pris les subventions. C'est l'argent du contribuable aussi, quelque part. Donc, même quand on donne des subsides, les entreprises s'en vont ou du personnel est licencié, alors que l'entreprise est en boni. Le système est à la limite crapuleux."

headline: Latour/Virton : l’usine Jintal à l’arrêt suite à l’annonce de 28 licenciements - RTBF Actus
summary_text: Arrêt de travail à l’entreprise Jindal suite à l’annonce de 28 pertes d’emplois et d’une demande d’augmentation de la production. Par Anaïs Stas © RTBF – Anaïs Stas / Fin de l’assemblée du personnel à Jindal, les travailleurs quittent le site. L’usine Jindal dans le zoning de Latour sur la commune de Virton est à l’arrêt ce lundi après-midi. Les travailleurs ont quitté le site après une assemblée du personnel. Un conseil d’entreprise extraordinaire s’est tenu en matinée. Il a été annoncé 28 pertes d’emplois qui concernent 11 employés et 17 intérimaires. Une chaîne de production bien spécifique sera fermée et l’activité délocalisée dans l’usine italienne. "Les annonces sont très floues, aucune garantie sur l’avenir ne peut être donnée" déplorent les syndicats qui craignent pour l’avenir de l’entreprise. "Il n’y a aucun investissement, l’outil est vieillissant, obsolète. Quatre de nos six machines ont plus de 40 ans. Le budget d’entretien est sans cesse raboté" détaille Rudy Gillet, délégué CSC au sein de Jindal. Depuis que le groupe Jindal a racheté l’entreprise de production de films plastiques à Latour c’est la première mesure de restructuration, mais les syndicats sont inquiets. "Quand on regarde l’historique de notre propriétaire indien, sur les 11 usines, il en a fermé 9. Il ne reste que la nôtre et celle en Italie. Il nous met en concurrence et nous explique que le coût de la main-d’œuvre ici en Belgique est trop élevé". ... ## Augmentation de la production En plus de l’annonce des licenciements, il a été demandé à l’entreprise de dégager plus de bénéfices et donc de produire plus. "Le groupe souhaite que la production ici passe de 2000 à 3000 tonnes sans investissement dans l’outil" explique Christelle Palermo, permanente à la centrale générale Namur-Luxembourg de la FGTB. "Comment y parvenir ? C’est laissé à l’appréciation de la direction locale, mais ce qui est sur la table, c’est notamment de modifier le rythme de travail. On repasse à un rythme de production de 7 jours sur 7". Rudy Gillet précise : "Ce rythme va être difficile à tenir pour le personnel vieillissant de l’entreprise, et je ne vois pas comment l’outil va pouvoir tenir".

headline: Naveen Jindal weighs bid for EU firm Celsa | M&A Critique

headline: Jindal Poly Films Q1 FY27: Sales of ₹696 Cr, Net Profit of ₹108 Cr, and a Factory Still Rebuilding After a Fire - Eduinvesting
summary_text: ## 1. At a Glance Jindal Poly Films makes thin plastic film for packaging, the shiny wrap around a biscuit packet. It also makes soft fabric sheets used in diapers and medical products. This article covers the three months that ended in June 2026. Sales in those three months came to ₹695.80 crore. The same three months a year earlier brought in ₹913.60 crore, a fall of 23.84%. After paying for materials, salaries and power, ₹9.89 crore was left, a figure called operating profit. The company earned a separate ₹169.77 crore outside its main business, mostly from money it has invested. Profit after every cost and tax came to ₹108.00 crore. The lower sales trace back to May 2025, when a fire hit the main packaging film factory at Nashik. A credit-rating agency says about a third of that factory’s capacity is running today. That is a bakery with six ovens and only two of them in working order. The bakery is still open, only quieter than it used to be. The year before this quarter was an eventful one for the company. It carried a fire loss of ₹1,064.24 crore and an objection written in by the auditor. It also brought two notices from SEBI, the market regulator, and a case that reached the Supreme Court. Each of these is covered in its own section. The stock market values the whole of Jindal Poly Films at ₹2,863.14 crore. ... The buying began in 2014 with a majority stake in Global Nonwovens, a fabric maker. Full ownership of that company followed in the year to March 2017. In 2022 it bought SMI Coated Products, which makes sticky labels. In 2023 it bought a holding company in the Netherlands, with film factories in France, Italy and the UK. Each purchase set another product beside the film the company already made. The biggest reshuffle came in August 2022. The company moved its whole packaging film business into a subsidiary, a separate company it owns, named JPFL Films. Brookfield, a global investment firm, had put ₹2,000 crore into that film business in March 2022. The family business now had a large outside partner sitting at the table. In 2025 the company raised its stake in Enerlite Solar Films, which makes film used inside solar panels. Enerlite became a subsidiary of Jindal Poly Films that year. Then came 21 May 2025, when a fire broke out at the JPFL Films factory at Nashik, in Maharashtra. The board said about 70% of the assets at that site were affected. The plant shut fully for about 20 days. It then restarted with the lines that the fire had not reached. ... Before the fire, the Nashik site could make 2,94,200 tonnes of BOPP and 1,70,000 tonnes of BOPET a year. A tonne of film this thin covers a very large area indeed. Most of it reaches a dustbin within a week of being bought, after doing its job perfectly. Non-woven fabric was about 14% of sales in the year to March 2024. It is cloth made by pressing fibres together instead of weaving them. It is the soft layer inside a diaper, a surgical mask or a hospital gown. The company has 60,000 tonnes a year of capacity on three production lines from Germany. Labels were about 7% of sales in the same year. The company sells over 200 kinds of self-adhesive label, the peel-and-stick sort on a shampoo bottle. ... The way the money works is simple: the company buys plastic pellets and melts them. The melted plastic is stretched and rolled up, and those rolls are what it sells. Pellets are made from crude oil, and their price moves with oil. Film prices move with how much film the whole industry is making. When too many factories make the same product, prices come down for everyone. About 70% of sales are in India and 30% outside it. The company sells to buyers in more than 80 countries.

summary_text: Jindal Stainless is advancing a ₹900 crore expansion to reach 2.67 MTPA cold-rolling capacity by FY28. While the company continues to serve established segments like coin blanks at its 10,000-tonne capacity, its primary focus remains on scaling its broader stainless steel manufacturing footprint amidst competitive import pressures. ... Jindal Stainless (JSL) continues to execute its multi-year expansion roadmap aimed at strengthening its market position in the stainless steel sector. The company's recent operational milestones include the commissioning of a 1.2 MTPA stainless steel melt shop in Indonesia in March 2026, which has pushed its total consolidated melting capacity to 4.2 MTPA. This facility is a key part of the company's strategy to bolster its supply chain and meet global demand for high-grade steel products. Building on this momentum, the company has committed to a ₹900 crore investment to increase its annual cold-rolling capacity to 2.67 MTPA by the 2028 financial year, up from the current 2.05 MTPA. This capital spending is designed to enhance the company's ability to cater to diverse industrial needs, including high-value applications such as razor blade strips and established product lines like coin blanks. The company maintains an annual production capacity of 10,000 tonnes for coin blanks, continuing its role as a key supplier for various national mints and international clients. ... Financially, Jindal Stainless reported a steady start to the 2027 fiscal year. Despite the growth, the company faces notable sector-wide challenges. The domestic stainless steel market is currently navigating pressure from lower-priced, often substandard imports that are frequently rerouted through ASEAN countries. This creates competitive headwinds for domestic producers who must contend with margin compression risks. headline: Supreme Court Reserves Verdict On Plea By Minority Shareholders To Recall Order Referring Jindal Poly Films Class Action To Arbitration
summary_text: The Supreme Court on Thursday reserved its verdict on a miscellaneous application filed by a group of 29 minority shareholders seeking recall of its June 8, 2026 order referring the Jindal Poly Films Ltd class action dispute to arbitration. The shareholders contended that the Court had not been informed that the proceedings before the NCLT had already acquired the character of a class action, with thousands of non-promoter minority shareholders becoming parties to the proceedings following statutory public notice. On June 8, 2026, the parties jointly requested the Supreme Court to refer the dispute to arbitration and placed draft minutes of a consent order before the Court. Accepting the request, the Supreme Court set aside the orders of the NCLT and NCLAT and appointed Justice Manindra Mohan Shrivastava (Retd. Chief Justice) as the sole arbitrator. It fixed Delhi as the seat of arbitration and kept all contentions open for determination before the arbitrator. ... Senior Advocate Amit Sibal, appearing for the 29 minority shareholders, argued that the June 8 order had been obtained without disclosing the true nature of the proceedings before the NCLT. He submitted that the original Section 245 petition had been filed on February 28, 2024 by Ankit Jain and two other shareholders, cumulatively holding 4.99% of Jindal Poly Films' share capital, alleging mismanagement and siphoning of company assets. ... Sibal further pointed out that SEBI had intervened in the NCLT proceedings on February 9, 2026 and placed its investigation findings on record, alleging diversion and transfer of funds and assets of Jindal Poly Films to promoter-linked entities. He submitted that SEBI's findings concerned transactions allegedly prejudicial to minority shareholders and involved an alleged fraud of at least ₹800 crore. The bench however, indicated that the merits of those allegations were not presently before it. The Court observed that the merits could be dealt with separately and that the immediate question was whether the June 8 consent order could stand in light of the circumstances now being brought to its notice. ... After hearing the detailed submissions, the Supreme Court reserved its verdict on the miscellaneous application seeking recall of the June 8 order.

headline: Jindal Photo shareholders approve voluntary delisting from BSE and NSE
summary_text: Key Highlights Jindal Photo Limited secured shareholder approval for voluntary delisting from Indian stock exchanges. The special resolution passed with 99.90% support, including unanimous backing from promoters and strong support from public non-institutional investors. Institutional shareholders did not participate in the vote. Jindal Photo Limited shareholders have approved the voluntary delisting of its equity shares from the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE). The company disclosed the voting results on August 19, 2026, confirming that the special resolution passed with overwhelming support from both promoter and public shareholders. The postal ballot process, conducted via remote e-voting and physical forms, ran from July 20, 2026, to August 18, 2026. Out of 16,623 shareholders as on the cut-off date of July 10, 2026, a total of 72 members cast valid votes. The resolution required approval under Regulation 44(3) of the SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015, and Regulation 11(4) of the SEBI Delisting of Equity Shares Regulations, 2021. ... ## Voting Results Breakdown The promoters and promoter group held 7,612,143 shares and voted unanimously in favour of the delisting. Among public non-institutional shareholders, who held 2,644,455 shares, 55.19% of outstanding shares were polled. Of these polled votes, 99.36% supported the resolution. | Shareholder Category | Shares Held | Votes Polled | Votes In Favour | % Support | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Promoter & Group | 7,612,143 | 7,612,143 | 7,612,143 | 100.00% | | Public Non-Institutions | 2,644,455 | 1,459,697 | 1,450,416 | 99.36% | | Public Institutions | 1,728 | 0 | 0 | 0.00% | | Total | 10,258,326 | 9,071,840 | 9,062,559 | 99.90% | ... ## Regulatory Compliance and Scrutiny Pragnya Pradhan & Associates, appointed as the scrutinizer, confirmed that the resolution met the statutory thresholds. Under the Companies Act, 2013, votes in favour must be at least three times those against; here, 9,062,559 votes supported the move against 9,281 dissenting votes. For public shareholders, excluding promoters, SEBI regulations require votes in favour to be more than twice those against. The public assent of 1,450,416 votes significantly exceeded the dissent of 9,281 votes, satisfying this criterion as well. ... The voting data reveals a stark divergence in participation rates between shareholder categories. While the promoter group achieved 100% participation on their entire holding, institutional public shareholders recorded zero participation despite holding 1,728 shares. This suggests that the delisting drive relied heavily on promoter backing and retail non-institutional engagement, with institutional investors abstaining from the vote entirely. The high level of dissent among the small number of participating public voters (0.64%) is statistically negligible but indicates minority opposition to the exit strategy. ... Jindal Poly Films reported a consolidated net loss of ₹10,618.94 crore for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, a sharp reversal from the net profit of ₹1,097.88 crore recorded in FY25.
