The consolidated bottom line was heavily impacted by exceptional items totaling ₹10,671.06 crore. This figure includes a massive write-off related to a fire incident at a subsidiary’s manufacturing facility in Nashik, Maharashtra, which occurred on May 21, 2025. The fire resulted in damage to property, plant, and equipment, capital work-in-progress, and inventories. Key components of the exceptional loss include: - Write-off of property, plant, and equipment: ₹9,108.76 crore (WDV) - Write-off of capital work-in-progress: ₹718.43 crore - Inventory write-offs: ₹4,962.84 crore - GST input credit reversal: ₹822.44 crore - Write-back of packaging incentive scheme: ₹4,970.03 crore Additionally, the company recorded impairment provisions for loans and receivables from a subsidiary considered doubtful due to financial stress, amounting to approximately ₹14,213.12 crore and ₹4,189.99 crore respectively, along with interest write-offs of ₹2,669.69 crore. ... Due to storage constraints and mixed conditions following the fire and subsequent rebuilding work, the auditors could not observe the physical verification at year-end. While a third-party firm performed verification using estimation techniques for some items, the auditors stated they were unable to determine if adjustments to the carrying value were necessary. In contrast, the auditors issued an unmodified opinion on the standalone financial results. ... Consolidated revenue from operations fell 45.6% year-on-year to ₹28,994.21 crore, down from ₹53,349.35 crore in FY25. headline: Jindal Films Europe - Business Focus
summary_text: ### The Future of Recyclable Packaging: Interview with CEO, Gilbert Davids As the packaging industry accelerates its transition towards circularity, Jindal Films Europe is helping customers deliver recyclable packaging solutions through innovation, collaboration and investment. - July 30, 2026 The packaging industry is undergoing a major period of transformation. Rising consumer demand, ambitious sustainability targets and the implementation of the upcoming PPWR (Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation) are accelerating the shift towards packaging solutions that can be more effectively recycled and integrated into a circular economy. For Jindal Films Europe, this challenge presents a significant opportunity. A leader in the development and manufacture of speciality biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) and biaxially oriented polyethylene (BOPE) films, the company is helping customers rethink packaging design by developing solutions that combine performance, product protection and recyclability. Part of the family-owned Indian BC Jindal Group, Jindal Films Europe operates manufacturing facilities in Belgium and Italy and serves customers globally. Its growth has been built on technical expertise, close customer relationships and long-standing commitment to innovation. ... As the industry prepares for PPWR implementation, many brand owners and converters are looking for alternatives to traditional multi-material flexible packaging structures that can be difficult to recycle. Jindal Films Europe is helping drive that transition through the development of advanced mono-material PP and PE film solutions designed to meet increasingly demanding recyclability requirements. “We are leading the transition from multi-material packaging structures to mono-material solutions, enabling customers to design packaging that can be more easily recycled while maintaining the performance required to protect products” Davids explains. ... . At the heart of the company’s innovation strategy is its Innovation Centre, established in 2016 and equipped with a dedicated pilot line for developing and testing new film technologies. “We have our own Innovation Centre with its own pilot line, dedicated to testing and developing new grades of film,” Davids says proudly. “I would describe it as a true hub for innovation, enabling us to test new products with our customers, and test new materials from our suppliers. It plays a vital role in helping us stay ahead of market needs.” ... “For instance, we run the ‘ University of BOPP & BOPE,’ sharing our knowledge with customers so they can better understand our capabilities and explore new opportunities for innovation,” says Davids. “It helps spark new ideas and demonstrates what these materials can achieve.” Investing in the Future Alongside investment in innovation, Jindal Films Europe is expanding its manufacturing footprint to support growing demand for recyclable packaging solutions. The company is investing approximately €60 million in a new hybrid production line at its Brindisi plant in Italy, scheduled to be commissioned in Q4 of this year. “We are very proud of the significant investment we are making in Brindisi,” Davids says. “The investment positions us to support the next phase of market growth as brand owners increasingly transition towards recyclable packaging structures.” The new line represents approximately 36,000 tons of additional BOPP and BOPE film production capacity. “We expect continued growth in both BOPP and BOPE applications, particularly as recyclability becomes an even greater focus for the industry.” Davids explains. “The new line will improve lead times, increase productivity and introduce the latest production technologies into our operations.” ... Innovation and investment are closely linked to sustainability, which Jindal Films Europe sees as one of the defining forces shaping the future of the packaging industry. “Sustainability is one of the most important drivers for our business. It is essential for staying ahead of forthcoming regulations and maintaining our relevance for the future,” Davids says. “The regulatory landscape is accelerating sustainability requirements across the packaging value chain, and that is becoming a major catalyst for innovation.” agrees Christophe Heintz, Market Development Manager for Labelling and Sustainability at Jindal Films Europe. ... For Jindal Films Europe, sustainability extends beyond the development of recyclable packaging structures. As well as partnering with businesses to develop more sustainable packaging solutions, Jindal Films Europe is also investing in the decarbonisation of its own operations, including installing solar panels across the entirety of its plants to generate its own electricity. ... PPWR provides a ticking clock to hit those targets. “ In the flexible packaging sector, regulations will dictate that by 2030 all packaging needs to be recyclable,” points out Mirek Tokaj, Jindal Films Europe’s Marketing Director. “Today 30 to 40% of flexible packaging is not recyclable because it combines different materials. “The challenge is to replace materials such as aluminium foil or polyester within multi-material structures with recyclable PP and PE solutions, without compromising product protection or performance. Our products are designed to deliver barrier properties comparable to the level of aluminium foil while maintaining recyclability.”

headline: Klöckner Pentaplast: Michael Zacka Appointed CEO Following Interim Period
summary_text: Packaging and film manufacturer Klöckner Pentaplast has appointed Michael Zacka as Chief Executive Officer (CEO), effective October 8, 2026. He had already been leading the company as interim CEO since June 2026 (see also plasticker-news dated June 26, 2026). The permanent appointment followed a selection process conducted by the Board of Directors, chaired by Andrew Berlin. According to the company, Zacka focused on implementing strategic initiatives, improving operational performance and strengthening customer relationships during his interim tenure. His permanent appointment is intended to ensure continuity in the company's existing strategy. ... Leadership Experience at Amcor and Tetra Pak Zacka has more than 30 years of leadership experience in the consumer goods, packaging and industrial sectors. Most recently, he served as President of Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) and Asia Pacific at Amcor plc. The business division under his responsibility generated revenue of more than €5 billion and comprised 80 manufacturing facilities in over 30 countries, employing more than 19,000 people. Previously, Zacka served as Chief Commercial Officer at Amcor, where he was responsible for the company's global sales and sustainability strategy. His responsibilities also included restructuring initiatives and the integration and divestment of business units. Earlier leadership positions at Tetra Pak took him to North America and the Asia-Pacific region. He also serves on the Board of Directors and Audit Committee of specialty chemicals company Nouryon. Klöckner Pentaplast Operates 27 Plants in 16 Countries Klöckner Pentaplast manufactures rigid and flexible packaging as well as specialty films. Its customers operate in industries including food and beverages, pharmaceuticals, medical products and card manufacturing. Founded in 1965, the company operates 27 production sites in 16 countries and employs approximately 5,000 people, according to its own figures. The company's existing sustainability strategy includes improving product recycling and recyclability as well as reducing CO₂ emissions. No specific new investments, operational targets or changes to the company's strategic direction were announced in connection with the CEO appointment.

headline: Klöckner Pentaplast has won two RECOUP Awards for its patented, lightweight mono PET tray – PETplanet
summary_text: # Klöckner Pentaplast has won two RECOUP Awards for its patented, lightweight mono PET tray 9 Oct 2026 1 minute Klöckner Pentaplast (kp) has won two RECOUP Awards for kp Elite Nova, its patented, lightweight mono PET tray, designed to help food producers reduce material use, increase recycled content and improve recyclability without compromising performance. Recognised in the Recycled Plastic Product of the Year and Best Plastic Product Development for Recyclability or Re-Use categories, kp Elite Nova was developed to address a key challenge facing the food packaging industry: how to improve recyclability and reduce material consumption while maintaining the performance requirements of modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) applications. According to the company, the result is a high-performance mono PET tray that combines lightweight design, the potential for high levels of recycled content and compatibility with existing PET recycling infrastructure. Cecilia Guardado, Marketing & Innovation Director Trays, at kp said: “ The development of kp Elite Nova focused on a clear challenge: reducing material use, increasing recycled content and improving recyclability without compromise. By combining advanced engineering with a mono PET design, we’ve created a solution that supports more circular material flows and helps customers respond to evolving regulatory requirements and sustainability goals.” The tray can contain up to 100% post-consumer recycled PET and has been independently endorsed by Petcore’s Tray Circularity Evaluation Platform (TCEP) for compatibility with existing PET tray recycling systems. It is claimed to be approximately 10% lighter than comparable MAP trays, helping customers reduce material consumption while maintaining seal integrity, rigidity and shelf-life performance for chilled and frozen food applications.

summary_text: # Klöckner Pentaplast Launches Expanded Polypropylene Pizza Packaging By Packaging Reporter September 30, 2026 Klöckner Pentaplast has expanded its foodservice packaging portfolio with kp Infinity Tavola, an expanded polypropylene pizza box designed to retain heat during takeaway and delivery. The product is launching in the UK and selected European markets from September 2026. It targets quick-service restaurants, pizzerias and delivery-led brands seeking to maintain product temperature and presentation during transport. According to kp, comparative testing showed pizzas remained up to 7.3°C hotter after five minutes than in traditional alternatives, with a temperature advantage still recorded after an hour. The 12-inch pack consists of two identical interlocking parts that form a lidded box for delivery and takeaway. The parts can also be separated for dine-in service and presentation. Kp said the expanded polypropylene structure does not absorb oil and helps contain grease and food residue. summary_text: ## Monday, 10 April 2017 ### Klöckner to acquire food packaging company in UK MONTABAUR, GERMANY: The Klöckner Pentaplast Group (KP), a global leader in rigid plastic film and packaging solutions, has signed a binding agreement to acquire Linpac Senior Holdings Limited and its direct and indirect subsidiaries (LINPAC). Linpac is an UK based film producer and converter for food packaging in Europe. The transaction will create a global leader in the rigid and flexible film market, with combined annual revenues exceeding $2 billion. And is expected to close in the summer of 2017. The combination of KP’s world class film production with Linpac’s highly innovative film production and conversion capabilities will create a one-stop-shop providing complete packaging solutions to customers. The acquisition of Linpac will further strengthen KP’s customer-centric business approach, a key pillar of the company’s strategy. The acquisition will also enable KP to expand its technological capabilities further into the rigid and flexible film market. This market benefits heavily from megatrends including customers’ desire for healthy and safe food with an extended shelf life. By bringing together two of the most innovative firms in the film and packaging industry, KP would create a true R&D powerhouse. By leveraging KP’s and Linpac’s combined and diverse customer universe, KP will be able to develop products, solutions and design capabilities that are tailor-made to address customer needs and will unlock further growth potential. Together, KP and Linpac will have 32 locations across 16 countries with about 6,300 employees. KP’s existing global footprint with operations on six continents will greatly accelerate Linpac’s geographic expansion ambitions, particularly in the Americas. The consolidated group will be led by Wayne Hewett, CEO of KP. Daniel Dayan, CEO of Linpac will lead the Food portfolio. “This is a highly complementary acquisition that will help KP expand our technological capabilities and presence into the food industry and the rigid and flexible film market, as well as further develop our offerings in end markets such as pharmaceuticals, food and beverage, and consumer and industrial products. KP will be enriched by Linpac’s innovations, adjacent products and know-how,” said Hewett.

headline: Driving Circularity in Food Packaging: A Practical Path Through Innovation and Regulation - Sustainable Packaging News
summary_text: Dr Samuel Pardo, Senior Innovation Manager at Klöckner Pentaplast (kp), works at the forefront of food packaging innovation and sustainability. With extensive experience across materials, recycling systems, and regulatory frameworks, he focuses on helping customers navigate the increasing complexity of packaging legislation while maintaining performance and food safety standards. A regular contributor to industry discussions – including PETCORE Europe (see video sent previously) – Samuel brings a practical, systems-level perspective on how the sector can accelerate progress towards more circular packaging solutions. ... The biggest challenge for packaging businesses is maintaining “business as usual” while managing increasing complexity. This means continuing to drive efficiency – controlling costs, securing raw materials, and maintaining resilient supply chains – against a backdrop of global uncertainty. These pressures are not new, but they are now compounded by growing legislative demands. Businesses must ensure compliance while continuing to innovate, particularly where packaging functionality plays a critical role in protecting food and reducing food waste. ... 2. The new Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation is set to reshape the industry. For businesses that are feeling overwhelmed by the scale of change, where would you advise them to focus their efforts first? The most effective starting point is to focus on what is coming first and prioritise against the legislative timeline. For example, PFAS requirements coming into force on 12 August 2026 represent an immediate and non-negotiable compliance priority. Beyond timelines, it is important to understand where your business sits in the value chain, as this determines which requirements are most relevant - from recyclability to recycled content targets. Recent European Commission guidance provides useful clarity, particularly for food packaging, where three areas are critical: - Recycled content: Requirements must not compromise food safety. Where suitable recycling technologies are not yet available at scale, exemptions can apply if appropriately documented. - Recyclability: A staged transition is expected, giving businesses time to adapt while aligning future designs with emerging EU criteria. - PFAS: Clear thresholds will apply from August 2026, and compliance will be essential for market access. At the same time, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) should not be seen as background compliance. It is becoming a key commercial driver in packaging design, with cost implications varying significantly across different national systems. EPR Fees in Europe explained: what packaging businesses need to know in 2026 and beyond ... 4. Innovation is clearly at the heart of your role. Can you tell us about an innovation project that genuinely excited you recently and why you believe it could make a real difference to the future of food packaging? Two recent innovations demonstrate how performance and sustainability can be aligned: - 100% rPET tray from kp Tray2Tray® (launched in 2024): This market-first solution is made entirely from recycled tray material, representing a major step towards true tray-to-tray circularity. It is supported by certified supply chains, ensuring quality, safety, and traceability, while helping customers manage eco-modulated fees and plastic taxes. - kp Elite® Nova MAP tray (launched July 2025): Designed using advanced engineering techniques, this tray is around 10% lighter than comparable solutions while maintaining strength, sealing integrity, and barrier performance. It is optimised for high-speed packing environments and reduces material usage without compromising functionality. These innovations reflect a broader principle: true circularity starts with design. Packaging must be engineered to be compatible with existing recycling systems so that it can be recovered and reused at scale. ... True circularity already exists in some formats, such as drinks and beverage bottles, where materials are routinely collected, recycled, and turned back into bottles. For pots, tubs and trays, progress is being made, particularly through the integration of recycled content from PET thermoforms streams. However, further progress depends on alignment across the entire value chain to increase both the demand for and supply of recycled material, alongside significant investment in collection and sorting infrastructures. ... Collaboration is becoming increasingly important, particularly with brands and retailers. Through EPR schemes, these stakeholders are ultimately responsible for packaging-related fees, which is driving closer interaction across the value chain. Stronger collaboration here will be key to accelerating progress, aligning design choices with both regulatory requirements and cost implications. ... DRS (deposit return schemes) systems are conceived to increase customer awareness. However, scaling up them have other side implications such as cost increase or feedstock restrictions due to complexity of laying down these systems into big countries ... One of the biggest lessons is the importance of aligning expectations early in the process. Upstream collaboration is essential to ensure all stakeholders agree on specifications, cost implications, quality standards, and material availability. Without this alignment, it becomes difficult to scale solutions that balance sustainability ambitions with the realities of food packaging performance. ... A clear indicator of progress would be a significant increase in recycling outputs beyond the most established streams such as PET bottles, metal cans, cardboard, and glass. Expanding effective recycling infrastructure and outputs for formats such as trays and films would demonstrate that the industry is moving meaningfully towards a more circular system.

headline: Klöckner Pentaplast adds fruit trays to kp Infinity range - Food Engineering & Ingredients
summary_text: # Klöckner Pentaplast adds fruit trays to kp Infinity range Klöckner Pentaplast (kp), a global supplier of rigid and flexible packaging and specialty film solutions, has extended its kp Infinity ® portfolio with a new fruit tray range built for packed fresh fruit. The launch moves the mono-material, fully recyclable format beyond food-to-go applications and into fresh produce packaging, addressing sector-wide demand for solutions that support recyclability and cut food waste. ### From food-to-go to fresh produce The kp Infinity range built its reputation in food-to-go packaging, and kp has now translated that format into dedicated tray designs for fresh fruit. Retailers, producers and consumers are placing growing weight on packaging sustainability, and fresh produce businesses in particular are seeking formats that reduce food waste and improve recyclability without compromising shelf appeal. The new trays have been developed specifically to meet that brief. ... ### Material and functional properties The trays are manufactured from expanded polypropylene (EPP), giving a lightweight but durable structure that helps protect fruit through the supply chain, an approach intended to limit product damage and associated waste. The format has a traditional, artisan-style appearance for on-shelf presentation and is stackable, supporting efficient handling, transport and storage. Clear, consumer-facing recycling messaging is built into the trays to simplify disposal and encourage recycling participation. kp also reports a lower carbon footprint for the trays, alongside reduced water and energy use in manufacture, relative to alternative packaging materials. ... ### A complete pack solution For customers wanting a full packaging system, the fruit trays can be paired with kp FlexiStretch ® overwrap or kp FlexiFlow ® films, combining protection and presentation from packing line through to retail shelf. Austin Schwarz, Sales Director UK&I at kp Food Packaging, said: “Following the success of kp Infinity in food-to-go applications, we identified a growing need for recyclable packaging solutions in the fresh produce sector. The new fruit tray range brings together the durability, presentation and recyclability customers are looking for in a format specifically designed for whole fruit such as apples and pears.” He added: “Combined with kp FlexiStretch overwrap or our kp FlexiFlow films, customers can source a complete packaging solution from one supplier, benefiting from streamlined procurement, technical expertise and consistent packaging performance across the supply chain.” ... The launch extends kp’s fresh produce packaging offer and continues the company’s “Investing in Better” sustainability strategy, which sets out ten targets covering recyclability, carbon reduction and workforce wellbeing.

summary_text: Packaging and film manufacturer Klöckner Pentaplast has appointed Michael Zacka as Chief Executive Officer (CEO), effective October 8, 2026. summary_text: # Klöckner Pentaplast has won two RECOUP Awards for its patented, lightweight mono PET tray 9 Oct 2026 1 minute Klöckner Pentaplast (kp) has won two RECOUP Awards for kp Elite Nova, its patented, lightweight mono PET tray, designed to help food producers reduce material use, increase recycled content and improve recyclability without compromising performance. Recognised in the Recycled Plastic Product of the Year and Best Plastic Product Development for Recyclability or Re-Use categories, kp Elite Nova was developed to address a key challenge facing the food packaging industry: how to improve recyclability and reduce material consumption while maintaining the performance requirements of modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) applications. According to the company, the result is a high-performance mono PET tray that combines lightweight design, the potential for high levels of recycled content and compatibility with existing PET recycling infrastructure. Cecilia Guardado, Marketing & Innovation Director Trays, at kp said: “ The development of kp Elite Nova focused on a clear challenge: reducing material use, increasing recycled content and improving recyclability without compromise. By combining advanced engineering with a mono PET design, we’ve created a solution that supports more circular material flows and helps customers respond to evolving regulatory requirements and sustainability goals.” The tray can contain up to 100% post-consumer recycled PET and has been independently endorsed by Petcore’s Tray Circularity Evaluation Platform (TCEP) for compatibility with existing PET tray recycling systems. It is claimed to be approximately 10% lighter than comparable MAP trays, helping customers reduce material consumption while maintaining seal integrity, rigidity and shelf-life performance for chilled and frozen food applications.

headline: Klöckner Pentaplast Launches Expanded Polypropylene Pizza Packaging | Packaging Reporter
summary_text: # Klöckner Pentaplast Launches Expanded Polypropylene Pizza Packaging By Packaging Reporter September 30, 2026 Klöckner Pentaplast has expanded its foodservice packaging portfolio with kp Infinity Tavola, an expanded polypropylene pizza box designed to retain heat during takeaway and delivery. The product is launching in the UK and selected European markets from September 2026. It targets quick-service restaurants, pizzerias and delivery-led brands seeking to maintain product temperature and presentation during transport. According to kp, comparative testing showed pizzas remained up to 7.3°C hotter after five minutes than in traditional alternatives, with a temperature advantage still recorded after an hour. The 12-inch pack consists of two identical interlocking parts that form a lidded box for delivery and takeaway. The parts can also be separated for dine-in service and presentation. Kp said the expanded polypropylene structure does not absorb oil and helps contain grease and food residue. The company describes the packaging as recyclable within appropriate polypropylene collection and recycling streams. “We spend a lot of time talking and collaborating with customers and stakeholders from across the industry. They tell us they’re being asked to do more than ever before. Operators are under pressure to deliver food quickly, maintain quality during transportation and create a better customer experience,” said Austin Schwarz, sales director, UK and Ireland, at kp. Schwarz said early operator trials identified potential space and time savings, alongside improved heat retention during transportation. The launch extends the company’s Infinity Hotpacs foodservice offering into pizza packaging. Larger orders can be customised with embossing.

headline: World of Chemicals - latest chemistry news, articles, research, jobs, academics: Klöckner to acquire food packaging company in UK
summary_text: ## Monday, 10 April 2017 ### Klöckner to acquire food packaging company in UK MONTABAUR, GERMANY: The Klöckner Pentaplast Group (KP), a global leader in rigid plastic film and packaging solutions, has signed a binding agreement to acquire Linpac Senior Holdings Limited and its direct and indirect subsidiaries (LINPAC). Linpac is an UK based film producer and converter for food packaging in Europe. The transaction will create a global leader in the rigid and flexible film market, with combined annual revenues exceeding $2 billion. And is expected to close in the summer of 2017. The combination of KP’s world class film production with Linpac’s highly innovative film production and conversion capabilities will create a one-stop-shop providing complete packaging solutions to customers. The acquisition of Linpac will further strengthen KP’s customer-centric business approach, a key pillar of the company’s strategy. The acquisition will also enable KP to expand its technological capabilities further into the rigid and flexible film market. This market benefits heavily from megatrends including customers’ desire for healthy and safe food with an extended shelf life. By bringing together two of the most innovative firms in the film and packaging industry, KP would create a true R&D powerhouse. By leveraging KP’s and Linpac’s combined and diverse customer universe, KP will be able to develop products, solutions and design capabilities that are tailor-made to address customer needs and will unlock further growth potential. Together, KP and Linpac will have 32 locations across 16 countries with about 6,300 employees. KP’s existing global footprint with operations on six continents will greatly accelerate Linpac’s geographic expansion ambitions, particularly in the Americas. The consolidated group will be led by Wayne Hewett, CEO of KP. Daniel Dayan, CEO of Linpac will lead the Food portfolio. “This is a highly complementary acquisition that will help KP expand our technological capabilities and presence into the food industry and the rigid and flexible film market, as well as further develop our offerings in end markets such as pharmaceuticals, food and beverage, and consumer and industrial products. KP will be enriched by Linpac’s innovations, adjacent products and know-how,” said Hewett.

headline: Driving Circularity in Food Packaging: A Practical Path Through Innovation and Regulation - Sustainable Packaging News
summary_text: Dr Samuel Pardo, Senior Innovation Manager at Klöckner Pentaplast (kp), works at the forefront of food packaging innovation and sustainability. With extensive experience across materials, recycling systems, and regulatory frameworks, he focuses on helping customers navigate the increasing complexity of packaging legislation while maintaining performance and food safety standards. A regular contributor to industry discussions – including PETCORE Europe (see video sent previously) – Samuel brings a practical, systems-level perspective on how the sector can accelerate progress towards more circular packaging solutions. ... The biggest challenge for packaging businesses is maintaining “business as usual” while managing increasing complexity. This means continuing to drive efficiency – controlling costs, securing raw materials, and maintaining resilient supply chains – against a backdrop of global uncertainty. These pressures are not new, but they are now compounded by growing legislative demands. Businesses must ensure compliance while continuing to innovate, particularly where packaging functionality plays a critical role in protecting food and reducing food waste. ... 2. The new Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation is set to reshape the industry. For businesses that are feeling overwhelmed by the scale of change, where would you advise them to focus their efforts first? The most effective starting point is to focus on what is coming first and prioritise against the legislative timeline. For example, PFAS requirements coming into force on 12 August 2026 represent an immediate and non-negotiable compliance priority. Beyond timelines, it is important to understand where your business sits in the value chain, as this determines which requirements are most relevant - from recyclability to recycled content targets. Recent European Commission guidance provides useful clarity, particularly for food packaging, where three areas are critical: - Recycled content: Requirements must not compromise food safety. Where suitable recycling technologies are not yet available at scale, exemptions can apply if appropriately documented. - Recyclability: A staged transition is expected, giving businesses time to adapt while aligning future designs with emerging EU criteria. - PFAS: Clear thresholds will apply from August 2026, and compliance will be essential for market access. At the same time, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) should not be seen as background compliance. It is becoming a key commercial driver in packaging design, with cost implications varying significantly across different national systems. EPR Fees in Europe explained: what packaging businesses need to know in 2026 and beyond ... 4. Innovation is clearly at the heart of your role. Can you tell us about an innovation project that genuinely excited you recently and why you believe it could make a real difference to the future of food packaging? Two recent innovations demonstrate how performance and sustainability can be aligned: - 100% rPET tray from kp Tray2Tray® (launched in 2024): This market-first solution is made entirely from recycled tray material, representing a major step towards true tray-to-tray circularity. It is supported by certified supply chains, ensuring quality, safety, and traceability, while helping customers manage eco-modulated fees and plastic taxes. - kp Elite® Nova MAP tray (launched July 2025): Designed using advanced engineering techniques, this tray is around 10% lighter than comparable solutions while maintaining strength, sealing integrity, and barrier performance. It is optimised for high-speed packing environments and reduces material usage without compromising functionality. These innovations reflect a broader principle: true circularity starts with design. Packaging must be engineered to be compatible with existing recycling systems so that it can be recovered and reused at scale. ... True circularity already exists in some formats, such as drinks and beverage bottles, where materials are routinely collected, recycled, and turned back into bottles. For pots, tubs and trays, progress is being made, particularly through the integration of recycled content from PET thermoforms streams. However, further progress depends on alignment across the entire value chain to increase both the demand for and supply of recycled material, alongside significant investment in collection and sorting infrastructures. ... is ... , ... with brands and retailers. Through EPR schemes, these stakeholders are ultimately responsible for packaging-related fees, which is driving closer interaction across the value chain. Stronger collaboration here will be key to accelerating progress, aligning design choices with both regulatory requirements and cost implications. ... DRS (deposit return schemes) systems are conceived to increase customer awareness. However, scaling up them have other side implications such as cost increase or feedstock restrictions due to complexity of laying down these systems into big countries ... One of the biggest lessons is the importance of aligning expectations early in the process. Upstream collaboration is essential to ensure all stakeholders agree on specifications, cost implications, quality standards, and material availability. Without this alignment, it becomes difficult to scale solutions that balance sustainability ambitions with the realities of food packaging performance. ... A clear indicator of progress would be a significant increase in recycling outputs beyond the most established streams such as PET bottles, metal cans, cardboard, and glass. Expanding effective recycling infrastructure and outputs for formats such as trays and films would demonstrate that the industry is moving meaningfully towards a more circular system.

headline: Klöckner Pentaplast adds fruit trays to kp Infinity range - Food Engineering & Ingredients
summary_text: # Klöckner Pentaplast adds fruit trays to kp Infinity range Klöckner Pentaplast (kp), a global supplier of rigid and flexible packaging and specialty film solutions, has extended its kp Infinity ® portfolio with a new fruit tray range built for packed fresh fruit. The launch moves the mono-material, fully recyclable format beyond food-to-go applications and into fresh produce packaging, addressing sector-wide demand for solutions that support recyclability and cut food waste. ... ### From food-to-go to fresh produce The kp Infinity range built its reputation in food-to-go packaging, and kp has now translated that format into dedicated tray designs for fresh fruit. Retailers, producers and consumers are placing growing weight on packaging sustainability, and fresh produce businesses in particular are seeking formats that reduce food waste and improve recyclability without compromising shelf appeal. The new trays have been developed specifically to meet that brief. ... ### Material and functional properties The trays are manufactured from expanded polypropylene (EPP), giving a lightweight but durable structure that helps protect fruit through the supply chain, an approach intended to limit product damage and associated waste. The format has a traditional, artisan-style appearance for on-shelf presentation and is stackable, supporting efficient handling, transport and storage. Clear, consumer-facing recycling messaging is built into the trays to simplify disposal and encourage recycling participation. kp also reports a lower carbon footprint for the trays, alongside reduced water and energy use in manufacture, relative to alternative packaging materials. ... ### A complete pack solution For customers wanting a full packaging system, the fruit trays can be paired with kp FlexiStretch ® overwrap or kp FlexiFlow ® films, combining protection and presentation from packing line through to retail shelf. Austin Schwarz, Sales Director UK&I at kp Food Packaging, said: “Following the success of kp Infinity in food-to-go applications, we identified a growing need for recyclable packaging solutions in the fresh produce sector. The new fruit tray range brings together the durability, presentation and recyclability customers are looking for in a format specifically designed for whole fruit such as apples and pears.” He added: “Combined with kp FlexiStretch overwrap or our kp FlexiFlow films, customers can source a complete packaging solution from one supplier, benefiting from streamlined procurement, technical expertise and consistent packaging performance across the supply chain.” ... The launch extends kp’s fresh produce packaging offer and continues the company’s “Investing in Better” sustainability strategy, which sets out ten targets covering recyclability, carbon reduction and workforce wellbeing.

headline: Australia Won the Work. Now it’s Time to Staff the Books. - Entertainment Partners
summary_text: Australia’s screen industry has spent the past several years proving it can win the work. International studios keep choosing Australian locations, the incentive framework is among the most competitive in the world, and local production volume has grown accordingly. Attracting the business, though, is only half of the equation. A government-commissioned study released this year points to a quiet problem sitting underneath all that momentum: the screen industry needs to ensure it has enough skilled talent to continue servicing the expanding sector. The 2026 Production Infrastructure and Capacity Analysis (PICA), commissioned by Screen Australia and conducted by Olsberg SPI, confirmed Australia’s status as a world-class, globally trusted production hub, while identifying four structural pressure points that could constrain that growth: limited business scalability, persistent skills gaps, unclear career progression and infrastructure constraints. Within the report is a finding that deserves the attention of every financial controller and production accountant working across Australian and New Zealand productions: among below-the-line roles, Production Accountant sits in the top five hardest-to-fill positions, alongside Line Producer, Location Manager, Production Coordinator and Production Manager. ... The first warning sign in the report is structural. PICA points out that local production companies are often small and project-based, built to deliver one show at a time, not scale thefinance function across a growing slate of concurrent productions. In practice, that means the same finance teams delivering domestic slates are increasingly expected to manage multi-territory studio compliance, co-financing structures and tighter reporting cadences — without a proportional increase in headcount or in the training available to prepare them for it. For an industry that measures its success in production volume and studio confidence, a finance function that can’t scale is a real constraint, not an abstract problem. PICA recommends targeted business development training, stronger links between academia and industry, and continuous upskilling as the way through. ... ## Responding to the Shortage: Taking Enablement to Where the Work Happens It’s this combination that Entertainment Partners is building its response around. Later this year, EP will launch an education and enablement program for production accountants and financial controllers across Australia and New Zealand, built around craft expertise and underpinned by SmartAccounting, EP’s accounting platform, and SmartPO, EP’s purchase order and payables solution. The series, titled On Location: Smart Production Finance Management, is designed less as a product demonstration and more as a practical, hands-on training in the workflows PICA identifies as under strain — scaling a finance function across concurrent productions, managing studio-grade compliance and reporting, and building the kind of structured, transferable skill set that keeps experienced production accountants in the industry, where they are needed. ... On Location: Smart Production Finance Management will visit key production states through the remainder of 2026, with sessions open to production accountants and financial controllers regardless of their current software environment. Details, including session dates, locations and how to register, will follow in the coming weeks.

headline: Beyond scale: making supplier M&A work for operators - G3 Newswire
summary_text: # Beyond scale: making supplier M&A work for operators M&A can expand a supplier’s portfolio, but adding scale alone does little for operators. RubyPlay CFO Motti Gil explains why acquisitions need to be built around strategic fit, disciplined integration and products that solve genuine commercial challenges, drawing on RubyPlay’s acquisition of Splash Tech and its move towards a broader content and engagement platform. There is no shortage of M&A activity in iGaming. Consolidation is happening across the value chain, from operators to platforms and content suppliers. From a supplier perspective, an acquisition is often seen as a quickfire route to growing their size and stature. However, these deals are worthless if they fail to benefit operators in helping to drive their business forward through third party partnerships. Too often, a supplier looks to grow its product portfolio through the purchase of a company without adding real value to the operators it serves. This tends to happen when a deal is driven primarily by opportunity rather than strategy, for example, acquiring a business simply because a competitor has made a similar move. Wider portfolios look good on paper but can make little practical change to what operators can actually access. That distinction often gets overlooked when analysing M&A within our industry. ... Fundamentally, effective M&A activity requires a thorough process that goes beyond simply looking at revenues or profits. Multiple factors need consideration to ensure a deal maximises its potential to benefit the wider ecosystem. ... The discipline behind a good deal Two companies can announce a deal with strong logic on paper, overlapping customer bases, complementary products, a clear commercial rationale, and still fail to deliver anything meaningful a year later. The difference usually comes down to what happens away from the headline announcement. Most of that work happens before signing. It begins with proper preparation to better understand what strategic initiative the company is aiming to fulfil, screening the market properly, and mapping out which targets will create value rather than just adding scale. Culture is the part most likely to get waved through in the excitement of a deal, and it’s often the reason integrations stall. Deals that are clear from day one on governance, how the acquired business will sit within the group, and what the complete package looks like tend to reach operators faster and with fewer surprises. Deals that leave those questions open, tend to show up as delays, inconsistent messaging, or products that technically exist but never quite land with the partners they were meant to serve. ... RubyPlay’s acquisition of Splash Tech is a good example of this approach in practice. We clearly identified from the outset that we wanted to move beyond the traditional content silo and firmly establish ourselves as a content and engagement platform provider. We wanted to address the challenge of player acquisition and retention that our operator partners face and concluded that M&A was the strategic route to elevate our offering and better serve them. Splash Tech brought jackpot and free-to-play capabilities that fitted directly into our existing engagement suite, alongside free spins, rewards, missions and tournaments. From our perspective, that gave us a broader, more complete engagement offering that would ultimately benefit operators worldwide. The jackpot engine works across verticals rather than being tied to a single product, so operators can turn slots, live casino or sports bets into a jackpot opportunity. That gives them more flexibility to differentiate their offering, both between brands and within the same market. The free-to-play tools add another layer, giving operators ways to drive acquisition and retention that sit outside traditional bonusing. Taken together, this widens the toolkit operators have for engagement and does so without adding the cost pressure that heavier promotional spend usually brings. ... None of this strategic value happens organically when two companies combine through M&A. It is the product of proven disciplines I apply to any acquisition: understanding what the target does well, looking at how it complements what already exists, and integrating it properly so operators see the full benefit. Unlocking these new revenue streams can define a successful supplier acquisition, leaving operator partners with better tools than they had before.

headline: The Capital Moment: Why Private Investment Belongs in the Australian Screen Industry - Entertainment Partners
summary_text: Australia’s screen industry has never looked more attractive from the outside. Record-breaking international productions are choosing Australian locations. A world-class incentive framework has been cemented into law. Studios are expanding and global streamers are deepening their local footprint. And yet, for all that momentum, one piece of the puzzle has remained underdeveloped: private investment. That is beginning to change, and 2026 may be the year the screen industry and the investment community finally find a common language. ... Screen Australia’s newly released Private Investment Toolkit, launched in June 2026, put the problem plainly: there has long been a structural disconnect between screen projects and the private capital that could fund them. Producers have traditionally lacked the tools to present their projects with the commercial rigour that investors expect. That toolkit, developed in consultation with finance, tax, investment, legal and production professionals, is a signal that the ecosystem is maturing. The question is who helps producers and investors navigate the bridge. ... The opportunity is substantial. Australia’s screen incentive architecture is among the most generous and structurally elegant in the world. Four fully refundable tax offsets—the 30-40% Producer Offset, the 30% Location Offset, the 30% Post, Digital and Visual Effects (PDV) Offset, and the 30% Digital Games Tax Offset—all underpin the financial logic of virtually every significant production in the country. Critically, the word “refundable” matters enormously to sophisticated investors: these are not deductions or concessions that merely reduce a tax bill. They are tax rebates paid from the Australian Taxation Office. For anyone structuring a return, that is a fundamentally different conversation. Together, these offsets represent a government-backed yield-enhancement mechanism embedded into the production finance model. For investors who understand how to structure around them, they materially alter the risk-return calculation. Entertainment Partners has been at the forefront of helping productions maximise these offsets, including the recently added training obligation—a workforce development requirement embedded in the rebate—fulfilled in part through Entertainment Partner’s education and enablement programs. ... The investment case for Australian screen is strengthened by a structural supply constraint that is only likely to intensify. The 2026 Production Infrastructure and Capacity Analysis (PICA) study, commissioned by Screen Australia and conducted by Olsberg SPI, confirmed Australia’s status as a world-class, globally trusted hub for high-value content, while simultaneously identifying four structural pressure points: limited business scalability among local production companies, persistent skills gaps in specialist crew roles, unclear career progression pathways, and infrastructure constraints. For investors, this is important context. The demand for high-end production in Australia is outpacing the sector’s current capacity to service it. Roles like line producers, production accountants, production coordinators and VFX supervisors are in short supply—precisely the senior infrastructure that large-scale productions require. In a functioning market, constrained supply against growing demand implies a premium for those operators who can genuinely deliver at scale. The industry needs more than creative capital, however; it needs operational and financial infrastructure. Full-service capabilities—managing a production end-to-end, from incentive structuring through to payroll, compliance, accounting and delivery—are becoming a source of competitive advantage, not merely a logistical convenience. It is precisely this gap that Entertainment Partners has built its Australian offering to close. ... There is also a sequencing consideration to understand: the Producer Offset can take monthsto arrive after a production wraps. The SPV must remain active, with a functioning bank account and ASIC registration, until that payment is received and tax return obligations settled. This complexity should not surprise a sophisticated operator but demands experienced financial management. Entertainment Partners’ production finance team and SmartAccounting platform are designed to maintain precisely that oversight, from first day of prep through final offset collection, giving investors real-time visibility at every stage. ... At the senior end sits debt, typically bridging facilities that advance against the expected offset receipt, secured over the receivable. The refundable nature of the offset is what makes this financeable as near-collateral: a lender is effectively advancing against a government payment, not against speculative box office returns. Equity sits above that, bearing more risk and expecting a corresponding return—whether through backend profit participation, upfront fees, or a combination. Pre-sales, co-production agreements, broadcaster licence fees and distributor advances can all slot into the capital stack at various points, each reducing the equity requirement and improving the overall risk profile for investors coming in at any level. ... The conditions that make 2026 a compelling entry point for private investment in Australian screen are not accidental. They are the product of sustained policy effort, deliberate industry development, and a growing recognition that public funding alone cannot sustain the growing sector. The Location Offset is bedded in. The Producer Offset cap has been removed. Screen Australia has published a private investment framework for the first time. The PICA study has provided an evidence base for where the growth opportunity sits. SPA’s Screen Forever 40 Financial Futures program strand put capital mobilisation at the centre of the industry’s conversation about its own future. ... For producers, this means removing the most significant barrier to accessing private capital at scale: the ability to present a project with the financial rigour, structural clarity and operational credibility that serious investors require. For investors, it means a partner who understands both sides of the equation. Entertainment Partners brings exactly that combination—deep expertise in how the offset regime works in practice; integrated production management, finance, and accounting tools that provide real-time governance and compliance oversight; workforce solutions that satisfy the training obligations embedded in the incentive framework; and a local team with the industry relationships and track record to guide a production from certificate application through to final offset payment.

headline: Paramount Sacrifices Universal Deal, But Will It Keep Cinema Safe?
summary_text: That’s because Paramount has agreed to exit UIP, its 50-50 joint venture with Universal Pictures, to secure regulatory approval for its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery in the European Union. In remedies laid down by the European Commission, the EU’s antitrust enforcer, Paramount will need to unwind its links to UIP within 13 months of closing the Warner merger, walking away from a company that has been part of the European cinema landscape for 44 years. ... So here’s what we know: Paramount will terminate its 50% stake in UIP, meaning it will have to seek alternative distribution arrangements in the 100 territories in which UIP has a presence. Paramount may be able to tap into Warner Bros. Pictures operations in some of these locations or piggyback on Warner’s existing partnerships, but only if the partner has no role in distributing Universal or Disney films. ... Whatever the outcome, UIP will have significantly fewer titles to handle, which will inevitably create uncertainty for the company’s 200 employees (even if it does distribute some non-Paramount-Universal titles, such as Lionsgate’s Michael). ... UIP posted sales of nearly £198M ($263M) in 2024, per its most recent accounts filed at the UK’s Companies House. It recorded a pre-tax profit of £12.2M. In its pomp, UIP boasted box office takings of $2.5 billion, but was much diminished in 2007, when Paramount and Universal took direct control of distribution in key markets, including France, Brazil, and Italy. ... A well-placed industry executive said: “I can’t see it making any difference, to be honest. The pieces will just move around between even fewer players, meaning even less competition. Maybe there needs to be further regulation introduced so that no single local distribution company has dominant market share, and other ways to stimulate competition and innovation.” ... The International Union of Cinemas (UNIC), which represents cinema operators across 39 European territories, agrees. Laura Houlgatte, UNIC’s chief executive, told Deadline: “While the remedy addresses an important structural issue, it does not tackle similar risks that arise from theatrical distribution arrangements outside the UIP territories, nor does the Commission decision address a number of wider concerns that UNIC raised throughout the review.” ... During the European Commission’s investigation process, Houlgatte said the UNIC advocated for “safeguards around theatrical exclusivity and release windows, as well as measures to help maintain a strong and diverse pipeline of films for cinemas and audiences.” Paramount CEO David Ellison has attempted to assuage these concerns with commitments to release more than 30 cinema films a year and hold to a minimum theatrical window of 45 days. He will continue making this case while the merger is on ice as Paramount fights a lawsuit from 12 U.S. state attorneys general, who argue the deal stifles competition for theatrical film distribution. ... The Balanced Economy Project, an apolitical UK non-profit that lobbies against monopolies, is not convinced. It said the European Commission’s UIP remedy “does nothing obvious about the future bargaining power of a combined Paramount-Warner studio.” The Balanced Economy Project added: “Cinemas would still face one fewer independent major studio. Broadcasters and platforms would still face a larger owner of premium rights. Producers and creative suppliers would still face another reduction in major routes to market.”

headline: Universal McCann Becomes One of Nigeria's First ISO Certified Advertising Agencies - BrandiQ
summary_text: # Universal McCann Becomes One of Nigeria’s First ISO Certified Advertising Agencies ## The agency says its new ISO 9001:2015 status formalises a quality push already visible in its recent revenue growth and faster turnaround times Last updated: September 10, 2026 9:01 pm Martin Ogumah ... Universal McCann Media Limited has secured ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System certification, positioning itself among the first advertising agencies in Nigeria to attain the internationally recognised standard. The certification, dated July 9, 2026, was issued by TNV Group and formally presented to the agency this week at a ceremony held at Universal McCann’s head office in Lagos. The award affirms that the agency’s quality management processes meet global benchmarks for consistency, efficiency and client satisfaction. It covers the full span of Universal McCann’s operations, from strategic planning through to media execution, and the agency says it reflects an ongoing commitment to quality assurance and continuous improvement across every part of its business. ... The presentation was attended by representatives from both organisations, including Sunni Otegwu of Panoramicsynergy Enterprises, Universal McCann’s human resources lead Omobola Olajide, finance director Abel Oghumu, and Panoramicsynergy project manager Olajumoke Akingbemila, alongside the agency’s Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Bimpe Fayemi. ... Speaking at the event, Fayemi described the certification as a landmark for both her company and the wider marketing communications industry. “Attaining the ISO 9001:2015 certification as the very first advertising agency in Nigeria is a watershed moment for our company and the broader marketing communications industry,” she said. She added that the standard validates the agency’s operational frameworks, strategy development, and media execution against global expectations, and gives clients and brand partners confidence that every project delivered is backed by rigorous quality assurance and a culture of innovation. ... Universal McCann, an affiliate of global network IPG Mediabrands, offers media planning, digital marketing, creative solutions, data driven brand strategy, and integrated campaign management for clients across multiple commercial sectors. The agency said the new certification would raise its own operational bar further and set a benchmark for professionalism across Nigeria’s advertising industry. BrandiQ Insight Read alongside the agency’s recent public track record, this certification looks less like a one-off achievement and more like the formal seal on a process already underway. Universal McCann has reported year over year revenue growth above 40 percent under Fayemi’s leadership, alongside the acquisition of three major brand accounts and an internal restructuring that reportedly cut average project turnaround time by two days. An ISO 9001 certification typically requires documented, auditable process discipline across an organisation, which is precisely the kind of operational tightening that tends to precede, rather than follow, the growth numbers an agency likes to publicise. Seen this way, the certification is best read as evidence for a claim Universal McCann has already been making about itself, not a new claim on its own. ... There is also a competitive signal worth noting for anyone tracking Nigeria’s advertising sector. Multinational clients and global procurement teams increasingly use ISO certification as a screening requirement before an agency is even invited to pitch, particularly for regional or pan African mandates that require proof of standardised process across markets. By becoming a first mover on this specific certification, Universal McCann is not simply making a domestic credibility claim aimed at the Lagos market. It is positioning itself to qualify for a category of multinational and cross border business that historically has gone by default to agencies with international backing rather than locally managed operations, even when those operations carry a global network’s name. ... Finally, the timing invites a broader industry question. If ISO 9001 certification becomes a genuine differentiator this year, it will not remain one for long. Once a market leader clears a credibility bar publicly, competitors tend to treat it as a new cost of entry rather than a lasting advantage, and Nigeria’s other major agency networks are likely already weighing whether to pursue the same certification. The real test of Universal McCann’s first mover claim will be how much client business it converts in the months immediately following this announcement, before the rest of the market catches up.

summary_text: # Universal McCann Malaysia explores the commodity of trust in advertising Conference Blog | 23 August 2026 ## By Yuki Liang Freelance writer INMA T he advertising business has changed dramatically in little more than two decades. First came mass reach. Then came data, targeting, and personalisation. Now Sue-Anne Lim believes the industry is entering a third phase: community. The CEO of Universal McCann Malaysia said this shift reflects a growing recognition that brands cannot build lasting equity through fragmented interactions alone. At the INMA Asia-Pacific News Media Summit 2026, Lim said advertisers are increasingly looking for three scarce commodities — attention, context, and trust — and news publishers are uniquely positioned to offer all three. ... Lim began by putting the scale of today’s advertising market into perspective. Global advertising spend surpassed US$1 trillion in 2025. Advertising now has reached its third stage: community. ... ’ ... this ... a ... for ... . ... of the ... . ... “Reach and data were ... you leveraged from platforms,” ... said. “ ... advertisers ... now is much harder ... — ... The timing is particularly significant because trust in the information environment is under pressure. Lim highlighted data showing that global trust in news has fallen to its lowest point in a decade, while four in 10 people now actively avoid the news. Yet 38% still turn to a trusted source when they need to verify whether something is true. With global trust in news falling, news publishers have both an opportunity and a responsibility to rebuild trust with audiences. ... The proliferation of AI-generated content adds another layer of uncertainty. Lim was careful to distinguish AI itself from what she called the “rubbish content” increasingly circulating online. The problem for audiences is that it is becoming harder to determine what is truthful, what is fake, and what is a scam. ... For news publishers, however, ... presents ... opportunity. As Lim ... : “ ... article. But ... reason ... reader trusts ... article ... the ... At the same time, AI is changing the way audiences find information. Lim pointed to a growing “zero-click” environment, with around 69% of news searches now ending without a click-through to a news site. Google referrals to news sites also fell by 33% in 2025, according to Lim. ... AI is changing the way audiences find information. ... publishers ... that simply attracting a click ... be ... audiences ... Nearly half of Malaysians now get their news on TikTok, one of the highest rates anywhere in the world, according to Lim. Attention has moved into the feed, while creators and influencers increasingly control discovery. But discovery does not automatically translate into trust. ... UM’s data showed that trust is strongly determined by proximity. Friends and family rank highest, followed by verified buyer reviews and other buyers, while influencers rank significantly lower. Lim noted that although influencer followers and advertising spending are rising, trust has not kept pace. ... Trust is strongly influenced by ... , according ... . ... advertisers, therefore ... to ... . ... Lim identified three things that brands cannot buy at scale from a platform: attention that is not paid, context that means something, and trust that has a rub-off effect. An audience that actively chooses to engage can be more valuable than a much larger audience exposed passively to an advertisement. Lim illustrated the point by noting that “200,000 organic shares and views are worth much more than 20 million paid impressions.” ... Context matters too. Brands are increasingly sensitive to the environments in which they appear, rather than ... whether their logo or message ... placed ... . ... ## Rethinking what news publishers sell So what does this mean for news media? Lim offered four practical directions for publishers looking to capture the advertising spend that brands are already moving into new channels. 1. Sell brands the community, not the leftover impressions. As Lim put it, “your loyal, engaged audience is really worth far more than the remnant inventory that you’re really pricing to clear.” The message is to place greater value on the relationship publishers have built with their audiences, rather than treating audience attention as simply another unit of inventory. 2. Give brands meaningful environments, not just eyeballs. Based on UM’s experience, Lim said clients are increasingly looking for “more sponsorships and activations,” particularly where audiences are genuinely engaged. “People are genuinely engaged. They have a unified experience of the brand, and that really beats a banner pop-up,” she said. For advertisers, the environment in which a brand appears can be just as important as the audience size. 3. Publishers should recognise the value of their subscribed audiences. Rather than viewing advertising as something that simply takes value from an audience, she suggested that brands can help “reward your audience with quality content and experience itself.” 4. Publishers should explore bespoke partnerships and ownable IPs. Brands, she said, are “really open for bespoke partnerships,” including “formats, data partnerships, commerce.” The key, she argued, is “community integration” — creating something that brands and publishers can build together rather than treating advertising as a one-way transaction. “That ... can create a win-win situation where you can work very closely with brands.” The bottom line, Lim said, is this: “Your priority customer should be your audience, not advertisers.”

So here’s what we know: Paramount will terminate its 50% stake in UIP, meaning it will have to seek alternative distribution arrangements in the 100 territories in which UIP has a presence. Paramount may be able to tap into Warner Bros. summary_text: 국내 대표 콘텐츠 제작사 초록뱀미디어(3,030원 ▲20 +0.66%)가 글로벌 숏폼 콘텐츠 플랫폼 릴숏과 손잡고 숏폼 드라마 공동 제작에 나선다고 2일 밝혔다. 이번 협업은 급성장하는 글로벌 숏폼 시장을 겨냥한 전략적 행보로, 제작 포트폴리오 다변화와 새로운 성장 동력 확보를 목표로 한다. ... 초록뱀미디어는 '올인', '주몽', '거침없이 하이킥', '나의 아저씨', '펜트하우스 시즌 1·2·3', '나의 해방일지', '서초동' 등 다수의 흥행작을 통해 국내 드라마 제작 역량을 입증해 왔다. 기존 방송 및 OTT(온라인동영상서비스) 중심의 제작 경험을 기반으로 안정적인 IP(지식재산권) 기획 능력을 이제 모바일 중심의 숏폼 영역까지 확장하게 됐다. ... 파트너사인 릴숏은 누적 다운로드 약 2억 5000만 건, 이용자 7500만 명을 보유한 글로벌 숏폼 드라마 플랫폼으로, 모바일 중심의 콘텐츠 소비 트렌드에 최적화된 제작 및 유통 구조를 갖추고 있다. 짧은 러닝타임과 높은 몰입도를 특징으로 하는 콘텐츠 경쟁력을 기반으로 글로벌 숏폼 시장에서 빠르게 영향력을 확대하고 있다. ... 양사의 협력은 초록뱀미디어의 검증된 스토리텔링과 릴숏의 글로벌 유통망이 결합했다는 점에서 시너지가 기대된다. 숏폼 콘텐츠는 일반 드라마 대비 제작비 회수 기간이 짧고 반복 시청이 잦아 수익성 개선에도 유리한 구조다. 이를 통해 제작 리스크를 분산하고, 글로벌 시장에서의 흥행 가능성을 높일 수 있을 것으로 기대된다. ... 선제적으로 제작이 진행된 'Daddy 엄마를 구해주세요!.'는 릴숏의 인기 IP를 기반으로 한 작품으로, 배우 고주원과 손담비가 주연을 맡아 완성도를 높였다. 해당 작품은 오는 6월 릴숏 플랫폼을 통해 전 세계에 공개될 예정이다. 또한 판타지 로맨스 장르의 후속 공동 제작 프로젝트도 현재 진행 중이다. ... 초록뱀미디어는 이번 협업 과정에서 인공지능(AI) 기술을 적극 도입하며 제작 효율화를 꾀하고 있다. 현재 제작 중인 판타지 로맨스 작품에는 AI 기반 촬영 기법을 적용해 비용 절감과 영상 품질 향상을 동시에 추진한다.

headline: コンテンツIPの総合プロデュースを担う「スモール・プラネット」へ出資～戦略的業務提携から資本提携へ、両社のシナジー創出をさらに加速～ | 株式会社ロッテホールディングスのプレスリリース
summary_text: 株式会社ロッテホールディングス（本社：東京都新宿区、代表取締役社長 CEO：玉塚 元一、以下「ロッテホールディングス」）は、このたび、コンテンツIP事業の強化を目的に、2026年9月1日付で株式会社スモール・プラネット（本社：東京都八王子市、代表取締役 吉野 廣樹、以下「スモール・プラネット」）の第三者割当増資を引き受け、同社の株式20％を取得しましたのでお知らせいたします。 ... ロッテホールディングスは、2026年1月にスモール・プラネットと戦略的業務提携に向けた基本合意（MOU）を締結し(*1)、「アジア圏への事業拡大」「新規グッズ・体験型イベントの共同推進」「高付加価値ビジネスモデルの構築」について協業の可能性を検証してきました。その期間中にも両社の強みを生かしたグループ横断的なプロジェクトが始動し、高い相乗効果と事業の成長性が見込めたことから、資本業務提携のもとで協業体制を本格化させるべく、出資を実行することにしました。 ... 本資本提携により、日韓ロッテグループの経営基盤や事業フィールドと、スモール・プラネットのコンテンツIPビジネスにおける川上から川下までを網羅する高い専門性を掛け合わせ、国内外における事業展開のスピードをさらに加速させます。また、両社のシナジーによりグローバル展開を目指すコンテンツの支援やイベント企画・運営の受託など幅広く展開し、国内外の各キャラクターのファンの皆さまに新たな体験価値を提供いたします。 ... 具体例 ... ロ ... が展開 ... ハード ... ミ「カジ ... ！」のキャンペーンにおいて、 ... ネットが販促物（ ... チェーン ... の企画・設計 ... 製造 ... 担 ... デザイナー ... デザイン ... 製造 ... ことで、 ... 魅 ... 最大限 ... 高い ... オリ ... 迅速 ... 体制 ... 同時に実現 ... 制作 ... ベリゴムは韓国のロッテホームショッピング社が展開する人気キャラクターで、ロッテホールディングスは2024年3月に日本国内におけるマスターライセンシー契約を締結しています。このたび、スモール・プラネットが日本国内におけるライセンシーに加わり、今後、新商品企画や売り場展開の拡大などを企画予定です。

headline: 자이언트스텝 자회사 빅인스퀘어 흑자 전환…일본 광고·콘텐츠 호조
summary_text: 일본 상업광고 수주 확대…영화·드라마 등 사업 영역 넓혀 ... [서울=뉴스핌] 양태훈 기자 = 인공지능(AI) 및 리얼타임 콘텐츠 전문기업 자이언트스텝은 프로덕션 자회사 빅인스퀘어가 일본 상업광고 수주 확대와 영화·드라마 등 신규 사업 성과에 힘입어 흑자 전환했다고 7일 밝혔다. 빅인스퀘어는 최근 일본에서 대형 상업광고 프로젝트의 기획·제작 물량을 잇달아 수주하며 매출을 확대했다. 회사는 일본 광고 사업의 수익성을 기반으로 재무 실적이 흑자로 전환됐다고 설명했다. 영화와 드라마 등 오리지널 콘텐츠 제작 사업도 확대하고 있다. 빅인스퀘어가 자체 제작한 영상 콘텐츠 '개인적인 택시'는 한국콘텐츠진흥원의 '2025년 OTT특화 콘텐츠 제작지원' 사업에 선정됐다. 자이언트스텝 로고. [사진=자이언트스텝] '개인적인 택시'는 국내 넷플릭스와 일본 후지TV의 자체 동영상 플랫폼 FOD를 통해 방영될 예정이다. 후지TV는 해당 작품에 투자했다. 회사 측은 다른 국가로의 판권 수출도 논의하고 있다고 밝혔다. 이 작품은 제천국제음악영화제에서 드라마 작품으로는 처음 상영됐다고 회사 측은 설명했다. 빅인스퀘어는 차기작인 영화 '강시: 공포의 워크샵'도 내년 공개를 목표로 제작하고 있다. ... 빅인스퀘어는 이 같은 콘텐츠 제작 과정에서 자이언트스텝 본사가 위탁 운영하는 남산 확장현실(XR) 스튜디오 인프라를 활용하고 있다. 자이언트스텝은 모회사와 자회사 간 제작 인프라 연계를 통해 제작 효율을 높이고 있다고 설명했다. ... 자이언트스텝 본사도 해외 프로젝트 수주와 제작 공정 효율화에 나서고 있다. 미국법인을 통해 미국 라스베이거스의 '스피어(Sphere)' 관련 실감형 콘텐츠 프로젝트를 수주했으며, 전사 제작 파이프라인에는 자체 AI 솔루션 'TabTo(탭토)'를 도입해 비용 절감을 추진하고 있다. 회사는 국내 시각특수효과(VFX) 및 영상 제작 시장 여건에 대응해 해외 수주와 AI 기술 적용을 확대한다는 방침이다. ... 자이언트스텝 관계자는 "자회사 빅인스퀘어의 글로벌 진출과 신규 사업 호조에 따른 흑자 전환은 연결 실적 개선의 동력"이라며 "본사 역시 미국 스피어 등 글로벌 프로젝트 수주 확대와 자체 AI 툴 TabTo를 활용한 원가 절감을 추진하고 있다"고 말했다.

headline: Great Island Productions Enters YA Space with Fantasy Novel Adaptation - ScreenMDM
summary_text: # Great Island Productions Enters YA Space with Fantasy Novel Adaptation - September 2, 2026 Great Island Productions in Ireland is moving into the YA space, optioning the adaptation rights to the best-selling fantasy novel Her Hidden Fire by Clíodhna O’Sullivan. The outfit is plotting an 8×50-minute adaptation of the novel, a best-seller in the U.S. and the U.K. The second installment will be published in November 2026 by Penguin Random House Children’s in the U.K. and Ireland, and by Viking in the US. A third book follows next summer. Great Island is developing the IP as a three-season series to encompass the entire trilogy. The deal was brokered by Marc Simonsson of International Creative Agency. ... Mark Kenny, CEO of Great Island, commented, “We’re always looking for distinctive IP and original voices that have the potential to connect with audiences beyond Ireland, and Her Hidden Fire has exactly that. Clíodhna is a wonderful writer, and she has created a rich fantasy world around a character-driven story with high emotional stakes, and the massive audience response to the novel so far speaks to the strength of the IP. Bringing the series into our slate is an exciting step as we expand our scripted offering with YA. There’s no better time for this as we continue to develop projects with international potential and look for partner production, distribution and studio companies to build them with.”

headline: 'Shinbyeong' Production Company Expands Aggressively Beyond Mid-Form to YouTube, AI, and Games... | STARNEWS
summary_text: 'Story Island,' the comprehensive content production company that demonstrated the potential of mid-form serialized dramas with 'Shinbyeong,' is now seeking to expand its content portfolio. 'Story Island' announced on the 27th that it will officially launch next-generation content businesses that transcend the boundaries of formats and platforms, ranging from mid-form dramas to YouTube, AI short-form dramas, and FMV (Full Motion Video) games. 'Shinbyeong,' which recently began its fourth season, is being praised for creating a success story for serialized dramas through differentiated strategies amid rapidly changing content environments. 'Story Island' is rapidly expanding its content production areas to include YouTube, short-form content, AI, and games based on the success of 'Shinbyeong.' Rather than simply supplying existing content to new platforms, it aims to transform the very approach to planning and production. ... 'Story Island' previously unveiled 'The Boss Is Crazy,' featuring broadcasters Choi Sung-hoon and Lee Eun-ji, through its own YouTube channel on the 19th. This commerce variety show was planned with consideration for how digital platform users consume content and react, focusing on direct communication with users through its own channel. ... Island ... This project attempts to introduce a new production method by combining its own IP with AI technology in the short-form market, characterized by rapid consumption and high production efficiency. 'Story Island' also plans to combine video and game genres. In collaboration with Story Taco, it is producing the FMV game 'Ancient Witches Live in My Basement.'
