headline: Bari Weiss Addresses CBS News Staff Post Paramount Merger
summary_text: CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss told staffers Tuesday morning that leadership still does not know what many of the newly merged company’s long-term plans will mean for the news division, even as she sought to reassure employees that no immediate changes are coming. “The truth is, there is a lot that we still don’t know,” Weiss said during CBS News’ 9 a.m. editorial meeting and in a memo obtained by TheWrap. “What we can tell you right now is that nothing is going to change. This is a process that’s going to unfold over time.” Her remarks came as Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery officially closed their merger, bringing CBS News and CNN under the same corporate roof and raising immediate questions about how the two major national news organizations will coexist inside the combined company. “Obviously, it’s a very exciting day for the company,” Weiss told staffers. “Tom and I know that it raises infinite questions about CBS News, about what’s next, and we wish that we could answer all of those questions.” ... Skydance has already settled one of the biggest leadership questions. Mark Thompson will remain atop CNN while Weiss continues to lead CBS News, preserving separate editorial leadership for the two organizations. But broader questions remain about resources, operations and whether the news divisions could eventually share functions as Paramount integrates Warner Bros. Discovery. ... For now, Weiss told CBS News staffers to focus on their reporting. “The best guidance that we can share is that we should focus always on the work that we do,” she said. Weiss pointed to what she described as momentum inside CBS News and urged the newsroom to continue producing journalism that distinguishes it from competitors. “We just have a lot of momentum, and we have done remarkable work that everyone here should be extremely proud of,” she said. “And at CBS, that shouldn’t change.” ... The comments offer an early look at how CBS News leadership is addressing employees as Paramount begins integrating Warner Bros. ... For CBS News, the immediate directive is continuity. The longer-term structure remains unresolved. “I know that everyone, again, has a lot of questions,” Weiss said.

headline: Judge allows Paramount to close $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery
summary_text: A California judge on Wednesday formally approved Paramount Skydance’s settlement with California and other states, the final hurdle required for it to close its $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. Judge clears way for Paramount to acquire Warner Bros. The seismic merger will bring together the likes of CBS News and CNN, HBO Max and Paramount+, and storied film studios Warner Bros. and Paramount Pictures. Shortly after the judge’s approval, David Ellison, the CEO and controlling shareholder of Paramount Skydance, announced that Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz would become co-CEO of the combined media giant. Kreiz will join the company Oct. 5, and the companies said in a statement the deal “is expected to close on October 6.” ... After the deal was approved by the U.S. Justice Department, the European Commission and dozens of other countries worldwide, it was held back by a lawsuit led by California’s Democratic attorney general, Rob Bonta. Bonta and other state attorneys general worried that the deal, if completed, would reduce competition and potentially imperil the journalistic independence of CNN. Paramount Skydance, led by Ellison, reached a deal with the states on Sept. 21, which will require the combined company to release at least 30 films a year and set up an editorial board to oversee both CNN and CBS News. Larry Ellison, the father of Paramount CEO David Ellison, is a close ally of President Donald Trump’s. He is personally backing the deal with tens of billions of dollars of his own fortune. After acquiring Paramount, David Ellison appointed former New York Times opinion writer Bari Weiss to run CBS News. She has clashed with longtime correspondents and faced accusations of meddling with their editorial independence. The merged company pledged to invest more than $1 billion in U.S. film production and worker training. Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín’s approval comes just hours before a so-called ticking fee kicks in for Paramount Skydance. In order to build confidence in the merger plan earlier this year, Paramount agreed to pay Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders 25 cents per share each quarter if the transaction did not close by Sept. 30. That penalty would be worth more than $600 million every three months. ... Shares of both Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery closed near their highest levels of the day following the news. Paramount shares have been beaten down by more than 20% since the start of the year as the merger remained in limbo.

headline: Trump announces plans for largest steel plant in U.S. history to be built in Iowa - CBS News
summary_text: Washington — President Trump on Monday announced that the company Mesabi Metallics will build a $15 billion steel plant in Iowa over the coming years, in what would be the largest of its kind in U.S. history. "There's a company known as Mesabi," the president said in the Oval Office. "And they're going to make a big investment in a place called Iowa. I love Iowa. I won Iowa every time. Today, we're thrilled to announce that Mesabi Metallics will be building the largest steel plant in American history in the great state of Iowa." The president and the Minnesota-based Mesabi Metallics unveiled the company's plans for what the White House is calling a mega steel plant, alongside Mesabi executives and Iowa officials. The announcement comes as several Iowa Republicans face competitive elections in the November midterms, including the party's candidates for Senate and governor. Although Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said Monday the steel plant won't receive direct federal support, he acknowledged that the government-run Export-Import Bank financed Mesabi's iron ore plant in Minnesota, which will provide the raw materials essential to making steel. Once it's up and running in 2030, the plant is expected to produce 7.5 million or more tons of steel per year. A White House official said the plant is expected to create 1,750 permanent jobs in Iowa. ... The plans for a new plant mark the Trump administration's latest move to boost domestic steel manufacturing in the face of overseas competition, a centerpiece of the president's trade agenda. Last year, he doubled tariffs on imported steel to 50%, and steel levies have been part of the ongoing trade dispute between the U.S. and Canada. He also approved a deal for Japan-based Nippon Steel to buy U.S. Steel, an arrangement that calls for new investments in the iconic Pittsburgh-based company. ... Mesabi has not announced where in Iowa the steel plant will be, but Energy Secretary Chris Wright mentioned that it would be in the southeast part of the state. A White House official said this will be the first mega steel plant built in the U.S. since the 1960s. The Trump administration expects the steel could support U.S. defense projects in the future. The Wall Street Journal was first to report the president's anticipated announcement of the new steel plant. ... The Export-Import Bank's board approved a $770 million direct loan to Mesabi Metallics for its iron ore endeavors on Sept. 24, a spokesperson for EXIM told CBS News. The board was initially considering up to $10 billion in support, according to a March news release. ... In 2008, the Essar Group's Essar Steel Minnesota LLC began work on a massive iron mine and processing facility in Minnesota. But after years of delays, missed deadlines and financial challenges, Essar Steel Minnesota LLC filed for bankruptcy in 2016. Frustrated with the delays, the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources took steps in 2019 to potentially bar Essar Global from working with the state, although the company sued over that move, and the state ultimately did not complete the debarment process.

headline: Paramount Skydance reaches antitrust deal with states over Warner Bros. Discovery purchase - CBS News
summary_text: A group of U.S. states has reached a deal with Paramount Skydance that addresses antitrust concerns over the media and entertainment company's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The deal with a coalition of 12 state attorneys general clears the way for Paramount, the parent company of CBS News, to complete its purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery. "This settlement is not a vote of support for this merger," said California Attorney General Rob Bonta at a press conference on Monday to announce the agreement. ... ## Settlement conditions The agreement includes pledges from Paramount to invest in domestic film production, Bonta said. The company will invest an additional $300 million per year in domestic production over five years, for a total of $1.5 billion in new investment, according to the proposed consent decree. Paramount also pledged to produce 30 films in each of the first two years after the merger, and then 32 films a year for the following three years. Under the deal, at least 20 of the films must be wide-release movies in the first two years, and 21 must be wide-release films in the following three years. Wide-release films are those that are distributed to at least 2,000 movie theater screens, according to the consent decree. If Paramount fails to meet those requirements, it will be required to sell the Miramax film studio, the document states. For each film the company falls short of its annual release commitment, it must make a $30 million payment, with half going to the healthcare and retirement funds serving movie production unions. The rest would be divided between the Motion Picture & Television Fund and the National Association of Attorneys General Fund. The agreement also bars Paramount from selling or closing the Paramount or Warner Bros. studio lots in the Los Angeles metropolitan area for at least five years. Paramount has also agreed to establish an independent board to "ensure independent, objective fact-based reporting at CBS News and CNN," Bonta said. Additionally, the merged company must commit to separate negotiations for the distribution of basic cable channels owned by Paramount and Warner Bros. for a period of five years. Under the settlement, a committee of five states will monitor and enforce Paramount's compliance with the terms of the antitrust agreement. The Department of Justice, Federal Communications Commission, and regulators in dozens of countries have already approved the deal. ... Paramount clinched a deal for Warner Bros. earlier this year. But state prosecutors, led by Bonta, filed a lawsuit in July to block the transaction, alleging the merger would weaken competition in the movie industry and lead to higher prices for consumers. The Writers Guild of America also filed suit in U.S. district court to block the merger, arguing that it would harm competition for writers and eliminate jobs in the industry. Paramount has rejected allegations that buying Warner Bros. would reduce competition. ... office hits such as the "Harry Potter" and "Lord of the Rings" franchises, and the company also owns cable networks including CNN, HBO Max, TBS and TNT. Paramount's stock price was largely flat at $10.15 after Bonta's announcement, while Warner Bros. shares rose 11% to $30.80.

headline: Connecticut AG Says State Wanted Paramount to Sell CNN, CBS News
summary_text: Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said Monday that his state demanded Paramount fully divest CNN and CBS News as part of negotiations over the company’s $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. “Connecticut wanted and demanded full divestiture of CNN and CBS News,” Tong said in a statement. “We wanted to save ethical and independent journalism and news. We fought aggressively for that remedy. I am deeply disappointed that we could not do more.” Instead, Paramount reached a settlement Monday with Connecticut, California and 10 other states that allows the company to retain both news organizations while establishing an independent editorial board intended to protect the editorial independence of CNN and CBS News. The fact that the settlement stopped short of requiring Paramount to divest either news organization raised questions about how much leverage regulators had to demand a more sweeping remedy. “To see that the outcome of the deal didn’t require a divestiture of one of the major news outlets … that was the most disenchanting aspect of it,” J. Christopher Hamilton, an entertainment attorney and professor at Syracuse University’s Newhouse School of Public Communications, told TheWrap. “We already have a canary in the coal mine with CBS News — why weren’t they more aggressive about CNN?” he added. ... The absence of a divestiture requirement suggests either that such a remedy was never seriously in play or that regulators lacked the leverage to force it, Hamilton said. ... The agreement cleared the final major legal hurdle for the merger, which Paramount CEO David Ellison told employees Monday is expected to close in approximately two weeks. ... CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a federal lawsuit Monday challenging the White House ban, arguing that the administration violated their First Amendment rights. The outlets are seeking a temporary restraining order restoring their journalists’ access. ... Under the settlement, the combined company must maintain editorial independence at CNN and CBS News through an independent board. The agreement also includes commitments on theatrical film releases and domestic production spending, among other provisions. Sen. Elizabeth Warren also criticized the settlement Monday, arguing that the combination would give the new company too much power over the media business. “Allowing one Trump-aligned, foreign-owned conglomerate to dominate American news and entertainment is a disastrous outcome,” the Massachusetts Democrat said in a statement. Warren accused the Trump

headline: How would consumers feel a U.S. ban on Canadian booze and other products? - CBS News
summary_text: Americans will see fewer Canadian brands on the shelf if a planned U.S. ban takes effect later this month. But one Canadian whiskey maker — Crown Royal — has positioned itself to escape the import restrictions the Trump administration has threatened to impose. President Trump on Tuesday announced the bans on Canadian exports of alcoholic beverages, dairy products and motorcycles after Canada imposed counter-tariffs on roughly $20 billion in U.S. goods. The ban is scheduled to take effect Sept. 29. While tariffs take time to work their way through supply chains and trickle down to consumers, a ban would be felt more immediately because the restricted Canadian products would be removed from store shelves and dealer lots as soon as existing inventory is sold, experts told CBS News. "Tariffs take time to get to consumers, but a ban effectively removes the product and supplier at any price, immediately," said Wendong Zhang, an economist at the Cornell SC Johnson College of Business. "There's no negotiating — when a consumer goes to a store, there is a 'deshelving' of Canadian product." The Trump administration ban applies only to the importation of the specified Canadian goods and doesn't prevent the sale of products already in the U.S. Brett House, an economist at Columbia Business School, criticized the ban. "It's bad for everyone. It either completely cuts off or raises the costs for American consumers to continue buying these goods," he told CBS News. U.S. consumers could turn to domestic substitutes, he noted. "None of those three categories are things you can only get from Canada. But the thing you're switching to might not be higher cost, but could be lower satisfaction resulting from not being able to get the exact product you want." ... Crown Royal, a popular Canadian whiskey brand sold in the U.S., had taken steps to protect its access to the American market before the Trump administration's ban on liquor imports from its northern neighbor. Although the company still distills its whiskey in Manitoba, Canada, it previously moved its bottling operations from an Ontario plant to Alabama. While a White House proclamation still bans the export of Canadian alcohol to the U.S., the ban's fine print offers a workaround for Crown Royal. Details in an annex outlining banned goods note that only whiskies in containers of less than four liters are banned from U.S. import. That means Canadian whiskies can still cross the border in containers larger than four liters.

headline: Bombardier caught in the crossfire of escalating U.S.-Canada trade feud - CBS News
summary_text: # Bombardier caught in the crossfire of escalating U.S.-Canada trade feud By Megan Cerullo Megan Cerullo Reporter, MoneyWatch Megan Cerullo Updated on: September 8, 2026 / 5:33 PM EDT / CBS News Canadian aircraft maker Bombardier is an emblem of the intricate economic relationship between the U.S. and its northern neighbor, and a prime example of how the countries' escalating trade feud can ensnare employers with thousands of workers on both sides of the border. On Truth Social, Mr. Trump threatened on Monday to block the Montreal-based company's sales in the U.S. if it doesn't manufacture its aircraft in America. "NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER IN THE UNITED STATES! Their products aren't good enough!" Mr. Trump posted hours before Canadian tariffs on $20 billion in U.S. goods took effect just after midnight on Tuesday. "If they want our Market, they must build here, and stop treating America like a 'piggybank.'" Wall Street analysts said it's unclear if Mr. Trump could legally ban Bombardier from selling its planes to U.S. customers, and noted that such a move would hurt domestic suppliers and buyers at a time of strong demand for private jets. The business jet "market remains historically tight, and a ban on Bombardier products would severely disrupt U.S. customers" who already face multi-year waits for private jets, analysts with investment bank Stifel said in a report. The White House didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. Bombardier shares fell roughly 3% on Tuesday following Mr. Trump's threat. Here's what to know about the company. ... Today, Bombardier is among the top three business jet manufacturers globally, specializing in medium- and large-size aircraft. The company manufactures and assembles its jets at plants in Canada, the U.S. and Mexico. ... Over its long history, it entered and left the train-making business and expanded for a time into making regional and commercial aircraft. But it sold off those parts of its business as it restructured to focus on making private business jets. ... Bombardier primarily sells private and commercial jets to individuals, businesses, governments, and military forces worldwide. High-net-worth individuals account for roughly 60% of its customers. ... In a statement on Monday following Mr. Trump's post, Bombardier sought to underline its contributions to the American economy, saying it accounts for "tens of thousands of jobs across the United States." Bombardier said it has workers in 20 U.S. states and plants in Arizona, California, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Illinois, Kansas, New Jersey, Texas and Washington, D.C. The company's supply chain also comprises 2,800 U.S. companies in 47 states, according to Bombardier. ... Bombardier said in its statement that the company spends over $2.5 billion with U.S. suppliers annually. It has headquarters in Wichita, Kansas, while its Challenger Jets are powered by American-made engines from U.S. aerospace manufacturer Honeywell, which are made in Phoenix, Arizona. "I reached out to the Trump administration to make certain the President is aware of the significant contributions of Bombardier to Kansas and the importance of its presence in Wichita to many Kansas workers at Bombardier and in the Bombardier supply chain," Sen. Jerry Moran, a Republican from Kansas, wrote in a social media post. ... Wings for Bombardier planes are made at the company's facility in Red Oak, Texas, while flight control components are manufactured at its Los Angeles, California, area facility. Bombardier also operates service centers in Dallas, Texas; Hartford, Connecticut; Miami, Florida; Tucson, Arizona; and Wichita, Kansas. In January, Bombardier said it was investing to expand its U.S. operations, including opening a new facility in Fort Wayne, Indiana. Bombardier sources more than 50% of its aircraft components from U.S. manufacturers — more than American competitors such as Gulfstream, according to Stifel. ... Whether the U.S. could enforce Mr. Trump's threat against Bombardier "is a question mark," Stifel analysts said, noting that buyers could take delivery of its aircraft offshore under a foreign registry. Yet White House pressure could still affect Bombardier's business.

headline: Chevron plans to double oil production in Venezuela with $7 billion investment - CBS News
summary_text: imee Picchi Associate Managing Editor, MoneyWatch Aimee Picchi Updated on: September 2, 2026 / 8:16 AM EDT / CBS News Chevron said on Wednesday that it plans to invest $7 billion in Venezuela over the next five years and double its oil production in the country after receiving additional acreage in the crude-rich Orinoco Belt region. Chevron, the only U.S. oil company operating in Venezuela, said the investment will allow it to boost production to about 600,000 barrels a day, twice its current capacity, according to a statement. The announcement comes after President Trump announced a deal on Aug. 28 with Venezuela to create a private joint venture to operate oil fields containing 65 billion barrels of petroleum. Chevron said on Wednesday that it costs the company about $20 per barrel to produce oil in Venezuela. "With improved terms and additional acreage, we are strengthening a portfolio that we believe can deliver attractive low-cost oil growth, support energy supply and create differentiated long-term value," Chevron CEO Mike Wirth said in the statement. Chevron said it has been assigned rights to develop the adjacent Carabobo 1 and Carabobo-2-South-A areas in the Orinoco Belt. ... Chevron officials and U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright are expected to visit Venezuela on Wednesday, where the new investment will be formally unveiled, according to a U.S. official. ... Venezuela holds the world's largest proven oil reserves, which contain more than 303 billion barrels of crude oil, according to OPEC's 2025 Annual Statistical Bulletin. Saudi Arabia is a distant second with 267 billion barrels. Mr. Trump said the Venezuela deal will help lower U.S. gasoline prices, while also refilling the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which has dropped to historically low levels. However, experts say it could take years for either goal to be reached because Venezuela's oil industry suffers from years of neglect and needs billions in fresh investment. "Meaningful new barrels are years away: Much of Venezuelan oil is extra-heavy crude sitting behind decayed infrastructure, so significant output growth will require substantial investment and time," Dan Alamariu, chief geopolitical strategist at investment advisory firm Alpine Macro, said in a research note. ... The White House's joint venture in Venezuela involves a private company called North American Blue Energy Partners, or NABEP, the White House said Monday. Under the agreement, the Venezuelan government granted the company 100-year concessions to drill in 17 oil fields that contain about 65 billion barrels, roughly one-fifth of Venezuela's total proven oil reserves.

headline: The market forces quietly adding thousands to patient bills - CBS News
summary_text: Hug's experience is a classic example of the predicted outcome of "vertical integration" in the healthcare system, when one company owns or controls multiple parts of a supply chain and can therefore direct patients to more expensive treatment options. ... In any case, such healthcare integration is occurring at a breakneck pace all across the nation, with endless permutations: Hospitals are buying doctors' practices and surgery and imaging centers. Insurers are buying doctors' practices and specialty pharmacies and sometimes merging with pharmacy chains. Hospitals are buying or creating insurers. Private equity firms are behind many of the deals, buying practices, reorganizing operations, paring costs, then selling at a profit in a few years to a hospital or insurer higher up the healthcare food chain. And while the stated purpose is generally greater efficiency, studies have shown that for patients the net result has been higher prices and no benefit, or worse health outcomes. That's in part because the purchases have been driven by financial efficiency, not more seamless and attentive care, said Soroush Saghafian, an associate professor at Harvard University's Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs. What's more, these transactions occur in a gray zone of competition law, and regulators' tools to examine or stop them are plodding and not up to the task. "Antitrust laws aren't fit for purpose at this point, and the agencies that enforce them are under-resourced," said Zack Cooper, an associate professor of public health and economics at Yale University who has sounded the alarm about the trend. The tools at the agencies' disposal are limited — warning letters, lawsuits, and consent decrees modifying the terms of a merger to restore competition — and often slow to get results. Meanwhile, the dealmaking is galloping ahead. ... Patients like Hug are often directed to a higher-priced location for procedures. They are effectively required to buy from their insurers' specialty or retail pharmacy, which may not stock the drug the doctor prescribes or provide it at the lowest price. ... The Federal Trade Commission and the Justice Department together police mergers in healthcare to protect competition and patient choice. Generally, the FTC oversees hospitals and doctors, while the Justice Department scrutinizes insurers, though their territories overlap and there are gaps. Middlemen like pharmacy benefit managers fall somewhere in between, though in recent years the FTC has taken the lead in this arena. But federal regulators are playing a tough game of catch-up. ... Over the past decade, the number of doctors working for hospitals rather than in private practice has more than doubled. Today 82% of physicians are employed by hospitals, other corporate entities (like insurers), or private equity firms. For example, UnitedHealth Group's then-CEO said in 2024 that it employed around 10,000 primary care physicians. That did not include UnitedHealth's 80,000 "affiliated" physicians. ... Many of these vertical transactions are too small for the regulatory agencies to spot. Under the 1976 Hart-Scott-Rodino Act, mergers valued over a certain dollar threshold set annually — this year it's $133.9 million — must be reported for antitrust scrutiny. Many hospital mergers or insurer mergers exceed the threshold. But mergers involving doctors' practices often do not, leading to consolidation and monopoly by slow accretion. Cooper and his group, the Health Care Affordability Lab, studied hospital acquisitions of physician practices and found that over 99% of the more than 275 deals examined fell below the reporting threshold. "I'm really struggling with this," Cooper said. "What you're talking about is sort of like death by a thousand paper cuts." ... The FTC has brought eight actions or suits against healthcare mergers and acquisitions in President Trump's second term. "The FTC has made healthcare competition one of our top priorities," said Daniel Guarnera, director of the FTC's Bureau of Competition. Nonetheless, he said the agency relied on complaints and news reports to learn about smaller mergers. The Justice Department has brought only two cases, both challenging hospital-insurer contracts rather than mergers. It has also settled a suit brought by the Biden administration that sought to block UnitedHealth's $3.3 billion acquisition of Amedisys, a home healthcare agency. The 2025 settlement required the divestiture of 164 home health and hospice locations across 19 states. ... Guarnera, at the FTC, noted that the agencies' task is to enforce regulations, limiting the challenges they can bring. "Some of the market distortion is caused by regulations that have anticompetitive effects," he said. For example countless health policy experts have proposed regulations mandating "site-neutral payment," a system in which providers would get the same amount for a procedure no matter where it was performed. That would prevent predicaments like Hug's, in which a vertically integrated system effectively backs doctors into directing patients to a more expensive venue for treatment. Within the government, the FTC has advocated for new pro-competitive regulations, suggestions that are now under review by the White House's Office of Management and Budget. They are not public, and Guarnera wouldn't say whether site-neutral payment is included. Meanwhile, the Trump administration in July proposed instituting site-neutral payments for some services for Medicare beneficiaries. ... But with money on the table and business interests governing healthcare, studies have shown that cons of vertical integration — the opportunity for gaming away those beneficial arrangements and raising revenue — prevail. ... When Harvard researchers sought to assess the effect of hospital purchases of gastroenterology physician groups on colonoscopy care, the negative impact was clear. "It changed the way they did business," said Saghafian, the paper's main author. All told, quality went down and prices as well as complication rates rose. "What improves is 'operational throughput,'" or the efficiency with which the system could move patients through colonoscopies fastest with the least staff involvement, Saghafian said. "That's a financial metric." ... In July the FTC reached a settlement in a suit against Caremark, requiring it to be more transparent and give patients and pharmacies more choice. It had previously reached such an agreement with Express Scripts and is working on one with Optum.

headline: Juul can sell updated e-cigarette with age-verification system, FDA says - CBS News
summary_text: # Juul can sell updated e-cigarette with age-verification system, FDA says August 28, 2026 / 6:26 PM EDT / CBS/AP Vaping company Juul Labs on Friday received federal permission to sell an updated version of its e-cigarette, which includes an optional age-verification system designed to prevent underage use. The decision from the Food and Drug Administration allows the company to sell a new version of its top-selling vaping device for the first time since it launched more than a decade ago. In recent years, the company has had to lay off hundreds of employees while paying roughly $3 billion to settle government and private lawsuits over teen use of its products. Juul plans to market the new device under the brand name Juul2, along with updated versions of its tobacco- and menthol-flavored cartridges. In 2019, the company discontinued several flavors, including mango, mint and creme, that drove most of its sales but were favored by teens. In a statement Friday, Juul CEO K.C. Crosthwaite said the company plans to seek authorization for "a portfolio of flavors — beyond tobacco and menthol — that are targeted to adult nicotine consumers." ... The latest announcement is not an approval or endorsement, and people who do not smoke should not use Juul or any other e-cigarettes, according to regulators. The FDA decision means that smokers who switch completely to Juul can reduce their exposure to deadly carcinogens and other chemicals found in traditional cigarettes. According to company studies reviewed by the FDA, between 20% to 50% of smokers who used Juul products were able to stop smoking at the end of six weeks. The rates of quitting varied based on which flavors were used. The FDA says it "considers the risks and benefits to the U.S. population as a whole — including the benefits to adults who currently use tobacco products and switch to a potentially lower-risk product, as well as the risks posed to youth and non-users of tobacco products." "To receive marketing authorizations, the FDA must have sufficient evidence that the new products offer greater benefits to population health than risks," the agency said Friday in a news release announcing the authorization. ... The new device also gives users the option to require age verification via an online app before the e-cigarette can be unlocked. According to Juul Labs, the optional 21-and-up app pairs with the connected device and "provides adult consumers insights into their product use, device location, real-time battery and pod-level information." The app will also allow consumers to "lock" a paired device "to prevent use by others."

headline: Georgia Power gets clearance to serve OpenAI's massive AI data center in Effingham County​ - CBS Atlanta
summary_text: Georgia Power's agreement to supply electricity to OpenAI's massive data center in Effingham County has cleared state regulatory review. The contract calls for Georgia Power to provide up to 3,200 megawatts of electricity to Project Camellia, with service delivered in phases from 2028 through 2032. OpenAI has said the long-term project represents a $20 billion investment. Under Georgia's rules for large data centers, Public Service Commission staff reviewed the agreement and declined to object, allowing it to move forward. The commission did not hold a public vote on the contract. Georgia Power said OpenAI will pay the full cost of the infrastructure needed to serve the facility. OpenAI has also agreed to let the utility company reduce the facility's electricity use by up to 1,000 megawatts when demand on the power grid is high. The utility company now projects that revenue from OpenAI and other large customers could save a typical residential customer using 1,000 kilowatt-hours about $15 a month beginning in 2029. That would amount to $180 annually, up from Georgia Power's previous estimate of $102. "We know every dollar counts," Georgia Power CEO Kim Greene said in a statement. "In December, we committed to $102 a year in savings for the typical family beginning in 2029. Today, that number is expected to be $180." ... The projected savings are not tied solely to OpenAI. Georgia Power said its growing group of data centers, manufacturers and other large electricity users is expected to generate about $950 million in additional annual revenue beginning in 2029. ... OpenAI said Project Camellia will create thousands of construction and permanent jobs, provide $80 million in community benefits and generate hundreds of millions of dollars in state and local taxes. The company plans to use a closed-loop water system and release an independent audit of its commitments each year.

headline: FDA approves new pancreatic cancer drug that could extend patients' lives - CBS News
summary_text: # FDA approves new pancreatic cancer drug that could extend patients' lives Updated on: August 26, 2026 / 8:07 PM EDT / CBS/AP The Food and Drug Administration on Wednesday approved a groundbreaking new drug for advanced pancreatic cancer, offering U.S. patients a more effective treatment against one of the deadliest types of cancer. FDA officials gave expedited approval to the first-of-a-kind pill, called daraxonrasib, which blocks a mutated protein that fuels tumor growth in more than 90% of pancreatic cancer cases. It's an approach that previously eluded drugmakers for decades. The daily pills will be sold by Revolution Medicines under the brand name Rasonque. A one-month supply would cost approximately $39,800, the company announced. Patients taking the drug nearly doubled their survival time, with fewer severe side effects, in a study that randomly assigned them to receive the experimental treatment or more chemotherapy. The company-funded study enrolled 500 patients whose metastatic, or spreading, cancer had quit responding to prior treatment. ... Patients getting the new treatment lived for a median of 13.2 months compared with 6.7 months for chemotherapy recipients. Side effects included skin rash, mouth sores, diarrhea and other digestive issues. "This is one of the most anticipated approvals I can think of," said Dr. Andrew Coveler of the Fred Hutch Cancer Center. "This medicine is not a cure but a significant improvement." ... FDA regulators noted on Wednesday that they approved the drug more than six months ahead of their target date. "It is our fundamental duty to deliver more cures and meaningful treatments to patients as quickly as possible," the FDA's acting commissioner, Kyle Diamantas, said in a statement. ... Doctors who treat pancreatic cancer hope the drug may usher in more new options for other forms of cancer, with scores of experimental drugs in development. "I think this has opened doors for many other companies," said Dr. Pashtoon Kasi of City of Hope Orange County, a California-based cancer center. "Downstream I think there are going to be a lot more trials looking at this approach in other tumor types." ... Revolution Medicines' drug uses what's essentially a molecular glue to bind with multiple KRAS subtypes. The Redwood City, California-based drugmaker is studying its technology for several other forms of cancer, including lung cancer.

headline: Taylor Farms recalls jalapeño products at Walmart and Target over salmonella risk - CBS News
summary_text: # Taylor Farms recalls jalapeño products at Walmart and Target over salmonella risk By Aimee Picchi Aimee Picchi Associate Managing Editor, MoneyWatch Aimee Picchi Updated on: August 10, 2026 / 7:33 PM EDT / CBS News Taylor Farms, the agricultural giant whose lettuce has been linked to the deadly cyclospora outbreak, is recalling several prepared products made with jalapeños amid a salmonella outbreak linked to the peppers. The products, which include pico de gallo salsa and guacamole, were distributed to national retailers, including Walmart and Target, in 26 states, the company said in a statement on Sunday. Taylor Farms said it isn't aware of any reported illnesses linked to the products. Taylor Farms said it voluntarily recalled the prepared foods after Coast Citrus Distributors, which had provided the company with its peppers, recalled its fresh jalapeños due to salmonella concerns. "A grower in Sinaloa, Mexico, that supplies to Coast Citrus Distributors was identified as the potential source in this outbreak," the company said. "Taylor Fresh Foods is no longer sourcing products from this farmer and will be filling orders from alternative suppliers." Salmonella can cause diarrhea, fever and stomach cramps within 8 to 72 hours after exposure, according to the Mayo Clinic, which said most healthy people recover within days to a week without treatment. The products have a "best if used by" date through Aug. 16, Taylor Farms added. ... Walmart said safety is a top priority for the retailer. "When notified of recalls, we move swiftly to remove the impacted products from our stores and implement a sales block at our registers and online," the company told CBS News in a statement. "We are working closely with our supplier, and customers who have this should discontinue use." ... In a statement, Trader Joe's said it is recalling 668 packages of fiesta salad with shrimp because the product contains salsa that may have been prepared with recalled jalapeño peppers. The retailer advised customers to throw out the product or return it to any Trader Joe's location for a refund. Taylor Farms also urged customers to throw away any of the recalled items. "Refunds are available at the location of purchase," it added.

headline: As FDA approves new marketing for nicotine pouches, some doctors sound alarms - CBS News
summary_text: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration authorized marketing of four new flavored nicotine pouch products this week, bringing to 30 the number of such products the FDA has recently greenlit after considering the public health impact. Tuesday's decision on pouches from the brand "on!" is the latest in a series of steps by the Trump administration aimed at boosting this fast-growing sector of the industry. Last week, the White House TikTok account posted a video showcasing the nicotine pouch brand ZYN that included Joint Chiefs Chairman Dan Caine saying the U.S. military consumes "a lot of nicotine." In June, the FDA cleared the way for ZYN to market 20 of its products with the favorable new claim that "Using ZYN instead of cigarettes puts you at a lower risk of mouth cancer, heart disease, lung cancer, stroke, emphysema, and chronic bronchitis." The new labeling, which designates it as a "Modified Risk Tobacco Product," was the first ever granted to a nicotine pouch brand. ... Marketing nicotine pouch flavors like Rich Berry, Cappuccino, Citrus and Cinnamon raises particular concerns for health advocates because of their potential appeal to kids. ... The brands covered by the FDA's orders are manufactured by subsidiaries of two of the world's largest tobacco companies: Philip Morris International, which makes ZYN, and Altria Group, for the "on!" brand. ... Nicotine pouches represent the fastest growing segment of the U.S. tobacco market. Between January 2023 and August 2025, monthly sales skyrocketed by 250%, CDC Foundation analysis found. Philip Morris International recently opened a $1.2 billion nicotine pouch manufacturing plant in Aurora, Colorado. ... According to the World Health Organization, 16 countries have banned the sale of nicotine pouches. ... An FDA spokesperson told CBS News that the government's "modified risk" authorization for ZYN "does not mean these products are safe or risk-free." Instead, the agency says it determined, "based on a rigorous scientific review," that there is evidence the product helps smokers quit cigarettes, so it believes the decision is "appropriate for the protection of the public health under the statutory standard." The FDA continues to warn "there is no safe tobacco product, and those who do not use tobacco products should not start." King emphasized that if pouches initiate new users, "it could jeopardize the considerable public health progress we've made in addressing tobacco product use over the past several decades." ... The FDA is requiring the owner of ZYN to "conduct postmarket surveillance and studies," and its status as a "Modified Risk Tobacco Product" will expire in five years. The FDA wrote, "If at any point the agency determines that, among other things, the continued marketing of the products as MRTPs no longer benefits the health of the population as a whole, such as if there is a significant increase in youth uptake, the agency may withdraw the orders."

headline: "California Forever" loses Saronic's $3B shipyard bid, thousands of jobs to Texas - CBS Sacramento
summary_text: In an economic blow to the billionaire-backed California Forever project, defense technology company Saronic decided to skip the group's proposed Solano Shipyard in Solano County, a location finalist, for its new $3.2B next-generation shipyard. The company decided instead to send the development to Texas. It would have created an estimated 10,000 new jobs in Solano County, which local leaders say has the worst unemployment rate in the Bay Area. Tuesday, the ghost of these jobs became a topic of debate at the county's Board of Supervisors meeting as local residents both in support of and against California Forever's efforts to shore up shipbuilding took to the podium during public comment. ... California Forever plans to create a new city of 400,000 people on Solano County farmland. The group owns undeveloped land equivalent to the size of San Francisco in the county. With it, the group also wants to build what they describe as the nation's largest advanced manufacturing park to be called The Foundry as well as to revitalize shipbuilding through the proposed Solano Shipyard near Collinsville. ... In a statement about the Saronic bid bust, California Forever and its supporters said, "Our coalition's warning about losing the opportunity to Texas has now become reality." They also blamed legislative red tape, which they say forced the company to look outside of California. "A key site selection criterion was the permitting framework to break ground within months, matching the speed required by America's national defense needs, which is not possible in California without special legislation... The coalition worked for months to draft a balanced proposal that would have enabled Saronic to choose California and Solano County. Local and state government leaders did not pass the legislation in time," the statement read. ... Last week, after the news of the lost Saronic bid, the Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development or "GO-Biz" sent a memo to state leaders saying that Solano County is at an economic crossroads and threw its support behind California Forever's efforts to bring in more local jobs. "None of this will happen automatically. Winning this competition will require collaboration among state and local government, labor, business, educational institutions, community organizations, and private investors. It will require thoughtful policy choices, disciplined execution, and a shared commitment to creating lasting public benefit," said GO-Biz director Dee Dee Myers."...GO-Biz believes the Solano Shipyard and Solano Foundry represent projects of statewide significance and the kind of transformational opportunity California should fight for and win."

Ellison acknowledged that operational efficiencies exist, but the executives did not specify whether the two networks would consolidate any newsgathering or other functions. CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss and CNN leader Mark Thompson are to continue leading their respective organizations.

headline: CNN now has a new owner. What will the future of the network be under Skydance?
summary_text: The article examines the implications of Skydance’s completed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, which places CBS News and CNN under common ownership. It reports that CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss and CNN chief Mark Thompson will remain in their roles, while the company has pledged editorial independence. A settlement with states challenging the deal requires Skydance to form a five-member News Editorial Independence Board within 180 days to establish editorial principles, address certain disputes, and monitor journalistic standards. The piece notes that how the combined ownership will affect the news organizations over time remains uncertain.

headline: CBS News Sued for $20 Million Over Report Linking Teen to Reflecting Pool Vandalism
summary_text: [CBS News: party] CBS News Sued for $ 20 Million Over Report Linking Teen to Reflecting Pool Vandalism. Getting your Trinity Audio player ready…. A 15-year-old Maryland teenager is suing CBS News for more than $ 20 million, alleging the network falsely portrayed him as a suspect in the vandalism of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in a report it later retracted. The complaint, filed Wednesday in federal court in Washington, D.C., accuses CBS Broadcasting and CBS Interactive of defamation and invasion of privacy through false-light publicity after footage of the teenager being handcuffed aired alongside a report about vandalism arrests. Although CBS later retracted the report, the teenager alleges the correction failed to undo the damage to his reputation.

headline: Paramount Settles Antitrust Lawsuit over WBD Merger
summary_text: [CBS News: party] Paramount has reached a settlement with a coalition of 12 attorneys general that would resolve the states' antitrust lawsuit alleging that the $ 111 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery (Warner Bros.) would harm competition by lowering output and raising prices, hurting both workers and consumers in the process. Separately the writers unions announced a settlement with Paramount that will prevent writer layoffs at CBS News for five years. The settlement, which still must be approved by the court, includes a five-year court enforceable commitment to increase film output, a minimum of an additional $ 1.5 billion commitment to bolster domestic film production, a $ 47.5 million fund for workers who are impacted by the merger, and restrictions on how the company handles cable negotiations to help keep prices competitive. In the wake of the settlement, Paramount is likely to move as quickly as possible to close the deal because it had promised to pay $ 7 million a day to shareholders if the merger did n't close by Oct. 1.

headline: Read the '60 Minutes' Memo Sent to Staff Ahead of Season Premiere Under New Leadership
summary_text: [CBS News: organization] CBS News leadership sent a memo to rally "60 Minutes" staffers Sunday morning, hours ahead of the program's high-pressure Season 59 premiere. In the memo, obtained by TheWrap, CBS News president Tom Cibrowski, CBS News editor in chief Bari Weiss and her newly appointed "60 Minutes" executive producer Nick Bilton touted the day as a "big moment for '60 Minutes' and CBS ." The letter also highlighted stories to be featured in the season premiere, including an "interview everyone's been chasing ," as well as segments on an unnamed NFL coach and AI. A representative for CBS News did not immediately respond to TheWrap's request for comment. Sunday's premiere comes after months of overhaul to "60 Minutes" staff and the installation of new leadership at the program.

headline: The Clock Is Ticking to Pull Off an Entirely New '60 Minutes'
summary_text: [CBS News: organization] CBS News, led by editor-in-chief Bari Weiss, needs the new 60 Minutes to work. Its success or its failure could define her tenure at the network. The overhaul was the talk of the business earlier this summer, with its EP and a slew of senior producers exiting, and high-profile correspondents choosing to exit (Anderson Cooper) or unceremoniously shown the door (Scott Pelley, Sharyn Alfonsi, Cecilia Vega) . 60 Minutes is the most-watched news program in America, and if it slipped and lost that title in the wake of the overhaul, it would be an embarrassment to the news division. That may be why CBS is playing it so safe as it prepares to debut its new season this Sunday.

The partnership, dubbed "CBS Sunday Morning At 92NY" will kick off Sep. 28 with correspondent Tracy Smith in conversation with Sylvester Stallone. The day before, Stallone will be interviewed by Smith on CBS Sunday Morning. According to Rand Morrison, the executive producer of CBS Sunday Morning, the series will focus on actors, musician, politicians and others that can speak to the audiences of both the morning newsmagazine, and the Y's loyal attendees. " There's a lot in common with the Sunday Morning viewership and the kinds of people who are interested in the live events at the 92nd Street Y ," says Morrison, in an interview with THR.

headline: Deloitte launches AI M&A platform used in 1,000 deals
summary_text: Del ... launches AI ... in ... 1,0 ... deals ... # Deloitte launches AI M&A platform used in 1,000 deals Mon, 28th Sep 2026 KAREN JOY BACUDO Finance Editor Deloitte has launched an AI-enabled M&A platform already used in more than 1,000 client engagements. The platform is designed for organisations handling mergers and acquisitions, supporting work across the deal lifecycle from strategy and due diligence to transaction structuring and post-deal integration. It combines AI tools with an agentic framework intended to help teams manage and oversee AI agents involved in deal processes. The launch reflects a broader push by professional services firms to embed AI more deeply into advisory work, particularly in corporate transactions, where speed, data analysis and coordination across specialist teams can shape deal outcomes. Deloitte is positioning the product as a way to bring together tax, technology and financial workstreams in a single operating environment. ... Survey findings Alongside the launch, Deloitte highlighted findings from a survey of 500 corporate and private equity leaders on the use of generative AI in mergers and acquisitions. The results suggest AI has moved beyond experimentation in this part of the market, with 90% of respondents saying they use it in some form. More than a third of dealmakers, or 37%, said they use AI across multiple stages of the M&A lifecycle. The survey also found that 35% of M&A leaders saw the greatest value in combining technology with advisory support, more than three times the share that pointed to value from individual task-specific tools. Respondents also reported operational gains from AI use. Automated status reporting was cited by 66% of those surveyed, while 60% pointed to better decision-making and 51% said AI had improved cross-functional coordination. ... Deloitte said the platform was built for the confidentiality and complexity of transactions. It is designed to protect and ringfence client and deal data, and was developed by M&A professionals with experience in target, transaction and diligence information. The product is being made available through Ascend, Deloitte's service delivery platform, giving clients different ways to use M&A-focused AI tools within a controlled environment. ... Deloitte also framed the launch as part of a wider effort to combine human advisers with AI tools rather than replace one with the other. That approach mirrors a broader pattern in professional services, where firms have stressed oversight and judgement as they introduce AI into regulated or high-stakes client work.

headline: Deloitte unveils new framework to quantify sustainability’s business value | Today News
summary_text: Deloitte ... business ... ## As investors and consumers increasingly demand measurable returns from ESG initiatives, Deloitte has introduced a framework that helps companies assess both the tangible and intangible value of sustainability investments, from improved competitiveness to stronger financial performance. Staff Writer Published 7 Aug 2026, 10:30 AM IST Shubhranshu Patnaik, Partner and G&PS Industry Leader, Deloitte South Asia (left) and Shailesh Tyagi, Partner & Leader, Climate Change & Sustainability, Strategy Risk & Transactions, Deloitte India, unveiling the report titled The RoI of Responsibility(Mint) For years, corporate sustainability has largely been viewed through the lens of regulatory compliance. Companies focused on meeting disclosure requirements, adhering to environmental standards and keeping pace with evolving regulations. But that approach is no longer enough. Investors, customers and boards are increasingly demanding a clearer answer to a fundamental question: What business value does sustainability create? That was the central message of The RoI of Responsibility, a new framework unveiled by Deloitte at the Mint Sustainability Summit. The framework argues that companies need to move beyond treating sustainability as a compliance exercise and instead evaluate it as a driver of long-term enterprise value. According to Shubhranshu Patnaik, partner and G&PS industry leader at Deloitte South Asia, existing sustainability frameworks have done a good job of measuring compliance but have fallen short of capturing the broader financial and strategic returns from sustainability investments. As a result, many companies continue to evaluate ESG initiatives primarily through the lens of short-term costs rather than long-term value creation. ... Hidden returns ... Deloitte's proposed framework seeks to change that by identifying both tangible and intangible value drivers. While businesses already account for measurable benefits such as energy savings, operational efficiencies and regulatory compliance, they often overlook less visible gains, including improved access to global markets, a lower cost of capital, stronger customer loyalty, higher employee retention and greater brand value. Many of these benefits materialize over several years and therefore do not feature prominently in conventional investment decisions. Yet they can have a significant impact on enterprise value, Patnaik said. ... ## Long view The framework also encourages companies to broaden their planning horizon. Instead of responding only to current regulations, businesses should assess emerging risks and opportunities over the next five to 10 years, including future climate regulations, changing customer expectations, shifting investor preferences, supply-chain disruptions and workforce trends. Scenario planning should become a central part of sustainability strategy, Patnaik said, allowing companies to evaluate multiple future outcomes rather than relying on a single regulatory or market forecast. Once these external triggers are identified, organisations can determine the ESG issues that are most material to their business—whether related to energy, water, carbon emissions, waste or supply-chain resilience—and link them directly to financial outcomes such as revenue growth, lower financing costs, avoided losses, improved cash flows and enhanced enterprise value. ... recognised ... . ... headline: Bloomberg Taps Allium to Bring Onchain Stablecoin Data to its Terminal
summary_text: [Bloomberg: organization] Bloomberg launched a stablecoin dashboard on its Terminal Wednesday, giving financial professionals direct access to onchain data on stablecoin supply, issuance and transaction activity. Terminal users can compare stablecoins by supply, mints, burns, transfer volume and velocity, and break activity down by blockchain network and peg type, including those backed by fiat currencies and commodities. Most tools can retrieve data points. Fewer can tell an agent what that data point means, how it was calculated, or whether it's the right one for the task at hand. Bloomberg Enterprise MCP is built to close that gap, combining semantic context, AI-ready metadata, and workflow - focused Skills that will give agents the information they need to interpret results correctly and act on them with confidence, across research, portfolio, risk, and operations.

headline: Earnings call transcript: ALPEK lifts 2026 outlook in Q3 2026 as stock falls By Investing.com
summary_text: ALPEK said third-quarter 2026 comparable EBITDA doubled from a year earlier to $276 million and it raised its full-year outlook, but the stock fell 4.72% to $15.56 after the call. The shares closed at $16.33 before the decline, leaving them near the top of their 52-week range of $8.07 to $16.62. The company did not provide actual EPS or revenue figures in the available data, but management said operating performance remained strong even as quarterly cash flow was held back by a large working-capital build. ## Key Takeaways - Comparable EBITDA rose 100% year over year to $276 million, though it fell 18% from the second quarter. - Reported EBITDA reached $303 million, up 161% from a year earlier, helped by a $27 million inventory adjustment. - ALPEK lifted full-year 2026 comparable EBITDA guidance to $990 million from a prior implied $950 million. - Leverage improved to 1.8x from 2.2x, moving below the company’s target range of 2.0x to 2.5x. - Free cash flow was limited in the quarter by a $226 million investment in net working capital as raw material prices rose. ... ## Company Performance ALPEK posted a solid third quarter, supported by stronger margins, stable volumes and a better product mix. Volume totaled 1.17 million tons, flat from the prior quarter and up 4% from a year earlier. Management said the increase was driven more by market share gains from imports than by broad demand growth. The company’s largest business, Polyester, generated comparable EBITDA of $205 million, up 134% year over year. Plastics & Chemicals posted comparable EBITDA of $62 million, up 32% year over year. The smaller Others/Emerging Business segment contributed $9 million. The results reflected a favorable market backdrop, especially for regional suppliers. Higher freight rates and supply disruptions continued to support ALPEK’s local-for-local model in the Americas. At the same time, the quarter showed some normalization from the stronger second quarter, with comparable EBITDA down sequentially. ... ## Financial Highlights - Comparable EBITDA: $276 million, up 100% year over year and down 18% sequentially. - Reported EBITDA: $303 million, up 161% year over year. - Volume: 1.17 million tons, flat sequentially and up 4% year over year. - Polyester comparable EBITDA: $205 million, up 134% year over year. - Plastics & Chemicals comparable EBITDA: $62 million, up 32% year over year. - Operating free cash flow: $5 million, pressured by working-capital needs. - Net working capital investment: $226 million, driven mainly by higher raw material prices. - Capital expenditures: $46 million, including $30 million in strategic spending. - Net debt: $1.72 billion, up 3% from the prior quarter. - Leverage ratio: 1.8x, down from 2.2x and below the target range. - Market capitalization: $1.75 billion - P/E ratio: 50.6, though the PEG ratio of 0.37 suggests attractive valuation relative to growth - Free cash flow yield: 23%, indicating strong cash generation potential ... ## Outlook & Guidance ALPEK raised its full-year 2026 comparable EBITDA guidance to $990 million. Management said the outlook assumes Chinese PET reference margins of $225 per ton for the rest of the year, polypropylene margins of $0.17 per pound and South America freight rates of $200 per ton. The company kept its full-year operating free cash flow guidance at $300 million to $350 million and expects net debt reduction of $200 million to $250 million by year-end. Management also said normalized annual capital expenditures should stay below $200 million. Looking further ahead, the company expects 2027 to be a strong volume year, with margins still above 2025 levels but likely below 2026 peaks. Detailed 2027 guidance will be given in February 2027. For investors seeking deeper analysis, ALPEK is one of over 1,400 US equities covered by InvestingPro’s comprehensive Pro Research Reports, which transform complex financial data into clear, actionable intelligence through intuitive visuals and expert analysis. ... ## Risks and Challenges - Working-capital volatility: Higher raw material prices can absorb cash and delay free-cash-flow conversion. - Margin normalization: Management expects some moderation from 2026 levels in 2027, which could pressure earnings growth. - Freight-rate swings: ALPEK benefits from high freight rates, but a sharp decline could reduce its pricing advantage. - Geopolitical uncertainty: The company’s market backdrop depends partly on supply disruptions and trade conditions that can change quickly. - Execution risk on growth projects: The company is investing in higher-margin products and new capacity, which must deliver returns to support the strategy. ... dividends. Management said ... reduction remains the top priority and that dividend discussions may begin in ... first quarter of 202 ... , after ... year results are reviewed. ... Jorge Young, CEO, ALPEK: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. During the third quarter, our teams once again delivered strong execution, responding quickly to evolving customer needs and maintaining high operating rates. Our focus on operational efficiency, commercial agility, and supply chain flexibility enabled us to adapt to market conditions, resulting in another exceptional quarter. As a result, we outperformed our comparable EBITDA expectations for the quarter. Building on our year-to-date performance and updated outlook for the last quarter of 2026, we are again raising our full-year guidance, which I will discuss in more detail later in the call. Our leverage ratio improved to 1.8 times, primarily reflecting higher last 12 months EBITDA. Our local-for-local production strategy and constant pursuit to strengthen our competitive position continue to be fundamental pillars for ALPEK’s success. ... Our global footprint and regional approach to key markets, including the U.S., Mexico, Brazil, among others, has enabled us to provide reliable long-term supply and service to our customers as a domestic supplier of choice. This has been particularly important amid continued global trade disruptions and raw material shortages, mainly in Asia, as the conflict in the Middle East extends. PET resin in Asia is facing reduced availability of key feedstocks and lower operating rates, supporting reference margins above our original expectations. In parallel, elevated ocean freight rates have made imports less competitive, further benefiting regional suppliers like ALPEK. These dynamics reinforce the importance of the action we have taken over the last several years to make our company more competitive and resilient. Our performance reflects the progress we have made in executing ALPEK’s long-term strategy. ... Over the past few years, we have taken deliberate actions to reinforce our competitiveness, improve the quality of our portfolio, and reinforce our financial position. Let me highlight some of the initiatives underway across our two strategic pillars and financial flexibility. First, strengthening our core business. We have continued to optimize our global footprint, directing production towards our most competitive and integrated facilities while improving cost efficiency. Since 2023, we have reduced installed capacity by 15%, including fibers capacity, and headcount by 29%, while maintaining similar volume levels. This demonstrates the effectiveness of our leaner operating model. At the same time, we continue identifying opportunities to further improve performance within the organization. Earlier this month, we hosted our annual innovation awards, where teams from across ALPEK presented projects to our executive team. This will focus on cost reductions, product improvements, business integrations, et cetera. We currently have more than 40 projects requiring minimal or no CapEx, representing over $20 million of potential incremental EBITDA. These projects reflect a culture of continuous improvement throughout the organization. Second pillar, growing and evolving our product portfolio. We are selectively investing in differentiated applications and differentiated products that offer higher margins. Key initiatives include expanding our thermoforming capacity in Saudi Arabia, increasing our copolymer production in our polypropylene business, and venturing into expandable polystyrene extrusion in North America. These investments, among several others in our pipeline, support a more resilient portfolio over the long term. We are also pursuing capital-efficient growth opportunities by leveraging our assets, capabilities, and customers’ relationships to unlock incremental value. As an example, in our energy commercialization business, we continue expanding into the electricity sector in Mexico and have begun supplying natural gas in Brazil. Third, financial flexibility is a key enabler of our strategy. ... Even though our leverage level is now below 2.0 times, our focus remains on generating cash flow and further reducing debt. This includes net working capital management, disciplined CapEx, and progressing asset monetization. These actions support our objective of maintaining a strong balance sheet while preserving financial flexibility to pursue attractive growth opportunities as they arise. With that, I will turn the call over to Rodrigo to discuss our financial results in greater detail. ... Rodrigo Prieto, CFO, ALPEK: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Let me go into our third-quarter results. Market conditions remain supportive, although PET spreads moderated from second-quarter peaks. Average Chinese integrated PET reference margins were $213 per ton, down 31% sequentially, yet still 59% above 2025 levels. Ocean freight rates to South America also remained elevated, averaging $321 per ton, up 43% quarter-on-quarter and 74% year-over-year. Taking a look at our earnings, comparable EBITDA totaled $276 million, down 18% quarter-on-quarter, yet doubling when compared to the same period last year. Reported EBITDA also saw a significant year-over-year improvement of 161%, totaling $303 million. These included a $27 million inventory adjustment primarily associated with higher raw material prices. Looking at our business segments, Polyester achieved a comparable EBITDA of $205 million, increasing 134% year-over-year. Plastics & Chemicals delivered comparable EBITDA of $62 million, 32% above the prior year. The remaining $9 million comes from the Others or Emerging Business segment, primarily consisting of our energy commercialization. Turning to free cash flow, ALPEK generated $5 million in operating free cash flow as higher reported EBITDA was offset by a larger than anticipated investment of $226 million in net working capital, driven mainly by higher pricing environment, particularly paraxylene, reaching multi-year highs. CapEx totaled $46 million, including $30 million in strategic CapEx. ... During the quarter, net debt increased 3% to $1.72 billion, primarily reflecting the investment in net working capital and, to a lesser extent, payments to minority shareholders. At the same time, our leverage ratio improved to 1.8 times from 2.2 times, primarily driven by higher last 12 months EBITDA and now below our target range of 2 to 2.5 times. Year to date, we have generated $222 million in operating free cash flow and reduced our net debt by $123 million. Our improved leverage position reflects the progress we have made in strengthening our balance sheet and reinforces our commitment to financial discipline. Looking ahead, we expect to further reduce net debt in the fourth quarter through continued cash generation, disciplined capital allocation, and debt prepayments. I’d also like to highlight the important milestone for ALPEK. ... Jorge Young, CEO, ALPEK: As we look to the remainder of the year, we’re expecting PET reference margins and ocean freights to moderate while remaining well above 2025 levels. Based on our year-to-date performance and updated market assumptions, we’re again raising our full-year 2026 guidance. Our key assumptions for the remaining months are Chinese PET reference margins at $225 per ton, polypropylene reference margins at $0.17 per pound, and ocean freights to South America at $200 per ton. On this basis, we are raising our comparable EBITDA to $990 million. For 2026, we continue to expect operating free cash flow in the range of $300 million-$350 million, and net debt reduction between $200 million and $250 million by year-end. This is considering some moderation in the raw material pricing environment. This continued focus on cash generation and deleveraging will further enhance our financial flexibility, supporting disciplined capital allocation and selective investment in future growth opportunities. The remaining guidance figures are unchanged. As a reminder, our guidance does not include potential upside from non-strategic asset sales. As we approach 2027, the actions we have taken to optimize our footprint, improve efficiency, and to strengthen our financial position have made ALPEK more competitive and better positioned to navigate changing market conditions. Our long-term strategy remains focused on leveraging our global capabilities and footprint to deliver consistent operational performance while reinforcing our position as a reliable domestic supplier. While industry conditions will continue to evolve, our priorities remain clear. We will continue focusing on reliable operations, serving our customers, managing costs, and allocating capital with discipline. ... headline: Alpek sale de pérdidas tras ganar 259,8 millones hasta septiembre y mejora previsiones - Infobae
summary_text: La petroquímica mexicana Alpek obtuvo unos beneficios netos atribuidos de 5.446 millones de pesos (259,8 millones de euros) hasta septiembre, lo que le permitió mejorar previsiones tras abandonar los 'números rojos' de 1.209 millones de pesos (57,7 millones de euros) de hace doce meses. Los ingresos ascendieron a 104.834 millones de pesos (5.001 millones de euros), un 6% más, de los que 37.565 millones de pesos (1.792 millones de euros) procedieron de México y 67.269 millones de pesos (3.209 millones de euros) del extranjero. De su lado, el sumatorio de gastos de actividad, operaciones y otros conceptos se redujo un 2,4%, hasta los 94.517 millones de pesos (4.509 millones de euros), mientras que el resultado bruto de explotación (Ebitda) se duplicó (122,3%), hasta los 15.166 millones de pesos (723,5 millones de euros). Las ganancias del tercer trimestre se situaron en los 2.421 millones de pesos (115,5 millones de euros) frente al saldo negativo de 807 millones pesos (38,5 millones de euros) del mismo periodo de 2025. La facturación avanzó un 21% y cerró en los 37.589 millones de pesos (1.793 millones de euros). "Alpek logró resultados muy sólidos en el tercer trimestre, reflejando una ejecución disciplinada y la continuidad de condiciones de mercado favorables, particularmente en nuestro segmento de poliéster", ha afirmado el director general de Alpek, Jorge Young. PREVISIONES Alpek ha revisado al alza sus previsiones para 2026 de Ebitda comparable hasta los 990 millones de dólares (884,5 millones de euros) desde el rango previo de 750 a 800 millones de dólares (670,1 y 714,8 millones de euros). Sin embargo, ha mantenido sin cambios la cifra del volumen de producción en los 4,6 millones de toneladas, el gasto de capital (capex) en los 150 millones de dólares (134 millones de euros) y el 'cash flow' operativo entre los 300 y 350 millones de dólares (268 y 312,7 millones de euros). "Se espera que los márgenes de PET [tereftalato de polietileno] y los costos de flete marítimo se moderen gradualmente hacia el cierre del año, en línea con la estacionalidad típica del cuarto trimestre, manteniéndose por encima de las expectativas iniciales establecidas durante el segundo trimestre", ha explicado la empresa en su hoja de resultados.

headline: Alpek has signed to buy Carpenter's loss-making Estonian foam converter | M&A Radar
summary_text: ## Alpek has signed to buy Carpenter's loss-making Estonian foam converter Estonia's Competition Authority published on 9 October 2026 a merger notification under which Alpek OÜ plans to acquire sole control of Carpenter Engineered Foams OÜ. According to the non-confidential summary, Alpek and the Finnish Carpenter Engineered Foams Oy have signed a share purchase agreement for 100% of the Estonian company, which has no subsidiaries. Third parties have seven days to comment. Both companies import polyurethane foam in blocks, convert it — sheet, vertical, CNC contour and profile cutting — and sell the converted products mainly to Estonian customers; their overlap is foam conversion and wholesale of converted products in Estonia. Carpenter Estonia stopped pouring foam blocks in summer 2025 and now only converts imported foam. The filing states that Alpek's foam unit has been loss-making since 2024 and that Carpenter's Estonian operation remained loss-making after production was closed. Carpenter is divesting as part of integrating the specialty foams business it acquired from Recticel in 2023. The price was not disclosed. Our take The filing is unusually candid: both sides are losing money in Estonian foam conversion, and the buyer describes the deal as a way to secure the 'long-term sustainability and survival' of the activity in Estonia. This is consolidation for capacity utilisation, not for growth — two half-loaded cutting operations become one. The realistic buyer of a sub-scale industrial processor is often the direct local competitor, and the seller here is a group that bought the business as part of a larger carve-out and now has no reason to keep a small loss-maker.

headline: Koch Technology Solutions and Alpek Sign License Agreement for PTA Steam Reduction Retrofit in Brazil - Koch Technology Solutions
summary_text: # Koch Technology Solutions and Alpek Sign License Agreement for PTA Steam Reduction Retrofit in Brazil October 8, 2026 KTS technology to support energy efficiency and competitiveness at Alpek’s Suape PTA facility. Koch Technology Solutions (KTS), the technology licensing business of Koch Engineered Solutions, today announced that Alpek Polyester Pernambuco S.A. has signed a license agreement with KTS for an energy efficiency retrofit at its purified terephthalic acid (PTA) facility in Suape, Brazil.
