headline: IFA 2026: Haier Intelligent Home Understands You Before You Ask - Haier Europe
summary_text: At IFA 2026, Haier Europe presents an advanced vision of intelligent living. An interconnected ecosystem that works in the background to improve home management and expand people’s possibilities. In the “ Home of Intelligent Possibilities”, Artificial Intelligence, product innovation, design and services blend naturally into everyday life, understand context and adapt to individual needs, turning small daily challenges into greater control, autonomy and empowerment. ... “Our aim is to make innovation increasingly natural and unobtrusive, allowing technology to observe, understand, learn and step in when needed, without requiring people to constantly act proactively”, says Neil Tunstall, CEO of Haier Europe. “AI creates value when it addresses real needs and turns them into practical, intuitive solutions. This is a long-term vision, underpinned by an equally tangible commitment. Over the next five years, Haier will invest around 13 billion Euros in strategic technology areas, including Artificial Intelligence, innovation and IoT. At IFA 2026, we want to show how this approach is already taking shape and how it can open new possibilities for people, both within and beyond the home.” ... Across these solutions, the hOn App acts as the connective layer of the ecosystem, bringing products and services together in a single digital environment and extending the intelligence built into each appliance. By enabling people to monitor and manage their appliances remotely, coordinate activities across different areas of the home, and support Smart Energy Management by optimising energy use across connected appliances according to the availability of renewable energy, including solar production, hOn makes connected living more intuitive, accessible and efficient, while providing personalised guidance and support and helping people make better use of time and energy. ... In garment care, Haier Vision 15 washing machines feature AI Vision Sense: an internal camera capable of detecting key information to enable more informed cycle management, including the size of the load, the colours of garments, foam levels, and any items forgotten or trapped in the drum. It operates alongside the AI Power Sense System, an integrated ecosystem of nine sensors that detects parameters including load weight and balance, water level and temperature, adjusting cycle settings accordingly. The same focus on care and individual needs translates into an advanced concept of flexibility: after creating a new segment in laundry with Candy MultiWash, the washing machine with three independent drums unveiled in Berlin last year, the company continues to develop this paradigm with the Haier Multi Care Collection. The range introduces a broad selection of multi-drum models, including the Multi Care Laundry Studio which combines four drums in a single architecture, allowing different washing and drying needs to be managed simultaneously. The concept therefore evolves from simply separating loads to providing complete control over garment care. ... In refrigeration, Haier confirms its pioneering role in the sector with Maestro, a prototype that brings together the brand’s most advanced preservation technologies within a single architecture. Among its most emblematic innovations, AI Defrost Zone uses intelligent sensors and Haier’s proprietary technology to defrost food gently, helping prevent juice loss and preserve texture and nutritional value. The Haier Horizon Collection evolves with Hydro Hub, which combines the AI Food Care System for food recognition and storage guidance with an advanced beverage experience. For Haier, food preservation is not only a product feature, but also a tangible company’s broad commitment to tackling food waste, which translates into support for Tafel Deutschland, the major German charitable network dedicated to recovering and redistributing surplus food. ... Haier sees the kitchen as a complete, connected environment in which different technologies work together to respond to different needs, habits and cooking styles. The ID Ultimate Series 6 oven uses AI Vision to recognise food, monitor its preparation and automatically stop cooking once the selected result has been achieved. Pure Flavour Steam combines 100% steam cooking with combination programmes. Completing the offer is Aura Collection, characterised by Aura Grey, a distinctive colour applied to glass surfaces through a specific treatment that creates its characteristic shade and finish while also providing anti-fingerprint properties. ... In the dishwasher segment, the Haier I-Pro Shine A-70% features intelligent sensors that detect the load, soil level and temperature, analyse the contents of the tub and automatically select the most suitable and efficient cycle. Candy PureWash introduces the 4DFlexWash system, a special spray arm that adjusts the distribution and intensity of water according to the level of soil detected, delivering more flexible and targeted cleaning. ... I ... The same ability to combine technology, performance and ease of use also extends to Haier’s small domestic appliances. In floorcare, the I-Pro Clean Series 5 range features the Double Roller System, which ensures fast and effective cleaning, while the Kitchen Small Domestic Appliances category introduces the I-Master Specialty Coffee Machine Series 5, which adjusts temperature, water quantity and extraction parameters for each kind of coffee, while progressively learning the user’s preferences to deliver consistently personalised results. ... Haier’s ability to respond to different needs stems from an approach to innovation that extends beyond the product and across the entire value chain. Innovative, integrated technologies support the company throughout a journey that begins by listening to people and observing real life, accelerates Research & Development, makes manufacturing and operations more flexible and efficient, and continues through to services and after-sales support. The same approach extends to manufacturing and the supply chain, where AI helps improve planning, quality control and operational efficiency, while integration with sustainability-focused technologies and intelligent manufacturing paves the way for increasingly efficient processes and new models of energy optimisation. The journey also continues after purchase: large language models, multimodal systems and predictive tools enable a shift towards more proactive support, capable of simplifying interactions, anticipating potential issues and providing faster responses. The hOn App acts as the digital connector of this intelligent ecosystem, bringing products, services and experiences together within a single digital environment. It enables more seamless interactions with appliances, helping people make the most of their technologies while supporting a more personalised and efficient home experience. The result is a consistent model across the entire value chain: listening, accelerating innovation and supporting people throughout their experience with the product and the brand.

headline: Haier Launches 10-Billion-Baht Air-Conditioner Plant in Chon Buri in Bid to Lead ASEAN Market - Thai Times
summary_text: # Haier Launches 10-Billion-Baht Air-Conditioner Plant in Chon Buri in Bid to Lead ASEAN Market First phase opens with annual capacity of three million units; expansion to six million units by 2027 with strong export focus Haier, the Chinese appliance giant, has inaugurated a 10-billion-baht air-conditioner manufacturing plant in Chon Buri, Thailand, located in the WHA Eastern Seaboard Industrial Estate 3. The facility spans 324,000 square metres. The first phase is launching this month with a production capacity of three million units per year. Expansion plans foresee output rising to 3.5 million units in 2026 and six million units annually by 2027. Zhou Yunjie, Chairman of Haier Group, emphasised that this “major investment reflects the company’s confidence in the Thai economy,” with the plant intended to serve both domestic and global demand. The plant is Haier’s second in Thailand: the existing facility in Kabin Buri, Prachin Buri province produces refrigerators and air conditioners. Haier expects to generate around 3,000 jobs with the new plant. For the domestic market, the company will continue an aggressive distribution strategy to cover every segment. Exports are projected to the European Union, North America and Middle East markets, which are expected to become the top external markets for the plant’s output once full capacity is reached. In financial forecasts, Haier anticipates Thailand sales of 5.5 billion baht for household air conditioners this year, and 1.1 billion baht for commercial units. The investment also celebrates enhanced Thai-Chinese cooperation, coinciding with the fiftieth anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two nations. The plant is set to become a strategic production base in Southeast Asia for Haier, reinforcing its role in regional supply chains and supporting Thailand’s industrial policy agenda to attract high-value foreign investment and enhance export capacity.

headline: Haier, China's Other Appliance Giants See Earnings Drop on Higher Costs, Weaker Demand, and Geopolitical Risks
summary_text: (Yicai) Aug. 28 -- Leading Chinese home appliance manufacturers Haier Smart Home, Supor and Robam Appliances all reported declines in both profit and revenue in the first six months, with the sharpest drop in profit approaching 20 percent, amid escalating costs and other pressures, including the conflict in the Middle East. Haier Smart Home, a subsidiary of home appliance giant Haier Group, posted a 14.2 percent drop in net profit in the six months ended June 30 from the year before to CNY10.3 billion (USD1.5 billion), while operating revenue edged down 2.8 percent to CNY152.1 billion (USD22.6 billion), according to the Qingdao-based company’s semi-annual report. The appreciation of the Chinese yuan resulted in a foreign exchange loss of CNY704 million (USD100 million), compared with a CNY882 million (USD131 million) foreign-exchange gain in the same period last year. ... Kitchen appliance maker Supor’s net profit tumbled 7.7 percent over the period to CNY868 million (USD129 million) while revenue dipped 0.6 percent to CNY11.4 billion (USD1.7 billion). The decline in profit was primarily due to a weaker export business and rising raw material costs, the Hangzhou-based firm said. Lower market interest rates also led to a decrease in returns on its monetary funds. ... The kitchen appliance manufacturer’s first-half performance was mainly affected by the scaling back of government subsidies for consumer purchases and continued pressure in the real estate market, the Hangzhou-based company said. Retail sales across China’s home appliance sector, excluding consumer electronics, slumped 9.9 percent in the first half from a year earlier to CNY425 billion (USD63.2 billion), according to industry research website All View Cloud. Overseas markets were also affected by geopolitical developments, including the conflict in the Middle East, resulting in regional disparities in the global home appliance market. At the same time, high prices of raw materials such as copper and plastics, along with the appreciation of the yuan, have added to companies’ operating pressures. ... China is expected to enter a household replacement cycle between 2029 and 2030, Guo Meide, president of AVC, told Yicai. The industry could focus on specific household-use scenarios, including air and energy management, leisure and entertainment and household cleaning.

Retail value shares for both categories exceeded 40% online and offline, while the Company’s overall retail value share increased by 1.5 percentage points offline and 3.1 percentage points online. In local-currency terms, revenue in India and Pakistan grew by more than 20% and 30%, respectively. ... Following the integration of residential air conditioning, Smart Building Solutions and water solutions at the end of 2025, shared customer and channel resources added 245 touchpoints for Smart Building Solutions, while greater product-platform sharing reduced the number of related SKUs by 18%. Integration across technology, products and channels also progressed at Kwikot, whose share of South Africa’s water-heater market has increased by 10 percentage points since acquisition. headline: Haier nâng công suất nhà máy Thái Lan lên 6 triệu máy lạnh mỗi năm, mở rộng xuất khẩu sang Việt Nam - Forbes Việt Nam
summary_text: Nhu cầu điều hòa dân dụng tại Đông Nam Á được dự báo tăng gấp ba lần vào năm 2035. Trước xu hướng này, Haier đang nâng cấp nhà máy tại tỉnh Chonburi, đưa Thái Lan trở thành một trong những cứ điểm sản xuất chiến lược, với công suất tối đa 6 triệu máy mỗi năm phục vụ cả thị trường nội địa và xuất khẩu, trong đó có Việt Nam. Nhà máy điều hòa thông minh của Haier tại tỉnh Chonburi, Thái Lan. Cơ sở này có công suất tối đa 6 triệu máy mỗi năm, phục vụ thị trường nội địa và xuất khẩu sang nhiều quốc gia, trong đó có Việt Nam. Hình ảnh: Haier. Haier đang đẩy mạnh vai trò của Thái Lan như một cứ điểm sản xuất điều hòa không khí, nhằm đáp ứng nhu cầu làm mát ngày càng tăng tại châu Á và nhiều thị trường trên thế giới. Tập đoàn đồng thời nâng cấp nhà máy điều hòa thông minh tại tỉnh Chonburi, có diện tích hơn 202 rai, tương đương khoảng 32 ha, với công suất tối đa 6 triệu máy mỗi năm. Nhà máy ứng dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo và tự động hóa, kết nối các công đoạn theo mô hình sản xuất thông minh và sản xuất xanh, nhằm nâng cao hiệu suất, tăng tính linh hoạt và đáp ứng đồng thời nhu cầu trong nước lẫn xuất khẩu. Qua đó, Thái Lan ngày càng giữ vai trò quan trọng hơn trong chuỗi cung ứng toàn cầu của Haier. ... Haier đang tiếp tục nâng cấp nhà máy Chonburi để đáp ứng sản lượng ngày càng cao, đồng thời đưa AI và các hệ thống tự động hóa vào nhiều công đoạn hơn nhằm nâng hiệu suất và chuẩn hóa chất lượng. Các công nghệ số được kết nối xuyên suốt dây chuyền sản xuất. Nhờ đó, mức độ tự động hóa tại nhà máy tăng khoảng 35%, hiệu suất sản xuất tăng 35%, trong khi chất lượng sản phẩm được cải thiện khoảng 28%. Một trong những công nghệ được triển khai là AI Vision, dùng để kiểm tra chất lượng theo thời gian thực, từ phát hiện lỗi linh kiện, kiểm tra độ chính xác khi lắp ráp cho tới đánh giá hiệu suất và độ an toàn của sản phẩm. ... ##### Xuất khẩu sang Mỹ, Brazil, Việt Nam và nhiều thị trường khác Hiện nhà máy Chonburi có thể sản xuất nhiều dòng điều hòa, từ điều hòa cửa sổ, điều hòa hai khối, hệ thống điều hòa dân dụng cho tới điều hòa dành cho xe RV. Sản phẩm từ nhà máy này đang được xuất khẩu sang nhiều thị trường lớn như Mỹ, Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ, Việt Nam và Philippines. Haier cũng tiếp tục mở rộng năng lực sản xuất để đáp ứng nhu cầu từ những thị trường khác trên thế giới. Việc nâng công suất nhà máy lên tối đa 6 triệu máy mỗi năm cho thấy Haier đang đặt cược vào đà tăng nhu cầu làm mát tại Đông Nam Á, đồng thời đưa Thái Lan trở thành mắt xích ngày càng quan trọng trong mạng lưới sản xuất và xuất khẩu toàn cầu của tập đoàn.

headline: 海尔智家2026H1显韧性：Q2营收同比增长，利润环比向好-海尔官网
summary_text: 2026上半年，全球家电行业延续承压态势。终端需求疲软行业Q2下滑12.4%，海外地缘与贸易政策持续扰动，叠加原材料价格高位运行，多重压力交织下，全行业经营压力普遍攀升。 ... 2026上半年，全球家电行业延续承压态势。终端需求疲软行业Q2下滑12.4%，海外地缘与贸易政策持续扰动，叠加原材料价格高位运行，多重压力交织下，全行业经营压力普遍攀升。 越是大潮奔涌之时，越能彰显企业的战略定力与经营韧性。多重冲击下，海尔智家交出了一份持续稳健的成绩单。8月27日，海尔智家发布了2026半年报：营收1521.15亿元，归母净利润103.16亿元，整体业绩承压。其中，Q2营收784.28亿元，同比增长1.36%；Q2归母净利润56.65亿元，环比增长21.78%。 承压的业绩主要受外部环境影响。作为一家海外业务占比超50%的全球化企业，汇率波动导致海尔智家2026上半年汇兑损失7.04亿元，而2025上半年的汇兑收益为8.82亿元，汇兑损益波动因素所造成的影响达人民币15.86亿元。除此之外，国内外消费需求放缓、大宗原材料及芯片成本上涨、家电补贴拉动效应减弱等行业共性因素，也给企业带来了一定经营压力。 可见，海尔智家经营基本面依然稳健。从Q1触底反弹，到Q2迎拐点营收同比增长、利润环比向好，这份业绩并非短期偶然，而是海尔智家全面推进AI转型、系统性重塑增长逻辑的结果。 ... 纵观全球商业发展史，单一市场的周期波动，往往是制约企业行稳致远的核心变量之一。而海尔智家内部通过研发、制造、营销、物流等十大能力的全球建设与拉通，实现从“品牌全球化”到“能力全球化”的深度全球化布局；外部通过AI赋能智慧家庭场景解决方案，提升用户体验，在北美、欧洲、南亚、东南亚、中国等核心区域齐头并进、互为支撑，既有效对冲了单一市场的周期风险，也共同筑牢了稳健增长的业绩基本盘。 ... 在北美市场，关税与高通胀双重压力下行业下滑，海尔智家不仅跑赢行业、跑赢竞品，还以美元口径Q2实现正增长。支撑这份成绩的，一方面是海尔智家加速向“国家本土化+全球化双循环”的全球供应链重构。通过全球生产基地与目标市场的精准匹配，海尔智家持续优化全球成本结构，如泰国冰箱工厂已正式承接对美大冰箱出口，优化单台出厂成本。同时，美国本土洗衣机、热水器制造基地稳步推进，也将进一步强化海尔智家本土制造的成本竞争力。另一方面，海尔智家持续加码高端品牌布局，放大用户价值，推动市场份额提升。下半年，海尔智家还将通过采购优化、供应链提效与全流程数字化转型持续对冲关税影响。 ... 在欧洲市场，海尔智家收入同比增长4.9%。通过全球能力的拉通，Horizon冰箱推动高端多门冰箱份额翻倍；三筒洗衣机获“法国年度消费者之选产品大奖”；高端T平台烤箱销量增幅达60%。高端爆款产品带动了海尔智家在英国、意大利、法国、西班牙四国市场冰冷、洗涤份额的全线提升。同时，海尔智家还签约利物浦、巴黎圣日耳曼、法网等全球顶级体育IP，结合线下高端场景体验，深度绑定高端品牌认知，持续拉升品牌全球溢价能力。 ... 在南亚市场，印度与巴基斯坦两大核心市场收入分别增长20%、30%（当地货币口径），远超行业水平。其中，印度市场更是实现全渠道、全品类的快速增长。这份增长的核心竞争力，源自扎根本土的深度产品创新。针对南亚极端高温、电压不稳、频繁停电以及本土饮食结构等特有市场痛点，海尔智家定制化推出的T3耐高温空调上半年销量翻番；针对印度素食家庭打造的侧T结构冰箱，以83%大冷藏的专属配比获得市场高度认可，高端产品的利润贡献持续提升。 ... 在东南亚市场，海尔智家收入实现双位数增长。其中，泰国白电销量持续引领，家空销量销额行业第一；越南白电销量第一。增长势能主要来自产品、渠道、供应链等方面的全方位协同发力：产品端空调聚焦AI+大风量与高能效迭代，中高端销量提升；渠道端越南电商业务增速超100%。同时，泰国、越南、印尼三大工业园区稳健运营，不仅充分支撑本土市场供应，更具备辐射全球的产能弹性，成为全球供应链网络中的坚实支点。 headline: Haier Smart Home Reports H1 2026 Results: Q2 Revenue Grows Year-on-Year; Net Profit Improves Quarter-on-Quarter | Corporate - EQS News

Haier Smart Home Reports H1 2026 Results: Q2 Revenue Grows Year-on-Year; Net Profit Improves Quarter-on-Quarter - Q2 revenue rose 1.36% year-on-year to RMB 78.43 billion. - H1 revenue was RMB 152.12 billion; net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company was RMB 10.32 billion; basic EPS was RMB 1.12. - H1 gross margin increased 0.4 percentage points to 27.2%. - Smart HVAC Solutions segment revenue grew 6.1% to RMB 45.36 billion; segment profit rose 26.8% to RMB 4.57 billion. Qingdao / Shanghai / Frankfurt / Hong Kong, 27 August 2026 — Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd. (A-share: 600690.SH; H-share: 06690.HK; D-share: 690D.DE), a global leader in smart home solutions, today announced its results for the six months ended 30 June 2026. The Company reported H1 revenue of RMB 152.12 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company of RMB 10.32 billion. Q2 revenue rose 1.36% year-on-year, H1 gross margin improved, and Smart HVAC Solutions segment profit grew faster than revenue. Management Commentary “Q2 revenue and net profit attributable to shareholders were both higher than in Q1, validating the changes we have made to our business structure and operations. While some regional markets will continue to face macroeconomic headwinds, we remain confident of achieving our full-year targets. Ongoing organisational change and innovation are the bedrock of Haier Smart Home’s ability to navigate business cycles. Smart HVAC Solutions is changing how we operate: by pooling R&D, supply chain and channel resources, we can bring products and integrated solutions to market more efficiently. H1 growth in segment revenue and profit shows that the integration is delivering results. In July, we applied a similar integration approach to Smart Home Appliances, bringing together refrigeration, laundry and kitchen appliances. As we enter the final phase of reshaping our global supply chain, a more regional, diversified and agile network — combined with the local teams we have built over many years — will strengthen cost competitiveness and resilience and support sustainable growth and consumer trust worldwide.” — Li Huagang, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Haier Smart Home Co., Ltd. ... Operational Update China Haier Smart Home maintained leading positions in China’s refrigerator and washing-machine markets. Retail value shares for both categories exceeded 40% online and offline, while the Company’s overall retail value share increased by 1.5 percentage points offline and 3.1 percentage points online. [1] [2] Cumulative retail sales volume of the Flash Ice refrigerator exceeded 20,000 units, helping lift the Company’s retail volume share in the RMB 4,000–5,000 segment by 4.8 percentage points year-on-year. Cumulative sales of the Effortless three-drum washing-machine range exceeded 600,000 units since launch. International North America: GE Appliances gained share within the core U.S. appliance industry and delivered year-over-year revenue growth in U.S. dollar terms in Q2 despite weaker demand. Pricing actions, new product launches, and double-digit revenue growth in Air & Water Solutions and small appliances supported Q2 performance. Europe revenue grew 4.9% year-on-year, with continued momentum in HVAC and commercial refrigeration. South Asia revenue grew 17.1% year-on-year in RMB terms. In local-currency terms, revenue in India and Pakistan grew by more than 20% and 30%, respectively. Southeast Asia delivered double-digit revenue growth. The Horizon refrigerator range demonstrates the Company’s “global enablement, local execution” model. A common product platform was tailored for fresh-food storage in Europe and for ice-making, water dispensing and food preservation in Vietnam. In H1, Haier ranked No. 1 by multi-door refrigerator retail value share in Spain and Italy, while the Vietnam rollout helped lift its Southeast Asian share in the category by 5 percentage points year-on-year. [3] ... Smart HVAC Solutions and Commercial Refrigeration Smart HVAC Solutions reported H1 segment revenue of RMB 45.36 billion, up 6.1% year-on-year, and segment profit of RMB 4.57 billion, up 26.8%. Following the integration of residential air conditioning, Smart Building Solutions and water solutions at the end of 2025, shared customer and channel resources added 245 touchpoints for Smart Building Solutions, while greater product-platform sharing reduced the number of related SKUs by 18%. Integration across technology, products and channels also progressed at Kwikot, whose share of South Africa’s water-heater market has increased by 10 percentage points since acquisition. Separately, Carrier Commercial Refrigeration continued its post-acquisition growth. H1 revenue grew at a near-double-digit rate in Europe and by more than 10% in Asia, where profitability also improved. ... headline: Kwikot launches HVAC offering under Haier Air & Water Solutions
summary_text: Water heating systems manufacturer Kwikot has formally entered the local heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) market. The new offering represents the latest expansion of Kwikot’s portfolio since its acquisition by Chinese home appliance brand Haier in 2024 and forms part of a broader air and water solutions offering spanning HVAC, water heating and water purification. Kwikot on August 21 said the move comes as households, businesses and property owners place increasing emphasis on the energy efficiency, running costs and long-term performance of the systems used to heat, cool and supply water to buildings. “Customers are no longer necessarily looking at heating, cooling, energy and comfort as separate needs. Our entry into HVAC allows us to broaden the role Kwikot can play, bringing Haier’s global technology into the South African market while retaining the local relationships, service and support our customers and partners know,” said Kwikot MD Murray Crow. ... The broader Haier Air & Water Solutions portfolio includes heat pump heating with Monobloc, Hydro Split and Hydro Split All in One systems designed to operate at temperatures as low as -30 °C and deliver hot water at temperatures of up to 85 °C. The portfolio also includes ventilation, where five platforms covering airflow requirements from 30 m 3 to 16 000 m 3 an hour, incorporating energy-efficiency, heat-exchange and space-saving technologies. The portfolio also includes air conditioning with solutions ranging from residential split and integrated units to light-commercial air conditioning, variable refrigerant flow (VRF) systems, chillers and control solutions for larger commercial applications. Additionally, the portfolio includes water purification with point-of-entry and point-of-use solutions including whole-house purification, under-sink reverse-osmosis and ultrafiltration systems, countertop drinking-water systems and water dispensers. ... Kwikot noted that it has recruited a dedicated HVAC team to support the expansion locally and is strengthening its technical and after-sales capability for dealers, consultants and contractors. According to Crow, this local support will be critical as the business moves into a category where specification, installation and maintenance have a direct impact on system performance. Kwikot’s support will extend from product selection and specification through to installation, commissioning and ongoing service. The expansion combines Kwikot’s established South African distribution, technical capability and relationships across the plumbing, construction, retail and property sectors with Haier’s international HVAC research, development and manufacturing infrastructure. Haier’s global innovation ecosystem includes more than 510 laboratories, with products developed to meet standards and certification requirements across more than 78 countries. Its manufacturing network includes 11 overseas smart industrial parks and 11 domestic smart factories, with combined manufacturing capacity exceeding 80-million units.

headline: FIEAM apoia expansão da Haier em Manaus e defende implantação de fábrica própria no Amazonas - FIEAM
summary_text: A Federação das Indústrias do Estado do Amazonas (FIEAM) recebeu, nesta quarta-feira (12), representantes do Grupo Haier, uma das líderes globais do setor de eletrodomésticos, para discutir a expansão da empresa no Brasil e as perspectivas de novos investimentos no Polo Industrial de Manaus (PIM). Durante o encontro, o presidente da FIEAM, Antonio Silva, defendeu ao CEO da Haier no Brasil, He Haifeng, a implantação de uma fábrica própria da companhia na capital amazonense e destacou o papel estratégico de Manaus para a expansão industrial e para a integração da Amazônia às cadeias produtivas nacionais e internacionais. ... A Haier oficializou a sua chegada no Brasil em maio de 2026, com estreia no mercado nacional com foco em produtos premium e tecnologias de casa conectada, estabelecendo uma parceria estratégica inicial com a Fast Shop para distribuição. Em Manaus, a empresa já começou a produzir televisores e condicionadores de ar em parceria com Jabil e TPV. Segundo os representantes, a produção teve início em maio e os primeiros produtos deverão chegar às lojas da Bemol, um dos principais parceiros comerciais da companhia no Amazonas, ainda no fim de agosto. Além da fabricação local de TVs e condicionadores de ar, a Haier importa atualmente para o mercado brasileiro outros produtos da marca, como geladeiras e máquinas de lavar. A estratégia, conforme apresentada durante a reunião, é consolidar a marca no país, conhecer o comportamento do consumidor brasileiro e, posteriormente, ampliar a produção local. ... Plano de expansão A reunião também tratou dos próximos passos da Haier no Brasil. O grupo afirmou que a intenção é construir uma fábrica própria em Manaus, inicialmente voltada à produção de televisores e condicionadores de ar. A empresa também sinalizou que outros produtos poderão futuramente ser fabricados no Amazonas. A estratégia prevê que a operação atual sirva como etapa de consolidação da marca no mercado brasileiro. A produção local de TVs já começou, enquanto os condicionadores de ar integram o processo de fabricação em Manaus. Segundo a empresa, os planos de expansão estão projetados para os próximos anos, com referência a 2027 e 2028. A perspectiva inclui não apenas a ampliação da fabricação dos produtos que já estão sendo produzidos localmente, mas também a possibilidade de incorporar outras linhas ao parque fabril amazonense.

headline: New Flint Group Packaging Solutions Whitepaper Examines Strategic Role of Coatings in Modern Packaging - WhatTheyThink
summary_text: ### New Flint Group Packaging Solutions Whitepaper Examines Strategic Role of Coatings in Modern Packaging Thursday, October 22, 2026 Press release from the issuing company Flint Group Packaging Solutions has published a comprehensive whitepaper exploring how coatings have evolved from a finishing step into an increasingly important and strategic component of packaging design and performance. Beyond the Surface: The Strategic Role of Coatings in Modern Labels and Packaging examines how coating technology now influences how packaging looks, performs, and is recovered at end of life, and why coatings are increasingly specified as part of the technical and commercial design of packaging rather than an afterthought. The whitepaper details the different roles coatings can play across the packaging lifecycle, from decorative finishes to performance and functional coatings. It also explores how coating choices increasingly influence recyclability, supporting wash-off, de-inking, and mono-material packaging formats. Paulo Vieira, Packaging Coatings & Global KA Technical Director at Flint Group Packaging Solutions, said: “Where coatings sit at the intersection of performance, aesthetics, and sustainability makes them one of the most valuable levers converters and brand owners have today. Getting coating specification right is increasingly important to ensuring packaging survives distribution and to helping it make a solid first impression with consumers. With this whitepaper, we aim to help converters and brand owners better understand these interdependencies and make more informed coating choices based on the packaging performance required. With an integrated portfolio spanning decorative, performance, and functional coatings, and technical expertise across labels and narrow web packaging, Flint Group Packaging Solutions is well placed to help customers make that specification decision with confidence.” The whitepaper is available to download here. headline: Flint Group Packaging Solutions plans for dynamic future following rebrand - Label and Narrow Web
summary_text: The rebrand of both Flint Group and Xeikon is intended to better serve customers on a global scale and account for a changing business landscape. ... October 21, 2026 ... The label and package printing business has evolved considerably over the last decade. The implementation of new technologies on a global scale has transformed the state of the industry. That shift was on full display at LOUPE Americas. The show catered to applications beyond labels – flexible packaging, shrink sleeves, and folding cartons, to name a few. Modern converters are increasingly growing their portfolios by expanding into new markets. In an embrace of the industry’s evolution, Flint Group and Xeikon recently underwent a significant rebrand to better position the company. Flint Group has become Flint Group Packaging Solutions (FGPS) and, within it, Xeikon has become Flint Group Digital Xeikon (FGDX). Both FGPS and FGDX operate symbiotically for the benefit of FGPS’ valued customers. ... “Our business today is very different from what it was 10 or 15 years ago, and the rebrands reflect that,” explains Pepyn Dinandt, CEO, Flint Group Packaging Solutions. “Our heritage is in publication printing, but we’ve had a strong presence in packaging and labels for more than 40 years. Today, the overwhelming majority of our business is focused on packaging. The Flint Group Packaging Solutions name reflects both where the business is today and where we see the greatest opportunities ahead of us in the market. The rebrands simply better reflect the business we’ve become. ... “Many label converters are expanding beyond traditional label applications into areas such as flexible packaging and folding cartons,” adds Dinandt. “The Flint Group Packaging Solutions name reflects this broader market and our ability to support customers as they enter new applications. Our narrow web expertise remains central to the business. Customers can also draw on a wider portfolio of inks, coatings, digital technologies, and technical services across multiple packaging formats. As converters diversify, they need partners that can help them manage new substrates, technologies, sustainability expectations, and regulatory requirements. Our packaging-focused identity signals that we are equipped to support them, whatever packaging demands next.” ... For Flint Group Packaging Solutions, the goal is to establish a clearer, stronger identity that reflects the company’s focus on packaging and the value we deliver for our customers. ... “Flint Group Packaging Solutions brings our inks, coatings, digital technologies, color expertise, and services together under one packaging-focused organization,” remarks Dinandt. “This makes it easier for customers to understand the breadth of our capabilities and access the right expertise across different applications and printing technologies. Ultimately, we want the rebrand to reinforce our position as a trusted partner that customers can rely on for quality, performance, regulatory support, and purposeful innovation. It also provides a strong platform for future growth as packaging requirements continue to evolve.” ... The changing nature of labels and packaging has prompted Flint Group Packaging Solutions and Flint Group Digital Xeikon, as part of the Group, to operate with far more synergy than in the past. For example, customers are becoming larger and more sophisticated. Many now operate across multiple sites, packaging formats, and printing technologies. They are seeking suppliers with the scale, breadth of solutions, service infrastructure, and regulatory knowledge to support these requirements. “The synergy comes from bringing Flint Group Packaging Inks and Flint Group Digital Xeikon together within Flint Group Packaging Solutions,” explains Dinandt. “Flint Group Packaging Inks’ core ink and coating portfolio remains the foundation of the business, generating more than €1 billion in annual revenue, while Flint Group Digital Xeikon broadens our capabilities through digital printing technologies across both toner and inkjet platforms for packaging and labels. This is also reflected in the way we combine Flint Group Packaging Inks’ expertise in coatings with Flint Group Digital Xeikon’s digital press technologies to provide integrated solutions for digital and hybrid print applications. “Together, these capabilities enable Flint Group Packaging Solutions to support customers across both conventional and digital printing,” Dinandt continues. “As converters expand into new technologies and packaging applications, they increasingly need larger, broader suppliers that can support multiple platforms rather than individual products. Bringing those capabilities together within Flint Group Packaging Solutions means we can continue to support our customers as their businesses evolve.” ... Digital printing continues to represent a significant opportunity within the packaging market, too. The new identity will allow the digital business to capture that growth. “When you look at growth rates, digital printing is one of the fastest-growing sectors within the packaging market and is expected to deliver double-digit annual growth over the coming years,” states Dinandt. “That is why Flint Group Digital Xeikon is such an important part of Flint Group Packaging Solutions.” ... ## Sustainable shift In addition to market expansion, the entire value chain has emphasized the importance of sustainability. From suppliers and converters to brands and consumers, the environment is top of mind for many. Increasing legislation plays a part in this shift as well. For example, the EU’s Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, which began applying in August 2026, is intended to reduce packaging waste and support a more circular economy by introducing requirements over time around packaging minimization, recyclability, recycled content, reuse and labeling. In North America, customers are also navigating an evolving range of requirements at the state level. “The direction of travel is toward packaging that uses less material and is easier to recycle, without compromising product protection, print quality, color consistency, or the look and feel that brands rely on,” says Dinandt. “This will influence decisions around packaging formats, substrates, inks, coatings, and print technologies and require closer collaboration between brands, converters, and their suppliers. ... “Flint Group Packaging Solutions is well placed to support customers through this transition. We bring together a broad portfolio of inks, coatings, color expertise, regulatory knowledge, and technical services with toner and inkjet technologies. By supporting customers across conventional, digital, and hybrid printing, we can help them understand evolving requirements and identify solutions that balance sustainability, performance and brand impact,” concludes Dinandt.

headline: Flint Group Packaging Solutions puts simplicity at the centre of Narrow Web innovation at LOUPE Americas 2026 | FlintGroup
summary_text: # Flint Group Packaging Solutions puts simplicity at the centre of Narrow Web innovation at LOUPE Americas 2026 02 Oct 2026 At LOUPE Americas 2026, Flint Group Packaging Solutions will showcase how an integrated ink, coating, and online platforms can help narrow web printers streamline and simplify their work. At Booth 5821, the Narrow Web team will guide visitors through a system designed to cut complexity, improve productivity, and support consistent print quality across a wide range of packaging and label applications. Making its show-floor debut is the latest addition to the already established and widely proven EkoCure®️ XS product line – EkoCure Fast Cure Ultralow COF Shrink White. This new high-performance, dual-cure last-down white ink is purpose-built for shrink-sleeve applications requiring low to moderate shrink performance. Combining high opacity, fast curing, strong adhesion, low transfer, and ultra-low-COF surface properties, EkoCure Fast Cure Ultralow COF Shrink White helps printers reduce build-up on sleeving equipment, improve press and converting performance, and achieve consistent, repeatable results. Its high opacity may allow for lower ink consumption while delivering greater white density. Where even greater opacity is required, the ink can also be trapped over itself. The launch forms part of a broader UV LED showcase supported by EkoCure installations already operating successfully worldwide. At the show, Flint Group Packaging Solutions will demonstrate how its established UV LED ink systems provide converters a practical, proven, lower-risk path to transition from conventional UV technology. The company will also discuss Flexocure®️ LEAP, its newest UV conventional technology for food packaging applications. Built on an advanced resin platform, Flexocure LEAP is engineered to reduce the risk of photoinitiator migration and to protect packaging integrity as food contact material regulations tighten. Sponsors that built multi-brand networks over the past half-decade are testing exits, and that calendar looks busy through the next 12–18 months and into 2027. Homepros reported this week that Kansas City–based Flint Group has launched a sale process, according to people familiar with the matter. Homepros describes Flint as a residential HVAC, plumbing, and electrical platform founded in 2019 that has partnered with 19 brands from Washington State to Florida, with a 2023 strategic investment from General Atlantic that remains in place. It also cites Ingram’s for Flint generating over $400 million in revenue in 2025 (up more than threefold from 2022), while noting current annualized revenue and EBITDA could not be ascertained. ... headline: Pepijn Dinandt, Flint Group Packaging Solutions
summary_text: After rebranding globally in March to express its years-long shift from publication to packaging inks, Flint Group Packaging Solutions brings color to every consumable. From developing low-migration, easy-to-recycle formulations to helping customers clear varying health, safety and environmental requirements, Flint is ready to bring color to the future. ... What inspired the global rebranding to Flint Group Packaging Solutions? The origins of Flint Group go back almost 100 years in publication inks. Around 10 years ago, the majority of our revenue came from this. But as magazines, newspapers and flyers declined, so did the business. Fortunately, my predecessors were smart enough to invest in packaging inks. Today, only about €200 million of our revenue comes from publication inks while about €1.2 billion comes from packaging inks. I came along and said, if this is the case, maybe we should rebrand the company from Flint Group to Flint Group Packaging Solutions. The word “solutions” has a deeper meaning. We do more than make inks. We also make coatings combined with ink formulations for different types of packaging. This specialization allows our research and development teams and regulatory experts to be very knowledgeable about the environmental and regulatory challenges within the 16 market segments we serve. Most of these are in food and beverage, and we also supply packagers of cosmetics and consumer goods. ... migration ... the movement of molecules from the printed surface into other areas of the packaging or its contents. This can occur via penetration-migration, where ink components move through the packaging substrate, or set-off migration, where components transfer from the printed surface to a non-printed surface. Ink migration is a particular concern for food packaging, where consumer safety is paramount. At Flint Group Packaging Solutions, food safety is our number one priority. Our Regulatory and Technical teams work closely together to ensure that both our raw material selection and customer formulations are designed to minimise migration risk. By carefully selecting raw materials with known migration data and ensuring compliance with migration limits established by relevant industry bodies, we can help our customers and brand owners create packaging that is safe for consumers. We are also developing innovative technologies to further reduce migration risk. One example is Flexocure® LEAP, a groundbreaking product range designed to limit the migration risk associated with photoinitiators used in UV-curable applications. Testing of the LEAP series has demonstrated a significant improvement in migration performance, helping to support safer solutions for food packaging. ... How have supply chain disruptions and sourcing networks affected your business? The crisis in the Gulf affects us in two ways. Many of our raw materials are derived from oil, so higher oil prices increased the cost of solvents and pigments, for example. We also experienced supply shortages when certain chemicals became scarce. Urea is used for both fertilizers and some of our input products. When that became short in supply, agriculture was given priority over our industry. Today, supplies have stabilized to a degree, but costs are still higher. Oil prices remain significantly above earlier levels and some suppliers have also used the crisis environment to increase prices and keep them there, even if one day everything should go back to normal. While some chemicals can be sourced locally, pigments are different. Today, pigment production is mainly concentrated in India for blues and greens and China for reds and yellows. Pigment production is a chemical process with significant environmental challenges, which is one reason it has become concentrated in regions where regulations are generally less stringent than they are in Europe. ... How are changing regulations around the world impacting packaging innovation? Each country has different standards, so our regulatory teams must ensure every product complies with the continuously evolving requirements of the global market. That is why having a global team of regulatory experts is so important. We have experts in each region who understand existing regulations such as the European Union’s Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH), the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) in the United States and food contact legislation, while monitoring and innovating to meet emerging requirements, including updates such as the German Ink Ordinance, European Printing Ink Association (EuPIA) Charter, and REACH-like chemical control laws multiplying in emerging markets. To stay ahead of these changes, we hold leadership roles in regional trade associations, giving us a voice in industry discussions, political advocacy and the development of future regulations. Sustainability regulations, in particular, are accelerating regulatory change and will continue to drive innovation across the entire supply chain. The European Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) poses a significant challenge for our customers by mandating that even packaging such as a potato chip bag must be recyclable. This requires not only breaking down plastics in the packaging but also reversing the printing process to remove ink. The historical use of nitrocellulose can cause issues for ink removal during the recycling process, so we developed a polyurethane alternative that is much easier to de-ink. Some customers are also replacing plastic with paper specially coated to protect against oxygen and humidity while making recycling easier. Our customers rely on us to ensure that every ink we supply meets the latest regulatory and sustainability goals and we strive to develop products that help customers meet future requirements. ... > The challenge for our industry is not to use less packaging, but to develop better packaging – solutions that provide the necessary protection and performance while ensuring circularity. Our role is to help customers and substrate suppliers create a virtuous circle. Lead battery recycling already recovers 97% to 98% of their materials. Our industry is not there yet, but over time we need to help build systems that move much closer to that standard. For Flint Group Packaging Solutions, that means developing inks, coatings and technologies that support packaging performance while enabling greater circularity.

summary_text: 传统UV固化技术已在印刷行业应用数十年，而LED-UV固化技术正在加速渗透。对于全球标签和包装印刷企业而言，一个现实难题持续凸显：旧设备无法立即淘汰，新设备又必须跟进升级。当一家工厂同时运行汞灯UV和LED-UV两类产线时，两类光源的光谱输出存在明显差异，部分常规油墨难以直接跨光源通用。双线库存增加、跨产线工艺难以统一等问题，拖累生产效率并推高运营成本。 ... 正因行业长期处于新旧设备交替的阵痛期，近期Flint Group、Siegwerk、Zeller+Gmelin三家国际包装油墨企业集中展示了双固化产品布局，让这一技术路线再次成为包装印刷行业的关注焦点。三大巨头的核心布局逻辑高度统一：一套油墨同时适配传统汞灯UV与LED-UV双光源，以降低产线并行期间的油墨切换和生产管理压力。 ... ### 三大国际油墨巨头的双固化布局 双固化并非全新概念，但近两年行业落地速度明显加快。三家国际包装油墨企业均已形成商业化产品布局，并持续完善相关体系。 Flint Group（弗林特） 将在2026年LOUPE Americas展会上展示EkoCure® Dual Cure双固化油墨体系。该系列可在传统UV和UV LED固化系统中运行，帮助印刷企业在不同设备配置和订单之间切换，减少分别建立油墨体系和生产流程带来的管理压力。对于正处于LED改造阶段的印刷企业，这意味着可以继续保留仍在使用周期内的传统UV设备，同时分阶段增加LED-UV机组，有助于减少重复库存和余墨管理。 同期展示的Flexocure® LEAP属于传统UV油墨，采用新的树脂平台以降低光引发剂迁移风险，面向食品包装及不断变化的法规要求。EkoCure系列主打光源兼容与产线过渡，Flexocure® LEAP主打低迁移和包装安全，两者形成差异化产品路线。 ... 三大行业龙头在同一周期集中加码双固化布局，折射出包装UV油墨行业的结构性变革。 LED-UV替代进入“新旧长期共存”的稳态阶段。 设备折旧周期、客户长期备案验证、成熟稳定的生产工艺、现有油墨库存消化等多重现实因素，让新旧产线并行成为未来数年包装印刷行业的常态。双固化体系恰好提供了一条低成本、低风险的平滑升级路径，适配工厂渐进式设备迭代节奏。 ... 固 ... 、 ... 彻底 ... 用品 ... 油墨 ... 考核维度 ... 适配双 ... 、多基材 ... 况 ... 更 ... 低 ... 味 ... 低 ... 低迁移 ... 满足 ... 严苛 ... 稳定的基础固 ... 能力 ... 入门 ... 控 ... 稳定 ... 企业 ... 需要客观厘清：双光源兼容不代表可以无视设备、基材、工况直接通用免调试量产。不同品牌 LED灯珠的波长、辐照强度、安装间距存在明显差异；传统汞灯的功率损耗、灯管老化程度、反射罩洁净度也会直接改变实际紫外输出剂量。同时，油墨涂布膜厚、印刷车速、颜料色相、承印材料表面特性都会直接影响最终固化效果。黑色、深蓝等吸光性强的深色油墨深层固化压力更大；厚涂白墨容易出现内部交联不充分的问题；PE、PP等低表面能薄膜还需搭配电晕处理、底涂工艺保障附着力。 ... 企业导入双固化体系后，仍需针对两类光源分别完成固化剂量、表里固化完整度、附着力、耐摩擦、耐化学品、小分子迁移等全套工艺验证。双固化的核心价值是解决油墨体系冗余、双线生产管理复杂的行业痛点，有助于降低产线升级期间的管理成本与试错风险，但无法替代生产端精细化的工艺调试与品控流程。

At the same time, there is a clear need for inks that perform across multiple substrates and applications without adding complexity for the converter. UV LED cures instantly, which helps reduce start-up waste, cuts downtime, and keeps production moving, all while using less energy than conventional UV systems. ... headline: Preparing for PPWR. Innovation in a Changing Regulatory Landscape | FlintGroup
summary_text: # Preparing for PPWR. Innovation in a Changing Regulatory Landscape 30 Jul 2026 The countdown has begun. For converters producing direct thermal labels for food packaging, PFAS restrictions pose both a regulatory challenge and an opportunity to future-proof their product portfolios. ... thermal ... printing ... on ... the ... Although direct thermal labels are found throughout the food, retail and logistics sectors, the chemistry behind them is highly sophisticated, requiring carefully balanced performance to withstand the heat generated during thermal printing while maintaining excellent print quality and durability. As regulatory expectations evolve, maintaining this performance while meeting new compositional requirements becomes increasingly important. Innovation beyond compliance At Flint Group Packaging Solutions, we believe regulatory change should drive innovation, not just adaptation. Building on more than 30 years’ experience with Thermokett water-based technology for direct thermal labels, we have developed Thermokett GT, the next generation of our thermal ink portfolio. Designed to support the evolving regulatory landscape, Thermokett GT is formulated without intentionally added PFAS and is compliant with the compositional requirements of the German Ink Ordinance (GIO). At the same time, it delivers high levels of adhesion, heat resistance, and scratch resistance. Thermokett GT offers: - Enhanced performance based on established Thermokett technology (better adhesion, better heat resistance, improved scratch resistance). - Improved printing and press performance. - Proven compatibility across a wide range of thermal printing applications. - Low impact on thermal printheads, helping minimise printhead wear. - Reliable performance on both uncoated and top-coated thermal papers, including excellent water resistance. - One-component, press-ready technology requiring no cross-linker addition. ... Looking ahead Regulatory requirements will continue to evolve, making proactive planning more important than ever. By evaluating compliant technologies early and validating them within existing production processes, converters can position themselves for a smooth transition while continuing to meet brand owners' and consumers' expectations. At Flint Group Packaging Solutions, we're committed to supporting our customers throughout this journey with innovative technologies that combine regulatory readiness with proven performance.

headline: Zeta Global to buy Digital Audience, its third data deal in two years
summary_text: Zeta Global said on October 6, 2026 that it has agreed to acquire Digital Audience, a data infrastructure company focused on identity and activation, in a transaction for which no price, structure or closing date was disclosed. The New York-listed company presented the deal as a way to extend the Zeta Data Cloud across the digital ecosystem and to strengthen its position in Europe. ... Short Zeta Global, a big American marketing data company, has agreed to buy a smaller company called Digital Audience that helps advertisers recognise the same customer across different websites and ad systems. It matters because Zeta wants more reach in Europe, where data rules are strict and markets are split by country, and Digital Audience already works there. Nothing changes for customers yet, since the deal has not closed and Zeta says it will keep things running as before afterwards. ... Three facts carry most of the weight. Digital Audience is "already integrated with Zeta," according to the company, which means the technical connection predates the deal. The acquisition "will also add an experienced team of data and AI engineers." And, according to Zeta, it "will also strengthen Zeta's European presence and will add established enterprise relationships in the region." What the release omits is just as notable. There is no purchase price, no split between cash and stock, no revenue figure for Digital Audience, no headcount, no list of the European markets involved and no expected closing date. Nor does it say whether the deal requires regulatory approval. The only reference to timing is a commitment that "following the close of the transaction, Zeta will work closely with the Digital Audience team to provide continuity for customers." ... That silence contrasts with Zeta's two previous data acquisitions. When it agreed to buy LiveIntent in October 2024, Zeta set out a $250 million package of $77.5 million in cash and $172.5 million in stock, plus an earnout of up to $75 million. Its agreement for Marigold's enterprise business in September 2025 was priced at up to $325 million, split between $100 million in cash, $100 million in stock and a seller note of up to $125 million. The absence of terms this time suggests a transaction small enough that Zeta did not consider the figures material, though the company has not said so. ... Europe is a harder market for identity vendors. Consent requirements under the GDPR and national e-privacy rules vary in their application from country to country, and each market has its own mix of publishers, telecoms operators and data providers. Flood's reference to "fragmented 'hard to crack' EU markets, compliant with local regulation" is a description of exactly that problem. A vendor already operating within those constraints offers a buyer something that is slow to build from scratch. ... The transatlantic legal backdrop has also grown less settled this year. In July, PPC Land reported that noyb argued the US Supreme Court's June 29, 2026 ruling in Trump v. Slaughter undermines the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, because the European Commission's adequacy decision relies heavily on the independence of the Federal Trade Commission. The framework remains in force, but a US company acquiring European data infrastructure is doing so while the legal basis for moving personal data across the Atlantic is under renewed challenge. Zeta's release does not address data transfers. ... Zeta has grown quickly. For the second quarter of 2026, it reported revenue of $442.8 million, up 44% from $308.4 million a year earlier, with adjusted EBITDA of $91.7 million and GAAP net income of $8.2 million. It raised full-year revenue guidance to $1,811 million to $1,824 million. The first quarter had brought revenue of $396 million, up 50%, with agency wins a significant driver and a rise in cost of revenue to 41% of sales. The company's product narrative has shifted toward AI. Athena by Zeta became generally available to Zeta Marketing Platform customers on March 24, 2026. In June, Zeta and Palantir said the Zeta Data Cloud would be rearchitected on Palantir Foundry, with Steinberg projecting that the partnership could drive more than $100 million in annual revenue to Zeta in the coming years. The Digital Audience release fits this framing: it uses "AI" repeatedly, but the assets being bought are matching, onboarding and distribution infrastructure. ... That infrastructure is also where Zeta faces the most scrutiny. In November 2024, short seller Culper Research alleged misconduct in Zeta's data collection practices, including claims that earlier acquisitions had been used to feed consent-farm websites. Zeta called the allegations false. In July 2026, a federal judge in New York refused to dismiss a securities suit centred on Zeta's past claim of more than 240 million opted-in US individuals, sending the case into discovery. The ruling was not a decision on the merits, and Zeta has called the claims meritless. Against that background, Digital Audience's European regulatory footing, which Flood emphasised, has a significance beyond geography. The release itself makes no claims about consent or compliance. ... ## What remains unknown Several questions are left open by the documents. Zeta has not said what it is paying, how the price will be funded, or when it expects to close. It has not named Digital Audience's European clients or markets, nor said how many engineers are joining. The release does not state whether the Digital Audience brand will survive, or whether its existing integrations with other platforms will continue to be offered to companies outside Zeta. The phrase "already integrated with Zeta" also invites a question the release does not answer: how much of Digital Audience's current business already runs through Zeta, and therefore how much of the acquisition is new capability rather than consolidation of an existing supplier. For advertisers and agencies that use Digital Audience independently at present, Zeta's only public commitment is continuity after closing.

headline: Zeta Global Corp - Zeta Live 2026: Zeta Introduces AthenaOS, the Enterprise Intelligence Operating System that Turns Intelligence into Growth
summary_text: Zeta Global Corp - Zeta Live 2026: Zeta Introduces AthenaOS, the Enterprise Intelligence Operating System that Turns Intelligence into Growth ### Zeta Live 2026: Zeta Introduces AthenaOS, the Enterprise Intelligence Operating System that Turns Intelligence into Growth October 8, 2026 - Built on the Zeta Data Cloud, AthenaOS combines enterprise knowledge with Zeta intelligence, dynamically builds around a business objective and learns from every outcome to drive smarter decisions, faster actions and measurable growth - Athena MCP, Zeta’s headless solution, brings Zeta intelligence into the applications, agents and workflows where enterprise teams already work - New Athena Inference Model (AIM), developed in collaboration with Fireworks using NVIDIA Nemotron, brings specialized AI to specific AthenaOS use cases - Zeta has begun work on development of a specialized AIM chip with partners to deliver faster intelligence more efficiently through a capital-light approach NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Today at Zeta Live 2026, Zeta Global (NYSE: ZETA), the intelligent AI infrastructure company, announced AthenaOS, its enterprise intelligence operating system. Built on the Zeta Data Cloud, AthenaOS combines enterprise knowledge with Zeta’s intelligence about who will buy, what they want and what they will do next. It connects that combined intelligence with Zeta’s intelligent AI infrastructure and then dynamically builds around an enterprise team’s objective, helping teams identify growth opportunities, take action and measure results. Instead of asking teams to navigate disconnected applications, assemble workflows, and interpret data across separate systems, AthenaOS starts with what a user wants to achieve. Users tell Athena by Zeta™, the conversational interface, their objective, and AthenaOS assembles the intelligence, applications, and actions needed to achieve it. It then operates through a continuous loop, using each outcome to improve the next decision. ... AthenaOS introduces new capabilities, including: - Intelligence organized around an objective: AthenaOS dynamically brings together the enterprise context, Zeta intelligence and actions needed to help users achieve a specific business outcome. - A continuous know, decide, act and learn loop: Every decision, action, and result that AthenaOS delivers strengthens the next one, helping improve the quality and speed of future decisions. - Shared enterprise context: AthenaOS creates a shared context framework across enterprise knowledge, customer and market signals, and partner technologies such as Palantir Foundry and OpenAI, allowing context, memory, and intelligence to move with the work rather than remain trapped inside individual systems. This preserves each enterprise’s data sovereignty and control over how its information is used. ... Athena MCP Brings Zeta Intelligence Wherever Enterprises Work Zeta also introduced Athena MCP, its headless solution, which enables enterprises to bring Zeta’s intelligence into their own applications, agents and workflows. Teams can work directly with Athena, or apply its intelligence within the systems where work happens, including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and other compatible enterprise AI environments. ... Underpinning AthenaOS is an enterprise-grade foundation of identity, governance, permissions, security and transparency. This foundation is designed to give enterprises greater control over how intelligence is applied across their data, applications and workflows. ... New Athena Inference Model for Enterprise Intelligence Zeta also unveiled the Athena Inference Model (AIM), a collection of proprietary models being developed in collaboration with Fireworks using NVIDIA Nemotron for specific AthenaOS use cases. These models are fine-tuned to understand specialized skills like domain language and follow defined brand voice, formatting and output requirements. The result is more relevant intelligence, more consistent execution and faster decisions at scale for AthenaOS customers. The Next Horizon for Athena Intelligence Zeta also announced that it has begun work on the development of a specialized chip and supporting data center infrastructure with a leading semiconductor partner. AIM gives Zeta unique insight into the intelligence workloads businesses need to run, creating the potential to optimize both the models and the computing beneath them. Together, this work has the potential to deliver faster intelligence, greater efficiency and more control over where enterprise data and intelligence run. Zeta contributes proprietary intelligence and an understanding of business workloads, while its partners contribute chip development and data center infrastructure expertise. This capital-light approach allows Zeta to explore specialized infrastructure while keeping its investment focused on the capabilities that differentiate the company. Availability AthenaOS is currently in limited internal beta, and expected to enter public beta later this year, with general availability planned for the first quarter of 2027. Additional capabilities will roll out over time. The development of the chip is in the early stages, and the architecture and development paths are still taking shape. Zeta will share additional details as it progresses.

headline: Zeta targets global profitability in FY27 as overseas business scales | Company Business News
summary_text: Summary The banking-tech firm expects years of investment in international markets to start translating into revenue, while larger bank partnerships drive its India expansion. Zeta, a homegrown banking-technology company that provides software infrastructure to financial institutions, is targeting full-year profitability in its global business in fiscal year 2027 (FY27), as customers it spent years onboarding and building technology for move into the scaling phase, top executives told Mint. The company has already reported several quarters of operational profitability in its global business, while its India business has been profitable for more than three years, said Ramki Gaddipati, chief executive Asia Pacific, global chief technology officer and co-founder of Zeta, on the sidelines of the Global Fintech Fest held in Mumbai recently. “This year will be a full year of profitability,” Gaddipati said. The company currently has annual revenue of more than $100 million, with roughly 75-80% coming from the US and 20-25% from India. While the US is its larger revenue market, India remains strategically important because of the depth of its bank relationships, deal pipeline and growth prospects. Zeta has long sales and implementation cycles, with revenue scaling only after a solution goes live and customers add users and transaction volumes. "As the fruits mature, you start getting the results,” said Sivaram Kowta, president, Zeta India. Once a solution goes live, revenue grows as customers add users and transaction volumes. Zeta’s focus, Gaddipati said, is on large, end-to-end technology projects rather than small pilots. Earlier last year, the banking software provider raised $50 million from US-based Optum, a subsidiary of UnitedHealth Group, at a valuation of $2 billion. Founded in 2015, by Bhavin Turakhia and Gaddipati, Zeta onboards banks for an end-to-end technological revamp. ... ## Bigger bank bets In October last year, Mint reported that Zeta was also looking to expand its India business through large bank partnerships. Its full-stack platform powers core banking systems, credit card issuance and digital banking applications. Its India journey took off with HDFC Bank, which turned to Zeta to rebuild its PayZapp app and build a second credit card issuance platform, in addition to its existing one, as part of a broader effort to strengthen its consumer-facing technology stack. The partnership marked a milestone for Zeta, which had earlier worked with RBL Bank and IDFC First Bank on more limited projects such as API integrations and authentication systems. Zeta’s platform can power products including credit cards, debit cards, UPI payments and digital banking services. But large new partnerships also require significant upfront investment in people and implementation. “New customers bring in both a lot of revenue and a lot of work,” Gaddipati said. ... ## Agentic commerce, DPDP push Agentic commerce is emerging as another potential growth area, particularly as banks prepare for AI agents to make payments on behalf of customers. Zeta believes the industry has so far focused largely on merchants and payment networks. The banking side will also need systems to manage consent, authentication, risk and control when customers allow AI agents to transact using their cards and accounts. “For the future, for sure, it’s a large one,” Gaddipati said, referring to agentic commerce as a growth driver. The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) framework could provide another opportunity. The framework could increase demand for technology that helps banks manage customer data and consent. Zeta is not positioning itself as a standalone DPDP compliance provider. Instead, it is building the requirements into its banking products. Its systems can, for example, capture consent when customers share information while applying for a credit card and control how that data is stored and accessed. “Any product that we do, it will be DPDP compliant,” the company said.

headline: Zeta, Pluxee launch passkey authentication for RuPay card payments - The HinduBusinessLine
summary_text: Zeta and Pluxee have gone live with passkey-based authentication for RuPay prepaid card transactions, replacing SMS one-time passwords with device-bound cryptographic credentials for online payments. The capability, enabled on the RuPay network by the National Payments Corporation of India, was announced in Mumbai on September 11, 2026. Under the new system, cardholders register a passkey once at checkout, confirmed by a single OTP, and subsequently authenticate transactions using biometrics such as a fingerprint or facial recognition, or a device PIN, with no further SMS OTP required. Zeta says passkey authentication completes in roughly 5–7 seconds, compared to 15–25 seconds for conventional OTP flows, and that registration completion rates in its implementation have been approximately 99 per cent. The launch comes against the backdrop of rising digital payment fraud in India, which crossed ₹21,367 crore in FY2025, more than five times the prior year, and the Reserve Bank of India’s two-factor authentication mandate, in effect since April 1, 2026, which pushes issuers beyond SMS OTPs toward dynamic, device-bound authentication factors. Passkeys use cryptographic credentials that cannot be phished or intercepted, reducing exposure to card-not-present fraud. For merchants, fewer checkout steps could lower authentication-related drop-offs and improve conversion rates. Zeta said it is working with additional RuPay issuers to extend passkey authentication to a broader cardholder base.

headline: Zeta Global at Citi’s 2026 Global TMT Conference: AI, data cloud push By Investing.com
summary_text: Wednesday, 09 September 2026 — Zeta Global Holdings, or Zeta Global Holdings (ZETA), used Citi’s 2026 Global TMT Conference to outline a broader push beyond marketing software into enterprise data, analytics and AI. Management described strong customer expansion and new partnerships, while also pointing to the challenge of turning those gains into sustained margin growth and larger-scale adoption. ... ## Key takeaways - Zeta said its business is shifting from a marketing platform to a wider enterprise data and intelligence offering. - Net revenue retention reached 120% in 2025, above the company’s guidance range and up from 112% in 2023 and 114% in 2024. - Multi-use case adoption rose 90% year over year, and average deal size for recent quarter closings increased 40% year over year. - The company sees Palantir, Snowflake and OpenAI as key partners in expanding sales, data integration and AI use. - Management kept a long-term goal of at least 30% adjusted EBITDA margin by 2030, up from a little above 22% now. The company’s shares have surged 64.65% over the past year, trading at $30.30 and approaching its 52-week high of $32.81, giving Zeta a market capitalization of $7.66 billion. According to InvestingPro analysis, the stock currently trades near its Fair Value. ... Management framed the company around three main growth drivers: - A proprietary data cloud with 535 million consumer profiles and more than 5,000 attributes and signals per person. - Athena, an AI-powered conversational layer launched in March 2024. - Strategic partnerships with Palantir, Snowflake and OpenAI. ... ## Financial results and business model Zeta highlighted a series of operating metrics that show customer expansion and stronger usage across products. - Net revenue retention reached 120% in 2025. - NRR was 112% in 2023 and 114% in 2024. - Through the first half of 2025, NRR remained above the company’s 110% to 115% guidance range. - Multi-use case adoption increased 90% year over year. - Average deal size for deals closed in the quarter rose 40% year over year. - Adoption of five or more channels increased 50% year over year. The company said its revenue model is split roughly into two parts: - About 60% comes from recurring subscription fees for data cloud licensing, analysis and campaign creation. - About 40% comes from consumption-based activation spending as customers deploy audiences across channels. Zeta said this structure creates a predictable land-and-expand pattern. It said initial pilots average about $100,000, then grow to about $700,000 in year one for super-scaled customers, $1.1 million in years two to three, $2.1 million in years three to five, and $3.9 million after five years. Management also said adjusted EBITDA margins are tracking slightly above 22%, with a target of at least 30% by 2030. Free cash flow margins, it said, have expanded faster than EBITDA margins while revenue has continued to grow about 20%. Chris said, “we have consistently grown free cash flow margins even faster than EBITDA margins, and EBITDA margins have been expanding every quarter and every year while we’ve been growing 20%. We haven’t had to make that trade-off for growth versus profitability.” The company also said about 90% of new code generation is now automated, which it sees as a support for future efficiency gains in research and development. ... Athena, Zeta’s AI-powered conversational intelligence layer, launched in March 2024 and is now available to all customers across enterprises and agencies. Management said Athena is changing how users interact with the platform: - About 40% of Zeta’s super-scaled customers are monthly active users of Athena. - More than 80% of Athena interactions are conversational rather than keyboard-based. - Thousands more audiences and campaigns are being created because the system is easier to use. Winnie said Athena can generate personas, sub-personas, PowerPoint slides, trend analysis and recommendations in minutes. She described a case in which an agency used Athena to build detailed personas for a news media pitch in under 45 minutes, a task that would normally take days. ... ## Partnerships with Palantir, Snowflake and OpenAI Zeta described its partnerships as central to its next phase of growth. Palantir - The partnership is structured as a seven-year contract with joint selling incentives. - Palantir’s revenue share comes off the top, which Zeta said leaves it with a higher-margin model. - The companies expect the relationship to generate at least $100 million in annual business. - Zeta said it has ring-fenced 20 opportunities with Palantir’s largest customers. - Those customers are brands spending more than $1 billion a year on marketing. - Pilot sizes are about $500,000 to $1.5 million, or roughly 10 times larger than Zeta’s usual pilot range of $50,000 to $150,000. Management said the Zeta Data Cloud has been migrated to Palantir’s Foundry platform, which should speed implementation and analytical delivery. It also said sales cycles are moving faster than usual and are reaching deeper into companies, including offices of the CFO, CTO and chief strategy officer. Chris said the partnership combines Palantir’s digital twin of internal enterprise information with Zeta’s digital twin of external market information. He said the combination can support market demand analysis, competitive intelligence and location strategy. Snowflake - Zeta said Snowflake helps create clean room environments for faster data integration. - Customers can run their own business intelligence models in Snowflake. - Zeta is offering a lightweight Customer Pulse product in the Snowflake marketplace. - OpenAI powers Athena’s voice. - Zeta has early access to newer models. - The company is testing advertising inside ChatGPT. ... Zeta said its “One Zeta” strategy is helping it sell multiple use cases together, rather than one at a time. The company said this is one reason average deal sizes are rising. Management said the platform now supports use cases across retain, grow and acquire functions, and that customers are adopting more channels at once. Zeta said it is also seeing more one-to-one selling with Palantir sellers and Zeta’s senior sales team. Chris said David, whom he described as Zeta’s best salesperson, is leading many of the Palantir engagements. The company said deal cycles for pilots remain about two to five months and are not tied to long request-for-proposal processes. It said the Palantir-linked opportunities are moving faster than historical norms. ... Zeta said it expects the Palantir relationship to remain a recurring topic on future earnings calls, with quarterly updates on pilots and customer wins. The company also repeated its longer-term margin goals, including at least 30% adjusted EBITDA margin by 2030 and free cash flow margins of about 20%. Management said it sees room for 100 to 300 basis points of gross margin improvement over time, along with further gains in sales, marketing, general and administrative costs, and research and development. It also said higher-margin analysis and business intelligence revenue could grow through the Palantir partnership. The company’s broader growth plan includes more AI integration across its applications, more international identity graph development, more data and signal sources, and more use cases outside marketing. It also sees room for expansion in agencies, the Snowflake marketplace and ChatGPT-related testing.

summary_text: BTG Begbies Traynor has advised on B S P Labels Limited acquisition from administration by Customark Ltd. on 22 July 2026, ensuring the best outcome for its creditors and securing the jobs of all its employees. The sale was conducted with the support of BTG Eddisons, the real estate and commercial sales arm of BTG. ... B S P Labels was founded in 2000 as Blue Star Pyramid Limited, changing its name in 2005. Acquirer Customark Ltd. was founded in 1968 and delivers from six locations across the UK. ... Simon Lowes, Partner at BTG Begbies Traynor, said: “The company has struggled with a range of issues in its recent history. Chiefly among its challenges were customers switching to overseas suppliers due to Brexit and Covid-19, increased business costs and the loss of a long-term employee with significant trade knowledge and skill. “After considering multiple options for rescue and revival the company directors were left with little alternative but to place the B S P Labels into administration. After a pre-packaged sales process the best offer came from Customark, which has secured the future of all employees as part of the deal. We wish the very best to the employees and the company as we are sure it has a good future ahead of it.”

headline: Berkshire Bought MF1. But It's Not the Berkshire You Think.
summary_text: - Berkshire Residential (unrelated to Warren Buffett's firm) acquired full control of MF1, a major CRE CLO issuer, from co-founder Limekiln. - MF1's business model packages apartment loans into CLO securities, transferring credit risk to institutional investors while retaining origination fees. - The 2022-2023 rate hikes triggered widespread defaults in MF1's $32B loan portfolio, but CLO investors bore most losses as the firm survived. - Post-2026 market recovery sees MF1 thriving again, but lingering risks include refinancing challenges and potential "extend and pretend" market fragility. - Berkshire's acquisition enables vertical integration of multifamily credit platforms, betting on CLO market durability despite cyclical risks. ... A few days ago, headlines announced that Berkshire had bought a major stake in MF1, one of the largest private apartment lenders in the country. ... first ... was Warren Buffett, you are ... alone. The buyer is Berkshire Residential Investments — a Boston-based real estate firm founded in 1966 that manages $34 billion of assets and owns or oversees more than 460,000 apartment units. It has no connection to Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway. The same word. Two completely different companies. (At least one news outlet had to issue a correction after confusing the two.) ... MF1 was launched in 2018 as a 50/50 joint venture between Berkshire Residential and Limekiln, a New York real estate credit firm founded by Scott Waynebern, a 30-year veteran who previously built lending platforms at Deutsche Bank and Benefit Street Partners. Over eight years, MF1 originated about $32 billion in apartment loans. The company also became one of the largest issuers of CRE CLOs — commercial real estate collateralized loan obligations — bundling those loans into securities that are sold to institutional investors. ... MF1 originates short-term, floating-rate bridge loans to apartment operators who are renovating properties, increasing rents, or preparing to sell. Then MF1 packages these loans into CLOs — structured securities with senior, mezzanine, and equity tranches — and sells them. The loans leave MF1's balance sheet. The investors in the CLO securities own the credit risk. MF1 keeps operating as the servicer and earns origination and servicing fees. ... This means MF1, over its lifetime, originated $32 billion in loans but the vast majority of that exposure was on the balance sheets of CLO investors, not on the balance sheet of MF1 or its owners.
