In the first half of 2025 alone, MF1 closed over $2 billion in newly originated loans, issued three multifamily securitizations, and invested $100 million in other multifamily debt. In Q1 2025, MF1 executed $5.6 billion in CLO volume across six transactions. By late 2025, the overall CRE CLO distress rate had fallen to its lowest point of the year, hitting 10.7%. ... Against this backdrop, Limekiln is walking away. On September 9, 2026, Berkshire Residential announced a definitive agreement to acquire Limekiln's 50% interest in MF1. Acquiring full control of MF1 lets Berkshire integrate origination, securitization, and debt investment under one roof. headline: Limekiln Bails on Turbulent MF1 Capital Joint Venture
summary_text: After a tumultuous period that thrust the firm into a glaring spotlight, MF1 Capital is seeing a significant change in management. Limekiln Real Estate is selling its 50 percent stake in the multifamily lender to Berkshire Residential Investments, its partner in the seven-year joint venture, Bloomberg reported. Financial details of Limekiln’s exit from the lender were not disclosed as Scott Waynebern’s company pivots away from multifamily credit. Launched in 2019, MF1 quickly became one of the most prominent lenders in the multifamily space. Between 2020 and 2021, MF1 originated at least $7.4 billion in debt, largely high-leverage loans handed to multifamily syndicators looking to act on aggressive fix-and-flip plans. As inflation took hold, however, MF1 kept issuing floating-rate loans on deals that hinged on the ability to substantially raise cash flows. By August 2023, across MF1’s almost $11 billion amortizing loan book, nearly half of the deals were either watchlisted or delinquent, according to The Real Deal’s analysis of Morningstar data. The bulk of MF1’s issued loans were set to come due in the succeeding 18 months, too. MF1 was a favored lender of multifamily syndicator Tides Equities. At least $425 million in MF1-issued loans in the Tides portfolio landed on servicer watchlists after rising rates hurt cash flow and made it tough for the firm to make interest payments on its debts. Tides scored at least 30 deals from MF1, according to Morningstar. ... MF1 has also bankrolled other syndicators that faced distress, including Rise48 and ZMR Capital, along with seasoned investors such as A&E Real Estate and Yat-Pang Au’s San Francisco-based Veritas Investments. ... Ultimately, MF1 issued more than $32 billion in debt since its founding, largely taking the form of commercial real estate collateralized loan obligations. It also branched into CMBS lending in the spring, according to CoStar.

headline: Inditex impulsa Bershka en los Estados Unidos con la apertura de su primera tienda
summary_text: # Inditex impulsa Bershka en los Estados Unidos con la apertura de su primera tienda Madrid – Completando una de las grandes apuestas estratégicas de Inditex para este ejercicio de 2026, Bershka, su principal cadena de moda joven y la segunda de mayor facturación de toda la compañía española, únicamente por detrás de Zara, ha abierto ya y finalmente las puertas al público de su primera tienda física en Estados Unidos. Continuando con ese primer anuncio, desde Inditex confirmaban la decisión tomada con respecto a Bershka coincidiendo con la presentación de sus cuentas anuales de 2025, ya este pasado mes de marzo de 2026. Un momento en el que del mismo modo que hiciera Maceiras a finales de año, desde la multinacional de la moda española destac ... como parte de sus principales iniciativas para el nuevo año, la apertura de las dos primeras tiendas de Bershka en los Estados Unidos, y de manera concreta dentro del área metropolitana de la ciudad de Miami, en el estado de Florida. Una inauguración de carácter doblemente estratégica para la compañía presidida por Marta Ortega, en la medida en la que de un lado llega para dar un decidido espaldarazo e impulso a la propia cadena de moda joven de Inditex en el mercado estadounidense; mientras del otro lo hace respecto a la misma Inditex, grupo que no solo continúa ensanchando su huella comercial dentro del estratégico mercado norteamericano, sino que además lo hace mientras impulsa su diversificación en el país, con la inauguración de la primera tienda de la que pasa ya a convertirse en su tercera cadena con presencia comercial física en los Estados Unidos. ... Un por tanto doble impulso el que recibe la cadena con este último hito que firma ahora en el mercado norteamericano, y que por otra parte no deja de responder a la naturaleza del modelo omnicanal que han asumido como propio las diferentes cadenas de moda del grupo Inditex. ... A este propósito, y empezando por esa recién estrenada realidad física que asume ahora Bershka en los Estados Unidos, las cadena dedicará esta primera tienda en el país a la comercialización de las colecciones de sus tres principales líneas de producto: Bershka, la línea de moda para chica; BSK, su línea para un público de la primera adolescencia; y Man, la línea de moda para chico de la firma. Tres tonos que se sitúan en sintonía con los empleados por la cadena para aperturas tan recientes como las de sus nuevas tiendas de Brasil y de Suecia, los referentes más directos de esta primera tienda en los Estados Unidos. Un punto de venta que en respuesta vuelve a poner en evidencia la apuesta cada vez más clara que desde Bershka están realizando por ambientes comerciales fluidos, pero más encapsulados y sensoriales; aspecto este que se busca potenciar, como es el caso, mediante el uso de una combinación de materiales capaces de generar diferentes impresiones y sensaciones, como lo son la madera, la piedra y la cerámica. ... Mientras tanto, y para lo hace referencia a la propia cadena de moda joven, y a falta del desempeño pormenorizado registrado por las firmas de Inditex del que informará la compañía española el próximo 9 de septiembre cuando de a conocer sus cuentas referentes al primer semestre del ejercicio de 2026, Bershka cerró el ejercicio anual completo de 2025 con unas ventas totales por valor de 3 286 millones de euros (+12,15 por ciento). In Q2, Berkshire made a net purchase of approximately $20 billion in stocks, ending the more than three-year streak of net selling under former CEO Warren Buffett. Meanwhile, the company spent about $4.5 billion on share buybacks, and acquired homebuilder Taylor Morrison Home for $6.8 billion. Its cash reserves dropped about 4% from the previous quarter to $364.7 billion, marking the first quarter-on-quarter decrease in four years. The company’s net profit more than doubled year-on-year to $25.7 billion for the quarter. ... Net ... of Nearly $20 Billion ... Three ... Year ... Berkshire bought a total of $23.5 billion worth of stocks in Q2, sold $3.7 billion, resulting in a net purchase of about $19.8 billion—the first time in over three years it became a net buyer of stocks. The scale of selling was also the lowest since 2022. The most notable among these was a $10 billion investment in Alphabet, the parent company of Google. Just days after Abel helped lead an $85 billion financing for Alphabet, Berkshire announced a purchase of Alphabet common stock, making it one of the company’s top five holdings, alongside American Express, Apple, Bank of America, and Coca-Cola. Regulatory filings show Berkshire made a net investment of about $21 billion in the “Commercial, Industrial and Other” category in Q2, with Alphabet falling into this category. Investors will receive more comprehensive details on Berkshire’s holdings once the company submits its quarterly holdings report to the US securities regulator later this month. ... ## Acquisition of Taylor Morrison, Industrial Empire Further Expands In addition to stock investments, Berkshire also announced the acquisition of homebuilder Taylor Morrison Home for an enterprise value of $8.5 billion (with an effective purchase price around $6.8 billion), making this one of the company’s largest M&A deals in recent years. ... ## Operating Income Steady, Insurance Business Drags Overall Performance Excluding investment gains and losses, operating income—Berkshire’s preferred metric for measuring subsidiary performance—rose about 16% year-on-year to about $13 billion, showing core business remains solid. Profits from the manufacturing, service, and retail segment jumped 24% to $44.7 billion, with industrial metal components, Duracell batteries, and Flying J gas stations all showing robust performance. BNSF railroad revenue grew 15% year-on-year, benefiting from increased imports at US West Coast ports and a shift in freight caused by trucking capacity shortages. Electronics component distributor TTI saw sales soar more than 26%, boosted by surging demand tied to the AI infrastructure investment boom. The insurance business was a drag on overall performance. Core insurance operating profit fell 13% year-on-year to about $1.7 billion, mainly due to higher claims at auto insurer Geico, along with increased advertising spending. Reinsurance premiums grew 4.1% year-on-year, partially thanks to a deal closed by Vice Chairman Ajit Jain this year—Berkshire acquired a 2.5% stake in Japan’s Tokio Marine in exchange for a share of business. The company noted that if this deal were excluded, reinsurance premium income would have declined. ... headline: Marcin Wasilewski, CHEP: “Our circular model helps optimise the entire supply chain” | Sustainability-Today.ro
summary_text: CHEP’s circular business model, based on sharing and reusing logistics equipment, helps companies improve resource efficiency, reduce environmental impact and access sustainability data for reporting, Marcin Wasilewski, Commercial Director Mid Europe at CHEP, said at the Sustainability in Business Forum, organised by Sustainability Today and The Diplomat-Bucharest. Speaking at the forum, Wasilewski highlighted the role of pooled pallets in creating a more efficient supply chain, explaining how CHEP manages, collects, inspects, repairs and reuses its assets while helping customers improve operational efficiency and prepare for evolving sustainability reporting requirements. ... CHEP operates a pooling model in which businesses share and reuse logistics equipment rather than managing their own separate inventories of pallets. The company’s distinctive blue pallets remain CHEP-owned assets, which are collected and returned to circulation after use. “Imagine that 350 million pallets around the world belong to us. Our blue pallets are easily recognisable and remain CHEP’s property. This is a major advantage for the companies that use them, because they do not have to worry about owning and managing these assets themselves,” he explained. Under this model, customers use the pallets to transport goods across the supply chain, while CHEP manages their recovery and subsequent reuse. The process includes inspection, repair and reintegration into the system, extending asset lifecycles and reducing the need for new resources. “We share this platform, and companies use it when they need to move goods from point A to point B or Z. Afterwards, we collect the assets as their owner, inspect them, repair them where necessary and put them back into circulation. This allows us to optimise the entire cycle,” Wasilewski said. ... Beyond managing logistics assets, CHEP also provides customers with information about the sustainability impact associated with their use of the pooling model. This data can support businesses in their environmental reporting and sustainability assessments. ... Wasilewski also addressed the questions businesses face regarding the implementation of the European Union’s Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR), as well as the broader challenges of sustainability reporting and decarbonisation. He said CHEP is focusing on transparency, data availability and cooperation with customers to help them navigate the changing regulatory environment. “There are many questions about PPWR: how the new rules will be implemented, how sustainability will be reported and how the requirements will affect each of our customers. We are preparing for these developments and remain committed to transparency in the information we share,” he said.

headline: Chep koopt transport op spotmarkt zonder planners - LogiNext
summary_text: ###### Marcel te Lindert 05 oktober 2026 Met vaste vervoerders slagen bedrijven erin om een groot deel van hun transportbehoefte in te vullen. Maar er zijn altijd situaties waarin die vaste vervoerders geen uitkomst bieden. Dan moet transport worden ingekocht op de spotmarkt. Transporeon biedt daarvoor een AI-tool die volkomen autonoom opereert. Dat scheelt veel tijd, vertelt palletpooler Chep tijdens een evenement van Transporeon. “Bovendien krijgen we nu toegang tot nieuwe transportpartners.” Chep is bekend van de pallets, maar voorziet het bedrijfsleven ook van andere ladingdragers zoals kratten en containers. Wereldwijd heeft het poolbedrijf maar liefst 352 miljoen ladingdragers in omloop. Om die op de juiste plek te krijgen, bestaat het netwerk van Chep uit meer dan 85.000 locaties waar de pallets, kratten en containers worden ingezameld en uitgeleverd. “We hebben meer dan 750 warehouses waar we onze ladingdragers opslaan. Maar om ze bij onze klanten te krijgen, hebben we ook transport nodig”, vertelt Max Mikus, senior procurement manager bij Chep. Alleen al in Europa verzorgt Chep zo’n anderhalf miljoen transporten per jaar. Meer dan 900 transportpartners leveren de daarvoor benodigde vrachtauto’s. “Met hen hebben we contracten afgesloten die al onze transportbehoefte afdekt”, vertelt Mikus. “Ik zou graag willen vertellen dat we geen gebruik maken van de spotmarkt omdat we alles hebben wat nodig is om die anderhalf miljoen transporten per jaar met onze transportpartners te managen, maar de realiteit is anders.” ... De realiteit is dat het distribueren, inzamelen, repareren en reinigen van ladingdragers een tak van logistiek met veel uitzonderingen is. “Regelmatig lopen we tegen de grenzen van onze transportcapaciteit aan, bijvoorbeeld als de vraag naar ladingdragers piekt of als een klant een spoedopdracht heeft. In die situaties zijn we gedwongen om een beroep te doen op de spotmarkt”, legt Mikus uit. Chep investeert veel in vraagvoorspelling om het gebruik van de spotmarkt tot een minimum te beperken. Hoe beter het inzicht in de vraag van klanten of in de vraag naar bepaalde ladingdragers, hoe beter de transportpartners in staat zijn om de inzet van hun vrachtauto’s te plannen en toe te wijzen aan de ritten van Chep. “Op basis van deze data hebben we in de contracten met transportpartners afspraken gemaakt over volumes. Daarin staat ook dat ze transportcapaciteit moeten kunnen leveren als de volumes iets hoger of lager zijn. Maar die flexibiliteit heeft zijn grenzen.” ... Dat veranderde toen Chep besloot om gebruik te maken van het platform van Transporeon. Dat beschikt over een tool voor autonoom inkopen van transport op de spotmarkt. “Het is nog steeds zo dat we onze transportopdrachten moeten plannen en versturen naar het platform. Het grote verschil is dat we transporteurs niet hoeven te vragen om een bod uit te brengen, maar dat we zelf een prijsindicatie kunnen afgeven. De transporteurs kunnen aangeven of ze het transport voor die prijs willen uitvoeren of meer geld willen ontvangen. Als er een match is, wordt alles automatisch in gang gezet.” ... ## Nieuwe transportpartners Autonoom inkopen op de spotmarkt levert meerdere voordelen op. Allereerst kon het platform van Transporeon worden ingericht naar de wensen van Chep, zodat het aansloot op de bedrijfsvoering. “Daarnaast hanteren we voor specifieke landen specifieke eisen. Soms is tijdigheid belangrijk en moeten we vervoerders inzetten die daar goed in zijn. Het platform stelt ons in staat om filters te gebruiken, die helpen om het juiste transport aan de juiste partner toe te wijzen”, legt Mikus uit. Een groot winstpunt is de toegenomen efficiëntie. Omdat de planners niet meer handmatig biedingen hoeven te vergelijken, bespaart het poolbedrijf vele uren. “Wat mij persoonlijk het meeste oplevert, is dat we via het platform toegang krijgen tot nieuwe partners. Die krijgen de gelegenheid om te ervaren hoe het is om voor Chep te werken. Als dat goed bevalt, kan dat reden zijn om de samenwerking uit te breiden. En als de samenwerking niet bevalt, gaan we allebei weer ons eigen weg”, legt Mikus uit. “Op die manier verschaft het platform ons de mogelijkheid om nieuwe mensen te ontmoeten en ons netwerk uit te breiden.”

headline: CHEP opens logistics center in Lacchiarella - ITJ | International Transport Journal
summary_text: CHEP opened a new logistics center in Lacchiarella, south of Milan, on September 30, 2026. This center represents the largest of its kind in Italy and is designed to support the company’s growth in the country. With an area of 35,000 m², the facility offers significantly higher capacity for handling pallets compared to previous locations. The new logistics center was developed in collaboration with AF Group, a long-standing partner of CHEP. Ugo Geraci, Director for the Supply Chain in Italy, Greece, and the Balkans, emphasized the importance of the three elements of scaling, innovation, and sustainability for the future development of the supply chain. „We have implemented an investment project in Lacchiarella aimed at making our network more efficient and resilient,“ Geraci explained. ... in focus The new center features a high degree of automation. The inspection of pallets is fully automated through a camera system that checks each individual pallet and analyzes its compliance with quality standards. If necessary, repairs or cleaning are initiated. To continuously improve the quality of the pallets in circulation, various automatic systems are integrated to remove surface contaminants, measure wood moisture, paint the pallets, and capture phytosanitary markings according to ISPM-15. The planning of the site was carried out from the outset with sustainability in mind. Planned measures include the installation of a photovoltaic system, the gradual transition of transport means to a 100% electric fleet, and the development of an electric pallet drying system. These initiatives aim to reduce environmental impact and increase operational efficiency.

headline: CHEP inaugura centro logístico em Lacchiarella - ITJ | International Transport Journal
summary_text: CHEP inaugurou um novo centro logístico em Lacchiarella, ao sul de Milão, em 30 de setembro de 2026. Este centro representa o maior de seu tipo na Itália e foi projetado para apoiar o crescimento da empresa no país. Com uma área de 35.000 m², a instalação oferece uma capacidade significativamente maior para o manuseio de paletes em comparação com locais anteriores. O novo centro logístico foi desenvolvido em colaboração com o AF Group, um parceiro de longa data da CHEP. Ugo Geraci, Diretor da Cadeia de Suprimentos na Itália, Grécia e Balcãs, enfatizou a importância dos três elementos: escalabilidade, inovação e sustentabilidade para o futuro desenvolvimento da cadeia de suprimentos. “Realizamos em Lacchiarella um projeto de investimento que visa tornar nossa rede mais eficiente e resiliente”, explicou Geraci. ... O novo centro se destaca por um alto grau de automação. A inspeção dos paletes é realizada totalmente de forma automatizada por um sistema de câmeras, que verifica cada palete individualmente e analisa sua conformidade com os padrões de qualidade. Se necessário, reparos ou limpezas são realizados. Para melhorar continuamente a qualidade dos paletes em circulação, vários sistemas automáticos estão integrados, que removem contaminações superficiais, medem a umidade da madeira, pintam os paletes e registram as marcações fitossanitárias de acordo com o ISPM-15. O planejamento do local foi realizado desde o início com foco na sustentabilidade. As medidas previstas incluem a instalação de um sistema fotovoltaico, a transição gradual dos meios de transporte para uma frota 100% elétrica, bem como o desenvolvimento de um sistema elétrico de secagem de paletes. Essas iniciativas visam reduzir o impacto ambiental e aumentar a eficiência das operações.

headline: Pallet: l'intervista ad Alessia Pascariello, Direttrice Commerciale CHEP Italia
summary_text: In alcuni Paesi europei nove movimentazioni pallettizzate su dieci passano già attraverso il pooling. In Italia, invece, il modello ha ancora un grande potenziale da esprimere. Un divario che, letto nella giusta prospettiva, non è un ritardo ma un’opportunità: quella di modernizzare la logistica nazionale seguendo una strada già tracciata altrove, con margini di crescita che i principali operatori del settore osservano con crescente attenzione. Tra questi c’è CHEP, che in Italia conta oggi oltre 1.600 clienti – più di 160 acquisiti solo nell’ultimo anno fiscale – una rete di oltre 26.000 punti di raccolta e più di 30 centri servizi sul territorio, inserita in un ecosistema europeo che supera i 300.000 partner della supply chain. Alessia Pascariello, Direttrice Commerciale di CHEP Italia, descrive un mercato in piena trasformazione, spinto da tre forze convergenti: “il mercato del pallet pooling sta vivendo una fase di forte evoluzione, trainata da tre grandi fattori: la ricerca di maggiore efficienza nelle supply chain, la crescente attenzione ai requisiti normativi europei sulla sostenibilità e la necessità di ridurre la complessità operativa. In Europa il pooling è ormai considerato uno standard consolidato in molti settori, soprattutto nel largo consumo, nel beverage, nel food e nella distribuzione moderna. In alcuni Paesi europei il livello di adozione supera il 90% delle movimentazioni pallettizzate, mentre l’Italia presenta ancora ampi margini di sviluppo. Questo rappresenta una grande opportunità per le aziende italiane che vogliono modernizzare i propri processi logistici”. ... Nel modello CHEP, invece, i pallet vengono condivisi tra molteplici aziende all’interno di un circuito chiuso di riutilizzo. Dopo ogni utilizzo, i pallet vengono recuperati da CHEP, ispezionati, riparati se necessario e reimmessi nel network. Questo consente di massimizzarne il ciclo di vita e ridurre drasticamente il consumo di materie prime. La differenza sostanziale è che il cliente non acquista un pallet, ma accede a un servizio completo. CHEP si occupa della disponibilità degli asset, della qualità, della manutenzione e della gestione logistica. Questo approccio trasforma il pallet da semplice bene fisico a infrastruttura condivisa della supply chain. Inoltre, tutti i pallet CHEP provengono da legno certificato e vengono costantemente ricondizionati per mantenere standard qualitativi elevati e costanti”. ... Pascariello indica tre dimensioni su cui i risultati sono verificabili: “i benefici sono concreti e misurabili su tre dimensioni fondamentali. La prima è quella ambientale. Studi indipendenti di Life Cycle Assessment dimostrano che il modello CHEP genera un impatto inferiore rispetto ai sistemi tradizionali di interscambio in tutte le principali categorie ambientali considerate: utilizzo delle risorse, generazione di rifiuti ed emissioni di CO₂. La seconda riguarda l’efficienza operativa. Grazie alla standardizzazione delle attrezzature e a rigorosi processi di controllo qualità, i pallet CHEP sono particolarmente adatti agli impianti automatizzati, riducendo il rischio di fermate di linea, danni ai prodotti e inefficienze di movimentazione. La terza dimensione è la continuità del business. Grazie alla capillarità del network, i clienti hanno accesso a pallet disponibili quando e dove servono, anche in presenza di picchi di domanda o tensioni nella catena di approvvigionamento. A livello sistemico, ogni azienda che entra nel network contribuisce a rafforzare l’intera supply chain: più riutilizzo, meno sprechi, minore necessità di produrre nuovi pallet e maggiore resilienza dell’ecosistema logistico complessivo”.

headline: Future of Reusable Packaging: Tim Debus, RPA | CHEP NA
summary_text: I would highlight two major trends. The first is public policy, which is finally recognizing the essential role of reuse as the preferred way to eliminate packaging waste. We are now seeing policies that, in some markets, are actively incentivizing the adoption of reuse systems. The second is the increasing capabilities of the services and technologies needed to make reuse work effectively to unlock its benefits. That includes washing and hygiene, transportation and logistics and asset management through technology enablement. The latter represent the fastest-growing segment of RPA membership. Importantly, these trends reinforce each other. While policy offers businesses more reason to make systems changes, technology can make those systems more efficient, visible and economically productive. ... Individual markets definitely hold characteristics that make reusable packaging work differently. Distance, scaled adoption, import-export trade and policy can all create very different conditions and, as a result, unique pooling models and applications. Policy highlights an interesting difference between North America and Europe. In Europe, the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation seeks to drive greater reuse by setting targets and corresponding penalties when those targets aren’t met. In North America, we’re seeing more direct financial incentives for adopting source-reducing practices. California, for example, applies a fee to single-use packaging while reusable and refillable packaging is exempt. Those approaches are different but are ultimately trying to influence the same systems change where solid waste is reduced and pollution is prevented. The important thing is that policy reflects the conditions of each market and creates the right incentives for reuse, rather than assuming one regulatory approach will work everywhere. ... There is a lot of movement in automotive lanes between the U.S. and Mexico, for example. Of course, cross-border reuse introduces additional complexity in terms of tariffs frameworks and customs classifications, but there are equally opportunities to be had. In many cases, reusable transport packaging, unlike expendable packaging, can benefit from duty-exempt status. Because of its continuous use rather than being consumed domestically, it can enter a country temporarily and leave again as part of the manufacturing process. At the same time, better asset management of reusable packaging makes longer-distance pooling increasingly worth exploring. In fact, the RPA is currently involved in a project looking at transatlantic pooling for specialty crops between the U.S. and Europe. The regions have traditionally operated separate pools, but we are exploring whether assets could be managed through export and re-import flows. This is still a research project, supported through a grant from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, but demonstrates the kind of cross-border opportunities we should be thinking about in the future, rather than dismissing them based on assumptions about distance. ... 7. You mentioned packaging regulations earlier. Can effective regulation encourage greater reuse? And what does that look like in practice? Replacing disposability and single use, by moving toward a circular model based on asset durability and repeated use, requires a holistic change in mindset, operations and culture. Policy can play a key role in providing the direction and incentives needed to encourage that systems change, leading to superior packaging performance and value-creating opportunities. I would also add the importance of policymakers distinguishing between consumer reuse and business-to-business supply chain reuse. Reuse is already well established in many B2B supply chains, so effective regulation should further enable and support that existing infrastructure rather than inadvertently creating barriers to what is already working well at scale. ... A barrier to wider adoption of reusable transport packaging is the commitment and resources needed for the systems change I mentioned earlier, as well as the inevitable disruption that comes with considering packaging as a valued asset rather than disposable waste. Many organizations are understandably reluctant to introduce operational disruption both up and downstream, particularly when they are focused on immediate business conditions and short-term financial performance. There is also a longstanding culture of a throw-away society. For decades, over generations, we have built systems around making packaging, using it and tossing it away. Reuse asks people and organizations to handle packaging differently. Ultimately, we need to challenge the idea that reuse has to be as convenient as disposal on day one. Systems change is inherently disruptive, but the objective is to build something better that becomes more convenient and efficient once established. ... I would hope to look back and see that today’s policy environment had acted as a catalyst for meaningful progress, particularly in consumer applications, while continued growth had taken place in B2B supply chain reuse. This would suggest greater synergies between those two areas. If we consider B2B reuse as the trunk of the tree, its established scale and infrastructure could potentially support the growth of consumer reuse as its branches. Beyond that, I think technology-enablement and its resulting data will be a major part of the story. Reusable packaging has the potential to generate valuable information that can support AI agents and autonomous decision-making for things like predictive demand planning and inventory management. Ultimately, I’d like to see the industry fully move from traditional to digital systems, and from reusable packaging to smart and connected reusable packaging. It’s achievable and starting to happen today. I believe there has never been a more exciting time for our industry.

headline: Pooling de paletes: CHEP amplia atuação na Bahia
summary_text: # CHEP leva pooling de paletes à Bahia e amplia presença no Nordeste 04/10/2026 15/09/2026 Por Igor Roberto A CHEP leva o modelo de pooling de paletes à Bahia ao participar, nos dias 16 e 17 de setembro, da Rodada de Negócios Só Pássaros, em Itaberaba (BA). Queremos mostrar às empresas da região como o pooling pode simplificar a gestão de paletes, reduzir custos e garantir maior disponibilidade de ativos para varejistas e fabricantes. Nossa alta capilaridade no interior e em outros estados do país é um importante apoio aos negócios em expansão. Estar presentes na Rodada de Negócios do Grupo Só Pássaros também nos permite conhecer de perto as necessidades do mercado local e construir novas conexões”, afirma Felipe Luz, gerente de Retail Solutions da CHEP Brasil. ... A companhia destaca que o Nordeste registrou crescimento de 2,6% no acumulado de 12 meses até janeiro de 2026, segundo o Banco do Nordeste, acima da média nacional no período. Para a CHEP, o desempenho reforça o potencial da região para negócios ligados à logística e à indústria. ... A CHEP informa que já mantém estrutura na Bahia, com um Centro de Serviço em Simões Filho, na Região Metropolitana de Salvador, e atende indústrias no estado, principalmente do segmento de alimentos. Na Bahia, a ampliação da atividade industrial também aparece nos números do governo estadual. Entre janeiro e maio de 2026, a Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Econômico assinou 46 protocolos de intenções, que somam R$ 3,5 bilhões em investimentos previstos. headline: Brambles delivers first year progress against its 2030 Sustainability Programme | CHEP
summary_text: # Brambles delivers first year progress against its 2030 Sustainability Programme ## September 9, 2026 ## Global logistics group and operator of CHEP publishes 2026 Sustainability Review Sydney, 9 September 2026: Brambles today released its 2026 Sustainability Review, highlighting progress in the first year of its 2030 Sustainability Programme, which advances the company’s vision to create regenerative supply networks. Reporting on material sustainability issues and achievements for the year ended 30 June 2026, the review demonstrates early momentum against Brambles’ broad range of targets across nature, business and communities. Juan José Freijo, Brambles’ Chief Sustainability Officer, said: “As we step into the next phase of our regenerative vision, we have focused on translating our ambition into clear strategies and frameworks that support accountability, transparency and delivery against these elevated sustainability goals.” ... Key achievements highlighted in the 2026 Sustainability Review include: - Enabling 10,000 hectares of land regeneration in South Africa’s Upper uThukela catchment through a new partnership with WildTrust, which aims to protect and restore approximately 75,000 hectares over five years, contributing to Brambles’ target to regenerate two hectares of land for every hectare required for its timber needs; - Reducing absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 36% and absolute Scope 3 emissions by 16% against a FY20 baseline, ahead of Brambles' validated science-based targets reduction trajectory; - Substituting 50% of virgin plastic purchases with circular materials or solutions (up from 41% in FY25), against Brambles' target of 80%; - Engaging in sustainability collaborations with 694 external partners across customers, suppliers and NGOs (up from 637 in FY25); - Issuing a record 7,440 Sustainability Certificates to customers, more than double the 3,702 issued in FY25, recognising environmental benefits achieved by using Brambles’ platforms instead of linear or single-use alternatives; - Achieving a 10% improvement in Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR) (0.9 in FY26 vs 1.0 in FY25) to deliver Brambles’ best safety performance on record; - Facilitating the rescue of 880,863 tonnes of surplus food using CHEP platforms, equating to 1.8 billion meals served to people in need; and - Supporting local communities with contributions totalling US$8.84 million through financial, in-kind donations and volunteering hours. ... The review also showcases initiatives from across Brambles’ operating regions that are supporting its regenerative ambition. These include efforts to protect biodiversity and endangered species in South Africa, collaborations with carrier partners on electric transport solutions in Australia, Mexico and Chile, and the deployment of Brambles’ digital technologies to help customers protect produce quality and reduce food spoilage in Latin America. ... “Climate change, resource scarcity and nature-related impacts are reshaping value chains and increasing the importance of resilience. ... Brambles continued to be recognised for its sustainability leadership in FY26. The company ranked #2 globally in the Commercial Services and Supplies category of the Dow Jones Best‑in‑Class World Index and was recognised in the S&P Sustainability Yearbook, having earned a Top 5% S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment Score. Brambles also maintained the highest possible AAA rating from MSCI and retained CDP ‘A’ rating for both climate and forestry. ... About Brambles Brambles Limited (ASX: BXB) Brambles is a global provider of logistics solutions, connecting the world’s supply network through its operations, people and technology. Brambles operates across ~60 countries primarily through its CHEP brand, harnessing its industry-leading expertise and the unmatched scale of its asset pool of 352 million pallets, crates and containers through a network of 750+ service centres. Through its regenerative ambition, built on decades of leadership in the circular economy, Brambles has become one of the world’s most sustainable companies. Since its origin in 1875, Brambles has been at the forefront of innovation. Today, it continues to invest in the future, bringing enhanced connections, visibility and foresight, developing solutions to unlock new value for customers, and making the world’s supply network more resilient and regenerative. Brambles is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange and an ASX20 constituent. The Group employs approximately 12,000 people, with its largest operations in North America and Europe. headline: Thin film resistors enable higher power density in smaller footprints ⋆ Electronics Weekly
summary_text: Vishay’s new series of thin film chip resistors in 0402 and 0603 case sizes are built on an AlN substrate in SMT footprints. The Sfernice CHEP series deliver standard power ratings of 1.2 W in the 0402 case size and 1.8 W in the 0603 case size. When mounted per datasheet guidelines, power ratings increase by 50 % to 1.8 W and 2.8 W, respectively, enabling higher power density in smaller footprints. The resistors are available with flip-chip or wraparound terminals. When mounted as flip-chip devices, resistors in the 0402 case size achieve frequencies to 50 GHz, while wraparound active face-up mounting supports operation to 20 GHz. Devices in the 0603 case size support frequencies up to 40 GHz. Designed to minimize internal reactance, the CHEP series features LC values down to 1 x 10⁻²⁴. The resulting low parasitics reduce phase shift, maintain consistent impedance, and minimize noise to improve RF performance, while standard 0402 and 0603 case sizes enable easy integration into widely accepted land patterns, simplifying design and layout. ... The devices are ideal for telecom and connectivity applications, including LEO satellites, base station terminals, 5G and 6G networks, and RF infrastructure such as remote radio units (RRUs) and antennas. Additional applications include aerospace and defense systems such as drones, satellite payloads, guidance and telemetry systems, data links, and phased array radar systems. The resistors offer a resistance range from 20 Ω to 120 Ω with tolerances down to ± 1 % and a temperature coefficient of ± 100 ppm/°C, with ± 50 ppm/°C available on request. RoHS-compliant, halogen-free, and Vishay Green, the devices operate over a temperature range from -55 °C to +155 °C. Samples and production quantities of the CHEP series are available now, with lead times of 16 weeks.

summary_text: # CHEP Workers Win New Agreement After Weeks On The Picket Line – FIRST Union By The Daily Blog 9 March 2022 Workers at CHEP service centre in Auckland – one of Aotearoa’s largest pallet suppliers – have voted unanimously in favour of a new agreement that contains meaningful pay increases, overtime rates for weekend work and a sign-on bonus after over a fortnight on strike, including an indefinite withdrawal of labour, FIRST Union said today. “We’re very happy to confirm that FIRST Union members at CHEP have voted ‘yes’ to a new Collective Agreement following mediated bargaining on Wednesday this week,” said Mark Muller, FIRST Union Secretary for Transport, Logistics and Manufacturing. “It has taken guts and resolve to withdraw their labour over the last two weeks, and it shows that solidarity and this kind of firm commitment is necessary to achieve great things.” “The new agreement will see the vast majority of staff at the Penrose plant earning a living wage or higher, with back-paid wage rises above 6% per annum, and further increases locked in from later in the year.” “It also contains important improvements to conditions at work, including overtime rates for weekend shifts as well as a sign-on bonus of $500 for union members.” “I’m enormously proud of our members, who sacrificed a lot in order to show their worth, and it has resulted in meaningful improvements to their situation when the cost of living is sky-high and times have been very tough.”

headline: British exporters urged to review pallet and container arrangements before new rules come into force | CHEP
summary_text: # British exporters urged to review pallet and container arrangements before new rules come into force ## August 11, 2026 ## EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation introduced this month Manchester, 11 August 2026 - UK businesses exporting food, drink, household and personal care products into the European Union are being urged to review the operating models for managing pallets, containers and other transport packaging used across their supply chains as the new EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) is phased in this month. August 12 marks the first step in the introduction of the regulations, with total implementation scheduled for 2030. The PPWR will cover all packaging placed on the EU market, including transport packaging such as pallets, containers and crates. It is intended to reduce the amount of packaging waste in Europe and promote the reuse and recycling of packaging. The EU hopes to drastically lower packaging emissions in this way. Although many detailed requirements are being phased in over time, it introduces significant reuse obligations from 2030. These include a requirement for at least 40% of specified transport packaging used within the EU to be reusable within a reuse system, with 100% requirements for certain movements within the same business group or within a single Member State. Katie Ingham, Commercial Director at pallet pooling leader CHEP, says: “PPWR puts transport packaging firmly in the spotlight. For British exporters, that means pallets and containers can no longer be treated as a low-profile operational issue, because businesses will need to show how those assets move through a genuine reuse system. The challenge is that once packaging moves across different sites, partners, and markets, visibility can easily be lost. Companies that act now to review their responsibilities, recovery processes and supporting data will be far better placed to manage compliance risk and keep goods moving smoothly across Europe.” ... Katie advises that British manufacturers and FMCG exporters act now and review their logistics models for managing pallets and containers, including their processes, data, recovery systems, repair capacity and responsibilities. This is made all the harder by exports as information will sit across different systems, sites or partners. She adds: “British manufacturing companies need to know where pallets and containers go in Europe, whether they operate within a genuine reuse system, who is responsible for recovery and repair, and whether reliable data can be produced.” CHEP warns that companies that do not comply with the new regulations risk having responsibility incorrectly assigned, relying on estimated rather than verified data for reporting, and facing costs for regulatory breaches. ... A part of the Brambles Group, CHEP manages ~348 million pallets and containers through a network of 750+ service centres, employing approximately 10,600 people worldwide with its largest operations in North America and Europe.

headline: EPAL alarmuje UOKiK – czy za decyzją Biedronki stoi zmowa? – Gazeta Przemysłu Drzewnego
summary_text: > Organizacja działająca na rzecz producentów palet EPAL złożyła zawiadomienie do Urzędu Ochrony Konkurencji i Konsumentów. Podejrzewa nadużycie pozycji dominującej przez lidera rynku FMCG i zawarcie przez niego porozumienia, ograniczającego konkurencję na rynku palet drewnianych. Zdaniem EPAL Polska działania największej sieci handlowej w Polsce mogą prowadzić do ograniczenia konkurencji na rynku palet oraz osłabienia otwartego systemu wymiany europalet. W ocenie organizacji Biedronka, wykorzystując swoją silną pozycję na rynku zakupów FMCG, może narzucać dostawcom określone rozwiązania logistyczne, eliminując alternatywne systemy. ... W zawiadomieniu skierowanym do UOKiK EPAL Polska wskazuje również na możliwość zawarcia niedozwolonego porozumienia pomiędzy Jeronimo Martins Dystrybucja a CHEP Polska. Celem takiego działania miałoby być ograniczenie konkurencji ze strony otwartego systemu europalet. CHEP, którego udział w polskim rynku paletowym szacowany jest na 40–50%, jest jednym z największych operatorów systemów zamkniętych. Zdaniem EPAL eliminacja białych europalet z obiegu w największej sieci handlowej w kraju byłaby dla operatora niebieskich palet istotnym wzmocnieniem pozycji rynkowej. ... Zgodnie z planowanymi zasadami, od 1 sierpnia 2027 roku dostawcy, którzy dostarczą towary do Biedronki na białych europaletach, mają utracić je bezpowrotnie. Sieć miałaby przejmować takie palety na własność, traktując je jako „jednorazowe”. EPAL Polska wskazuje, że w praktyce oznacza to dodatkowe obciążenie finansowe dla dostawców, którzy staną przed wyborem: ponieść koszty przejścia na zamknięty system paletowy albo zaakceptować utratę własnych palet przy kolejnych dostawach. – Dostawca staje przed wyborem: ponieść dodatkowe koszty przejścia na system kolorowy lub tracić palety przy każdej dostawie. Przy skali dostaw do Biedronki ta kalkulacja wypada jednoznacznie – wyjaśnia Elżbieta Modzelewska-Wąchal, radca prawny specjalizująca się w prawie konkurencji. ... W zawiadomieniu EPAL wskazuje trzy potencjalne naruszenia przepisów ustawy antymonopolowej: - narzucanie warunków zakupu poprzez wymaganie od dostawców określonego rodzaju opakowań transportowych (art. 9 ust. 2 pkt 1), - działania ograniczające konkurencję i prowadzące do marginalizacji systemu palet białych (art. 9 ust. 2 pkt 5), - narzucanie uciążliwych warunków umów poprzez przejmowanie palet bez ekwiwalentu (art. 9 ust. 2 pkt 6). ... Organizacja zwróciła się również do UOKiK o zastosowanie środka zabezpieczającego, który zobowiązałby Biedronkę do dalszego przyjmowania dostaw na paletach białych do czasu zakończenia postępowania. Argumentem EPAL jest ryzyko trwałych i nieodwracalnych skutków rynkowych. Zdaniem organizacji wdrożenie nowych zasad może doprowadzić do likwidacji części zakładów produkujących i naprawiających europalety oraz zmusić dostawców do przejścia na zamknięte systemy poolingowe. – Jeśli setki producentów palet zbankrutują, zakłady naprawcze zamkną działalność, a dostawcy przestawią się na systemy zamknięte, powrót do stanu sprzed decyzji będzie nieosiągalny – przekonuje Roman Malicki. ... Co może zrobić UOKiK? Urząd może najpierw wszcząć postępowanie wyjaśniające, a następnie – jeśli znajdzie podstawy – postępowanie antymonopolowe. W przypadku potwierdzenia praktyk ograniczających konkurencję przedsiębiorstwom mogą grozić kary finansowe sięgające do 10% rocznego obrotu. Przy przychodach Biedronki przekraczających 100 mld zł potencjalna kara mogłaby sięgać miliardów złotych. Branża paletowa i logistyczna oczekują teraz na decyzję regulatora, która może mieć znaczenie dla całego rynku obrotu europaletami w Polsce.

headline: Revista FactorRH - Grupo Altex y CHEP impulsan modelo logístico circular
summary_text: Ante este panorama, empresas del sector alimentario impulsan soluciones que fortalecen la resiliencia de sus operaciones y contribuyen a reducir su impacto ambiental. Este es el caso de Grupo Altex, que recientemente obtuvo el Certificado de Sustentabilidad CHEP gracias a la implementación de un modelo circular, por medio de pallets reutilizables. “Frente a un entorno cada vez más retador a las necesidades del cliente, la eficiencia logística deja de ser únicamente una cuestión operativa para convertirse en un elemento estratégico, así como la resiliencia de las redes de suministro. "Soluciones basadas en la economía circular, como el reúso de pallets, ayudan a optimizar el movimiento de mercancías, mejorar la trazabilidad, reducir el impacto ambiental y fortalecer la resiliencia de la cadena de suministro, especialmente en sectores tan sensibles como el alimentario", comentó Carlos Álvarez, Strategy, Customer Experience, Marketing and Sustainability Director CHEP LatAm. ... Durante 2025, este modelo permitió a Grupo Altex 34,736 boards de madera evitados — equivalente a preservar 79 árboles—, evitar 909, 447 kilogramos de emisiones de CO₂ y evitar la generación de 89,664 kilogramos de residuos sólidos. Según estimaciones de la propia compañía, esta reducción de emisiones equivale a la capacidad de captura de carbono de 1,109 acres de bosque, mientras que el volumen de residuos evitados corresponde al que generaría 111 personas diariamente. CHEP, pionero en economía circular en el sector, contribuye a estos resultados a través de su sistema de pooling, basado en el uso compartido, recuperación y reutilización de pallets. Este modelo permite a las empresas avanzar hacia operaciones más eficientes y regenerativas, al tiempo que documenta sus beneficios ambientales y operativos mediante análisis independientes realizados bajo estándares internacionales de ciclo de vida. ... Con presencia en más de 25 países, operaciones industriales en Michoacán, Guanajuato, Tabasco, Nayarit, Veracruz, Estado de México y Baja California, y una reducción acumulada de 108 mil toneladas de CO₂ equivalente durante los últimos tres años, Grupo Altex continúa fortaleciendo una estrategia donde la sostenibilidad forma parte de la operación cotidiana del negocio.

The planned acquisition marks Triton Partners’ third acquisition of an Industrial Tech company this year. It is also the seventh acquisition overall for Triton Fund 6. headline: Inditex, Tageos and JD Sports headline a packed day two at RAIN in Action Madrid 2026 | RFID News
summary_text: RAIN in Action Madrid 2026 ran from 29 September to 1 October 2026 at the Novotel Madrid Centre, and the second day opened to a room that had outgrown the first. “There are some five hundred and some people here with us today,” RAIN Alliance president and chief executive Aileen Ryan told the Day 2 opening session on 30 September, noting “an extra 150 people also on site today” and that the previous evening’s reception had been “pretty full and it was pretty noisy”. The programme matched the turnout: a keynote, eight awards, two end-user presentations and a five-person panel, run back to back in a visibly packed venue, with Ryan cutting her own slides short to protect the schedule. ... We defend the infrastructure” The harder-edged part of the keynote was about who protects the conditions the technology depends on. Ryan put the Alliance’s membership at “over 200 member companies all around the world”, and framed that number as a negotiating position rather than a marketing statistic. > “If a small number of small companies went to a regulator to discuss a spectrum issue, the likelihood of them being listened to is pretty small. But if two hundred member companies, large and small, can go together and speak with one clear voice, now we have the opportunity to be heard.” The same gap applies when policymakers write law without knowing the technology exists. “They probably don’t know anything about this technology. They probably don’t know that this technology can help them, either in the implementation of the law or in testing compliance against it.” Her summary of the job was blunt: “We defend the infrastructure. The standards, the spectrum, the regulatory environment. And that’s what enables this community to make the impact.” Then an admission you rarely hear from a stage: that this work “is costly and time-consuming”, that a large share of membership fees goes on it every year, and that “in my opinion, we need to be spending more”. For a live example of why spectrum defence is not an abstraction, see our explainer on what NextNav’s 900 MHz plan would mean for RAIN RFID worldwide. ... The other awards recognised work that is almost invisible from outside the Alliance: representation to the European Commission on digital product passports, chairing the Asia Pacific advisory council, government affairs and spectrum defence, the RAIN Communication Interface simulator and the push to get RAIN support into smartphone operating systems, and encoding. On that last one, Ryan made the point that matters most to anyone starting a deployment: “If you get the encoding wrong, everything else is wrong too.” ... ## Tageos: 42.7 billion tags, and 0.5 per cent of the opportunity Matthieu Picon, co-founder and chief executive of Tageos, took the “next 100 billion tags” slot. Tageos is a French RFID inlay and label manufacturer based in Montpellier, with plants in Asia and the United States, best known for paper-based constructions that strip plastic and adhesive out of the tag. It ships to 49 countries and sells only through partners. Picon was unusually honest about a flat year. RAIN Alliance members shipped 42.7 billion UHF tag chips in 2025, short of expectations, which he put down to “very challenging international and commercial tensions”; he expects 2026 to recover “in the range of fifty billion”. Set against that, his estimate of the headroom was the figure worth writing down. > “We estimate only 0.5 per cent of RAIN potentially connected items are today connected.” Four forces will close that gap, he said: regulation, with digital product passports and food traceability rules both demanding “accessible and trustworthy product information”; the economics of visibility; automation, because “labour costs are increasing” while “workforce availability is decreasing”; and customer experience, from self-checkout to product authentication. The AI argument was the one he pressed hardest, and it was a warning rather than a pitch. ... The headline figure concerned loss prevention. Inditex has spent years trying to retire the detachable hard tag, which slows the till in stores seeing “more than 10,000 people a day”, in favour of RAIN tags built into the garment and readers at the entrance. Early trials went badly, with readers interfering with each ... The session closed with a panel, “Closing the Loop: RAIN in Action Across Retail, Recycling and the Green Transition”, moderated by Dr Susanne Guth-Orlowski, the RAIN Alliance’s digital product passport specialist. A digital product passport is the EU requirement that a product carry a data carrier linking to structured information about what it contains, where it came from and how it should be handled at end of life; we have covered what the EU DPP Registry rules mean for RFID separately. ... Dan McGrath, JD Group head of customer operations at JD Sports, the UK-headquartered sports fashion retailer, described a rollout measured in months: “It’s been a 14-month journey for us, and we’ve had a massive acceleration programme in terms of global adoption of RFID.” JD took 1,000 directly managed stores live in that window, and 2,700 across the wider group, work the retailer has since described as the end of phase one. What the data is for reaches past stock accuracy: “it’s very much about the transfer of ownership of that product from a factory to a brand, to also the retailer, but then also to the end consumer”. That chain of custody feeds ESG reporting, resale and authentication in a market where “there are a lot of fake goods”. ... Pressed on what “does not disturb the process” means in practice, Gomez was concrete. Quality thresholds differ by waste stream, so “I can give you 20 different answers”, but today a tag is harmless because “we just shred it”; the risk arrives when a recyclate has to meet a specification and the tag has pushed its metal content up. He also reported learning at the previous day’s tyre workshop, “less than 24 hours ago”, that tags can carry temperature and pressure sensing. Recycling plants lose time and material to fires started by batteries in the waste stream, and active sensing of those parameters “would be a game changer”. Guth-Orlowski took that as the argument for the event itself, noting how often a supply chain this large only discovers such things by sitting in the same room.

headline: What the FBI Phishing Warning Means for Event Planners
summary_text: A new warning from the FBI highlights a cybersecurity vulnerability familiar to the meetings industry: Attackers can exploit the trust people place in event invitations and communications. The latest warning focuses on cybercriminals impersonating government officials and other public figures. But the FBI says previous phishing campaigns used the same tactic, with attackers posing as event professionals and sending malicious links disguised as event invitations. Targets were then asked to verify their identities through an application controlled by the attacker. The tactic, known as OAuth consent phishing, presents a particular challenge for an industry that routinely sends registration links, invitations, speaker portals, calendar requests, and other digital communications to attendees. Unlike traditional phishing used to steal passwords, consent phishing persuades a target to authorize a malicious application to access an existing account, potentially allowing an attacker to read and send emails and access sensitive information. That access can persist even after the password is changed. ... “Event invitations carry built-in legitimacy and urgency,” said Mike Bushman, chief technology officer at RainFocus. “People expect to receive registration links and calendar invites from names they don't personally know but trust because of the brand hosting the event, and deadlines make people feel like they should click fast.” Taylor said organizers should make legitimate communications easier to verify by identifying the domains and vendors an event will use and providing contact information for checking suspicious messages. Attendees should also pay attention to the permissions an application requests, Bushman said. “Legitimate event registration rarely needs broad access to your email, files or contacts.” “Registering for a conference should never require granting an app access to a mailbox,” Taylor said. “If a consent screen appears after clicking an event link, the correct action is to close the window.” ... Taylor said the FBI alert demonstrates why meeting planners need closer relationships with their organizations’ IT and cybersecurity teams. One concern is shadow IT or shadow AI — applications and AI tools employees use without the knowledge or approval of their technology or security teams. “The natural inclination may be to search for tools that seem to add efficiency to operations,” Taylor said. “It is vital that new technology integrations be handled in the right way.” Because the attack relies on a user authorizing access rather than surrendering a password, the FBI warned that OAuth consent phishing can bypass password and multi-factor authentication protections. Taylor said victims should remove the application's access, change their password and notify their organization's IT or security team. Planners should also ask registration, housing, mobile app and matchmaking providers what permissions their products request and how quickly they would notify clients of a breach. “If a vendor can't answer clearly, that's the answer,” Taylor said. ... Taylor recommends adding cybersecurity guidance to communications attendees already read, including registration confirmations and know-before-you-go emails. Bushman recommends telling attendees the exact domains official communications will come from and which apps, if any, will request account access. ... ## Key Points - OAuth consent phishing tricks attendees into authorizing malicious apps to access their accounts, which bypasses password and multi-factor authentication protections and persists even after a password reset—making event invitations, registration links, and calendar requests a prime attack vector. - Organizers must take active responsibility for attendee security by specifying the exact domains and apps that official communications will use, vetting vendors on requested permissions and breach-notification speed, and building closer relationships with internal IT teams to avoid shadow IT/AI risks. - AI has made impersonation faster and more convincing, so planners should prepare for breaches in advance—running tabletop exercises, predefining who can alert attendees and how, and embedding cybersecurity guidance into existing communications like registration confirmations and know-before-you-go emails.

headline: Report: Business Travel Increasing, With Caveats | Associations Now
summary_text: Travel for events remains healthy, outpacing pre-Covid levels according to one new study, but attendee demands and expectations remain in flux. The Mid-Year State of Events Report, released last week by the marketing technology firm RainFocus, is based on a survey of approximately 100 events and meetings professionals. A majority of respondents (62 percent) said that attendance has increased in the past year, but that attendees are looking for opportunities for deeper engagement. For instance, the average number of sessions attended at an event has decreased in the past year, from 5.3 to 4.2, suggesting that there’s a greater appetite for workshops and deep-dive sessions than traditional keynotes and breakouts. ... The urge for connection—as well as attendees’ closer attention to budgets—means that planners are also designing shorter and more localized events, according to the survey. More than a third of planners (36 percent) said they planned to increase the number of “ancillary events,” and nearly half (49 percent) said they planned to increase the number of webinars they host.

headline: Meetings and Connection Key for Events in 2026, RainFocus Report Finds | RainFocus
summary_text: LINDON, Utah, September 2, 2026 – RainFocus™, provider of the next-generation event marketing platform, today released the 2026 Mid-Year State of Events Report, a data-driven analysis for event professionals, marketing leaders, and revenue teams seeking to understand and adapt to fundamental shifts in attendee expectations and event industry trends. The report offers a comprehensive look at how organizations are redesigning event programs to drive real business impact and enhance attendee engagement in the evolving 2026 event landscape. ... ## What It Means for Event Professionals The report’s findings reflect a fundamental shift in what attendees expect and what organizations need from their events. Event teams are hosting up to three times more meetings at their events compared to last year. In addition, at the end of 2025, 36% of companies surveyed said they planned to host smaller ancillary events, roadshows, and webinars in 2026, with small-event attendance up 6.4% year-over-year. The report also highlighted 69% more meeting participation at small events, a trend continuing in 2026. As AI becomes more embedded in everyday work, event attendees are finding greater value in experiences that feel human and trustworthy. The most impactful events create opportunities to build genuine relationships and catalyze career development. Alongside the data findings, the report offers concrete steps that event teams can take to improve the attendee experience and their company’s ROI from events. ... The report covers five key areas: connection-first event design, the rise of smaller event formats, sponsor activation strategies, AI and data adoption, and the evolving role of event professionals. Key takeaways for optimizing event programs and achieving business objectives include: - Designing for Connection: Average session attendance per person dropped from 5.3 sessions in spring 2025 to 4.2 sessions in spring 2026, while meeting participation rose sharply, signaling that attendees are gravitating to networking opportunities over passively viewing presentations. - Small Events Bring Big ROI: As attendance, session, and meeting participation across smaller in-person events rise year-over-year, their value increases. Small events are a strong source of rich attendee behavioral data, contributing to more complete customer profiles over time. - Traditional Event Roles Are Evolving: When event professionals connect event data to pipeline and revenue metrics to prove business impact, they can earn a seat as strategic advisors to leadership.

headline: RainFocus adds two Adobe AEM integrations for event teams
summary_text: # RainFocus connects event data directly to Adobe Experience Manager, closing the content supply chain gap for enterprise marketers RainFocus has integrated its platform with Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) to enhance data synchronization capabilities. The new integrations allow synchronization of event session, speaker, and exhibitor data directly into AEM. This advancement aims to improve brand governance and streamline content supply chain processes for enterprise marketers. ... RainFocus on July 14 announced two new integrations with Adobe Experience Manager: the AEM Sites Connector and the AEM Content Advisor. The additions extend a content supply chain that already includes a RainFocus and Adobe Workfront Fusion integration, giving enterprise event teams a connected pipeline that runs from project intake through web publishing without manual data handoffs, according to the company's announcement on PR Newswire. The platform hosts more than 10,000 events annually and earned a Leader designation in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Event Marketing and Management Platforms for the third consecutive year. The new integrations are designed specifically for the operational pain points those teams face: duplicate data entry, asset version sprawl, and delayed website updates when speaker or session details change. ... The Sites Connector maps RainFocus data fields, session titles, speaker bios, exhibitor profiles, directly to AEM Content Fragments using the platform's native authoring environment. Updates can be pushed on demand or on a configured schedule, removing the need for a developer or content manager to manually replicate changes across web properties. For teams managing a large user conference with thousands of speaker profiles, that means real-time accuracy without proportional staffing increases. The Content Advisor takes a different angle. Instead of pushing event data into AEM, it pulls approved AEM assets into the RainFocus interface through a native modal browser. Marketers building event emails or landing pages can search that library using natural language descriptions rather than exact file names or metadata strings, a function powered by AI-powered semantic search built into the integration. Only assets that have been individually approved in AEM Assets are visible, which enforces brand compliance at the point of creation rather than in a downstream review cycle. ... The Workfront Fusion integration, announced earlier, handles the upstream portion: automatically creating events in RainFocus from approved Workfront requests, standardizing templates, and automating handoffs between planning and production teams. Together the three integrations cover the full arc from a marketing brief through a published event web page. ... Both integrations are available through the RainFocus Integration Suite. The Sites Connector requires installing a connector package in AEM and authenticating via OAuth before field mapping can begin. The Content Advisor is enabled at the organizational level first, then individual users authenticate to access their approved asset sets. Neither route requires custom development work, which matters for enterprise teams operating under change-management constraints. RainFocus maintains ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, and SOC 2 Type II compliance across all five trust criteria, a relevant detail for procurement and security teams evaluating the platform alongside existing Adobe enterprise agreements. Organizations already running AEM and Workfront can add these connectors within the existing Adobe licensing framework, though specific contract terms would require direct engagement with both vendors.

headline: Edible oil refiners to scoop 10-12% revenue growth despite lower duty
summary_text: ### Edible oil refiners to scoop 10-12% revenue growth despite lower duty Strong cash flows, stable margins and controlled debt levels to keep credit profiles resilient ## India's edible oil refiners are set to clock healthy revenue growth of 10-12% this fiscal despite a lowering of import duty on crude edible oil. That compares with 14-16% growth last fiscal, which benefited from a price rise in the second half. While the duty cut this September would soften domestic realisations in the second half of this fiscal, elevated global edible oil prices, strong first-half performance and improving consumption would support revenue growth. An analysis of 84 edible oil refiners rated by us, accounting for nearly half of the industry's revenue, indicates that healthy cash generation, stable profitability and controlled leverage will continue to support their credit profiles. India imports over 60% of its edible oil requirement, making the industry highly sensitive to global price movements. Crude palm oil (CPO), which accounts for more than half of India's edible oil imports, is the key pricing benchmark for the domestic edible oil basket. Consequently, movements in global CPO prices are quickly transmitted to domestic markets. Global edible oil prices are expected to remain elevated this fiscal amid weather-related supply concerns in major producing regions and sustained biodiesel demand. Crisil Ratings expects global CPO prices to rise 9-11% this fiscal. While higher production of soybean, sunflower and mustard oils could provide some relief, tight palm oil supplies are likely to keep global edible oil prices firm. In the first half of the current fiscal, global CPO prices rose 11-13%, pushing average landed costs to around $1,240 per tonne. Coupled with import duties of 16.5% on crude edible oils, this led to higher domestic edible oil prices and stronger realisations for refiners. To moderate food inflation and improve affordability, the Government of India recently reduced import duties on crude edible oils. Consequently, the effective import duty on crude palm and soybean oils has declined to 11.0% from 16.5%, and that on crude sunflower oil to 5.5% from 16.5%. However, a meaningful duty differential between crude and refined oils remains, continuing to support domestic refining activity. Says Rahul Guha, Senior Director, Crisil Ratings, “The duty rationalisation should temper industry realisations by 5-6% in the second half, but the resultant improvement in affordability should lend fresh impetus to consumption. The full-year picture, however, remains favourable, with firm global edible oil prices and strong first-half realisations expected to keep average realisations 8-10% above last fiscal.” Consumption has remained resilient despite higher prices and is expected to strengthen further as lower retail prices improve affordability in the second half, particularly during the festive season. Demand is likely to grow across households, food processing companies and the hotel, restaurant and catering (HoReCa) segment. Overall edible oil consumption is projected to rise 2.7-3.0% to about ~26.5 million metric tonne this fiscal. Thus, the combination of higher average realisations and healthy volume growth should drive robust industry revenue growth this fiscal, despite softer pricing in the second half. Says Jayashree Nandakumar, Director, Crisil Ratings, “Healthy volume growth and operating leverage should support profitability. Ebitda per tonne is seen up 10-12% from last fiscal to ~Rs 3,850-3,950. Inventory gains of the first half are likely to offset softer pricing in the second half, keeping operating margins broadly stable at 3.4-3.6%, while prudent hedging should limit the impact of commodity price volatility.” With demand rising steadily, refiners have expanded capacity over the years. This fiscal, the capex of refiners rated by is seen at Rs 1,600-1,800 crore, translating into ~10% increase in refining capacity. Prudent funding of capex, supported by healthy cash accruals, should keep incremental borrowings in check and support stable credit profiles. Net cash accrual to total debt and interest coverage are expected to remain comfortable at around 0.17 time and 2.4 times, respectively, this fiscal. Total outside liabilities to adjusted net worth is expected to remain range-bound at 1.5-1.7 times over the medium term. The trajectory of global edible oil prices, developments in the Middle East, changes in India's import duty regime and evolving global trade dynamics will remain key monitorables for the sector.

The backdrop is an intensifying campaign against Russia's oil infrastructure. According to a Meduza report drawing on a BBC Russian Service interview, an underground network called Chernaya Iskra, or Black Spark, says it has helped Ukraine strike nine refineries across Russia since September 2025, including the Omsk refinery, the country's largest by crude processing volume. White oils are highly refined mineral oils used across pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, food processing and industrial applications, and disruption to a major processing hub such as Omsk can tighten global availability and lift prices for the product and its feedstock. For Indian white oil and speciality petroleum makers such as Gandhar Oil Refinery and Panama Petrochem, firmer international prices can support realisations, though the effect on margins depends on how their own input costs move at the same time. There are two sides to how such supply disruptions play through to these companies. Higher global white oil prices can improve realisations and, if input costs lag, widen margins for Indian producers who can supply into markets facing shortages. At the same time, these players rely on crude derived feedstock themselves, so a broad rise in oil prices tied to the same geopolitical tension can raise their costs, which is why the net impact is not uniform and depends on the timing and spread of price moves across the chain. ... headline: Merger Alert: Tribunal approves FPG’s acquisition of Constantia Emporium and transaction involving offshore oil and gas exploration
summary_text: ##### Notice The following Merger Alert is for information purposes only and is not binding on the Competition Tribunal or any member of the Tribunal ##### Lead Text The Tribunal has unconditionally approved a merger that will see FPG Holdings (Pty) Ltd acquire sole control of the Constantia Emporium shopping entre and adjacent vacant land; as well as a transaction involving offshore oil and gas exploration... ##### Type of matter Large merger Large merger ##### Parties involved FPG Holdings (Pty) Ltd and the immovable property and shopping centre known as Constantia Emporium as well adjacent erven Impact Energies Ltd And Impact Africa Ltd together with certain related Assets ... ##### Tribunal Decision Approved without conditions Approved without conditions ... Tribunal approves transaction involving offshore oil and gas exploration The Tribunal has unconditionally approved a merger in which Impact Energies Ltd (“Impact Energies”) will acquire Impact Africa Ltd (“IAL”) and related assets involving offshore petroleum exploration rights along South Africa’s coast. Impact Energies is controlled by Deepkloof Ltd, which is ultimately a subsidiary of diversified South African investment group, Hosken Consolidated Investments Ltd (“HCI”). HCI has interests spanning energy, media and broadcasting, transport, property, hospitality and other sectors. The assets comprise participating interests in offshore oil and gas exploration rights. These rights permit exploration for petroleum within defined offshore areas but do not confer a production right.
