headline: Metcash exercises right to acquire Peries Group of IGA Supermarkets | RW
summary_text: Metcash Limited has announced that following receipt of a First Rights Notice, the Company has exercised its right and entered into a binding agreement to acquire the Peries Group, a leading Queensland-based food business. The Peries Group operates 15 medium and large-format IGA supermarkets across Queensland, spanning South-East, Central, Far North and Wide Bay-Burnett regions. The supermarkets business generated approximately $264 million in retail sales in FY26 [1] and employs around 1000 people. Metcash’s wholesale sales to the Peries Group were ~$150 million in the same year. The acquisition follows the recent receipt by Metcash of a First Rights Notice from Peries under existing contractual arrangements, following their decision to sell the business. Metcash’s acceptance of that notice has prompted the immediate entry into a binding business sale agreement. ... The acquisition is expected to help protect, grow and strengthen the IGA network in the strategically important Queensland market which has delivered stronger retail and wholesale growth than most other states over the past three years. “Metcash currently holds a 45% share of the Queensland-based Cornetts Group that operates 35 supermarkets. “The Peries Group has meaningful retail scale, strong regional market positions and an established operating platform. Its store network is concentrated in regional Queensland markets where IGA has a very strong customer proposition and, in several communities, is the leading or only full-line grocery offering. “Metcash’s primary objective is to retain the stores within, and for the benefit of, the IGA network and accordingly will actively assess the optimal long-term ownership structure for the stores, which may include divestments or joint venture arrangements with independent operators, consistent with prior practice.” ... Transaction details Metcash estimates the purchase price [2] to be between $80 – $85 million [3], funded through debt facilities. The transaction is expected to be marginally earnings per share accretive. Completion of the acquisition is anticipated by end of April / early May 2027, and remains subject to customary conditions, including lease assignments and approval from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission. Further details will be provided with the Company’s 1H27 financial results materials scheduled for release on 7 December 2026.

headline: Alta takes control of Serbia’s Idea, Mercator and Roda network as €780 million retail business faces profitability test - Doing Business in Serbia - Serbia business country gateway, companies industry sectors
summary_text: Serbia’s Alta Group has completed its acquisition of the Idea, Mercator and Roda retail businesses from Croatia’s Fortenova Group, taking control of a nationwide food distribution and retail network whose annual revenue approaches €780 million but whose deteriorating profitability presents a significant operational and financial restructuring challenge. The transaction, completed on October 13, transfers ownership of Idea Marketi and four associated businesses involved in fresh-food distribution, customer loyalty programmes, property operations and information technology. The acquisition gives Alta Retail access to more than 300 retail outlets operating across over 80 Serbian cities and municipalities. The system employs thousands of workers and maintains commercial relationships with more than 600 suppliers. The purchase price and financing structure have not been publicly disclosed. ... ## Financial performance makes restructuring central to the acquisition According to reported figures from Idea Marketi’s 2025 financial statements, operating revenue declined approximately 14% to €780 million, from around €911 million a year earlier. The company recorded a net loss of approximately €34.5 million, compared with a loss of around €3.2 million in 2024. EBITDA declined by approximately one-third to €50.3 million. These figures indicate that the retail network maintained positive earnings before financing costs, depreciation and other charges but failed to translate operating activity into a positive final financial result. For the new owner, improving profitability may require a combination of procurement savings, better inventory management, improved store productivity, property-cost optimisation and stronger customer retention. ... returns The acquisition includes Enna Fruit Grocka, a business involved in fresh-fruit and vegetable supply, as well as Super Kartica, M-Profil SPV and mStart Business Solutions. This structure gives Alta control over more than retail storefronts. Distribution capacity, supplier relationships, customer data and technology platforms are important sources of potential operational improvements. Fresh-food logistics are particularly relevant because spoilage, transportation efficiency, inventory turnover and product availability directly influence retail profitability. Investments in refrigerated distribution, warehouse automation and demand forecasting could improve operational performance, although no detailed investment programme has yet been published. For domestic food producers and agricultural suppliers, the ownership change could also influence purchasing arrangements, payment terms and opportunities to enter the retail network. Serbia’s food retail sector remains highly competitive, making it difficult for operators to protect margins without continuously improving distribution and purchasing efficiency. ... The undisclosed purchase consideration leaves important questions about the transaction’s financial structure. A retail acquisition of this scale can involve several financing requirements beyond the initial payment to the seller. The new owner may need to fund store renovation, information-system integration, warehouse improvements, supplier obligations and working-capital requirements. Retail businesses generate substantial cash receipts but also carry significant payment commitments to suppliers, property owners and employees. The management of these cash flows can become especially important during a change of ownership. Commercial banks and other lenders assessing the enlarged business will focus on sustainable EBITDA, debt-service capacity, inventory turnover, lease liabilities and the quality of operating cash flows.

headline: Europe roundup: Lidl’s new look, Zabka update & more | IGD Retail Analysis
summary_text: ## Normal accelerates Central and Eastern European expansion with Romania debut Danish variety discounter Normal has officially entered Romania, marking another milestone in its expansion strategy. The retailer opened its first Romanian store in Mega Mall Bucharest on 30 September, followed by a second location in Shopping City Timișoara on 2 October, through a partnership with retail real estate investment firm NEPI Rockcastle. First reported in July, the transaction would add Zabka’s more than 13,000 stores across Poland and Romania, together with its expanding online operations, to Couche-Tard’s portfolio. With approval now secured, Zabka is expected to be de-listed from the Warsaw stock exchange before becoming part of the Couche-Tard group alongside Circle K. Analyst, Theo O’Flynn’s view: > Polish regulatory approval removes an important obstacle to the deal progressing. Bringing the two businesses together would combine Couche-Tard’s international scale and purchasing strength with Zabka’s advanced digital capabilities and innovative approach to convenience. The Green-score, which rates products from A+ to F based on lifecycle assessments and other environmental criteria, is now displayed on more than 4,800 private label products and 11,000 national-brand products across the retailer's banners. Colruyt Group has also rebranded its sustainability-focused loyalty programme as “Every Step Counts”, rewarding shoppers for choosing products with stronger Green-scores and converting those choices into shopper benefits or support for social and environmental causes. Insight Partner, Dan Butler’s view: > the certification gives Colruyt Group a first-mover advantage as retailers and brands across Europe adapt to EmpCo, which is designed to crack down on unverified environmental claims and improve transparency around sustainability communications. By independently validating its Green-score methodology, Colruyt Group can continue using environmental labels with greater credibility while encouraging suppliers to provide more robust sustainability data, helping them prepare for a stricter regulatory environment. ... ## Lidl Denmark begins rollout of new store concept Lidl Denmark has begun the first phase of a programme to introduce its new store concept across the country, following successful trials in several locations. headline: Sobeys, Safeway parent Empire refuses tariff price hikes
summary_text: Fewer food items are seeing price increases related to tariffs despite the escalating trade dispute between Canada and the United States, executives from grocery chain Empire Co. Ltd. say. “It is minimal impact on our business this time around,” chief customer officer Luc L’Archevêque told analysts during the company’s fiscal first-quarter earnings call on Thursday. While the grocery retailer — whose banners include Sobeys, Safeway, FreshCo and Farm Boy — received a handful of requests from suppliers to raise prices, L’Archevêque said it hasn’t accepted any so far. “Our position will remain the same as the first time around: it’s too early, so we won’t accept any cost increases related to tariffs, and we’ll work very closely with our supplier partners to find solutions,” he said. ... Earlier this week, Canada’s retaliatory duties, ranging from 15 to 50 per cent, kicked in on a laundry list of imports from the United States, including food products like dairy, molasses and honey, matching the dollar value of duties the U.S. imposed on Aug. 22. That further prompted U.S. President Donald Trump to introduce new tariffs and outright bans on some Canadian exports starting Sept. 29. ... But grocers are finding themselves better positioned more than a year after the tariff war initially flared up between the two countries. Since then, all the major players — Empire, Loblaw and Metro — have established stronger relationships with local and non-U.S. suppliers to be able to offer more alternatives to tariffed food items and better respond to a resurgence of the buy Canadian sentiment among shoppers. ... headline: Impact Handling to become Aprolis Handling in UK rebrand - Materials Handling World News
summary_text: # Impact Handling to become Aprolis Handling in UK rebrand 8 Sep 2026 | by MHW Magazine Team | Logistics, News, Warehouse The materials handling specialist will transition to the Aprolis Handling name over the coming months Impact Handling is to be renamed Aprolis Handling as the materials handling specialist moves closer to its French parent company five years after being acquired. The rebrand follows Aprolis Group’s acquisition of the UK business in 2021 and is intended to create a more unified identity across its European operations. Founded in Hull in 1985, Impact Handling has grown from a regional supplier into a nationwide provider of forklift trucks, warehouse equipment and materials handling solutions. Its offering includes counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks, powered pallet trucks, stackers, warehouse equipment and specialist machinery for different industries and operating environments. The business also provides servicing, maintenance and fleet support throughout the equipment lifecycle. Impact Handling has maintained a long-standing relationship with Cat Lift Trucks, while also working with manufacturers including Carer, Konecranes and Mol. The company said the rebrand follows a period of growth since joining Aprolis Group and will support further expansion in the UK. Steve Shakespeare, chief executive of Aprolis UK, said the company had deliberately retained the Impact Handling name following the acquisition because of its established reputation. “When Aprolis Group initially acquired Impact, we deliberately made the decision to retain the company name because of the strong reputation the business had built over many years and the respect it commanded throughout the industry,” he said. ... The transition will become increasingly visible over the coming months as the Aprolis Handling name is introduced across the business. Shakespeare said the change was designed to retain the foundations of the existing operation while opening up new opportunities through the wider group. “The rebrand builds on the strong foundations that have made the business successful, while creating new opportunities for the future with the support, investment and expertise of Aprolis,” he said. ... Aprolis Group specialises in the sale, rental and maintenance of industrial materials handling equipment and operates in markets including France, the UK, Spain, Italy, Portugal, Luxembourg and China. The group forms the materials handling division of Monnoyeur, a France-headquartered family-owned business operating across 23 countries. Monnoyeur employs more than 9,000 people and reports annual revenues of more than €3.4 billion, with operations spanning construction, industrial, energy and agricultural equipment.

headline: TrevIQ | Analiză rezultate semestriale (S1 2026). Profit în scădere, miza pe finalul anului
summary_text: IMPACT a raportat pentru S1 2026 un profit net consolidat de 5.98 mil. RON, în scădere cu 87% YoY, pe fondul unui număr redus de apartamente livrate și al unui prim trimestru încheiat pe pierdere. Rezultatele au rămas mult sub cele din 2025 și acoperă doar circa 13% din profitul net anual bugetat, într-un model de afaceri concentrat pe livrări în a doua jumătate a anului. Compania mizează pe un portofoliu amplu, 970 de unități în construcție și pre-vânzări solide la ARIA Verdi - pentru a recupera în T3-T4, însă blocajul de la ANCPI amenință calendarul livrarilor și recunoașterea veniturilor. ... S1 2026 a fost un semestru slab: IMPACT a ratat clar nivelurile din 2025, atât pe venituri, cât și pe profit. La nivel de grup, veniturile consolidate au totalizat 112.1 mil. RON (-37% YoY), iar profitul net a coborât la 5.98 mil. RON, de la 45.5 mil. RON în S1 2025. Deteriorarea a venit din livrări: numărul unităților rezidențiale vândute a scăzut la 31 (de la 153), iar suprafața vândută cu 78%. Primul trimestru a fost pe pierdere (venituri de 55.4 mil. RON și o pierdere netă de circa 0.7 mil. EUR), afectat de scumpirea TVA, de inflație și de un mediu de cerere mai selectiv. Revenirea pe profit în T2 s-a sprijinit în mare parte pe câștiguri din reevaluarea investițiilor imobiliare de 21.6 mil. RON, fără impact în numerar; excluzând acest efect, rezultatul operațional de bază a fost aproape de zero. La nivel individual, veniturile au fost de 29.5 mil. RON (-64% YoY), iar profitul net de 19.6 mil. RON (-66%). Profitul individual, mai mare decât cel consolidat, este susținut de venituri financiare de 16.3 mil. RON (în principal dividende și dobânzi intragrup); la nivel de grup, aceste sume se elimina, astfel că rezultatul consolidat (5.98 mil. RON) este reperul mai reprezentativ pentru performanța operațiunii. ... Raportat la BVC 2026 realizarea la jumătatea anului este redusă: circa 26% din venituri și doar 13% din profitul net anual prognozat. Este un profil puternic dependent de semestrul doi, specific dezvoltării imobiliare, unde veniturile se recunosc la finalizarea și predarea unităților. ... Cel mai important reper pentru recuperarea din a doua jumătate a anului este portofoliul aflat în execuție. La 30 iunie 2026, compania avea autorizații de construire pentru 2,496 de unități (292,532 mp), din care 970 de unități (valoare brută de dezvoltare 1.68 mld. RON) se află în construcție în trei proiecte: 435 în GREENFIELD Baneasa, 401 în ARIA Verdi și 134 în BOREAL Plus. În S1, IMPACT a vândut unități de 24.4 mil. RON și a pre-vândut 70 de apartamente în valoare de 98.5 mil. RON, din care 70.8 mil. RON provin din ARIA Verdi, proiectul mixed-use de lux din Barbu Văcărescu lansat la începutul anului. Stocul de apartamente finalizate, disponibile imediat la vânzare, era de 308.6 mil. RON, iar centrul comercial GREENFIELD Plaza (grad de ocupare peste 97%) a adus venituri din chirii de 3.74 mil. RON. Conducerea a încadrat 2026 drept un an de tranziție către cel mai amplu ciclu de dezvoltare anunțat (2026-2034): 7,870 de unități rezidențiale, o suprafață brută de 892,204 mp și o valoare brută de dezvoltare de 1.68 mld. EUR. Pentru finanțare, compania a aprobat în AGA un program de răscumpărare de acțiuni și pregătește o emisiune de obligațiuni de până la 50 mil. EUR. Compania a inițiat, începând cu 20.08.2026, programul de răscumpărare a maximum 50,000 de acțiuni (0.04% din capital), în limita a 250,000 RON și la un preț de maximum 6 RON/acțiune, pentru alocarea către angajați/administratori/directori și anularea parțială a acțiunilor, programul fiind autorizat până la 23.01.2028. ... Pe partea de context, piața rezidențială trece printr-un blocaj administrativ major. Noile reguli introduse prin Legea 207/2025 (obligația de preapartamentare, plafon de 5% la rezervări, conturi distincte pentru avansuri) întârzie recunoașterea veniturilor conform IFRS 15 - efect vizibil deja la alți dezvoltatori. În plus, un atac cibernetic asupra ANCPI (14 iulie 2026) a paralizat sistemul e-Terra și cartea funciară, blocând mii de tranzacții. Parlamentul a prelungit până la 30 septembrie 2026 termenul pentru păstrarea cotei reduse de TVA de 9% la locuințe noi. ... Față de One United Properties, IMPACT se tranzacționează la un discount consistent pe activul net. P/BV (preț/valoare contabilă) este de circa 0.5x, adică acțiunea cotează la aproximativ jumătate din capitalul propriu contabil, față de 1x la ONE. Raportat la activul net evaluat la prețul pieței (NAV de 263.4 mil. EUR), discountul este și mai mare: P/NAV de circa 0.37x. Discountul reflectă însă fundamente mai slabe: rentabilitatea capitalului propriu (ROE) este redusă, 1-2%, față de //12% la ONE, iar profitul volatil (aproape de break-even în ultimele 12 luni) face ca P/E istoric să fie nerelevant. Pe profitul bugetat prin BVC pentru 2026, P/E forward ar fi de circa 11x. ... ## Riscuri - Blocajul ANCPI: atacul cibernetic asupra cadastrului (e-Terra nefuncțional din 14 iulie) și noile reguli de preapartamentare pot întârzia perfectarea vânzărilor și recunoașterea veniturilor tocmai în semestrul de care depinde atingerea BVC. - Profit volatil și dependent de reevaluări: profitul S1 s-a sprijinit pe câștiguri din reevaluări (21.6 mil. RON), fără impact în numerar; operațiunile de bază au fost aproape la break-even, iar realizarea BVC pe profit este redusă la jumătatea anului. - Cerere și finanțare: cererea rezidențială este temperată de TVA majorat și de dobânzi încă ridicate, în timp ce ciclul de investiții 2026-2034 și emisiunea de obligațiuni de până la 50 mil. EUR cresc nevoia de finanțare și expunerea la costul creditului.

headline: Michael Hill picks Impact Analytics for AI merchandise planning | The Datatech Times
summary_text: The fine jewellery retailer will deploy Impact Analytics' AI-native platform across demand forecasting, replenishment and assortment planning in three markets. ... Michael Hill, the international fine jewellery retailer operating more than 280 stores across Australia, New Zealand and Canada, has selected Impact Analytics to overhaul its merchandise planning capabilities. The deployment will cover demand forecasting, inventory replenishment, store clustering and assortment planning, consolidating those functions onto a single AI-native SaaS platform. The contract follows a competitive evaluation process in which Michael Hill said it prioritised retail-specific AI maturity over general-purpose planning tools. Richard Price, Head of Supply Chain Systems at Michael Hill, cited confidence in the forecasting engine as a decisive factor, particularly for high-value, low-volume product categories such as fine jewellery. "Accurate forecasting underpins every planning decision we make, and the results we saw across our assortment reinforced that we had selected the right partner," he said. ... Matt Keays, Chief Technology Officer at Michael Hill, framed the change as a structural shift in how planning teams operate, moving from spreadsheet-driven, line-by-line analysis to an exceptions-management model. The company did not disclose contract value, implementation timeline or the name of any incumbent vendor being replaced. ... Impact Analytics, founded over a decade ago, positions its platform as purpose-built for retail rather than adapted from manufacturing or FMCG planning systems. The vendor says its platform is powered by more than one million machine learning models and covers end-to-end planning, pricing and promotions. The company has previously highlighted recognition from Inc. 5000 and the RIS Leaderboard, though independently verified benchmark comparisons were not included in the announcement. ... ## Regulatory and standards read-across Because Impact Analytics processes transaction and inventory data across three jurisdictions, the deployment will need to satisfy data-handling requirements under Australia's Privacy Act, New Zealand's Privacy Act 2020 and Canada's PIPEDA, with the latter currently undergoing reform under Bill C-27. None of those obligations were addressed in the release, and Michael Hill's data-residency arrangements with the vendor are not publicly disclosed. The broader enterprise AI procurement context is also shifting: the EU AI Act's requirements for high-risk AI systems do not apply here, but both UK and Australian regulators have signalled interest in transparency obligations for algorithmic decision-making tools used in commercial settings. For now, retail planning AI sits outside mandatory disclosure regimes, but enterprise buyers are increasingly asking vendors for explainability documentation as part of their own governance frameworks.

headline: Regus expands into Johor on rising demand
summary_text: Sunday 25 Oct 2026 KUALA LUMPUR: Regus plc, the world’s largest provider of flexible workspace, has expanded into Johor, riding on the robust investment activities in the southern state. Regus Management (M) Sdn Bhd (Regus Malaysia) opened a business centre in Johor Baru City Square office tower in April this year. “We are targeting the manufacturing, logistics, biodiesel business and other project-based business,” Regus Malaysia country manager Vijayakumar Tangarasan told The Edge Financial Daily in a recent interview. Measuring about 8,000 sq ft, he expects demand to come from multinational companies (MNCs), small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and start-ups. Vijayakumar said business activities have started to pick up in Johor, which is also seeing an improvement in its infrastructure. He noted that there is massive development in the state, not only in Iskandar Malaysia, but also Senai, Skudai and Pasir Gudang. “We did not see a slowdown in Iskandar Malaysia last year, but we expect investments to pick up due to the tax relief and other benefits provided,” he explained. Despite the glut and overdevelopment in Iskandar Malaysia, the robust activities in Johor are expected to provide opportunities for local SMEs and MNCs. Vijayakumar sees Johor being developed into a logistics hub over the next three years and Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) Refinery and Petrochemical Integrated Development project in Pengerang boosting demand for serviced offices. Regus provides more flexibility to its clients in terms of the tenure and the rental space, enabling cost savings for businesses. Its other services include virtual office (VO) and business lounge membership. VO provides it clients a business address in the right place, a local contact number answered in their company name, and a team that manages calls and handles mails. Regus' Businessworld exclusive membership scheme allows its clients to access its business lounges across its network. Describing it as the “right time” for Regus to expand into Johor, Vijayakumar said some of the project-based companies do not look for conventional office space, but smaller and more flexible workspace like what Regus has got to offer. He also pointed out Johor’s proximity to Singapore has played a role to increase demand for serviced offices in the state where rental costs and labour costs are comparatively lower. “We are going into Iskandar Malaysia in a year’s time. The demand is already there,” he added. Regus Malaysia is also looking to expand into Pasir Gudang, Skudai and Tampoi. headline: Regus Launches Its First Business Center in Haikou_大风号_凤凰网
summary_text: # Regus Launches Its First Business Center in Haikou 2026年10月14日 14:38:43 来自北京市 For companies exploring the Hainan market, entrepreneurs starting out with a small team, and business travelers in need of a professional workspace for a short-term engagement and flexibility can be just as important as location. The newly opened Regus Haikou Center aims to meet these needs by providing fully equipped offices and workstations that can be rented for periods ranging from several hours to longer terms. The center officially began operations in Haikou, the provincial capital of the island province in Southern China in late September, marking Regus' first business center in the city. Why Regus Is Entering Hainan Now As a brand under IWG, a global leader in flexible workspace solutions, the launch raises an important question: Why has Regus chosen this moment to expand into Hainan? According to Su Hongtao, head of the Regus Haikou Center, the immediate driver is the accelerating pace of business activity in Hainan, fueled by the policies of the Hainan Free Trade Port. "As the development of the Hainan FTP continues to advance, Hainan is increasingly becoming a buzzword in the business world," Su said. "That has also drawn the attention of Regus." The trend is reflected in the latest business-registration figures. In the first half of this year, Hainan registered 124,700 new enterprises, up 90.09 percent year on year. Among them, 1,303 were newly established foreign-funded enterprises, representing an increase of 38.62 percent from a year earlier. "These figures show that more and more companies are looking to establish a presence in Hainan," Su said. "As policies supporting the FTP become increasingly comprehensive — including reforms to facilitate the registration of foreign-funded enterprises and the implementation of cross-regional mutual recognition mechanisms — more companies are expected to set up operations here. This means significant market potential for us in Hainan." ... Unlike conventional business incubators or fixed-term office leasing models, Regus provides flexible workspace solutions tailored to different business needs. The Regus Haikou Center occupies approximately 1,500 square meters and follows Regus' standardized global interior design and service standards. It provides a range of services, including front-desk reception, meeting-room reservations and business support. The center has 60 private offices and around 200 workstations, offering spaces for day-to-day operations, business meetings and negotiations. Entrepreneurs and companies can rent an entire office or simply a workstation, with rental periods ranging from longer-term arrangements to as little as half a day. The flexibility is further supported by IWG's global network, which spans more than 120 countries and regions. Members can access and rent space at approximately 4,700 IWG locations around the world, allowing them to maintain a professional working environment without having to search for a new office every time they enter a different market. ... The opening of the Regus Haikou Center also adds a new dimension to the business-service ecosystem of the Hainan FTP. A representative of Haikou's Xiuying District, where the center is located, said the center helps address the demand among companies entering Hainan and individuals starting businesses for lightweight and flexible office space, reducing the uncertainty and decision-making pressure involved in establishing a presence on the island. In this sense, the center can serve as a "buffer" for companies exploring the Hainan market before making larger, longer-term commitments. ... The representative noted that in April this year, the Global Service Center – Hainan Station was established at the same address, providing an integrated platform combining business services, policy consultation and resource connections. The two facilities serve complementary functions. The Global Service Center – Hainan Station focuses more on government services, policy consultation and connections with industry resources, while the Regus Haikou Center provides an international workspace and professional operational services. Together, they extend the building's service offering beyond conventional office leasing to cover a broader range of functions, including government liaison, business operations and resource coordination. Companies based at the site can connect with local government services, tap into the surrounding business ecosystem and access value-added services such as business registration and tax services, legal consultation, and investment and financing matchmaking. At the same time, the international-standard workspace enables companies to begin operations as soon as they establish a presence in Hainan.

headline: Brave drives 51% higher ROI for IWG’s Regus Flexible Workspace brand
summary_text: B ... # Brave drives 51% higher ROI for IWG’s Regus Flexible Workspace brand Brave | August 20, 2026 | Brave IWG expands Brave search campaigns after finding incremental, high-intent demand beyond its established paid search channels London, UK, 20th August 2026: Brave Browser & Search Engine, the independent, privacy-first browser and search engine, today revealed how IWG is using Brave to reach incremental, high-intent demand beyond the major search platforms, with performance significantly outperforming its established search channels. IWG, the world’s largest flexible workspace provider and owner of the Regus office brand, maintains an always-on presence on the major paid search platforms to drive bookings for its workspaces and meeting rooms. Early in 2026, the company began looking for additional sources of demand that could complement its existing search activity and reach incremental audiences. IWG subsequently tested Brave in the UK and US, using two search advertising formats: Keyword Triggered, which places an ad at the top of Brave Search results for relevant queries, and Organic Triggered, which turns a brand’s existing organic search listing into a paid search placement. IWG’s ROI through Brave is currently 51% higher than through Microsoft, while its enquiry-to-deal rate is 10%, 53% higher than through Microsoft. Following the initial test, IWG has expanded its Brave campaigns, and they are now running continuously across five markets. “Search is spreading across more places than ever before,” said Loïc Blanchard, Head of Performance Marketing – Paid Search & AI at IWG. “Privacy-focused browsers and independent search engines are building real audiences of their own, made up of people we were not reaching through the usual channels. Brave is one of those places, and being there first means we are in front of these users while the space is still new. “The traffic it is driving is incremental to our existing platforms, which remain a key part of our plans. It is also high-quality and highly efficient.” ... “Brave has demonstrated its strength against traditional search engines, clearly showing the higher-quality audiences available with much higher intent, which is why we are continuing to expand our efforts into more markets,” said Ananda De Abreu, IWG Global Senior Paid Search Manager.

headline: IWG sees debt rise as reports cash outflow and first-half pretax loss | MarketScreener UK
summary_text: (Alliance News) - International Workplace Group PLC on Tuesday raised its dividend despite posting a half-year loss and increased debt. The Zug, Switzerland-based provider of hybrid workspace under Regus and other brands swung to a pretax loss of USD20 million in half-year ended June 30 from a USD12 million profit the year prior. Operating income dropped to USD38 million from USD68 million on-year. The bottom line was hurt by higher selling, general and administrative expenses which rose 26% to USD315 million from USD250 million. However, IWG said that following a period of increased investment, overheads are expected to reduce "significantly" in the second half which should strengthen cash flow. It expects cash flow performance in the second half of 2026 to be ahead of the prior year. Cash outflows totalled USD55 million in the half-year compared to inflows a year prior. Given this, net debt increased to USD880 million from USD754 million. Shares in IWG were marked down 3.1% at 179.90 pence each in London on Tuesday morning. System-wide revenue increased to 11% USD2.40 billion from USD2.16 billion with group revenue of USD1.97 billion, up 6.5% from USD1.85 billion. System-wide revenue is the total made by every single workspace in the IWG network, including partner and franchise locations. Group revenue includes sales from company owned sites, and service fees from partner centres. IWG said the Managed & Franchised segment now represents 22% of system-revenue, up from 18% a year ago, and 32% of all open rooms, up from 25% a year ago. "Our strategy remains clear. We continue to expand our global coverage at pace, building an unrivalled network that extends from the world's largest cities to smaller towns and regional markets," said Chief Executive Christian Schmitz. Expectations for 2026 remain unchanged. IWG expects adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of USD585 million to USD625 million, company-owned revenue growth of at least 4% and recurring management fee income of USD80 million. Adjusted Ebitda was USD265 million in the first half, up marginally from USD262 million the year before. In 2025, IWG reported adjusted Ebitda of USD531 million. A dividend of USD0.48 per share was declared, compared to USD0.45 a year ago.

headline: IWG rachète Wojo, le coworking d'Accor
summary_text: International Workspace Group (IWG) annonce l’acquisition de Wojo, l’activité de coworking d’Accor, qui devient désormais une filiale à 100% du groupe. Cette opération élargit le réseau d’IWG, qui réunit notamment les marques Regus, Spaces, HQ, Signature et Stop & Work, de 186 espaces de travail supplémentaires. Wojo était auparavant détenue en coentreprise par Accor et Bouygues Immobilier. Lancée avec l’ambition de faire des hôtels Accor des lieux d’accueil pour les travailleurs nomades, l’enseigne s’est imposée avec un positionnement associant espaces de travail flexibles haut de gamme et univers hôtelier, jusqu’à essaimer au-delà de la France, avec des implantations récentes en Afrique de l’Ouest. Pour IWG, cette acquisition marque également le début d’une relation de long terme avec Accor, ouvrant de nouvelles perspectives pour développer des espaces de travail flexibles gérés par des professionnels au sein de son réseau hôtelier, alors que la demande pour le travail hybride et les déplacements professionnels mêlant travail et loisirs continue de croître. Un rapprochement dans la continuité de collaborations déjà engagées entre les deux groupes, à l’image de l’accord signé entre Spaces et l’Accor Arena pour l’exploitation de postes de travail. ... Déjà présent dans plus de 120 pays avec plus de 6 000 sites sous contrat, IWG consolide ainsi sa position de leader sur le marché français des espaces de travail flexibles, l’un des plus importants d’Europe. Le groupe entend créer une nouvelle source de revenus pour les hôteliers tout en élargissant son réseau mondial, au croisement du travail hybride et de l’hôtellerie.

(PRESS RELEASE) LONDON, England, United Kingdom, 22-Oct-2026 — / EuropaWire/ — J Sainsbury plc has reported interim results for the 28 weeks ended 12 September 2026, with continued grocery volume growth and higher underlying operating profit from continuing operations as it progresses the agreed sale of Argos. ### Chief executive statement Simon Roberts, Chief Executive of J Sainsbury plc, said: “We know many households are finding things tough at the moment and we’re making it easier for customers to enjoy good food every day, whatever their budget. That’s why more people are choosing us for their weekly shop, driving continued volume growth in the first half. “We’re delivering trusted value for customers. Through Nectar Prices and the biggest Aldi Price Match in the market, Sainsbury’s is helping customers save on the products they buy most often and inflating behind the market. “Innovation is powering our progress. We’re bringing more choice and exciting new food to customers and expanding ranges in more stores. Taste the Difference sales grew by more than six per cent and our restaurant-quality Taste the Difference Discovery range will soon have 200 products. We’re also making healthier choices easy, affordable and delicious through our expanded Full on Fibre range. “Our long-term relationships with British farmers and suppliers help us deliver the food customers love at great value, while giving producers a predictable profit and the confidence to invest and plan for the future. My huge thanks go to our colleagues, farmers and suppliers whose passion, expertise and commitment make this possible every day. “As we progress the sale of Argos and further sharpen our focus on food, we are building a simpler, more focused Sainsbury's. With great value, outstanding quality and exciting new food across our ranges, we’re looking forward to helping customers enjoy a really special Christmas.” ### Financial highlights * Agreed sale of Argos to Swift Partners; transaction expected to complete by the end of February 2027 and full separation expected by February 2029. Argos has been classified as a discontinued operation * Sales from continuing operations (excluding Fuel) £14.0bn, up 2.6%. Grocery sales £13.2bn, up 2.9%, reflecting continued volume growth and lower inflation. Sainsbury’s General Merchandise & Clothing sales £0.8bn, down 3.4%, reflecting General Merchandise space reduction and a subdued clothing market. Fuel sales £2.3bn, up 17.8%, reflecting higher wholesale prices * Continuing underlying operating profit £525m, up 3.6%, reflecting volume growth, continued cost savings delivery and consistent balanced investment in value, quality, availability and service * Statutory loss after tax £(164)m (H1 2025/26: profit £155m), primarily relating to discontinued operations * Free cash flow £333m. On track to deliver more than £500m for the full year * Completed £200m of previously announced £300m share buyback, with the remaining £100m to be completed in H2 * Interim dividend of 4.1 pence per share. Consistent with prior years, this is 30 per cent of the prior year’s full year dividend per share ### First-half financial summary |Measure|H1 2026/27|H1 2025/26|Year-on-year / change| |Underlying sales (excl. fuel)1,2|£13,959m|£13,611m|2.6%| |Underlying operating profit1|£525m|£507m|3.6%| |Underlying profit before tax1|£366m|£348m|5.2%| |Underlying basic earnings per share1,3|11.7p|10.6p|10.4%| |Proposed interim dividend per share|4.1p|4.1p|–| |Free cash flow4|£333m|£276m|£57m| |Net debt (inc. lease liabilities)5|£(5,634)m|£(5,527)m|£(107)m| |Non-lease net debt5|£(75)m|£(81)m|£6m| |Return on capital employed6|9.2%|9.0%|20bps| |Revenue (inc. fuel)1|£16,243m|£15,596m|4.1%| |(Loss)/profit after tax1,3|£(164)m|£155m|n/a| |o/w Continuing operations|£212m|£190m|11.6%| |o/w Discontinued operations|£(376)m|£(35)m|n/a| |Total basic (losses)/earnings per share3|(7.4)p|6.8p|n/a| |Net cash generated from operating activities – continuing1|£890m|£703m|£187m| ### 2026/27 outlook Sainsbury’s said value, quality, availability and service investment helped sustain first-half volume and profit growth. Sainsbury’s has raised the lower end of its continuing-operations underlying operating-profit forecast to £1,025 million–£1,065 million and continues to expect full-year free cash flow exceeding £500 million. ### Strategic highlights and Next Level Sainsbury’s The Next Level Sainsbury’s plan, announced in February 2024, set out eight commitments: * Food volume growth ahead of the market * Customer satisfaction higher 26/27 vs 23/24 * Colleague engagement higher 26/27 vs 23/24 * Deliver our Plan for Better commitments * Deliver profit leverage from sales growth * £1bn of cost savings over three years to 26/27 * £1.6bn+ Retail free cash flow over three years to 26/27 * Higher return on capital employed In the plan’s final year, Sainsbury’s reports progress against the commitments through market-share gains, ongoing investment in colleagues, technology, infrastructure and long-term suppliers, stronger free-cash-flow generation and enhanced shareholder returns. headline: Nectar Launches Customer Atlas, Extending Amazon Marketing Cloud Audience Targeting From Display Into Search Bidding
summary_text: The capability indexes a brand's own purchase history against all 6,728 audience segments Amazon exposes, builds both a targeting list and a suppression list, and applies them where the majority of Amazon advertising budget actually sits. NEW YORK, October 14, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nectar, an Amazon Advanced Advertising Partner managing more than $2.5 billion in annual client sales, launched today Customer Atlas, an Amazon Marketing Cloud capability that changes the unit of targeting in Amazon search advertising from the keyword to the shopper. Amazon search campaigns bid on words. A brand sets one price for a category term and pays approximately that price for every click it buys, whether the shopper is a likely high-value buyer or someone who will never purchase at that price point. Amazon Marketing Cloud made it possible to tell those shoppers apart. In practice, that capability has been aimed almost entirely at Amazon DSP, which for most advertisers is the smaller half of their spend. Customer Atlas points it at the larger half. ... The capability has three parts. A full segment index. The method analyzes up to five years of a brand's Amazon purchase history and indexes it against all 6,728 audience segments Amazon exposes, 5,268 in-market and 1,460 lifestyle, rather than selecting the few category segments a media plan would reach for. It corrects for the fact that repeat buyers belong to roughly 10% more segments by default, an adjustment that otherwise manufactures a false signal in every segment measured. Two lists, not one. The index produces segments that concentrate among a brand's high-value buyers and segments that concentrate among people who buy once and never return. Most media plans carry the first. Almost none carry the second, which means most brands pay full rates to reach shoppers their own data already identifies as unlikely to return. Activation in search. Both lists deploy as audiences in Amazon DSP and as audience bid modifiers in Sponsored Products and Sponsored Brands, using a low base bid with a boost applied only when a targeted shopper searches. No new campaigns are required, and the budget is already committed. ... Every Customer Atlas engagement ships with a pre-registered test design: one variable per cell, equal budgets across cells, a control cell any advertiser could run without Nectar, and decision gates written before the first impression serves. In the first live deployment, campaigns using audience bid modifiers cut cost per click by a third against the same brand's standard campaigns. "It is a change to bids on spend that is already happening," said Harriet Carson, VP of Advertising at Nectar. "It works alongside whoever runs the search account today." ... About Nectar Nectar (thinknectar.com) is a full-service e-commerce performance marketing agency for mid-market and enterprise brands, managing more than $3 billion in Amazon sales across 200+ brands and $250M in ad spend. Founded in 2018 by former Amazon sellers, Nectar combines an in-house creative studio, marketplace advertising, retail operations, and its proprietary iDerive analytics platform under one roof.

headline: Nectar360 First UK Retail Media Network to Earn IAB Europe Certification — Martech Beacon
summary_text: Nectar360, the retail media network behind Sainsbury's and Argos, has become the first UK retail media network to achieve IAB Europe's Retail Media Certification — a first-of-its-kind credential in the British market. The certification, awarded under IAB Europe's pan-European programme, signals that Nectar360's retail media operations meet an independently defined standard rather than a self-declared one. For an industry still wrestling with measurement inconsistency and trust gaps, a named network clearing an external bar matters. ... What does the certification actually cover? IAB Europe's Retail Media Certification framework assesses retail media networks against criteria spanning transparency, operational standards, and adherence to industry-agreed definitions. In practice, it's a check that a network's claims about its capabilities and reporting line up with an external benchmark. For Nectar360, that means the network operating across Sainsbury's and Argos — two of the UK's largest retail estates — now carries a credential no other UK retail media network holds. The distinction is chronological, not qualitative: first to be certified, not the only one eligible.

headline: ASA Pulls The Covers Back On Nectar Sleep's "Save Up To 65%" Ad - Consumer Trading & Unfair Trading - United Kingdom
summary_text: The UK's Advertising Standards Authority has ruled against Nectar Sleep's "Save up to 65%" promotional campaign, finding that the basis of the savings claim was unclear and materially misleading to consumers. The decision highlights critical issues with how retailers calculate and present competitor price comparisons, particularly when using narrow product selections and averaging methodologies that may not reflect genuine market conditions. ... The ASA also took issue with the construction of the comparator itself. The "Similar Brands Average Price" was derived from only three competing products selected by Nectar Sleep. The ASA considered that consumers would be likely to understand an "average price" claim as reflecting a broader cross-section of the market rather than a narrow selection chosen by the advertiser. It considered that because the Similar Brands Average Price was based on an average, and consumers could not purchase a competing product at that price, the claimed 65% saving was not based on an established, genuinely available reference price. The ASA was also critical of the methodology used to derive the headline "up to 65%" claim. Rather than identifying a particular product against which consumers could achieve a 65% saving, Nectar Sleep calculated average savings across its mattress range and used that figure as the basis for the headline claim. The evidence showed that the highest savings levels applied only to certain memory foam mattresses, while savings on other products were considerably lower. The ASA concluded that the claim exaggerated the savings consumers were likely to obtain. Therefore, the ad breached the rules in the CAP about misleading advertising, substantiation and pricing claims. ... compliant With the government consulting on pricing claims later this year, the decision is a timely reminder that advertisers need more than a comfortable methodology to support savings claims. In practical terms, advertisers relying on competitor price comparisons should ensure they use a genuinely representative sample of the market, make the basis of the comparison prominent and intelligible to consumers, and verify that "up to" claims are achievable on identifiable products. When it comes to price comparisons, the ASA expects businesses to be able to show that consumers are not being sold a dream.

headline: Nektar Raises Cash to Fund Rezpegaldesleukin Phase 3 Trials Through 2028
summary_text: Nektar Therapeutics ended June with $1.02 billion in cash and investments, a figure that jumped from $245.8 million at year-end 2025 largely on the back of a $373.8 million equity offering completed in April. That balance matters because it buys time in a direct and measurable way: Nektar says the runway extends into the third quarter of 2028, past the initial Phase 3 data readouts expected in mid-2028. The structure of that runway is what makes this quarterly report worth reading beyond the financials. ... The money is already flowing into the clinic. R&D expense rose to $39.1 million in Q2 2026 from $29.9 million in Q2 2025, driven by startup costs for the Phase 3 ZENITH AD program in atopic dermatitis and manufacturing scale-up for rezpegaldesleukin. Two of the three ZENITH AD trials launched in July. The program’s design is notable: ZENITH AD-1 and AD-2 enroll biologic and systemic JAK inhibitor treatment-naive patients, while ZENITH AD-3 targets patients with prior biologic or JAK inhibitor experience. That stratified enrollment reflects a crowded treatment landscape where dupilumab and approved JAK inhibitors have already carved distinct patient segments, and where any new entrant needs to demonstrate differentiated durability, not just response rates. Rezpegaldesleukin’s mechanism, regulatory T cell stimulation, is biologically distinct from IL-4/IL-13 blockade or kinase inhibition, which is precisely why the maintenance-phase data from the Phase 2b REZOLVE-AD study, scheduled for an oral presentation at EADV on October 1, will attract close attention from trial designers and payers alike. ... The alopecia areata timeline adds another layer. Nektar plans a single registrational Phase 3 study in early 2027, and rezpegaldesleukin already holds FDA Fast Track designation for severe-to-very severe alopecia areata. The competitive clock is ticking: AbbVie has submitted an sNDA for upadacitinib in severe alopecia areata based on Phase 3 data, meaning any approved-therapy window is narrowing. Positive 52-week data from the REZOLVE-AA blinded extension, showing deepening responses with continued twice-monthly dosing, is a meaningful biological signal, but a single Phase 3 study will face intense regulatory scrutiny and will need to differentiate on durability and safety profile rather than novelty alone.

headline: Dominion Energy files IRP with plans to build 3.5GW of BESS - Energy-Storage.News
summary_text: The 2026 IRP addresses three converging pressures: rising and shifting demand, evolving policy, and tightening capacity markets within PJM. Image: Dominion Energy US utility Dominion Energy plans to build 3.5GW of battery energy storage systems (BESS) over the next 20 years, according to its recently filed integrated resource plan (IRP). On 15 October, Dominion filed a full comprehensive IRP with the North Carolina Utilities Commission (NCUC) and an interim update with the Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC). The 2026 IRP addresses three converging pressures: rising and shifting demand, evolving policy, and tightening capacity markets within PJM. As the utility noted in its IRP, demand in Dominion Energy’s delivery zone continues to grow, with peaks shifting to winter mornings and summer evenings when weather-dependent resources produce less. Meanwhile, new generation and transmission projects face longer timelines, interconnection constraints, supply-chain pressures, and siting challenges. The IRP also reflects Virginia’s expanded storage mandate. In February, the Virginia General Assembly passed legislation to promote new energy storage investments by Dominion and Appalachian Power, the state’s primary utilities. In April, Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger signed the legislation into law. It requires Dominion to add 16,000MW of short-duration BESS capacity and 3,480MW of long-duration energy storage (LDES) capacity by 2045. PJM conditions add further pressure. Dominion relies on PJM’s capacity market for resource adequacy, and the 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction cleared at the price cap, with committed capacity over 6,800MW below PJM’s requirement and reserve margin at just 14.4% against a 20% target — the second straight auction to clear short, reflecting load growth, generation retirements, resource delays, and updated ELCC accreditation standards. The IRP stated, “Notably, the LDES targets do not become effective unless and until the SCC determines such technology is technically viable and that the construction, acquisition, or procurement targets are reasonably achievable.” ... Dominion has petitioned for SCC approval of new company-owned and power purchase agreement (PPA) resources totalling 712MW of BESS capacity and nearly 5,000MW of solar in its annual Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) Development Plan proceeding. The utility currently has over 170MW of approved company-owned BESS projects and has approximately 50MW in operation. 459MW of BESS has also been approved under PPAs. Dominion received approval from SCC to pilot three non-lithium-ion (Li-ion) projects, two of which are LDES projects. At the Darbytown Power Station in Virginia, two electrochemical systems will be tested, a zinc-hybrid battery from zinc battery storage player Eos Energy and an iron-air battery capable of discharging for up to 100 hours from US startup Form Energy. ... Dominion’s preferred plan prioritises solar, wind, and BESS petitioned by 2035 and built by 2039, with remaining capacity selected on a least-cost basis. For BESS, only the portion not requiring additional commission review (petitioned by 2030) is included upfront, with the rest selected on a least-cost basis — totalling 3.5GW. The plan also builds over 21GW of solar, exceeding Virginia Clean Economy Act (VCEA) requirements, plus three small modular reactor (SMR) sets starting in 2042 and 3.4GW of additional offshore wind. To “preserve existing generation” and meet future reliability needs, the plan requires invoking the VCEA’s reliability exception and adding 8.9GW of gas-fired capacity.

headline: Dominion’s energy roadmap keeps fossil fuels in the mix, expands solar • Virginia Mercury
summary_text: Brief Dominion Energy plans to add more than 39 gigawatts of new power generation over the next 20 years as electricity demand surges across Virginia, according to the company’s latest filing with the State Corporation Commission. Over that period, Dominion plans to build more than 21 gigawatts of new solar energy, 3.5 gigawatts of battery storage, 9 gigawatts of natural gas, 3.3 gigawatts of wind, and 2 gigawatts of small modular reactors. The filing is part of the annual update to Dominion’s integrated resource plan (IRP). It is not a concrete list of projects but a roadmap of how the company expects to meet energy demand. While this year’s update will not be litigated or subject to changes through final order, the filing outlines where the company expects demand to go and how it plans to meet it. A key part of the plan is continued reliance on fossil fuels despite the Virginia Clean Economy Act’s mandate to retire carbon emitting energy sources – namely coal and natural gas. The company’s filing states green energy sources are not commercially viable or dispatchable enough to meet annual load growth of roughly 4%, or 500 to 700 megawatts, with power demand expected to double by 2045. Those figures do not include load growth for the cooperative utilities that also rely on Dominion for power and transmission. “To meet the energy and capacity needs associated with the load forecast, and in the absence of a commercially viable carbon-free, dispatchable generation alternative, natural gas generation will remain a critical component of the (Dominion’s) strategy to reliably meet generation demand,” the filing stated. ... Projections for increases in the average residential customer’s bill will vary depending on whether they use the company’s preferred calculation or the method directed by the SCC. Under the company’s calculation, a household using 1000 kilowatt-hours a month would see its monthly bill rise to an estimated $258.03 by 2036 and $283.65 in 2046. Under the SCC’s mandated calculation method, monthly bills are projected to reach $320.26 in 2036 and $458.22 in 2046. Dominion has continued to push back on the SCC’s methodology for calculating bills in later years. “(Dominion) believes that this methodology results in overstated bill projections because it does not reflect anticipated growth in sales over the period on which each portfolio is based,” the filing stated. ... The company says bringing more energy generation projects online will reduce its reliance on power purchases from the regional grid operator, PJM. Virginia is one of the largest importers of energy on the East Coast. “Our preferred plan calls for more than 39 gigawatts of new power generation assets over the next 20 years – more than three-fourths of which is carbon-free solar, offshore wind, energy storage and advanced nuclear technology – and a decreasing reliance on more costly purchases from the PJM market,” Dominion spokesperson Jeremy Slayton said. The SCC will review the filing and accept the plan if it is deemed sufficient. A full trial on the updated integrated resource plan is scheduled for fall of 2027.

headline: Virginia regulators approve Dominion’s fuel cost recovery, securitization | Utility Dive
summary_text: ### Dive Brief: - The State Corporation Commission last month approved Dominion Energy’s fuel factor rate to recover $2.691 billion in projected fuel costs from the 2026 and 2027 rate years, and about $65.8 million in underrecovered costs from the 2024 to 2025 rate year. - The Commission also approved the utility’s legislatively authorized request to securitize, or issue bonds, for about $922 million in underrecovered fuel costs from the previous 2025 and 2026 rate years. - The securitization avoids a $21.79 increase in a typical residential monthly bill and instead results in a $7.97 increase for the fuel factor, plus a $2.26 increase for the securitization by spreading out recovery of the underrecovered fuel costs over a seven year period. ... ### Dive Insight: Securitization spreads out fuel payments, lowering their immediate impact on bills, but also winds up costing more as interest adds up, customer advocates note. ... Virginia regulators’ decision came after a two-day hearing in which Dominion argued cold temperatures in the lead-up to and days after Winter Storm Fern between Jan. 23 and Feb. 2 contributed to unexpected increases in fuel costs. Those freezing temperatures increased demand for power and caused the utility to purchase more power from PJM, which is also recovered through the fuel factor. T he cost of purchased power went up 28% for the 2026-2027 rate years, according to testimony from Katherine Farmer, energy market strategic advisor at Dominion. ... The latest securitization comes after the commission in 2023 approved a legislatively authorized securitization of about $1 billion in deferred fuel costs, which the company said rose because of global events, including the Ukraine War. Scott Gaskill, vice president of regulatory affairs at Dominion, said during the hearing that he agreed fuel costs are “becoming more volatile and more difficult to forecast as supply and demand across PJM has tightened,” but he added that this time was different than the 2023 securitization. ... Carol Myers, SCC deputy director in the commission’s Division of Utility Accounting and Finance, was more blunt, saying “the repeated securitizations of deferred fuel costs on an ongoing basis is untenable.” Myers' analysis found that approving Dominion’s fuel factor request will charge a typical residential customer $43.59, up from $20.45 during the 2021 fuel year. “Staff believes this has likely put upward pressure on power prices and significant upward pressure on the Company’s purchased power expenses, which is only further exacerbated during periods of extreme weather,” Myers said. During the hearing, Myers added that the 2023 securitization, or deferral, of fuel costs haven’t been paid off yet. Yet, customers will be saddled with a “pancaking” of paying for another securitization from this ruling. “I don't think we can keep doing this,” Myers said, adding, “I think continuing down this path, it's dangerous and puts customers in a bad position.” ... Environmental groups said fuel price volatility resulted from uneconomical coal-powered generation decisions, the Iran War and liquefied natural gas exports increasing natural gas prices. The Southern Environmental Law Center, representing Appalachian Voices, and the Sierra Club argued for more renewable energy use as well as cost-sharing mechanisms that put Dominion on the hook for fuel cost overruns as an incentive to reduce recovery from customers. A new law signed by Democratic Gov. Abigail Spanberger that will scrutinize the cost effectiveness of Dominion’s fuel use took effect July 1, meaning it will be followed in next year’s fuel factor case.

headline: Dominion, NextEra defend proposed $67 billion merger as Virginia leaders raise concerns | 13newsnow.com
summary_text: VIRGINIA, USA — Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy defended their proposed $67 billion merger before Virginia lawmakers this week as state leaders raised concerns about energy costs, jobs and whether regulators have enough time to evaluate the deal. Executives from the two utility companies appeared before the General Assembly’s Energy Commission on Tuesday, outlining their plans for Virginia and pledging to help keep energy costs affordable. Ed Baine, president of Dominion Energy Virginia, told lawmakers the two companies are growing businesses and said Dominion has continued hiring as it works to meet increasing demands on the electric grid. “At Dominion Energy in Virginia, we’ve been hiring 600 to 800 people a year in order to execute on the work that’s in front of us," Baine said. Several delegates questioned the companies about the long-term impact of the proposed merger, including job security and safeguards for competing utility projects. The proposal has also drawn opposition from state leaders. Lt. Gov. Ghazala Hashmi announced Tuesday that she opposes the merger, citing the cost of energy in Virginia. “Virginians are reaching their breaking point with the high price of energy,” Hashmi said Tuesday. On Wednesday, Del. Mark Downey, D-Williamsburg, held an event in Williamsburg with about a half-dozen state leaders who voiced opposition to the proposed merger. Downey said Virginia needs more time to address current and future demands on the electric grid, including increased electricity use from data centers. “We need time to kind of sort out what we’re doing currently right now with future electric demands coming from data centers, from all the demands on the grid up and down the coast,” Downey said. Attorney General Jay Jones has asked the State Corporation Commission to delay its decision on the proposed merger. Downey said additional time is needed for regulators to fully evaluate the deal. “I don’t know if we’re too far along in this process where that can actually be extended, so that’s why we’re saying we oppose the merger,” Downey said. “If this is all the time they’re going to give the SCC to review, then I don’t feel like they’re going to be able to do a proper evaluation of this merger.” Dominion Energy disputed Hashmi’s concerns in a statement to 13News Now. “We respectfully disagree with the Lieutenant Governor. Everything in the enhanced Virginia package begins with customers,” a Dominion spokesperson said. NextEra Energy also defended the proposed deal, saying its experience and resources would benefit Virginia customers. “By bringing NextEra Energy’s scale, experience and proven record to Virginia, it would help keep power affordable and reliable for years to come,” a NextEra spokesperson said. The proposed merger remains under review by the State Corporation Commission.

headline: Dominion Energy Newsroom - NextEra Energy and Dominion Energy announce transformational Virginia benefits package that puts customers first and positions the Commonwealth as a global energy leader

JUNO BEACH, Fla. & RICHMOND, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- In direct response to feedback from policymakers and other stakeholders, NextEra Energy, Inc. (NYSE: NEE) and Dominion Energy, Inc. (NYSE: D) today announced a transformational Virginia benefits package as part of their proposed combination, designed to put customers first while positioning the Commonwealth as a global energy leader with long-term bill relief for residential customers, long-term affordability benefits, data center cost protections, accelerated clean energy deployment and thousands of new direct and indirect jobs in Richmond and across the Commonwealth. ... It puts customers first by proposing four years of residential bill credits, delivering long-term affordability benefits, expanding low-income financial assistance and ensuring data centers pay their fair share. At the same time, it would position ... The companies would also expand low-income financial assistance by increasing EnergyShare, Dominion Energy’s shareholder-funded energy bill assistance program, by $100 million through 2038 and reaffirm their existing commitment to hold customers harmless from all merger costs. Customers will not pay one cent for this combination. The companies said the package would support long-term affordability by using the combined company’s scale to buy, build, finance and operate more efficiently over time, with future base rates continuing to be set by the SCC once every two years. When combined with the credits, customers are receiving long-term affordability benefits that a standalone Dominion Energy cannot offer. ... Since 2006, NextEra Energy’s utility subsidiary, Florida Power & Light Company (FPL), has increased customer accounts by more than 36% and generation capacity by more than 60%, while improving reliability by more than 40% and lowering bills by 20% in real dollars. Today, FPL’s non-fuel operations and maintenance expense is more than 70% below the national average, its typical residential bills are 37% below the national average, and its reliability is more than 60% better than the national average, all while making investments in affordable generation to keep pace with increasing electric demand in the 14th largest economy in the world. ... The expanded package would help accelerate the buildout of Virginia generation, including solar, storage, dispatchable resources and nuclear, while leveraging the combined company’s existing Virginia assets, like the Virginia City Hybrid Energy Center, to support reliability as the Commonwealth builds the next generation of energy infrastructure. The investment would include working with union partners to support career development, hands-on training and apprenticeships and establish a newly created independent organization to operate a workforce development fund for Virginia, governed by a board drawn from the Commonwealth's trade schools, colleges, universities, technical colleges and community colleges, directed at training Virginians for the jobs this global leadership opportunity would create. headline: Dominion ordered to directly assign some transmission costs to data centers | Utility Dive
summary_text: ### Dive Brief: - Dominion Energy will need to change its transmission cost allocation policy to directly assign the cost of certain transmission infrastructure to the new large-load facilities — such as data centers — which made that infrastructure necessary, the Virginia State Corporation Commission said in an order filed July 31. - The mandatory contribution in aid of construction, or CIAC, will apply to “direct connect” facilities, and apply to the cost of the substations and the transmission lines which connect those facilities to the grid. - The SCC’s case concerned Dominion’s proposed increase to its Rider T-1 line-item charge for cost recovery for transmission investments, as the company sought to recoup around $1.5 billion. The commission approved an amended version of Dominion’s new 12 coincident peak demands allocation factor, or 12CP, reducing the proposed monthly cost increase for a typical residential customer from $2.90 per month to $0.94 per month — a 67.5% decrease. ... ### Dive Insight: “At the extremes, this minimum demand adjustment decreases the residential class’s allocation factor by 2.84% and increases the GS-4 rate class’s allocation factor by 4.33%,” the SCC wrote in its order. Dominion’s GS-4 rate class applies to large commercial or industrial customers that demand at least 500 kW and receive power directly from the grid. The SCC ordered Dominion to craft an amendment to its existing line extension policy “that would require a mandatory CIAC for defined types of transmission facilities,” and directed Dominion to file that proposed amended policy in a new docket within 90 days from the date of the final order. “Under the SCC’s oversight, we already have among the strongest protections in the country to prevent data center driven costs from being borne by our residential customers,” Dominion spokesperson Jeremy Slayton told Utility Dive in an email. “When we file our amended line extension policy, we will be adding even more protections for our residential customers to ensure our more energy intensive customers continue to pay their fair share.” ... The SCC said it may use the new docket to consider whether the amended line extension policy “could or should” be extended to those higher-level costs, as well as the merits of “a blended approach” where those higher-level costs are directly assigned to Dominion’s new GS-5 rate class for energy users requiring 25 MW or more. ... Hyperscaler companies including Google and Amazon also testified in the SCC’s hearings about the case, and both of those companies requested the introduction of voluntary CIACs, but the SCC ruled that the payments will be mandatory.

headline: Virginia to offload more grid costs onto data centers - E&E News by POLITICO
summary_text: The data center capital of the world is shifting more transmission costs onto the energy-hungry sector. Virginia regulators have ordered Dominion Energy, the commonwealth’s largest utility, to create a process for assigning to data centers the direct costs of their electric service, such as substations built to meet their power demand. Those costs are currently spread across all ratepayers. Regulators also opened the door for data centers to pay more of the grid’s transmission costs further upstream, such as regional projects that are harder to tie to any specific demand source. The move by Virginia’s State Corporation Commission came during the annual adjustment of Dominion’s transmission rate rider — a usually routine proceeding that turned into a blockbuster utility case. The decision is expected to shift hundreds of millions of dollars in transmission costs away from the public, with details to be finalized during future regulatory proceedings. ... The order envisions requiring data centers to pay what’s known as a contribution in aid of construction, or CIAC (pronounced “kayak”), which amounts to an up-front payment for part of a project’s cost. Regulators ordered Dominion to amend its line-extension policy so the utility could charge data center developers a CIAC for “direct connect” transmission facilities, such as the substations and power lines that connect a data center to the bulk transmission system. The CIAC would cover the costs of a project that aren’t otherwise captured by a facility’s transmission charges. Further changes are on the table too. Only charging data centers for their “direct connect” projects, regulators said, might still leave the public on the hook for infrastructure needed further upstream in the transmission system. As they review Dominion’s new line-extension policy, regulators said they might also consider whether to add those higher-order costs to data centers’ CIAC or spread them across the entire GS-5 large-load rate class. Those changes, commissioners said, would require “a more deliberate approach.” ... “It’s an important first step, but more work remains,” said Chris Miller, president of the Piedmont Environmental Council, which participated in the rate case. “The ruling appears to apply only to substations and the other transmission infrastructure that connect data centers to the bulk power system,” he said in a statement. “It does not resolve who should pay for the billions of dollars in other supplemental and regional transmission projects driven by unprecedented data center growth in Virginia. The ruling also does not address the substantial new generation resources — including multiple natural gas-fired power plants — that Dominion has proposed to build to meet this rapidly growing demand.” ... Virginia’s order gives Dominion 90 days to propose a new line-extension policy with a CIAC framework for the State Corporation Commission to review.

headline: Dominion offshore wind project cost rises nearly $300M | Utility Dive
summary_text: Dominion Energy estimates its 2.6-GW Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind project will cost about $11.7 billion when all is said and done, up nearly $300 million from its most recent cost estimate in April, the company said Friday. The $288 million cost increase is due to revised network upgrade costs assigned by the PJM Interconnection, tariffs imposed by the Trump administration in April and updated turbine installation projections, Dominion said in its second-quarter filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The company now estimates it will complete all work on the project by the end of 2027, a change from previous projections that saw work wrapping up early next year. The Virginia-based company, which operates regulated utilities in Virginia and South Carolina and owns commercial power plants in other Eastern states, provided the offshore wind update alongside other substantive updates on its data center pipeline, nonregulated generation assets and proposed merger with NextEra Energy. Rising offshore wind costs and charges related to those nonregulated assets were among the drags on Dominion’s second-quarter earnings, according to the company’s quarterly 10-Q filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Others included higher fuel costs and Dominion Virginia’s June “reentry” into the PJM Interconnection capacity market, the company said. Dominion reported net income of $340 million in the second quarter, down from $760 million in Q2 2025. ... ### Next steps for the NextEra merger Dominion Energy will begin seeking state and federal approvals next quarter for its proposed merger with NextEra Energy and could reach financial close by the end of 2027, Dominion said Friday in its quarterly shareholder presentation. If the Dominion-NextEra transaction succeeds, the combined enterprise would be the country’s largest regulated utility company with 10 million customers and a 130-GW large-load interconnection pipeline. Dominion’s portion of that pipeline has grown 11% since December, the company said Friday. “Over the longer term, customers and communities would benefit from a stronger company with the scale and capabilities to buy, build, finance, and operate critical energy infrastructure more efficiently,” Robert Blue, Dominion Energy CEO, said on Friday’s earnings call. ... For Dominion investors, it’s “discouraging to see another offshore wind delay and cost increase but unfortunately not a major surprise,” Dumoulin-Smith said last week. Blue put an optimistic spin on the project’s progress, noting that work is 81% complete and “every type of component is in service and functioning as expected,” he said. The operational turbines can collectively produce more than 450 MW of power, according to Dominion’s investor presentation. “In recent weeks, as we've set new demand peaks, we've done everything possible at the request of system operators to deliver the maximum possible amount of power from CVOW,” Blue said. As he has on previous investor calls, Blue said Dominion expects CVOW to save customers about $5 billion on fuel during its first 10 years of operation. ... In its filing with the SEC, Dominion said it agreed in May to sell a portfolio of nonregulated solar assets in its Contracted Energy segment for $140 million to Enel, the Italian energy conglomerate. It expects that transaction to close by the end of 2026. Dominion said it also expects to sell its nonregulated renewable natural gas assets before their anticipated retirement dates. It did not provide a timeline or identify a potential buyer for those assets, however. Dominion warned earlier this year that one of the two nuclear reactors it operates at the 2,106-MW Millstone generating station in Connecticut could retire by 2035 without a long-term power purchase contract past 2029, when the company’s current contracts with Eversource and United Illuminating expire. Dominion said in a March filing with Connecticut regulators that one or more utilities or “well-capitalized counterparty” like a data center operator could step up to support a license extension through 2055. On Friday, Blue said Dominion expects Connecticut to decide soon if it will approve Millstone’s bid to participate in the state’s zero-carbon energy procurement, after which he said the company would begin negotiating contracts to submit to state regulators. Dominion believes its bid will save Connecticut ratepayers $900 million over 10 years, he said.
