headline: SEERS Reports First-Half Revenue of 60.9 Billion Won and Operating Profit of 26.8 Billion Won… Exceeding Last Year’s Full-Year Results - EDAILY
summary_text: [Edaily Reporter NA EUN-KYUNG ] #SEERS Technology, a wearable artificial intelligence (AI) diagnostics and monitoring company, announced on the 13th that it recorded consolidated revenue of 60.9 billion won and operating profit of 26.8 billion won in the first half of 2026, surpassing its full-year results from last year. Compared to the same period last year, revenue increased by 407% and operating profit by 2,888%. Second-quarter revenue totaled 28.4 billion won, with operating profit at 13.0 billion won. As the company expanded its business primarily at top-tier general hospitals—including the “Big 5”—some revenue from large hospitals with relatively long contract periods was deferred to the second half of the year, and overseas project schedules were partially adjusted due to geopolitical factors in the Middle East. However, thanks to improved platform operational efficiency and enhanced cost competitiveness, the second-quarter operating profit margin reached 45.6%, up 3.0 percentage points from the previous quarter’s 42.6%. This marks the highest quarterly operating profit margin in the company’s history. First-half performance has already surpassed last year’s full-year results. Last year, SEERS Technology’s annual revenue and operating profit were 48.2 billion won and 16.3 billion won, respectively. First-half revenue this year is 26.3% higher than last year’s full-year figure, while operating profit is up 64.4%. The company explained that economies of scale resulting from the expansion of its platform business and improvements in production and operational efficiency have led to improved profitability. This earnings growth was driven by “thynC,” an AI-based inpatient monitoring platform. thynC’s second-quarter revenue was 26.8 billion won, and its cumulative revenue for the first half reached 58.0 billion won, accounting for approximately 95% of total first-half revenue. thynC has expanded its customer base to major tertiary hospitals, including Seoul National University Hospital, Asan Medical Center, and Samsung Medical Center, and has gained experience operating approximately 20,000 hospital beds across 220 medical institutions nationwide. The company plans to expand its customer base to hospital-level medical institutions and long-term care hospitals in the second half of the year. It expects the number of installed beds and related revenue to increase starting in the third quarter, as installations for orders carried over from the second quarter and new contract beds are concentrated during this period. “mobiCARE,” the company’s wearable AI ECG analysis solution, recorded sales of 1.5 billion won in the second quarter and cumulative sales of 2.8 billion won for the first half of the year. First-half sales increased by 29% compared to the same period last year. In addition to demand for examinations centered on cardiology, the company is expanding the solution’s scope of use to include health screening services and expects related sales to increase starting in the third quarter, when demand for health screenings typically rises. The company also plans to expand its overseas business starting in the second half of the year. Although the schedules for some projects were adjusted due to geopolitical uncertainties in the Middle East during the second quarter, the company plans to pursue its U.S. business based on its U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) marketing authorization while also launching its operations in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in earnest. Lee Young-shin, CEO of SEERS Technology, stated, “The first half of the year proved that SEERS’ platform business model can generate both growth and profitability.” He added, “In the second half, we will expand our domestic business scope to include hospitals and long-term care facilities, and fully launch our operations in the UAE and the U.S. to demonstrate the success of our AI medical platform’s growth model—which has been validated in Korea—in the global market as well.”

headline: Seer Q2 2026 results show revenue drop, lower loss | SEER Quarterly Report (10-Q)
summary_text: ## Rhea-AI Filing Summary Seer, Inc. reported continued operating losses while tightening expenses in the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Total revenue was $3.1 million, down 23% from $4.1 million a year earlier, driven by lower product and service sales and the absence of related-party revenue. For the first six months, revenue was $5.9 million, down 29% year over year. Cost controls were significant: research and development expense fell 27% to $17.0 million for the first half and selling, general and administrative expense fell 11% to $19.6 million. As a result, the net loss narrowed to $33.7 million for the first six months of 2026 from $39.4 million in 2025, and operating cash outflow was $25.0 million versus $26.1 million. Liquidity remains a key strength. As of June 30, 2026, Seer held $209.5 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments and reported no debt, and management believes this will fund operations for at least 12 months. The company also continued a share repurchase program, buying 1.7 million shares for $3.0 million in the first half. Seer is investing in its Proteograph Product Suite while absorbing $3.8 million of losses from its equity investment in PrognomiQ. ... Our ability to generate product and service revenue sufficient to achieve profitability, if ever, will depend on the successful commercialization of the Proteograph Product Suite and related products and services. In May 2025, we advanced our commercial offering with the launch of the new Proteograph Product Suite, featuring the Proteograph ONE assay and SP200 automation instrument. With the new Proteograph workflow, we believe we have achieved a transformative milestone by significantly improving the performance and scalability of deep, unbiased proteomic analysis. These advancements push the boundaries of the original capabilities of the Proteograph Product Suite launched in 2021, further addressing limitations in deep, unbiased proteomic workflows, including prohibitive costs of large-scale studies, time-consuming manual workflows, and performance variability introduced by manual handling. ... We market and sell the Proteograph Product Suite as an integrated solution comprised of consumables, our automation instrument and software. Our commercial strategy is focused on growing adoption of the Proteograph by researchers in academic and commercial settings, expanding the installed base, increasing utilization to generate revenue from the purchase of Proteograph consumables and growing our service offering through the Seer Technology Access Center (STAC). We expect a highly efficient sales model because our workflow integrates with most existing proteomics laboratories’ workflows and also complements large-scale genomics research. We are focused on removing barriers to access to the Proteograph, including through the STAC service offering. ... We sell the Proteograph Product Suite through a direct sales channel in the United States, and through both direct and distributor sales channels in regions outside the United States. We have built, and will continue to build our sales, marketing, support and product distribution capabilities. In addition, we will continue to build the necessary infrastructure for these activities in the United States, European Union, the United Kingdom, and other countries and regions, including Asia-Pacific, as we execute on our commercialization strategy for the Proteograph. ... We leverage well-established unit operations to formulate and manufacture our NPs at our facilities in Redwood City, California. We procure certain components of our consumables from third-party manufacturers, which includes the commonly available raw materials needed for manufacturing our proprietary engineered NPs. We are currently manufacturing using our production-scale lines and continue to build out our manufacturing capabilities to support broad commercial availability of our products. We obtain some of the reagents and components used in the Proteograph workflow from third-party suppliers. While some of these reagents and components are currently sourced from a single supplier, these products are readily available from numerous suppliers. While we currently perform some filling and packaging of the Proteograph assay and the related consumables, we may eventually have our filling and packaging outsourced to a third party. We conduct vendor and component qualification for components provided by third-party suppliers and quality control tests on our NPs. ... We designed the automation instrument and have outsourced its manufacturing to Hamilton Company, a leading manufacturer of automated liquid handling workstations. We have entered into a non-exclusive agreement with Hamilton that covers the manufacturing of the automation instrument and its continued supply on a purchase order basis. Starting in January 2025, we renewed the agreement under an extended term through December 2027. Following this extended term, the agreement will automatically renew annually for a maximum of two one-year renewal periods. Hamilton has represented to us that it maintains ISO 9001 and ISO 13485 certifications. ... During the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, we incurred a net loss of $33.7 million and $39.4 million and used $25.0 million and $26.1 million of cash in operations, respectively. As of June 30, 2026, we had an accumulated deficit of $499.7 million, and cash, cash equivalents, and investments of $209.5 million. We expect to continue to incur significant losses and do not expect positive cash flows from operations for the foreseeable future. Our expenses may increase in connection with our ongoing activities, as we: broadly market and sell the Proteograph Product Suite; attract, hire and retain qualified personnel; continue to build our sales, marketing, service, support and distribution infrastructure as part of our commercialization efforts; build-out and expand our in-house NP manufacturing capabilities; continue to engage in research and development of other products and enhancements to the Proteograph Product Suite; implement operational, financial and management information systems; obtain, maintain, expand, and protect our intellectual property portfolio; and build the infrastructure to operate and scale as a public company. ... We take a long-term view in growing and scaling our business and regularly review opportunities that meet our long-term growth objectives. Our future capital requirements will depend on many factors including our revenue growth rate, investments in continued commercialization efforts, acquisitions of complementary or enhancing technologies or businesses, including intellectual property rights, the timing and extent of additional capital expenditures to invest in existing and new facilities and equipment, the expansion of sales and marketing and international activities and the extent and magnitude of our ongoing research and development programs.

headline: SEERS: "We Will Maintain Our Market Leadership Through Platform Competitiveness, Not Price Competition" - EDAILY
summary_text: [Edaily Reporter NA EUN-KYUNG ] Medical artificial intelligence (AI) company SEERS TECHNOLOGY(458870)stated on the 6th, in response to concerns recently raised in some quarters about intensifying price competition in the patient monitoring market, that “we are maintaining our market leadership based on platform competitiveness, not price.” SEERS explained, “To date, there has been no decrease in orders or damage to revenue due to price competition,” adding, “Hospitals select vendors by comprehensively evaluating implementation experience, platform operational capabilities, and after-sales support systems, rather than simply choosing the lowest price.” The company also emphasized that its AI inpatient monitoring platform, “thynC™,” is not merely a medical device but a platform business that includes integration with hospital electronic medical records (EMR), AI analysis, operational processes, and customer support (CX). Ciers explained that, based on its extensive experience in deploying and operating systems at the largest number of medical institutions in Korea, it has secured numerous cases where it was selected as the final contractor even amid recent instances of price competition. Furthermore, the company stated that the real-world clinical data and customer feedback (VOC) accumulated as the number of partner medical institutions increases are key competitive advantages that enhance AI performance and service quality. It also added that it is securing cost competitiveness through proactive procurement and direct production of core components, while strengthening its market competitiveness based on economies of scale resulting from expanded operations. SEERS officials stated, “We are maintaining our number one position in the domestic market based on platform competitiveness, not price competition,” adding, “We will continue to expand our competitive advantage based on our accumulated operational experience and economies of scale.”

headline: SEERS Enhances 'Think' Operating System… Raises Barriers to Entry for the Platform - EDAILY
summary_text: [Edaily Reporter SONG YOUNG-DOO ] SEERS TECHNOLOGY(458870), a wearable AI diagnostic monitoring company, announced on the 5th that it has reorganized its operational structure into a business division system and enhanced the operational framework of its “thynC Connected Hub” in line with the expansion of its “thynC™” AI inpatient monitoring platform business. This reorganization is a measure aimed at enhancing the platform’s operational competitiveness rather than simply expanding the organization. Based on the field experience accumulated through its current operations at approximately 220 medical institutions nationwide—covering about 20,000 hospital beds—SEERS’ strategy is to further widen the gap with competitors by enhancing customer experience (CX) and operational efficiency. The company expanded its existing operations organization into a business division structure and separated the Operations Team from the Infrastructure Team. The Operations Team is dedicated to hospital operations and customer experience (CX), strengthening engagement with medical institutions, while the Infrastructure Team is responsible for hardware and AI software operations, as well as the procurement of key materials and cost management, thereby enhancing supply chain stability and price competitiveness. A dedicated hospital CX (Customer Experience) organization has also been newly established. By building a hybrid support system that combines an AI-based customer support system with specialized consultants, the company plans to respond swiftly to hospital inquiries and VOC (Voice of Customer) and incorporate accumulated customer feedback into product and service improvements. SEERS emphasized that the competitiveness of its AI healthcare platform lies not simply in increasing the number of hospitals, but in the data and know-how accumulated during operations. The company explained that as the number of hospitals grows, installation experience, operational standards, incident response history, and customer requirements are accumulated, creating a virtuous cycle that leads to the advancement of AI services and product improvements. In particular, given that the total number of hospital beds in South Korea is approximately 700,000, the company believes that its current scale of 20,000 beds is merely the beginning. It expects that if the number of operational beds expands to 50,000 or 100,000 in the future, the accumulated operational data and customer experience itself will become platform assets that competitors will find difficult to match in the short term. Jeong Hoon, Director of Think’s Business Division, stated, “The core competitive advantage of an AI healthcare platform lies in continuously incorporating the operational data and customer experiences accumulated in clinical settings into the improvement of AI services and products.” He added, “Based on the accumulated operational data, we will enhance service quality and operational efficiency to continuously strengthen the competitiveness of the Think platform.”

headline: Patient Monitoring Market: A Silent Battle... SEERS’ Strategy to Expand into Neurology - EDAILY
summary_text: [Edaily Reporter SONG YOUNG-DOO ] As competition in the domestic patient monitoring market intensifies, SEERS TECHNOLOGY(458870)is seeking to differentiate itself by expanding its market presence based on clinical data. Rather than engaging in price wars in the existing cardiology arrhythmia testing market, the company’s strategy is to create new prescription demand by expanding the scope of its wearable ECG solution, “Mobicare,” to neurology departments and stroke centers. SEERS has secured evidence—through Korea’s first prospective, multicenter clinical trial targeting patients with cryptogenic ischemic stroke—that its solution can detect latent atrial fibrillation, a condition often missed by conventional 24-hour monitoring. Once atrial fibrillation is confirmed, new strategies for preventing recurrence, such as anticoagulant therapy, can be established. In effect, Mobicare is expanding its role beyond that of a simple arrhythmia monitor to become a diagnostic tool that helps determine the treatment path for stroke patients. The significance of this strategy lies not in dividing the existing market with competitors, but in pioneering a new market—neurology—without the need for separate product development. If this leads to the establishment of separate reimbursement codes distinct from standard hospital care pathways, Mobicare’s target audience could expand from patients suspected of having arrhythmia to those at high risk of stroke recurrence. When combined with “Think,” the inpatient monitoring platform, it is expected to be possible to establish an integrated management system that connects patient monitoring during hospitalization to the tracking of latent atrial fibrillation after discharge. ... According to the company on the 27th, the results of the “Detection of Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Idiopathic Embolic Stroke: The AVANT-GARDE Clinical Trial,” which utilized Mobicare, were recently published in the international academic journal *Journal of Stroke and Cerebrovascular Diseases*. This study is the first prospective, multicenter clinical trial in Korea to directly compare the performance of long-term wearable ECG with conventional Holter monitoring in patients with cryptogenic embolic stroke (ESUS). Eight domestic medical institutions participated, including Eunpyeong St. Mary’s Hospital of the Catholic University of Korea, Kangdong St. Heart Hospital of Hallym University, Bucheon Hospital of Soonchunhyang University, Gil Medical Center of Gachon University, and Seoul Boramae Medical Center. The research team simultaneously administered 72-hour patch-type ECG monitoring and conventional 24-hour Holter monitoring to 113 patients with acute ischemic stroke. The results showed that the atrial fibrillation detection rate for the 72-hour test was 16.7%, approximately three times higher than the 5.6% rate for the 24-hour Holter test. When long-term monitoring was repeated six months later in patients in whom atrial fibrillation was not detected during the initial test, the cumulative detection rate rose to 18.9%. An embolic stroke is a type of stroke in which a blood clot blocks a cerebral blood vessel, but the exact origin of the clot cannot be clearly identified. It accounts for approximately 16% of all ischemic strokes. One of the major causes identified is silent atrial fibrillation, which occurs intermittently without symptoms. When atrial fibrillation occurs, blood clots can form inside the heart; if these clots block a cerebral blood vessel, they lead to a stroke. However, because the timing of silent atrial fibrillation is irregular, it is difficult to detect with a standard 24-hour test alone. This is why the likelihood of detecting atrial fibrillation increases as the duration of monitoring is extended. Once atrial fibrillation is confirmed, the secondary prevention strategy for stroke patients also changes. This is because anticoagulant therapy can be considered in addition to standard antiplatelet therapy. This means that extended monitoring does not merely identify more abnormal signals but can also lead to treatment decisions aimed at preventing recurrent strokes. A SEERS representative stated, “Atrial fibrillation in stroke patients is often intermittent, so observation for at least three days is necessary to increase the likelihood of detection,” adding, “This study is significant because it identified additional cases of atrial fibrillation—which might have been missed by conventional 24-hour monitoring—using long-term wearable ECG.” Numerous companies, including Huino, MEZOO Co., Ltd., and AT Sense, have entered the domestic wearable ECG market. These companies also offer products capable of long-term ECG monitoring. SEERS’ “first in Korea” distinction lies not in its product but in its clinical approach and business model. SEERS is the first company to conduct a prospective, multicenter clinical trial targeting Korean patients with embolic stroke, confirm the utility of long-term ECG monitoring, and leverage this to enter the neurology prescription market. A company official explained, “While domestic competitors also have products capable of measuring long-term ECG, they have not conducted clinical trials to apply this technology to stroke patients and expand into the neurology market,” adding, “Simply having a product is one thing; establishing actual evidence for prescribing through clinical trials involving medical staff from multiple university hospitals is another matter entirely.” Even if competitors possess similar devices, it is difficult for them to secure the same level of evidence in the short term without a hospital network, clinical trial experience, and patient data. In effect, the clinical network acts as a new barrier to entry in addition to the performance of the medical device itself. This strategy also shifts the competitive criteria in the domestic wearable ECG market from price and device performance to clinical data. In the existing market, key competitive factors included test duration, comfort, AI interpretation accuracy, and hospital supply prices. In contrast, once the value of the device in aiding treatment decisions for specific patient groups is proven, clinical evidence and clinical outcomes become more important than price. ... In particular, cardiology is already a market where several wearable ECG companies are competing. This is the reason why SEERS is focusing its efforts on expanding the medical departments that use Mobicare. From SEERS’ perspective, pioneering new medical departments that utilize Mobicare is more advantageous for growth than dividing the existing market with competitors. Entering the neurology field is a strategy aimed at creating additional demand—specifically among stroke patients—rather than taking away from existing demand for arrhythmia testing. The company explains that, within the scope of current approvals and ECG monitoring reimbursement rates, the use of Mobicare for stroke patients can be gradually expanded once hospital-specific treatment protocols are established. Since there is no need to build new hardware or AI analysis systems, the cost burden associated with increased testing is relatively low. A SEERS official stated, “Once a clinical pathway is established to allow the use of existing ECG monitoring reimbursement rates in neurology as well, we can immediately apply it to testing stroke patients,” adding, “Since this involves expanding the scope of use for Mobicare—a product that is already on the market—rather than developing a new product from scratch, market expansion could occur rapidly.” In the medium to long term, the company may also pursue securing separate indications and reimbursement codes. To secure an explicit indication such as “diagnosis of atrial fibrillation in patients with embolic stroke” or a separate reimbursement code, follow-up clinical trials to increase the patient sample size may be necessary. This study serves as the first domestic evidence to initiate discussions on additional clinical trials and reimbursement codes. A company official explained, “To establish reimbursement rates under the separate disease category of ‘stroke,’ additional clinical trials with a larger patient population may be necessary,” adding, “As this study provides the first data of its kind in Korea, it has laid the groundwork for initiating follow-up clinical trials and reimbursement rate discussions.” ... The expansion of Mobicare’s neurology services is also expected to create synergies with “Think,” a platform for monitoring hospitalized patients. While Think monitors the vital signs of hospitalized patients in real time, Mobicare measures long-term ECG data in outpatient and home settings after discharge. Stroke patients must continuously manage their risk of recurrence even after completing acute-phase treatment. This allows for a system where Think is used to monitor patients’ conditions during hospitalization, and Mobicare is used to track intermittent episodes of atrial fibrillation after discharge. This connects vital sign data—which was previously disconnected between inside and outside the hospital—onto a single platform. There is also potential to expand the scope of application beyond neurology to other medical departments. SEERS is conducting research to broaden the application of ECG analysis technology beyond the prediction of atrial fibrillation and myocardial infarction to include fields such as sleep medicine, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynecology, and hypocalcemia. The company emphasized, “Expanding Mobicare to multiple medical departments is a strategy that goes beyond simply increasing sales of a single product; it enhances the overall utility of SEERS’ monitoring platform,” adding, “Once we secure diverse clinical evidence in Korea, we can leverage it for our overseas business as well.” Mobicare recently obtained 510(k) clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). SEERS plans to conduct outpatient pilot studies at U.S. medical institutions before entering the Medicare reimbursement market. The experience gained from over 700,000 tests conducted in Korea, along with clinical results from stroke patients, can be leveraged during the pilot studies with U.S. medical institutions and the process of entering the insurance market.

headline: SEERS Begins Full-Scale Preparations to Supply Initial Shipment to the UAE… Accelerates Expansion into the Middle East with Participation in August’s IFM - EDAILY
summary_text: [Edaily Reporter SONG YOUNG-DOO ] SEERS TECHNOLOGY(458870), a wearable AI diagnostic monitoring company, announced on the 28th that it is proceeding as planned with the production and supply of the initial batch of mobiCARE™ under a supply contract with the United Arab Emirates (UAE), and will accelerate its expansion into the Middle East market by participating in the “IFM 2026 (International Family Medicine Conference & Exhibition)” to be held in Dubai this August. SEERS’ Middle East business gained momentum last February with the signing of a strategic memorandum of understanding (MOU) with PureHealth, the UAE’s largest healthcare group. Although concerns about potential delays arose due to geopolitical uncertainties in the region, the company has continued to advance its business as scheduled through ongoing collaboration with local medical institutions and partners. As a result, the company entered the commercialization phase in May by signing a supply contract worth approximately 22 billion won with One Health, a digital healthcare company affiliated with PureHealth. Currently, the company is preparing to produce and supply the initial batch for the UAE market and is sequentially advancing follow-up projects—such as outpatient care and health screening services—in collaboration with local partners. The company also plans to expand its reach into the Middle Eastern hospital market—comprising approximately 800,000 hospital beds—with a focus on the UAE and other GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council) countries, in line with growing demand for smart hospital infrastructure, through its AI inpatient monitoring platform, “thynC™.” To expand its business in the Middle East, SEERS will participate as a Gold Sponsor in IFM 2026, taking place at the Dubai World Trade Centre from August 25 to 27. IFM is the Middle East’s largest academic event for primary care and digital healthcare, featuring participation from the UAE Ministry of Health and the Dubai Health Authority, among others. It attracts a large number of attendees, including medical institutions from major GCC countries such as Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Oman, as well as global healthcare companies and medical professionals. At this event, the company plans to showcase Mobicare and Think, with a strategy to expand cooperation with medical institutions and partners in GCC countries based on the operational track record it has established in the UAE. The company intends to treat the UAE not as a single market but as a strategic hub for entering the Middle East, with plans to expand its business in phases. A company official stated, “Our UAE operations are proceeding as planned, and we are currently moving forward without a hitch with the production and supply of the initial batch.” The official added, “We will use our participation in IFM 2026 as an opportunity to expand our network in the Middle East market and ensure the stable growth of our core businesses—Think in the domestic market and Mobicare overseas.”

The plastic bottles production plant with extrusion blow molding will mark Alpla’s 19th North American site and represents a key part of its “long-term North American growth strategy.” The site will begin operations in spring 2027 and create 36 new jobs, Alpla said. - Cube Packaging Solutions is investing $30 million to expand its U.S. manufacturing capacity at a facility in St. Charles, Illinois, that first began production in 2025. The Canadian company specializes in recyclable, reusable polyethylene food containers and is backed by private equity firm Kent Road Capital. “St. Charles gives us a scalable American manufacturing platform, brings us closer to our customers, and provides the capacity, automation, and infrastructure to support their growth for years to come,” Cube CEO Philippe Erhart said in a statement. - CurTec USA, the American arm of the Dutch supplier of chemical and life sciences-safe packaging, is investing $10 million to expand its Westminster, South Carolina, facility that first opened in 2023. “A new blow molding line will significantly increase capacity and extend local production to smaller packaging sizes,” according to the announcement. CurTec first plans to produce 6- and 10-liter pails, followed by wide-neck drums. The company expects the 27,300-square-foot expansion will be completed in Q2 2027 and create 10 new jobs. - Dart Container announced it recently reached full operational capacity at a Lancaster, Pennsylvania, facility that is producing molded fiber trays, containers, bowls and other food packaging products. Dart says the site is helping to meet “growing customer demand for renewable, compostable packaging options.” - Midland, an Illinois-based paper and packaging specialist, added a distribution center in Nashville, Tennessee, which the company says positions it “for continued growth throughout the Southeast.” - Novolex opened a 17,500-square-foot applied innovation center in Roanoke, Texas. It features “five simulated market environments” spanning foodservice, grocery, retail, café and bakery, and quick-service restaurants, and also has a prototype room for forming, sealing, and printing. - Sealed Air has expanded manufacturing capacity for protective closed-cell polyethylene foam products at its existing Madera, California, facility to service industrial, automotive, electronics and medical customers in North America and Latin America. “We heard from customers and fabricators that dependable access to closed-cell PE foam is essential, and this investment is a direct response to that need,” said Byron Racki, president of protective packaging at Sealed Air, in the announcement.

headline: Circulate Capital Invests in Bumi Baru Plastik to Scale High-Performance Polyolefin Recycling in Indonesia | Circulate Capital
summary_text: [Indonesia, October 15, 2026] – Circulate Capital, a leading investment management firm advancing the circular economy in high-growth markets, today announced an investment in Bumi Baru Plastik (BBP), an Indonesian polyolefin recycler, to expand its operations. It is the firm’s sixth investment in Indonesia. BBP specializes in polypropylene (PP) and polyethylene (PE) recycling, converting post-consumer and post-industrial waste into OEM-grade recycled compounds. Its inputs include end-of-life vehicle (ELV) parts, woven and jumbo bags, rigid containers, industrial packaging, and manufacturing offcuts. ... Much of this waste, particularly contaminated rigid scrap, multilayer packaging, and mixed-resin industrial scrap, is typically downcycled into low-value applications. BBP’s processing technology instead produces high-purity recycled pellets that meet the technical standards of automotive, electronics, and industrial manufacturers, offering a cost-competitive alternative to virgin resin. Its primary customers today are the automotive sector, where its pellets go into spare parts for two- and four-wheelers such as back fenders and floor panels, and the woven packaging sector, which recycles bag to bag. BBP also plans to expand into high-purity PP extrusion, a market that still relies heavily on virgin plastic. ... The investment provides BBP with growth capital to move from pilot-scale production to a consolidated industrial site. Key operational objectives include: - 5X Capacity Expansion: Scaling current recycled PP and PE processing capacity over the next two years. - Site Consolidation: Streamlining operations at the Jonggol site in West Java, including upgrading wastewater treatment and strengthening on-site operations. - Downstream Integration: Establishing downstream manufacturing lines to convert recycled polyolefins directly into finished goods, such as specialized compounds and bubble wrap for industrial and commercial customers. - Feedstock Supply Security: Expanding domestic feedstock sourcing through an expanded network of more than 400 collection partners. ... At scale, the expansion is expected to deliver meaningful environmental benefits, including the additional 114,100 MT of accumulated plastics diverted or avoided and the accumulated avoidance of 435,000 tonnes of CO2e emissions until 2030-31. The investment will also support responsible sourcing programmes that improve traceability and uplift informal waste workers across the value chain.

headline: Gwangmu Completes Acquisition of Ubiz Solution... "Expanding Scale and Profitability Through Additional M&A" - The Asia Business Daily
summary_text: Gwangmu is expanding its business portfolio by making Ubiz Solution, a smart factory automation control specialist, a wholly owned subsidiary. The company plans to continue its growth in scale and profitability by pursuing additional mergers and acquisitions (M&A) following the acquisition of a company with stable profitability and cash generation capabilities. On September 30, Gwangmu announced that it had finalized a share purchase agreement worth a total of 30.7 billion won by paying a remaining balance of 28.1 billion won to acquire Ubiz Solution. Earlier, on September 9, the two companies signed a share purchase agreement (SPA) for the acquisition of Ubiz Solution. With the completion of this deal, Ubiz Solution has become a 100% subsidiary of Gwangmu. ... Ubiz Solution specializes in establishing smart factory automation control systems. The company possesses the technological capability to handle the entire process, from designing factory automation systems tailored to each client's production environment to equipment construction and installation, verification, and trial operation. ... In particular, the company has strong expertise in the pharmaceutical and biotech sectors, providing manufacturing and quality management systems (GMP-compliant production facilities) and process automation control. In the automation control business, Ubiz Solution offers building management system (BMS) and energy management system (EMS) automation, process automation, as well as design and consulting services. In the smart factory sector, it has secured the technology to respond to all five levels of ISA-95, the international automation standard. ... Such regulatory changes are driving increased demand for production process automation and data management system construction. As pharmaceutical and biotech companies continue to invest in automation and respond to GMP-related regulations, Ubiz Solution has continued to see steady growth in its performance. ... Ubiz Solution’s sales increased from 15.2 billion won in 2023 to 17.1 billion won in 2024 and reached 20.0 billion won in 2025. Operating profit also grew during the same period from 2.0 billion won to 3.5 billion won, and then to 4.6 billion won. The operating margin rose from 12.9% in 2023 to 20.3% in 2024, and to 22.9% in 2025. Net income continued to grow. Net income surged by approximately 73.3% from 1.9 billion won in 2023 to 3.3 billion won in 2024 and then rose by another 30.3% to 4.3 billion won in 2025. Over two years, the net income nearly 2.3 times increased. ... Major clients include SK Plasma, GC Green Cross Corporation, Chong Kun Dang, SK Biotek, DongA Pharm, and Dongkook Pharmaceutical. These are mostly pharmaceutical and biotech companies operating GMP production facilities. As GMP facilities require ongoing production line expansion, maintenance, and system upgrades even after initial construction, Gwangmu stated that existing clients are likely to have long-term relationships with the company. ... Gwangmu, having secured a cash-generating subsidiary through the acquisition of Ubiz Solution, also plans to pursue further M&A opportunities. A Gwangmu representative stated, "Cash generation capability is a key indicator for evaluating a company’s business competitiveness and financial soundness. Ubiz Solution continually generates free cash flow based on stable operating cash flow." They further said, "We plan to accelerate growth in scale and profitability by pursuing future additional M&A, focusing on companies with excellent operating profit and stable cash flow as acquisition targets." They added, "The next M&A is planned to be pursued on a scale that surpasses the current Ubiz Solution acquisition." ... Through this acquisition, Gwangmu aims to establish a new business foundation in pharmaceutical and biotech smart factory automation, securing a stable base for profit and cash generation, and to expand its business through additional M&A activities.

headline: InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply: International industry at a turning point - Intertabac
summary_text: # InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply: International industry at a turning point Erschienen am: 21. September 2026 Innovations and regulatory issues shaped the trade shows After three intensive days, the trio of InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply came to an end in Dortmund. Around 750 companies from 64 countries and numerous international trade visitors gathered in the ten exhibition halls to exchange views on current developments, new products and innovations. “This year, the trade show trio took place at a pivotal moment for the industry. Regulatory decisions are currently being prepared both in Germany and at European level that will shape the industry’s future development. The resulting need for orientation and dialogue was clearly evident,” said Sabine Loos, Managing Director of Westfalenhallen Unternehmensgruppe, which owns and operates the Messe Dortmund venue. ... Experiencing new products first-hand From Tuesday onwards, the trade show activities moved into the ten exhibition halls. For three days, direct dialogue between manufacturers, distributors, retailers and other market participants shaped the event in Dortmund. The focus was on numerous new products, innovations and market launches, which could be tested directly on site. For exhibitors, the immediate feedback from trade visitors provided valuable insights from the market and important findings for further product development. The exchange with international experts, associations and market participants made InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply a platform where current trends, opportunities and challenges became visible from a wide range of perspectives. ... Jan Mücke, CEO of the German Association of the Tobacco Industry and Next-Generation Products (BVTE), summarized why this exchange was particularly important for the association’s members at the present time: “Far-reaching decisions are pending regarding tobacco taxation in Germany and forthcoming European regulations. For our members, this is specifically about reliable and realistic conditions that reflect actual market developments. The openness and intensity of the discussions in Dortmund demonstrated the strong demand for direct dialogue about the future of our industry. InterTabac is the central meeting place for this purpose and once again underlined its importance as the industry’s leading platform.” ... Particularly high demand for information on regulation Especially in times of change, the conference program at the trade shows takes on particular importance. It creates space for well-founded information, the exchange of different perspectives and new insights into the future of the industry. In view of the current regulatory debates, the strong interest in panels and presentations on regulatory issues came as no surprise. The positive response to the international top speakers who travelled to Dortmund to share their expertise with the trade audience was all the more pleasing. ... The presentation “The uncertain future for nicotine pouches in Europe” by Jonas Lundqvist and Robert Casigne of the European Nicotine Pouches Alliance (ENPA) also attracted considerable interest. Nicotine pouches are one of the most dynamic segments in the market for next-generation products. This development was reflected at NUBIZ in the strong presence of relevant suppliers and product solutions. On the first day of the trade fair, PouchXchange also provided an exclusive forum for the pouch and snus industry, focusing on the segment’s key issues. These included rapid market development, regulatory questions and the different perspectives of market participants. The focused side event highlighted the importance of sound expert knowledge and direct dialogue in a rapidly developing market whose regulatory framework in Europe is still evolving. ... Shem Baldeosingh, Director of the Global Institute for Novel Nicotine (GINN), which once again acted as the event’s knowledge partner and contributed to the conference program, said: “InterTabac remains a major international meeting point for the nicotine-products sector, while PouchXchange gives modern oral nicotine its own dedicated forum for exchange, connection and collaboration. At the 2026 Dortmund events, GINN brought expert discussion, member engagement and partnership to the forefront, reinforcing that building a credible and sustainable pouch category requires more than product innovation alone. The conversations focused on the regulatory, sustainability and standards challenges that will define the sector’s future, alongside the need for stronger dialogue across the value chain. Together, InterTabac and PouchXchange demonstrated how informed collaboration can help shape a responsible, globally connected future for modern oral nicotine.” ... Another side event recognizes the innovative strength of the NGP industry Another side event brought the second day of the trade show to a close and placed the innovative strength of the NGP industry center stage. At the presentation of the InterTabac World Alternative Awards, companies were recognized for solutions that convinced the NUBIZ audience with their future-oriented approach. The winners were selected not only by a seven-member expert jury before the trade show, but also by members of the industry in an online vote. The awards went to: Best Pouch Product of the Year: iNIC Nicotine Pouches (Votary Investments) Best Pouch Flavor of the Year: FEDRS ONLY Mango Storm 20 mg/g (FEDRSz.oo.) Best Pouch Innovation of the Year: Energy Pouches (DENSSI) Best Pouch Manufacturer of the Year: UAB Global Snus Best Vape Device of the Year: NURA ZERO (Greentank Technologies) Best E-Liquid / Flavor of the Year: Lemon Tart (Dinner Lady) Best Vape Innovation of the Year: Spark 2 Series (KIWI Vapor) Best Next-Generation Product of the Year: Spark 2 Series (KIWI Vapor) Best Reduced Risk Concept / Innovation of the Year: Quantum Chip (Greentank Technologies) Best Branding & Marketing of the Year: ALP Best Overall Alternative Brand: WHAM (W&D Lifestyle Private Limited) ... Save the date: The 2027 date has already been set The three days of the trade shows initiated important discussions, enabled new contacts and strengthened existing networks. At the same time, they demonstrated that, despite regulatory and economic challenges, the industry has considerable innovative strength and is determined to actively shape its own development. Anyone wishing to start preparing for next year’s trade show visit can begin by making a note in their calendar: in 2027, InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply will take place from 14 to 16 September.

headline: Sibur to sell new Tobolsk polypropylene line's output to Africa and Asia — Packaging News Daily
summary_text: ### Sibur to sell new Tobolsk polypropylene line's output to Africa and Asia Sibur plans to export surplus output from a new 570,000 tonne-a-year polypropylene line at its ZapSibNeftekhim complex in Tobolsk, due to start up in 2027, once domestic demand is met. CEO Mikhail Karisalov said the plant's efficiency would make it competitive against overseas producers as the group expands supply to Southeast Asia and both coasts of Africa. Why this matters A new low-cost, high-volume Russian polypropylene source aimed at Africa and Asia could pressure resin pricing for packaging converters outside sanctioning markets. - The new ZapSibNeftekhim polypropylene line in Tobolsk has capacity of 570,000 tonnes a year. - The facility is due to start up in 2027. - Sibur CEO Mikhail Karisalov says volumes beyond domestic demand will be sold on the global market. - Sibur is expanding supply channels to Southeast Asia and both coasts of Africa. - Karisalov cites polypropylene as one of the fastest-growing plastics globally, used from construction to food packaging.

headline: Dortmund's Ten Halls Take the Measure of Nicotine's Shift - Pouch Insider
summary_text: InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply run 15 to 17 September in Dortmund with around 750 exhibitors from 64 countries spread across ten halls, according to Tobacco Journal International. Three fairs, ten halls and three days. From 15 to 17 September, Dortmund hosts InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply, with around 750 exhibitors from 64 countries showing products, machinery and supply-chain services to a trade audience that increasingly buys things that are not cigarettes. The architecture of the event is itself the story. A generation ago a tobacco fair was a tobacco fair. Now the programme splits: InterTabac for the classic trade, NUBIZ for the newer nicotine and lifestyle categories, and InterSupply for the machinery, materials and packaging businesses that have to retool for whatever the first two decide to sell. That three-way division is a fair reading of where the industry's money and anxiety currently sit. ... Around 750 exhibitors from 64 countries is a large number, but the more useful signal is the mix. Oral nicotine pouches, heated products, vapour hardware and e-liquid formulation now occupy floor space that once belonged exclusively to leaf, cigars and pipe accessories. Those categories bring different suppliers with them — flavour houses, foil and film converters, pouch-filling machinery builders, child-resistant closure makers — and it is the supply side, gathered under InterSupply, that reveals which product formats manufacturers actually expect to be producing in volume two and three years out. Machinery orders are placed long before shelves change. The internationalism is the second signal. A trade with buyers from dozens of countries is a trade operating under dozens of regulatory regimes at once. A pouch legal in Sweden may be restricted in the Netherlands, taxed differently in Germany, and unavailable in Australia. Exhibitors arriving in Dortmund are effectively pitching the same hardware into a patchwork, and the conversations on the stands tend to be less about the product than about which markets will still permit it next year. ... The wider market backdrop into the show was constructive rather than fearful. At the most recent close on Friday, 11 September 2026, the S&P 500 tracker SPY finished at $764.29, up 0.85% on the day from a previous close of $757.83. The Nasdaq 100 proxy QQQ closed at $714.88, up 0.87% from $708.69, and the Dow 30 fund DIA ended at $525.79, a gain of 0.97% against a prior $520.75. Those are broad benchmarks, not consumer-staples readings, but they set the risk tone in which any capital-allocation decision taken on a trade-show floor gets financed. ... ## What to watch across the three days - Machinery, not marketing. InterSupply's filling and packing exhibits indicate production capacity being built for specific formats. Capacity is a harder forecast than a press release. - NUBIZ's share of the floor. The relative prominence of the newer-category hall against the classic InterTabac halls is a rough proxy for how far the transition has actually travelled. - Country of origin. With exhibitors from 64 countries, the balance between European, Asian and North American suppliers hints at where pouch and vapour manufacturing is consolidating. - Regulatory talk. Flavour restrictions, nicotine-strength caps and excise treatment of oral products are the variables that decide whether any premiere shown this week reaches a shelf. ... The risk for exhibitors is that the transition they are showcasing is not theirs to control. Regulation, not innovation, has been the dominant variable in nicotine for a decade, and product categories that look ascendant in a hall in September can be constrained by a national ban before the next edition. Ten halls of premieres is a statement of intent. How much of it survives contact with lawmakers is the question the show cannot answer. ... ### What is the main uncertainty facing exhibitors? Regulation rather than product development. Flavour restrictions, nicotine-strength caps and the excise treatment of oral nicotine vary by country, so a format that draws crowds in Dortmund can be restricted or banned in a given market before it reaches retail. Exhibitors selling into dozens of jurisdictions face dozens of different rulebooks.

headline: Kwangmoo Acquires Ubiz Solution With 23% Operating Margin, Laying Foundation for Profit Turnaround - The Asia Business Daily
summary_text: KOSDAQ-listed company Kwangmoo is restructuring its business portfolio to focus on profitability by acquiring Ubiz Solution, a smart factory automation control solutions company, for 30.7 billion won. The strategy is to make Ubiz Solution, which boasts a high operating margin and stable financial structure, a 100% subsidiary and thereby improve consolidated results and turn a profit. Kwangmoo announced on September 10 that it held a board meeting on September 9 and signed a stock purchase agreement (SPA) to acquire all 60,000 shares (100% stake) of Ubiz Solution, held by CEO Mi-Sook Ji and nine others, for a total of 30.7 billion won. An initial payment of 2.6 billion won was made on the 9th, with the remaining 28.1 billion won to be paid on the 29th. Once the transaction is completed, Ubiz Solution will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Kwangmoo. ... Founded in 2008, Ubiz Solution specializes in building automated control systems for smart factories. Its main businesses include automation control, smart factory platforms, big data platforms, building and energy automation, and Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Validation for the pharmaceutical industry. In particular, Ubiz Solution is equipped to provide integrated solutions involving operational technology (OT), building and energy automation, GMP Validation, and smart factory platforms. The company’s major customers include large corporations such as POSCO, SK, Dong-A Pharm, and Chong Kun Dang, which is considered a competitive advantage. ... Ubiz Solution’s performance and financial condition are also stable. Last year, the company posted sales of 20 billion won, operating profit of 4.6 billion won, and net profit of 4.3 billion won. Its operating margin was 22.9%, generating about 23 won in operating profit for every 100 won of sales. Last year’s total equity stood at 18.7 billion won, and the company held 13.5 billion won in liquid assets and short-term financial products, with no financial debt. Kwangmoo expects that incorporating Ubiz Solution, with its strong profitability and financial soundness, will significantly contribute to improving its consolidated performance. ... This acquisition marks the first M&A since Kwangmoo’s change of largest shareholder in April last year. Kwangmoo has been reviewing acquisition targets centered on companies with both growth potential and profitability.

headline: [더벨]광무, 유비즈솔루션 307억에 품는다 - 머니투데이
summary_text: 코스닥 상장사 광무가 스마트팩토리 자동제어 솔루션 기업 유비즈솔루션의 지분 100%를 307억원에 인수하는 계약을 체결했다. 이번 인수는 광무의 최대주주 변경 이후 처음 추진되는 인수합병으로 수익성 중심의 사업구조 재편과 실적 개선을 목표로 했다. 유비즈솔루션의 지미숙 대표와 정성진 사장은 인수 이후에도 경영에 참여하여 경영 공백을 최소화하고 수주 경쟁력을 유지할 방침이다. ... 코스닥 상장사 광무(1,263원 ▼2 -0.16%)가 스마트팩토리 자동제어 솔루션 기업 유비즈솔루션을 인수하며 수익성 중심의 사업구조 재편에 나선다고 10일 밝혔다. 광무는 지난 9일 이사회를 열고 지미숙 대표 외 9인이 보유한 유비즈솔루션 주식 6만주(지분 100%)를 총 307억원에 인수하는 주식매매계약(SPA)을 체결했다고 전했다. 거래대금 중 계약금 26억원은 9일 지급했으며 잔금 281억원은 오는 29일 지급할 예정이다. 거래가 마무리되면 유비즈솔루션은 광무의 100% 자회사로 편입된다. ... 지난 2008년 12월 설립된 유비즈솔루션은 스마트팩토리 자동제어 시스템 구축 전문기업으로 자동제어, 스마트팩토리 플랫폼, 빅데이터 플랫폼, 의약품 제조·품질관리 기준 검증(GMP Validation) 등의 사업을 영위하고 있다. 포스코, SK, 동아제약, 종근당 등 대기업 중심의 고객사를 확보하고 있다. 지난해 매출액 200억원, 영업이익 46억원, 당기순이익 43억원을 기록했다. 같은 기간 자본총계는 187억원이며 금융부채 없이 현금성자산(단기금융상품 포함) 135억원을 보유하는 등 수익성과 재무건전성, 현금 여력을 두루 갖춘 기업이다. ... 광무는 이번 인수를 기점으로 연결 실적 개선이 본격화될 전망이다. 회사 측은 유비즈솔루션이 수익성에 안정적인 재무구조까지 갖춘 만큼 자회사 편입 이후 외형 확대와 영업이익 흑자전환에 도움이 될 것으로 기대했다.

headline: InterTabac, NUBIZ und InterSupply 2026 | Cigar Journal
summary_text: Drei Messen, zehn Hallen und eine Branche im Wandel: In wenigen Tagen wird Dortmund erneut zum internationalen Treffpunkt der Tabak- und Nikotinbranche. Vom 15. bis 17. September präsentieren rund 750 Aussteller aus 64 Ländern im Rahmen von InterTabac, NUBIZ und InterSupply ihre aktuellen Produkte, Neuheiten und Lösungen. Etablierte Marktführer und vielversprechende Newcomer treffen hier auf ein Fachpublikum aus Handel, Industrie und Distribution. Zahlreiche Unternehmen nutzen die drei Messetage, um neue Produkte erstmals vorzustellen und wichtige Impulse für das kommende Geschäft zu setzen. ... Philip Morris setzt auf der NUBIZ mit „Veev One Plus“ auf neue Flexibilität. Unter der Kappe des Geräts befindet sich Platz für einen zweiten Pod. Nutzer können dadurch eine Reserve mitführen oder zwischen zwei Aromen wechseln, ohne ein separates Behältnis in der Tasche zu suchen. Ein besonders konsequentes Mehrwegkonzept kommt zudem von Innokin. Beim „Trine Pod System“ lässt sich nicht nur der Pod, sondern auch der 1000-Milliamperestunden-Akku entnehmen und ersetzen. AIRSCREAM hingegen präsentiert erstmals die neue Produktlinie semi-gelartiger Nikotinbeutel M13 Cadence. Die Produkte setzen unter anderem auf eine schrittweise Freisetzung des Nikotins.

headline: 광무, 307억원에 유비즈솔루션 100% 인수 - TokenPost
summary_text: 광무가 스마트팩토리 자동제어 시스템 구축 기업 유비즈솔루션을 307억20만원에 인수한다. 거래는 9월 29일 종결될 예정이다. ... 광무(029480)가 스마트팩토리 자동제어 시스템 구축 기업 유비즈솔루션을 307억20만원에 인수한다. 거래가 끝나면 유비즈솔루션은 광무의 완전 자회사가 된다. 광무는 9일 이사회에서 유비즈솔루션 발행주식 6만주 전량을 지미숙 대표 등 10명으로부터 양수하기로 결정했다고 밝혔다. 양수 후 광무의 지분율은 100%다. 이번 거래 목적은 수익 증대를 위한 사업다각화다. 양수금액은 광무의 지난해 말 연결 기준 총자산 2314억4099만원의 13.26%, 자기자본 2159억2718만원의 14.22%에 해당한다. 대금은 현금으로 지급한다. 계약금 26억950만1700원은 9일 지급하고, 잔금 280억9051만8300원은 거래 종결 예정일인 9월 29일 지급할 계획이다. ... 유비즈솔루션은 스마트팩토리 자동제어 시스템 구축을 주요 사업으로 한다. 자본금은 3억원이며 발행주식 총수는 6만주다. 유비즈솔루션의 2025년 감사보고서 기준 자산총계는 229억9700만원, 부채총계는 42억8100만원, 자본총계는 187억1600만원이다. 같은 기간 매출액은 199억6600만원, 당기순이익은 42억7500만원으로 집계됐다.

headline: InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply: premieres, trends and new perspectives for the industry - Intertabac
summary_text: Three trade shows, ten halls and an industry in transition: in just a few days, Dortmund will once again become the international meeting place for the tobacco and nicotine industry. From 15 to 17 September, around 750 exhibitors from 64 countries will present their latest products, innovations and solutions as part of InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply. Established market leaders and promising newcomers will meet trade visitors from retail, industry and distribution. Numerous companies will use the three days to showcase new products for the first time and set important impulses for the future. ... For trade visitors, this creates an opportunity to meet key market players in one place, discover and test new products at an early stage, and identify the topics that will shape their business over the coming months. At the same time, personal and interdisciplinary exchange is becoming increasingly important: discussions about regulation and taxation, changing consumer habits and new product categories have a direct impact on markets and business models. ... At NUBIZ, Philip Morris is focusing on greater flexibility with “Veev One Plus”. The device’s cap contains space for a second pod. This allows users to carry a spare or switch between two flavors without having to look for a separate container in their bag. Innokin is also presenting a particularly consistent reusable concept. With the “Trine Pod System”, not only the pod but also the battery can be removed and replaced. AIRSCREAM, meanwhile, will present its new range of semi-gel nicotine pouches, M13 Cadence, for the first time. Among other features, the products are designed to release nicotine gradually. ... The need for this exchange is considerable: cigar culture combines traditional craftsmanship and a strong awareness of quality with a market that is constantly changing. Regulatory conditions, global supply chains and new consumer habits raise questions that are best assessed in depth through international dialogue. With three high-caliber thematic streams, the Summit provides a focused framework for this purpose. The Main Stage will focus on growth markets and strategies for entering international markets. The conference room “London/Bruges” will explore the connection between quality leadership, brand development and technological progress. Sessions will cover topics including tobacco cultivation and seed breeding, fermentation and storage, the selection of suitable distribution channels, and the relationship between production growth and brand exclusivity. The third stream, held in German in the “Bergen” conference room, is aimed specifically at representatives of the cigar and pipe retail trade from Germany, Austria and Switzerland. From 7.30 p.m., the exclusive Cigar Reception will provide an opportunity to continue discussions, expand international contacts and get into the spirit of the trade shows together. InterTabac: strong brands, new products and living cigar culture Following this focused professional opening, attention will turn to the three trade shows and their respective areas of focus from Tuesday onwards. In Halls 4 to 8, international exhibitors will showcase the broad range of products represented at InterTabac. In the conventional tobacco products segment, leading companies including Landewyck, Joh. Wilh. von Eicken, Philip Morris International (PMI), Karelia, KTNG, Continental Tobacco Germany, CAGS Tobacco and Lex Tobacco will be represented. The wide range of smoking accessories extends from lighters and ashtrays to rolling aids and filters. Corresponding products will be presented by companies including BIC, Gizeh, OCB, Zippo, AKRA Kotschenreuther, Hermann Hauser and Moosmayer. High-quality pipes will be presented by companies including VAUEN and Chacom. Cigars have traditionally formed one of the core areas of InterTabac. This year, more than 170 exhibitors will be concentrated primarily in Halls 4 and 7. Trade visitors will meet companies including Joya de Nicaragua together with Quesada, E.P. Carrillo, La Flor Dominicana, Villiger Söhne, August Schuster, GRE Trade with Drew Estate, Ferio Tego and Arturo Fuente. Promising brands such as Dynasty Cigars together with Victor Calvo Cigars, Rocky Patel, Matilde Cigars, Casa DR together with SansPareil, Blackbird Cigar and Don Emmanuel Cigars will also be exhibiting for the first time. LA FLOR DE ZAIDA, a US manufacturer of high-quality cigars, is bringing a prominent aficionado to the trade show as well: on the first day of the event, Hollywood star Ralf Moeller will visit the company’s stand in Hall 4, stand A22, between noon and 3 p.m. Football fans will be particularly excited by the presence of Don Fabio Cigars (stand 8.E08): entrepreneur and football manager Fabio Cordella is bringing several of his former colleagues to the trade show. Among them, Diego Lugano, Sébastien “Seba” Frey and Amauri will sample the exclusive cigars, which are made with tobacco fermented in Italian barrique wine barrels. The manufacturers’ presentations will be complemented by practical formats that offer particular benefits for specialist retailers. On Tuesday and Wednesday, master blender Claudio Sgroi will provide an in-depth insight into the art of cigar blending. The popular “Blending Experience” is designed as an exclusive format for retailers. The workshop “Decoding Cigars – by ICSI” is another new feature and will be offered on all three days of the trade show. Anthony Azar, founder of the International Cigar Sommelier Institute (ICSI), will present a structured approach to understanding, selecting and making optimal use of cigars. “The Modern Cigar Consumer Series” will also examine the market from a contemporary perspective. In a new three-part masterclass series, certified cigar sommelier Mechelle Merkerson will explore topics including the influence of digital platforms and the growing importance of women as consumers, business leaders and contributors to the industry’s growth. In the Crossover Lounge at the North Entrance, stand NE.D02, Cigar & Spirits Consultant Jens Tausch will guide trade visitors through the complex flavor profiles of selected spirits and specially matched cigars. NUBIZ: innovative products and international market impulses NUBIZ will primarily occupy the Westfalenhalle, Halls 1, 1B and 2, parts of Hall 3 and the passage leading to Hall 3. Around 300 exhibitors will showcase current products and developments in the fields of vaping and pouches as well as other novel nicotine products. Participating companies include Fox Electronics FZ LLC, Flerbar, HQD, Vaporesso, TRULO, Fumot, AIRSCREAM, Intrade Concepts and InnoCigs. Oral products such as pouches and snus will be presented by companies including SnusGlobe, Camo Snus, Premium Pouch Finland, Nicopods ehf (ICE) and ALP Supply. Focused side events will address key developments in these product segments. The third PouchXchange will kick off the program on the first day of the trade show. Organized in cooperation with the Global Institute for Novel Nicotine (GINN) and supported by industry sponsors, the event will focus on global market trends, regulatory developments and current challenges relating to nicotine pouches and snus. Participants will receive practical insights for their day-to-day business and an exclusive opportunity to expand their international networks in a targeted way. On the second day of the trade show, the InterTabac World Alternative Awards will follow. First held in 2024, the awards recognize pioneering innovations in the reduced-risk tobacco and nicotine segment. Manufacturers, brand managers, distributors and decision-makers will gain a concise overview of products and developments that could shape the market in the future. Ten awards will be presented in four categories: “Pouch Products”, “Vape & Vapor Solutions”, “Next Generation & Reduced Risk Products” and “Brand & Market Impact”. InterSupply: international solutions for production and processing Around 160 exhibitors from 38 countries will once again make InterSupply in Hall 3 an international meeting place for the production and supply industry. Almost 90 per cent of the companies are travelling from outside Germany. Established exhibitors include Universal Leaf Tobacco, Körber Technologies, Focke & Co., G.D. SpA and Hertz & Selck. At the same time, a number of newcomers will expand the range on offer, including Eckel & Sohn, Atlantic Chemicals Trading, Sachee Fragrances & Chemicals, Bamet, Honeywell and SYMETAL ALUMINIUM FOIL INDUSTRY. Inspiration for the point of sale For specialist retailers, the range of products and services at the trade show offers inspiration beyond the product assortments themselves. In the foyer at the North Entrance, visitors will find innovative solutions for the point of sale – from displays and shopfitting to shelving, security and merchandise management systems, as well as press products and spirits. In Dortmund, visitors can therefore discover not only new products but also concrete ideas for product presentation, sales areas and day-to-day business. Exhibitors include providers such as Ingenieurbüro Hoffmann, Familybro, 7concepts, HAROMEX and SCHAPFL GmbH. Conference program continues to gain importance Discover products, assess market developments, gain knowledge for your own business and expand international contacts: InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply are far more than product showcases. With their high-caliber conference program, the Dortmund trade show trio becomes a central meeting place for everyone who wants to understand the industry’s current transformation, take away new impulses for their business and expand their network in a targeted way. Key topics include European regulation, tax developments and questions relating to science, consumer realities and innovation. Manufacturers, specialist retailers, distributors and suppliers will gain additional perspectives on issues that have a direct impact on business models, product categories and supply chains. High-profile speakers and experts will include representatives from Tamarind Intelligence, Tobacco Europe, Euromonitor, the Independent European Vape Alliance (IEVA), the European Confederation of Tobacconists (C.E.D.T.), the European Cigar Manufacturers Association (ECMA), the Cigar Association of America (CAA), the Premium Cigar Association (PCA), the Polish Tobacco Association, the European Nicotine Pouches Alliance (ENPA), the Polish Government, Yunnan University, osapiens, Sanova, REJO and Chemnovatic. The full program, including all sessions, speakers and times, is available here. CB Expo creates additional points of connection Alongside InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply, the Cannabis Business Expo and Conference – CB Expo – will also return to Dortmund for the fourth time. It provides the European cannabis industry with a platform for business development, knowledge transfer and networking. In 2026, it will be integrated even more closely into the overall concept of the three trade shows. Exhibitors from the cannabis industry will present their products and services, with a particular focus in Halls 6 and 8, at the heart of the international trade show activity. This will allow the growing points of connection between cannabis, tobacco, next-generation products and accessories to be used in a targeted way. The CB Conference will also move closer to the conference program of the three trade shows. While deep-dive sessions in the “Bruges” conference room will address cannabis-related topics, the Main Stage at the North Entrance will offer cross-industry topics and insights. Tickets for CB Expo are also valid for InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply – and vice versa. Strong partners underline the importance as an international industry platform The presence of numerous national and international associations and organizations confirms InterTabac’s importance as a central industry platform. Representatives of the German Association of the Tobacco Industry and Next-Generation Products (BVTE), the German Cigarette Association (DZV), the North Rhine Westphalia Retailers‘ Association, State Tobacco Association, VdR – Der Tabakmittelstand, the German Cigar Industry Association (BdZ), the German Federal Association of Tobacco Retailers (BTWE), the German Shisha Tobacco Association, the Alliance for Tobacco-Free Enjoyment (BfTG), the German E-Cigarette Retailers‘ Association (VdeH) and the German Association of Tobacco Wholesalers and Vending Machine Operators (BDTA) will all travel to Dortmund. International organizations represented will include the Independent European Vape Alliance (IEVA), the Federatie van de Sigarenindustrie in België en Luxemburg (FECIBEL), Tobacco Europe, ProCigar, the UK Vaping Industry Association (UKVIA), the European Cigar Manufacturers Association (ECMA), the Cigar Association of America (CAA), the European Rolling Paper Association (ERPA), the European Smoking Tobacco Association (ESTA), the International Tobacco Growers’ Association (ITGA) and the Premium Cigar Association (PCA). The Confédération Européenne des Détaillants en Tabac (CEDT) will travel to Dortmund with members from several countries. Dortmund will therefore provide an international overview of the industry that can only be found in a small number of locations: products can be experienced at first hand, developments can be assessed by industry experts, and contacts can be established across markets and segments. Anyone who wants to understand the topics, innovations and decisions that will shape the tobacco and nicotine industry in the future will find the relevant contacts in one place at InterTabac, NUBIZ and InterSupply from 15 to 17 September. Notes for journalists We warmly invite you to cover the trade shows. In our press shop, you can register online in advance for your complimentary press ticket for the trade shows and the Cigar Culture Summit. Our accreditation guidelines are available here. On the first day of the trade shows, 15 September, at 11 a.m., the press event in the Bergen conference room will provide an opportunity to speak with leading industry associations about the current issues facing the sector. All information is available here. Please register in advance via email: presse@intertabac.de. To help you prepare for the trade shows, we have compiled extensive information in our digital press kit. The documents are available for download here.
